papers.title: A Success Model at the End of Its Life Cycle: 30 Years of Regionalised Regional Rail in Germany
papers.abstract: On 1 January 1996, Germany transferred responsibility for regional passenger rail services from the federal government to the states. Three decades later, passenger-kilometres have doubled and competitive tendering has lowered operating costs substantially, making regionalisation the most successful element of the German rail reform. Its organisational model, however, has reached the end of its life cycle: tenders now attract on average only 1.3 bids, 26 contracting authorities and some 60 transport associations maintain overlapping structures, rolling-stock procurement has repeatedly shifted risk onto passengers, and since the Court of Justice of the European Union struck down the German track-access charge cap in 2026, funding no longer covers the ordered service volume. This article reviews the motives and results of regionalisation, identifies three structural design flaws, and argues for a second reform: consolidating authorities, standardising rolling stock, deciding between a repaired market model and integrated public operation, and indexing funding to real infrastructure cost development. The submission contains an English translation followed by the German original.

authors.name: Lukas Ifflander
authors.institution: Hochschule für Technik und Wirtschaft Dresden – University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: Flatness and Tightness in Hypertopes
papers.abstract: A hypertope is a thin, residually connected incidence geometry. For each pair of types $\{i,j\}$, the residues of that type must be polygons, and if all residues of that type are the same type of polygon, then we can record this information in a diagram $D$. Given such a diagram, we prove a lower bound on the number of chambers of a hypertope with that diagram. A hypertope that achieves this bound is called \emph{tight}. We prove that a hypertope is tight if and only if its diagram $D$ is a forest and, for every pair of types $\{i,j\}$ that is not an edge of $D$, every $i$-element is incident to every $j$-element. This generalizes a previously known result about abstract polytopes. Finally, we describe a combinatorial method and an algebraic method for constructing tight hypertopes.

papers.title: DNA: Unlocking Depth Scaling in CTR Models
papers.abstract: Long user behavior sequences are among the strongest signals for click-through rate (CTR) prediction. Cross-attention makes these sequences practical for industrial ranking by keeping compute linear in sequence length. Yet the gains from stacking cross-attention layers taper off: on Taobao search, growing a cross-attention stack from 16 to 28 layers adds only 0.02 percentage points (pt) of AUC. We argue that the key-value side is the bottleneck. Each layer projects the same behavior sequence into keys and values, so adding depth gives the model more reads of a fixed sequence. We propose DNA (Dual-stream Nexus Attention), which lets the sequence itself evolve with depth. At each layer, the request representation (the search query, user features and scene) first reads the sequence. Each behavior token then attends to the updated request representation and uses what it reads to update itself, so the next layer reads a sequence shaped by the current request. The update runs once per request, all candidates share the resulting sequence, and both the reads and the update keep linear complexity in sequence length. At comparable forward FLOPs, DNA improves AUC over cross-attention stacks by 0.08 to 0.26 pt and keeps improving in the depth range where those stacks level off. DNA-4 is deployed in Taobao search. In an online A/B test against the production model, it improves CTR by 0.8% and GMV by 0.5%.

papers.title: Informative Local Average Treatment Effects Using Propensity Scores
papers.abstract: In instrumental variable (IV) models, comparisons of conditional local average treatment effects across covariates can mix effect heterogeneity in observed covariates with changes in the complier population, that is, those whose treatment responds to the instrument. Compliers at different covariate values may differ in unobserved characteristics that may also drive effect heterogeneity. We propose informative conditional local average treatment effects (ICLATEs), which condition on a subset of covariates of interest and on the treatment propensity scores under both values of a binary instrument. Fixing these scores holds constant the range of unobservables that drive treatment selection and thus compliance, while the composition of the covariates not conditioned on may change. Under conditional IV assumptions and suitable support conditions, we establish nonparametric identification and characterize the relationship of the ICLATEs to marginal treatment effects. We distinguish effect homogeneity in the unobservables driving treatment selection from effect homogeneity across excluded covariates. We clarify their roles in extrapolating complier effects to population effects and show that, jointly, they yield a testable implication even with a single binary instrument. For estimation, we combine cross-fitted machine learning of the nuisance functions with pooled local linear regression of doubly robust scores. Under undersmoothing and regularity conditions, we establish pointwise asymptotic normality, which a simulation study supports. As an empirical illustration, we apply the method to the Job Corps program to assess how the earnings effects of training participation vary with age.

papers.title: Nondefective lifts of stationary discs and the 2-jet determination problem
papers.abstract: We introduce a natural notion of defect for lifts of stationary discs attached to a CR nondegenerate submanifold $M \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ of codimension $d$. We prove that the existence of a nondefective lift of a stationary disc implies that germs of CR automorphisms of $M$ are uniquely determined by their $2$-jet. We emphasize that, in particular, this unifies all previously known results on this question.

papers.title: Constraints and biases: impact of light-cone effects on power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts
papers.abstract: Next-generation galaxy surveys will map large-scale structure over unprecedented volumes, bringing two goals within reach: constraining primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) and detecting relativistic effects on the largest scales. On these scales, relativistic and wide-separation (light-cone) effects share the scale dependence of local-type PNG, so they must be modelled to avoid biased inferences and to recover the true uncertainties. We present joint power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts that include these effects, with a multi-tracer bispectrum covariance including the odd-parity multipoles and leading non-Gaussian terms. Neglecting light-cone effects biases local-type $f_{\rm NL}$ by $\sim2\sigma$ for a Euclid-like H$\alpha$ survey and $>10\sigma$ for a MegaMapper-like LBG survey, mostly through lensing; wide-separation and local relativistic effects contribute $<1\sigma$. With these corrections included, marginalising over the evolution and magnification biases without informative priors increases the uncertainty on local-type $f_{\rm NL}$ by $\sim60\%$ for a Euclid-like power spectrum and by $\sim50\%$ for a joint power spectrum and bispectrum analysis of the even multipoles. However, the odd-parity multipoles of the single-tracer bispectrum and the multi-tracer power spectrum, which are sensitive to leading-order relativistic corrections, break most of this degeneracy. Non-local shapes are less affected; for these, a bright-faint split of the MegaMapper-like survey improves the joint constraints on the equilateral and orthogonal shapes by a factor of $\sim2$. Finally, local relativistic effects should be detectable at SNR $\sim13$, with a bright-faint split of a DESI-like BGS survey, provided the magnification bias is known to a few per cent, but only marginally, SNR $\lesssim2.5$, for the higher-redshift surveys, and not with the single-tracer bispectrum dipole.

papers.title: On the non-extendibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs $\{n,2n\}$ with $n = 2k^2 \pm k$
papers.abstract: We study a class of Diophantine problems arising from triangular analogues of classical Diophantine tuples. A set of positive integers is called a triangular $D(n)$-tuple if the product of any two distinct elements, increased by $n$, is a triangular number. In this paper, we investigate the extensibility of triangular $D(n)$-pairs of the form $\{n,2n\}$, where $n = 2k^2 + \varepsilon k$, with $k$ an odd positive integer and $\varepsilon \in \{-1,1\}$ such that $4k + \varepsilon$ is prime. We prove that for all $(k,\varepsilon)$ in a finite explicitly determined set, the pair $\{n,2n\}$ cannot be extended to a triangular $D(n)$-quadruple. The obtained results give further evidence for a general non-extensibility phenomenon, which we formulate as a conjecture.

papers.title: Curvature Integrability in Twinor Theory: An Ambitwistor Approach to the Twinor Googly Problem
papers.abstract: The twinor analogue of the googly problem is addressed through an ambitwistor structure defined by null autoparallels, retaining both chiralities, sources and torsion without requiring chiral null surfaces. Under the stated quotient, evaluation and descent assumptions, holomorphic affine sections reconstruct the twinor field equation $DY=J$. Correspondence-space cohomology realizes the contracted chiral and ladder equations, including the ladder's soldering coupling and mass-normalization source. For a prescribed non-normal conformal connection, infinity-twistor parallelism recovers the energy--momentum equation, supplemented by independent spin-current equations. These constructions give a conditional auxiliary formulation; constitutive sources and gravitational prescriptions remain dynamical input.

papers.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part I: physical-space structures and energy variance budget
papers.abstract: Vertically resolved budget analyses of frozen moist static energy (FMSE) variance within a cloud-resolving model provide a rigorous perspective on the equilibrium state of deep convective self-aggregation. The analysis reveals that the variance budget is governed by a leading-order balance between vertical variance advection and the gradient term, which quantifies the coupling between vertical covariance FMSE fluxes and the mean vertical stratification. Because vertical FMSE covariance fluxes are strictly positive throughout the atmospheric column, the sign of the gradient term is entirely dictated by the vertical gradient of mean FMSE. The primary peak of variance production occurs at the boundary layer top, driven by the interplay between sharp FMSE gradients, intensified in dry regions where the moist boundary layer decouples from the dry free troposphere, and robust vertical covariance fluxes. The persistent positivity of these fluxes implies that moist (dry), high-energy (low-energy) anomalies are systematically tied to updrafts (downdrafts), regardless of the mean gradient sign. This breakdown of classical down-gradient mixing indicates that vertical transports are governed by non-local, long-distance interactions driven by large-scale overturning circulation. The large variance produced near the boundary layer top is subsequently transported upward and dissipated in the upper troposphere, where the gradient term turns into a sink. While radiation does not directly force local variance, it indirectly shapes the budget by establishing the mean stratification. Overall, local thermodynamic forcings are translated by the overturning circulation into the spatial redistribution of variance across multiple scales.

authors.name: Lorenzo Silvestri
authors.institution: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

papers.title: Multi-scale dynamics of deep convective self-aggregation. Part II: scale-by-scale budget and mesoscale self-similarity
papers.abstract: This work investigates deep convective self-aggregation in the space of scales, extending the physical-space analysis of Part I. We introduce a novel theoretical framework by examining and deriving a generalized Yaglom equation for the second-order structure function $\langle \delta h_f^{\prime 2} \rangle$, the scale-dependent variance of Frozen Moist Static Energy (FMSE). Self-aggregation is found to be sustained by an inverse energy cascade driven by boundary-layer production and mediated by mesoscale circulations with horizontal scales $r \sim$(100-250 km). The inverse cascade of energy is found to be realized through a series of shallow and mid-level mesoscale circulations which behave in a self-similar way. Accordingly, the scale-energy variance exhibits an extraordinary collapse across all atmospheric layers onto a robust self-similar power law, $\langle \delta h_f^{\prime 2} \rangle \sim r^{6/5}$. In contrast, horizontal velocity increments show a degree of self-similarity ($\langle \delta u_r^{\prime 2} \rangle \sim r^{2/5}$) that retains a residual height dependence. Interestingly, the FMSE scaling breaks down at elevations lower than 750 m and at small local scales below 100 km, allowing us to identify the boundary layer top as a scale-dependent dividing layer where the strong stratification filters the interactions between the surface and free-troposphere, so that small scale dynamics of the low and high atmospheric layers are decoupled while those at large mesoscale are coupled. The derived scaling laws are also used to quantify the moisture-convection feedback via scale-dependent correlation coefficients that show that vertical transport strengthens with scale ($\rho_{mc\perp} \sim r^{2/5}$), while horizontal convergence weakens at the exact inverse rate ($\rho_{mc\parallel} \sim r^{-2/5}$).

authors.name: Lorenzo Silvestri
authors.institution: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia

papers.title: Exact guarantees and faster algorithms for $k$-rollercoasters
papers.abstract:
For $k\ge3$, a $k$-rollercoaster is a sequence of distinct values whose maximal increasing and decreasing runs all have length at least $k$. We discover the maximum guaranteed length $f_k(n)$ of $k$-rollercoasters appearing as subsequences of $n$-point permutations. In particular, letting $q=k-1$, we prove that $f_k(n)= \lceil n/q\rceil$ for $n\ge2q^2$, $f_k(n)= 2q-\lfloor \sqrt{2q^2-n}\rfloor$ for $q^2<n<2q^2$ and $f_k(n)= 0$ otherwise. We prove that the guarantees are tight by constructing an $n$-point permutation whose longest $k$-rollercoaster has exactly $f_k(n)$ points. Our proof extends Seidenberg's argument [Journal of the London Mathematical Society, 1959] for proving the Erd\H{o}s--Szekeres theorem by representing points in a subsequence with respect to the lengths of longest monotonic (increasing and decreasing) subsequences that reach each point.
  The combinatorial proof yields a deterministic comparison-based algorithm that finds a rollercoaster of length at least $f_k(n)$ in $O(n\log f_k(n))$ time and $O(n)$ space for $n>q^2$. Independently, we give an $O(nk\log k)$-time, $O(nk)$-space algorithm for a longest $k$-rollercoaster, improving the previous $O(nk^2)$ bound. We use the dynamic program of Gawrychowski et al. [STACS 2019, Algorithmica 2022], and process its weighted predecessor queries through monotone subsequences with finger-search trees. Both algorithms return such subsequences.

papers.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
papers.abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. The approach uses satisficing planning and replans when changes during execution invalidate the current plan. PLANTA is evaluated in two robotic scenarios involving underwater inspection and ground navigation. The results support the feasibility of runtime co-adaptation and show lower planning time and memory consumption compared with optimal-policy generation in the evaluated navigation scenario, while producing plans of similar quality.

papers.title: Nematic equilibria on a M\"obius strip: topology and extrinsic curvature
papers.abstract: We investigate the equilibrium configurations of a nematic liquid crystal confined in a thin tubular neighbourhood of a M\"obius strip. Assuming degenerate tangential anchoring and a director uniform across the thickness, we derive an effective two-dimensional Frank energy that accounts for both the intrinsic and extrinsic curvature of the mid-surface. The non-orientability of the substrate imposes identification conditions that couple the reversal of the local frame to the head-to-tail symmetry of the nematic director. We show that the resulting topological classification depends on the parity of the number of half-twists: the sector index is a winding number for even parity, whereas only its parity is physically meaningful for odd parity, in which case the net director rotation is not quantised. We analyse the narrow-strip limit and solve the full two-dimensional equilibrium problem by finite-element methods. The competition between topological sectors depends on the strip aspect ratio and elastic anisotropy. In particular, for a single half-twist, the preferred sector changes at an aspect ratio of approximately 0.58, while for two half-twists two distinct minima of the same sector exchange their energy ordering near 0.60, without any change of topology. These results reveal how non-orientable topology and extrinsic curvature jointly shape nematic equilibria on curved substrates.

papers.title: Extracting Value from Grey Literature: processes and technologies for aggregating and analyzing the hidden big data treasure of organizations
papers.abstract: Grey literature can be a valuable source of information about organizations activities and, to a certain extent, about their identity. Some of the major problems that hinder their full exploitation are the heterogeneity of formats, the lack of structure, the unpredictability of their content, the size of the document bases, which can quickly become huge. The collection and mining of grey literature can be applied to individual organizations or classes of organizations, thus enabling the analysis of the trends in particular fields. To this end, some techniques can be inherited from the best practices for the management of structured documents belonging to well identified categories, but something more is needed in our case. Obvious steps are: identifying sources, collecting items, cleansing and de-duplicating contents, assigning unique and persistent identifiers, adding metadata and augmenting the information using other sources. These phases are common to all digital libraries but further steps are required, in our opinion, in the case of grey literature in order to build document bases of value.

authors.name: L. Reggiani
authors.institution: IRCCS Azienda Ospedliero-Universitaria di Bologna Policlinico di Sant'Orsola

papers.title: You Have Mail: Set-Theoretic Types for Actors
papers.abstract:
We present a type system for the processes of Elixir, a dynamic language based on the actor model whose static type system covers only its functional core. Each process is typed by $\mathtt{pid}(t)$, where the ``interface'' $t$ is the type of the messages the process expects in its mailbox: sends are checked against the recipient's interface, and receives rely on the interface of the process that performs them.
  One of the difficulties of typing Elixir is that mailboxes are implicit: a function shipped in a message may evaluate $\mathtt{self()}$ and execute receive instructions, and both refer to whichever process eventually runs the function---$\mathtt{self()}$ returns that process's pid, receive reads that process's mailbox---so the mailbox they act on is not known where the function is written. We solve this problem by inferring, for every function, bounds on the type of the mailboxes it can be used with; as a result, the system types higher-order functions that travel in messages even when they contain reference to $\mathtt{self()}$ and receive instructions.
  The only new annotation the programmer writes is the interface of each spawned process; everything else is inferred by reusing the existing subtyping and constraint-resolution machinery of Elixir, and the system is proved sound.
  For legacy code, the interface can be reconstructed from the receive clauses: what the branches do with their messages bounds it from above, and the most permissive solution is sharp enough to recover received pids and closures.

authors.name: Giuseppe Castagna
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Neutral hydrogen in the Shapley Supercluster core II. Gas content and star formation in the filaments connecting the core
papers.abstract: We investigate the neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) content of galaxies across the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) at z = 0.048 by combining new deep MeerKAT L band observations of five filament pointings with archival MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey observations of the supercluster core. Together with optical data from the Shapley Supercluster Survey, these observations provide a homogeneous view of galaxy evolution from the virialised cluster environment to the surrounding filaments. We compare the HI content, star formation activity, gas depletion timescales, and morphological properties of galaxies relative to the gas fraction and star forming main sequences. The global HI detection fraction increases from 30 per cent in the cluster centre to 45 per cent in the filaments. While HI detected galaxies in the cluster centre are dominated by transition zone systems, the filament population is shared nearly equally between star forming main sequence and transition zone detections, indicating ongoing environmental transformation. Their gas properties also differ: cluster galaxies exhibit progressively depleted HI reservoirs towards the red sequence, whereas filament galaxies remain primarily gas rich. Within the filaments, long HI depletion timescales exceeding the Hubble time are concentrated in specific populations, notably 71 per cent of transition zone and 57 per cent of gas rich detections, indicating the inefficient conversion of atomic gas into stars. The HI detected filament population is dominated by late type galaxies, while the underlying non detected population is primarily composed of early type systems, consistent with environmental pre processing before cluster infall.

authors.institution: Laboratoire de Physique Subatomique et des Technologies Associées

authors.institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Magnolia: a highly magnetized galaxy at redshift $z\simeq9$
papers.abstract: The theory of galactic magnetic field growth via dynamo action predicts that the interstellar medium (ISM) of early galaxies would remain virtually unmagnetized on large scales. However, recent observations of strong dust polarization in galaxies at redshifts $z\simeq2.6$ and $z\simeq5.6$ challenge this paradigm. If galaxies indeed host strong, large-scale, coherent magnetic fields at high-$z$, then galaxy evolution and current theories of magnetic field amplification in galaxies should be revisited. To address the full physical complexity of early magnetic field growth in galaxies, we have designed MAGNA SERRA, a suite of radiation-magneto-hydrodynamical (RMHD) cosmological zoom-in simulations with non-equilibrium chemistry. In this first paper from the MAGNA SERRA suite, we present Magnolia, a galaxy hosted in a $\simeq 10^{11}~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ dark matter halo simulated with RAMSES-RT with a $\simeq 10^4~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ mass ($\simeq 10 \,\mathrm{pc}$ spatial) resolution. We find that, at $z\simeq9$, Magnolia has a stellar mass of a few times $10^8~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and is strongly magnetized, reaching a magnetic field of a few $\mu G$ and a plasma beta $\beta\simeq 0.1$ in the densest regions. This strong amplification occurs over a timescale of about 40~Myrs due to the highly dynamical nature of the galaxy, which creates strong compressions and shear. The power spectra of the magnetic and kinetic energies and the spectral energy transfer functions do not suggest dynamo action, but rather an initial magnetic field amplification through a large-scale compression, and a later re-organization of this field from small to large scales. Our findings show that strong galactic magnetization is possible at very high redshifts, which means that magnetic fields can play a dominant role throughout a galaxy's evolutionary history. (abridged)

authors.name: Mahsa Kohandel
authors.institution: Osservatorio di Astrofisica e Scienza dello Spazio

papers.title: Structure and Complexity of Perfect Functional Representations
papers.abstract: For given random variables $(X,Y)$, functional representation lemma states that there exists a random variable $Z$ and a deterministic function $g$ such that $Y = g(X,Z)$, and $X$ is independent of $Z$. In other words, $Z$ captures all the information about $Y$ not contained in $X$. We refer to $Z$ as a `perfect functional representation' if it satisfies $I(Y;Z) = H(Y|X)$. We show that the existence of perfect representation depends solely on the conditional distribution $p_{Y|X}$ and define the corresponding conditional distributions as perfectly representable. We provide a necessary and sufficient condition for $p_{Y|X}$ to be perfectly representable. Moreover, we cast the problem of checking perfect representability as a linear program, give an algorithm whose complexity is polynomial in $|\mathcal Y|$ and exponential in $|\mathcal X|$, and prove that deciding perfect representability is NP-complete for rational input matrices encoded in binary.

papers.title: Robust BUG dynamical low-rank integrators based on the Euler-Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations. Part I: a closed-moment approach
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce Euler-Maruyama-based Basis-Update & Galerkin (EM-BUG) dynamical low-rank integrators for stochastic differential equations (SDEs). These integrators extend the standard BUG integrator to the Euler-Maruyama scheme by incorporating diffusion directions into the augmented physical basis and exploiting the second moment to update the physical basis independently of the new Brownian increments. This construction avoids the inversion of the reduced second-moment matrix and allows us to derive convergence estimates that are robust with respect to small eigenvalues. We establish preservation of positive semidefiniteness, exactness with respect to Euler-Maruyama at full rank, and second-moment stability. Strong and weak convergence estimates show that the time-discretization accuracy of the underlying Euler-Maruyama scheme is preserved up to the low-rank approximation error. We also derive Monte Carlo error estimates recovering the standard sampling rate up to the time-discretization and low-rank approximation errors. Numerical experiments on linear SDEs with additive and multiplicative noise support these theoretical results and demonstrate accuracy comparable to the standard BUG integrator.

papers.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort. Our key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient candidate coverage from excessive deep expansion, and these conditions require different allocation decisions. Raptor therefore extracts complementary rejection-aware signals to characterize speculative progress, frontier coverage, and redundant expansion. These signals jointly guide bounded, momentum-smoothed updates of tree depth, branching width, and drafting budget, together with execution control that limits unnecessary drafting and progressively restores expansion when appropriate. Extensive experiments with two VLMs across seven multimodal benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of Raptor, achieving up to 2.39x average speedup over autoregressive decoding.

authors.name: Qishu Hu
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

authors.name: Haozhao Wang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the Smallest Cayley Table Fill That Uniquely Determines a Group
papers.abstract: The article investigates the minimal number of cells in a Cayley table that must be filled in order to uniquely determine a group. An exact result is obtained for groups of orders \(2\)--\(23\), and an upper bound is given for an arbitrary order.

papers.title: Decoupled Knowledge Retrieval and Compact Memory Enable Reliable Lifelong Model Editing
papers.abstract: Lifelong model editing requires continuously incorporating new facts into deployed large language models (LLMs) without expensive retraining or compromising existing capabilities. Memory-based editors offer an appealing solution by keeping the base parameters untouched, yet their practical use is hindered by linearly growing storage requirements and deteriorating retrieval performance as edits accumulate. To tackle these problems, we introduce BiSpace, a lifelong model editing framework that decouples memory retrieval from knowledge injection across two distinct representation spaces. BiSpace routes queries and identifies relevant edits in an external semantic space, while injecting the corresponding knowledge into the internal representation space of the LLM through sparse and storage-efficient updates. Extensive experiments show that BiSpace shrinks each entry's storage to only about 10.2% of the original and shows strong resilience to long edit sequences of up to 16K edits. On a more challenging benchmark, BiSpace further improves Overall Performance by more than 23% over existing methods. These results advance memory-based editing toward reliable long-term model maintenance at scale.

authors.name: Mingkun Xu
authors.institution: Guangdong Institute of Intelligence Science and Technology

papers.title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion
papers.abstract: Animals use many different gaits to locomote at different speeds across varying terrains. A longstanding question in biology and robotics is: which gait is best? This question is most often addressed from an energy-efficiency perspective on flat terrain, leaving open how the answer depends on terrain and on the criterion optimized. Here we show that gait optimality is determined jointly by terrain, performance metric, and velocity. We use deep reinforcement learning and networks of abstract oscillators, modeling spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across diverse challenging terrains, together with the locomotion style (base height, foot ground clearance, foot offsets) that each requires. A second policy then selects among them to optimize a user-specified criterion such as cost of transport, base stability, or joint smoothness. Across these performance metrics and within this repertoire, every gait is optimal under at least one terrain-metric-velocity combination. The framework adapts zero-shot to gait couplings and styles never seen during training, to terrains far beyond the training distribution, and to larger quadrupeds five times the training mass. With a single additional pitch-tracking reward term, the same gait couplings also support bipedal-mode locomotion. Our method provides a general and systematic way to produce expressive locomotion and to select the gait best suited to a given terrain and criterion. Project page: https://guillaume10.github.io/terrain-gaits.

papers.title: SenseAlign: Learning Decision-Aligned Predictive Representations for Active Urban Sensing with UAVs
papers.abstract: Active urban sensing orchestrates a mobile sensor fleet to proactively inspect a dynamic road network and gather critical information for system management. This problem simultaneously requires understanding the complex spatio-temporal evolution and making decisions with partial observations. In this work, we focus on active sensing in a large-scale urban road network with utilities grounded in dynamic traffic states, while prior work has rarely considered these factors jointly. We propose \emph{SenseAlign}, a Reinforcement Learning-based (RL) framework that learns decision-aligned predictive representations for coordinating an urban sensing drone fleet. SenseAlign first trains a privileged teacher agent that exploits future ground-truth traffic for optimal sensing choices. The student agent has an auxiliary branch that learns to predict future traffic with partial observations, in addition to the RL-trained actor and critic branches. During student learning, our framework matches the action distributions of the teacher under ground-truth and student-predicted future traffic, while keeping the teacher's observations unchanged. Such a design shapes the latent space for decision-making instead of prediction alone. At inference time, the student agent has no overhead as all this learning is done in training. We conduct comprehensive experiments with the real road network of central Barcelona containing 1570 road segments, and demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms the baselines on multiple utility formulations. The codebase will be made publicly available upon paper acceptance.

papers.title: Sliding-ferroelectric control of dipolar and quadrupolar excitons in R-stacked WSe$_2$
papers.abstract: A fundamental property of interlayer excitons is their dipolar character, enabling electrical tunability, enhanced exciton-exciton interactions and extended lifetime. It is important for studying collective phenomena and realizing novel optoelectronic devices. However, in homo- or heterostructures based on two-dimensional semiconductors, the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment are commonly locked due to spatially confined charges and nature of the band transition. Here, we use gate-dependent photoluminescence of few-layer R-WSe2 to harness sliding ferroelectricity for controlling the exciton dipole configuration of emerging layer-hybridised excitons. The sliding-ferroelectric control enables a pronounced on/off switching of the diffusive transport of hybrid dipolar excitons, while further facilitating gradual and abrupt dipole reconfigurations with emerging quadrupolar excitons. Our optical probe reveals intermediate states of vertically aligned interfacial polarisation with magnitudes that confirm cumulative polarisation in multilayers. Overall, our work presents sliding ferroelectricity as a powerful tool to tune interlayer coupling and layer hybridisation. These results represent a step toward ferroelectric-controlled exciton interconnects and novel multi-bit optical memories.

papers.title: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity
papers.abstract: Attention heads specialize into distinct functions during training, often emerging in stages together with sharp changes in model behavior. While this phenomenon has mostly been studied as a function of training time, we ask how head specialization depends on the amount of available training data. Empirically, we find that heads specialized to syntactic relations in BERT emerge as the dataset size increases. We then study this phenomenon in a solvable high-dimensional model of multi-head attention and establish that, in this model, head specialization is a genuine phase transition in sample complexity, corresponding to a non-analyticity in the test error and other observables. Depending on data structure and regularization, specialization can follow uninformative head differentiation or occur through a cascade of phase transitions that progressively recover weaker latent features, providing a statistical form of simplicity bias. Finally, we relate these statistical transitions to the stagewise emergence of specialized heads during online learning, disentangling statistical from dynamical origins of head specialization.

authors.name: O. Duranthon
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware
papers.abstract: Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories. Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.

papers.title: MKA: Evaluating Multimodal Knowledge Agents on end-to-end professional tasks
papers.abstract: We introduce the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark, which measures how well autonomous agents perform end-to-end professional knowledge work that depends on visual understanding. Each task requires an agent to extract and combine information from multiple visually dense files, such as CAD blueprints, electronics schematics, radiographs, complex charts and geospatial maps, and to produce a standalone deliverable in .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, .docx, .html or .png format. Existing benchmarks leave this capability largely untested: removing image-viewing tools leaves Gemini 4 Carbon's score on GDPval unchanged, and single-format evaluations such as GDP.pdf and GDP.xlsx do not require reasoning across files or modalities. MKA contains 200 tasks across 10 economic sectors. Deliverables are graded against expert-weighted rubrics by a sandboxed agentic autorater that agrees with human domain experts on 96.2% of criterion judgments in our expert-graded study (Cohen's $\kappa = 0.91$), scored by weighted satisfaction rate (WSR) overall and on frontier criteria unsaturated by prior-generation models (Climb-WSR). Across the frontier models we evaluate (Gemini 4 Carbon, Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Astra), Claude Fable 5.2 (56.6% Climb-WSR, 73.3% Overall WSR) and Gemini 4 Carbon (54.3% Climb-WSR, 71.9% Overall WSR) achieve the highest scores, while Carbon uses $5.7\times$ fewer tokens. Even for the strongest models, Climb-WSR remains below 57%, leaving substantial headroom for multimodal agents.

papers.title: Markov processes with jump kernels blowing up at the boundary of $C^{1, \eta}$ open sets
papers.abstract: We study the boundary behavior of nonnegative harmonic functions for a class of purely discontinuous symmetric Markov processes in $C^{1,\eta}$ open sets $D\subset\mathbb R^d$. The jump kernels are allowed to blow up at the boundary of $D$ and the processes may have a critical killing potential. We identify the exact boundary decay exponent $p$, characterized by the coefficient of the critical killing potential. We establish a boundary Harnack principle which yields the comparability of $f(x)/\delta_D(x)^p$ for nonnegative harmonic functions that vanish continuously on a portion of the boundary. The key ingredient of the proof combines estimates of the exact decay rate for the survival probability of the killed process with a modified box method and uses a regularized distance function to handle the limited boundary regularity.

papers.title: Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations
papers.abstract: We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^\rho u - \Delta u + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^\rho$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $\rho \in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $\rho \in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $\rho = 1$, and the super-diffusive case $\rho \in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(\Omega)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $\Gamma_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $\Gamma_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $\Gamma_0 \cup \Gamma_1$, provided that $\Gamma_0$ and $\Gamma_1$ overlap. When $\Gamma_0 \cup \Gamma_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(\Omega)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.

authors.name: Abdelmalek Metidji
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Higher-order magnetic hopfions in uniaxial chiral magnets
papers.abstract: Chiral magnets host hopfions, but their experimentally observed configurations are largely limited to hopfion rings, heliknotons, and their clusters. Here, we show that uniaxial anisotropy stabilizes a diverse family of knotted and linked hopfions with zero and arbitrary positive Hopf indices. We identify their stability regions in the anisotropy -- field parameter space and introduce a systematic construction based on mapping skyrmion braids into three-dimensional magnetic textures. We find that the minimum energy of stable hopfions increases approximately linearly with the Hopf index.

papers.title: Domain-Aware Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy Spacecraft Pose Estimation under Sim-to-Real Shift
papers.abstract: Autonomous rendezvous and proximity operations require not only an accurate estimate of the pose of the target spacecraft, but also a reliable indication of when this estimate can be trusted. Conformal prediction provides such an indication with a formal guarantee, by producing pose uncertainty sets that contain the true pose with a specified probability. Such a guarantee, however, assumes that calibration and test data follow the same distribution, an assumption that is violated in orbital perception, where labelled calibration images are available only from synthetic renderings while operational images are real. In this work, we show on the SPEED+ dataset that conformal pose estimation calibrated on synthetic images loses its coverage guarantee on real images, and that many of the resulting failures are silent: the predicted pose set appears valid but excludes the true pose. To address this, we calibrate on synthetic images translated to the appearance of real images. Since translation alters appearance while preserving geometry, the synthetic pose labels remain valid and no labelled real images are required. Experiments with two translation models show that this calibration restores coverage above the specified level for miscoverage levels of 0.1 and above, and reduces silent failures from up to 43.5% to at most 3.3% of the test images, bringing conformal pose estimation a step closer to trustworthy deployment in space.

papers.title: Static Analysis Guidance for Secure LLM Code Generation
papers.abstract: Static analyzers are cheap and widely deployed, which makes their reports a candidate feedback signal for secure LLM code generation. Existing approaches place the analyzer inside an iterative repair loop with intermediate steps, which is costly and makes it hard to isolate the report's effect on the model. We introduce two strategies that give the finding to the model during generation. When the analyzer raises an alert, generation is rolled back, and the finding is inserted either as a code comment (Comment) or in the user message (Steering). We compare them with two iterative approaches and a control without the analyzer, across three models and three Python benchmarks, and we measure security using each benchmark's oracle. Guidance during generation is cheap and can be effective, at 0.9 to 1.9 times the baseline's output tokens against up to 24.1 times for iterative approaches. With DeepSeek-V4.1-flash on RiskyPy, Steering raises the share of functional and secure programs from 52.5% to 64.4%, close to the best iterative approach (66.2%) while using less than a fifth of the tokens. A per-rule analysis shows that rules with a local fix benefit most, and replacing the XML parser is net-positive on two of the three models. The study also identifies when guidance should not be applied. Analyzers flag at most 5.6% of the functional but insecure programs on SecEvalPlus, leaving little guidance to act on. When a static analysis alert (warning or error) contradicts the task, models tend to follow the analyzer and break the program. The two Qwen2.5 models often fail when the fix requires restructuring the code. These results indicate that static-analysis guidance is worth applying with a capable model, on rules with a local fix, and after filtering alerts that conflict with the task specification.

papers.title: Decision Age: Information Freshness under Fusion Rules in Multi-Sensor Command and Control
papers.abstract: Command and control systems decide automatically on evidence that a fusion rule requires from several sensors. The Age of Information measures how current a datum is when it reaches the fusion node, but existing multi-source results treat additional sources as redundancy: the age at the monitor falls as sources are added. This paper addresses the opposite regime. When a rule demands corroboration the decision waits for the slowest required source, so the binding quantity is a maximum, not a minimum, of source ages. We define the decision age of an arbitrary monotone fusion rule, obtain its distribution in closed form for periodic and event-driven sources, and show that the mean decision age grows linearly with the corroboration level, from the floor of the age sawtooth to its peak. We add a dominance criterion that identifies which sensor governs decision freshness, and a measurement methodology for fielded systems. Freshness becomes a verifiable requirement, and adding sensors is shown to make automatic decisions older rather than fresher.

papers.title: Calibrate in Context: Efficient Data-Free Quantization from Small Synthetic Pools
papers.abstract: We enable accurate low-bit recovery from small synthetic pools by improving both image synthesis and student preparation. A grid with lower local response error can incur greater error in the student's block context. Functional Grid Calibration (FGC) selects activation scales and integer offsets against full-precision responses constructed from the student's current block input. With weights fixed during calibration, FGC evaluates candidates only at their consuming operators, bringing block context to calibration at nearly local-scoring cost. For DeiT and ViT, progressive inversion updates the same images through increasingly deep teacher prefixes. With 1,000 images, the complete pipeline exceeds MimiQ's reported accuracy in all 18 W4A4/W5A5 settings across nine backbones. With 256 images, DeiT-S and ViT-S reach 68.20% and 66.90% ImageNet top-1 accuracy at W4A4 in 26-27 minutes on one RTX 5090. The pipeline outperforms strengthened 1K-image MimiQ by 13.03 and 24.36 percentage points at lower preparation cost and the same recovery-update count. The same low-budget checkpoints retain their advantage on ImageNetV2.

authors.name: Yaokun Huang
authors.institution: South China National Centre of Metrology

authors.name: Zeyd Boukhers
authors.institution: Fraunhofer Institute for Applied Information Technology

papers.title: A Note on Spherical Images of Convex Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: A theorem of Wu states that the closure of the image of the Gauss map of an open convex hypersurface is geodesically convex, although the image itself may not be. We show that the general version of this theorem follows from a short proof for smooth hypersurfaces due to do Carmo and Lawson. We also show that all closed, geodesically convex subsets of spheres are attained as spherical images of convex hypersurfaces and give examples of convex surfaces whose spherical images cannot be attained as spherical images of smooth surfaces.

papers.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. However, in many large-scale annotation settings, items are annotated by different subsets of annotators. We therefore propose the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test), a statistical test that does not require that all items are annotated by the same annotators. AltRA-Test uses a bootstrap that resamples items, draws k human annotations for each item, and substitutes one of them with an LLM annotation. This produces paired all-human and mixed human-LLM panels. A replacement is supported when the inter-annotator agreement (IAA) of the mixed panel is statistically non-inferior to the IAA of the all-human panel, i.e., when the LLM preserves the signal that the human annotators share. We establish that AltRA-Test is a consistent test of asymptotic level alpha. We then evaluate it through simulations and real-world experiments in which we test 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets across text, image, audio, and video. Across these evaluations, about 100 items often suffice for the test. In simulations, where we know whether the LLM is a better or a worse annotator than the humans, AltRA-Test makes more correct replacement decisions than existing baselines. In real-world data experiments, LLMs pass the test in about half of the setups, depending mainly on the task. Since replacement is not always justified, we encourage researchers to test it for their task.

papers.title: Globally promoting legumes by production or use subsidies
papers.abstract: Despite consensus on the positive economic, environmental, and health effects of expanding legume production and consumption, the share of cropland devoted to them remains relatively small, and their share of human consumption is negligible compared with other protein sources such as meat. The presence of externalities associated with legume production and consumption gives room for policy interventions. In this context, we estimate the effects of global subsidies on legume production and consumption using CGEBox, an open-source and open-access Computable General Equilibrium modelling platform, with integrated accounting for land use, land cover, and energy, and considering agricultural and non-agricultural households. The analysis offers high agri-food detail and a special focus on Ghana and Germany, two countries with different agroecological and socioeconomic conditions facing multiple food system issues. Compared to production subsidies, we find that use subsidies are more effective at reducing consumer prices of legumes and stimulating household intake of macronutrients, without displacing consumption of other foods. In contrast, production subsidies are more effective at boosting domestic supply, but also stimulate their feed use. Furthermore, subsidies drive up crop land to the detriment of pasture land and forests. The impact of these subsidies also reveals profound regional disparities, influenced by patterns of land use and of production and consumption.

papers.title: Compact GridPix Tracking: Test Beam Performance and Detector Response Modelling
papers.abstract: We characterise a Timepix-based GridPix detector with a 21 mm drift length using 2.6 GeV electrons at ELSA. Tracks entering through the window at several angles are reconstructed as compact $\mu$TPC tracklets, providing position and local direction from one layer. Measured angular widths are approximately 5--10 mrad. An empirical response model calibrated to these data augments Geant4 ionisation information with gas-transport and readout effects, reproducing ten of twelve angular widths within approximately 20% and all spatial-residual widths within approximately 12%. Application without re-tuning to an independent 5 mm-drift measurement shows larger angular discrepancies. Our response model therefore provides input to feasibility studies of future compact tracking detectors.

papers.title: Polylogarithmic Approximation for Packing Convex Polyhedra
papers.abstract:
We study translational packing of convex polyhedra in three dimensions. Given $n$ convex polyhedra in $\mathbb{R}^3$, we seek a placement with pairwise disjoint interiors that minimizes the volume of an axis-parallel bounding box. Constant-factor approximation algorithms are known when rotations are allowed, but no approximation guarantee was previously known for arbitrary convex polyhedra with fixed orientations.
  A central difficulty is that, unlike in the plane, the total volume and the coordinate extents of the objects do not provide a useful lower bound on the optimum: even objects with small total volume and small diameter may require a container of large volume. We overcome this difficulty using a better geometric lower bound based on a surprising connection to Wang and Zahl's celebrated recent proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture.
  Using this, we obtain a polynomial-time $n^{o(1)}$-approximation algorithm. A recent strengthening of Wang and Zahl's theorem claimed by OpenAI gives a polylogarithmic approximation ratio for the same algorithm.
  Our ideas extend to bin and strip packing: for any fixed $\delta>0$, we obtain the same approximation guarantees for translational packing of convex polyhedra whose coordinate widths are at most a $1-\delta$ fraction of the corresponding container widths.

papers.title: Entry Deterrence with Public Signals: Revisiting the Chain-Store Paradox
papers.abstract: We revisit the classic chain-store paradox by introducing exogenous public signals about the incumbent's private type that arrive each period over a finite horizon. We fully characterize perfect Bayesian equilibria in terms of sequences of reputation cutoffs that increase over time: entrants enter below their cutoff, while the normal incumbent mixes below its cutoff and fights above it. The equilibrium outcome is generically unique. Information arrival dampens the incentive to build a reputation, so full deterrence need not emerge as the horizon grows arbitrarily long, even when the incumbent is very patient. We characterize exactly when there is full deterrence in the limit, along with the limiting equilibrium when there is not.

papers.title: Nonlinear Fourier series
papers.abstract: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.

papers.title: The low-degree sample complexity of clustering Gaussian mixtures with more groups than dimensions
papers.abstract:
We study the computational limits of clustering $n$ observations drawn from a mixture of $K$ isotropic Gaussian distributions in $\mathbb R^d$, when the number $K$ of groups is much larger than the dimension $d$. In this regime, distance-based and spectral procedures require a squared separation $\Delta^2$ of order $\sqrt d$. In contrast, tensor-based procedures cluster at a polylogarithmic separation but need a sample size that is a large polynomial of $dK$, and the low-degree lower bounds known for random centers only show that $n$ must exceed $dK^2$.
  Focusing on normally distributed centers, we characterize the minimal separation for clustering with low-degree polynomials in the regime $K>d$, through a low-degree lower bound and a matching upper bound, up to subpolynomial factors. In particular, for $K=d^{p/2}$ with $p> 2$ a real number, we show that a sample size of the order of $K^3 d^{(\lceil p\rceil-p)/2}$ is required to recover the clustering with subpolynomial separation, and that it suffices when $p$ is not an integer.

authors.name: Nicolas Verzelen
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.title: Weak Degeneracy with Availability for Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: Every planar graph admits exponentially many proper colorings for any assignment of lists of five allowed colors to its vertices. In this paper, we show that very little beyond degeneracy is needed to prove that this statement holds. In particular, given a planar graph G (but not the list assignment), our argument provides an algorithm consisting entirely of instructions of the following form: ``Color the vertex v using any color c from its list, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' and ``For the edge uv, choose any k colors from the list of u, then color v by any color c from its list that does not appear among these k colors, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' For every assignment of lists of size five to vertices of G, following this algorithm in all possible ways guarantees that at least $2^{|V(G)|/7}$ different proper colorings of G are produced (and at least one color choice is guaranteed to be available in each step). We also show that this result has the following consequence: for every planar graph G, there exists a set $R\subseteq V(G)$ of size at least 0.06|V(G)| such that G can be properly colored from any assignment of lists of size four to vertices in R and lists of size five to the rest of vertices of G. Moreover, these statements remain true even in stronger settings, such as for correspondence coloring.

papers.title: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
papers.abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-\beta.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $\beta$ as $\beta_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $\beta_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

papers.title: On a critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the cooperative case
papers.abstract:
We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schr\"odinger system with $K\ge3$ components and $K$-wise interaction, in the Sobolev critical regime. We consider bounded domains with Brezis--Nirenberg-type assumptions, and the associated homogeneous problem in $\mathbb R^N$.
  For every positive coupling, we prove the existence of a nonnegative ground state and identify a strictly positive threshold separating semi-trivial ground states from fully non-trivial ones. When the linear coefficients coincide, a finite-dimensional reduction gives an exact formula for the ground state energy and a characterization of all nonnegative ground states. In particular, above the threshold all ground states are synchronized; for sufficiently strong cooperation, their amplitude vector is unique and has an explicit asymptotic behavior. We also establish existence results for positive synchronized solutions beyond the ground state regime.
  For sufficiently weak cooperation, we obtain least energy positive solutions in the critical ternary case $N=K=3$, by minimizing on the component-wise Nehari set and ruling out critical concentration. The analysis includes the endpoint interaction exponent $q=1$, where the energy functional is not differentiable.

papers.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
papers.abstract: Programmable Radio Access Networks (RANs) enable runtime deployment of traffic-control functions, but selecting the appropriate configuration remains challenging as network conditions and service requirements change over time. Conventional solutions often rely on static rules or learning-based controllers with predefined state and action spaces, limiting their ability to accommodate changing intents. This paper introduces an LLM-driven xApp for traffic control in programmable RANs. The proposed architecture combines operator-defined service intents, runtime E2 interface telemetry, and the currently deployed configuration to generate traffic-management policies without blocking packet forwarding or the processing of incoming E2 measurements during LLM inference. Experiments on an OpenAirInterface 5G environment show that the proposed controller dynamically adapts the traffic-control pipeline to runtime intent changes, achieving an average intent satisfaction ratio of 0.91, compared with 0.52 for a static TC-RAN configuration. When channel conditions degrade, the controller maintains an intent satisfaction ratio of approx. 0.88, compared with approx. 0.4 for the static baseline.

papers.title: HALTT: A HAte Lexicon Through Time
papers.abstract: Automated hate speech detection degrades over time as everyday vocabulary is weaponized into covert slurs while retaining original benign meanings (polysemy retention). Existing lexical semantic change detection (LSCD) frameworks struggle with this phenomenon due to a lack of standardized, sense-delineated diachronic resources. We propose a multi-stage framework to construct and validate a diachronic lexicon of semantically shifted hate speech terms. Filtering > 20,000 candidates, our pipeline combines historical (1770-1964) and modern (2001-2024) corpus frequency grounding, masked definition-level scoring to mitigate LLM temporal bias, and a dual-persona reasoning prompt paradigm. We release HALTT, a grounded lexicon of 19 polysemous terms with literal and derogatory senses, analyze shift typologies, and establish evaluation protocols for downstream diachronic benchmarking.

authors.name: Dario Franzese
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale Tumori IRCCS "Fondazione G. Pascale"

authors.name: Farah Benamara
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Veronique Moriceau
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Mauve Observations of the Eclipsing Binary System $\beta$ Lyrae
papers.abstract: We present a broadband, synoptic observing campaign of the complex eclipsing binary system $\beta$ Lyr, obtained with the first commercial astronomical satellite, Mauve, developed and operated by Blue Skies Space Ltd. Mauve's capabilities have resulted in the first multiphase monitoring of $\beta$ Lyr, covering UV and optical photometry, as well as low-resolution spectrophotometry, including the phase-folded mapping of the intensity of a number of emission lines. The different components in its spectrum vary in very different ways, indicative of a system with a number of physical components. Our data show that while most of the components show repeatable cycle-to-cycle variability, the thus far hardly observed UV emission (2000-3000 Angstrom) varies significantly from one cycle to the other, pointing to the need for simultaneous observations to understand and model the system. These observations reveal that the ultraviolet-emitting structures in this benchmark interacting binary evolve on timescales of individual orbits, challenging the assumption of a stationary accretion geometry commonly adopted in models of interacting binary stars. The quality of the data set and the fresh view that they bring to a well studied, but still poorly understood object demonstrate the scientific value of small telescopes with focused scientific capabilities, as well as the value of a new generation of commercial astronomical instrumentation.

authors.name: Jonathan Tennyson
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Control of Complex Social Systems via Committed Minorities and Opinion Broadcast
papers.abstract: Complex social systems are often characterized by a deep interconnection between individuals' opinion formation and their decision-making processes. In this chapter, we show how these two dynamics can be incorporated within a unifying game-theoretic coevolutionary model for actions and opinions. We present the main theoretical results concerning the convergence of the coevolutionary model, and its recent extensions to incorporate further features of real-world social systems. Then, we focus on the problem of controlling such a coevolutionary model. In particular, we present two distinct approaches: i) introducing a committed minority in the population, and ii) broadcasting information to some target individuals. For both of these methods, we discuss their implementation and provide theoretical guarantees on their performance. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control methods on different case studies, illustrating their implementation on simple academic examples, as well as exploring their performance in realistic scenarios using network structures inferred from real-world data. In summary, this chapter provides an overview of the mathematical approaches developed to model a population of individuals with coevolving actions and opinions, providing effective tools to study and, ultimately, control this complex socio-technical system.

papers.title: TWIN-2: Timing Solar Radio Bursts between 180-350 MHz Against GOES and Aditya-L1 X-ray Detections
papers.abstract: We have conducted continuous solar observations for approximately two and half years using the Two-Element Interferometer (TWIN) at Gauribidanur Radio Observatory (RRI). During which several solar events have been detected. Our observational period coincides with the maximum events phase of the Solar Cycle 25, providing us opportunity to analyse the evolution of the solar activity. Our analysis of two and half years data show a clear increase in the occurrences of solar events, which is consistent with the expected rise in the solar activity towards the peak phase of the Solar Cycle 25. We further investigate the detected solar radio events using X-ray observations from the space based Aditya-L1 and the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES) satellites. For the automated detection of SRBs, a machine learning suite has been trained. This also serves as an instrument for space weather monitoring. On the 7th of November 2025, a solar storm was detected by our pipeline in realtime. A brief overview of the data-processing pipeline, along with the RFI mitigation techniques employed to identify and characterize the solar events, is also presented. Observation data of two and a half years of TWIN is available for public access. The data has been used in student training programmes on solar radio data analysis, with students carrying out the analysis and contributing to the initial analysis of the detected events.

papers.title: Beyond geometric lattices: pseudo-atoms and redundant join representations in the face lattice of the permutohedron
papers.abstract: We study the lattice obtained from the poset of ordered set partitions (the Fubini poset), ordered by merging adjacent blocks, by adjoining a bottom element of rank -1. It is the face lattice of the permutohedron. We look at it from the point of view of geometric lattices: it is graded, atomic and coatomic in the strong sense that every element is a meet of coatoms, but it is not semimodular. Its atoms are the $n!$ permutations, and its elements of rank one, which we call pseudo-atoms, are the edges of the permutohedron. Describing ordered set partitions by chains of subsets, the cuts, we show that the rank is modular whenever the meet is above $\bot$, while the join of two distant atoms can have large rank, so that the rank of the join is a metric on permutations. An element has a unique representation as a join of atoms only up to rank one; above it, irredundant representations have sizes ranging from two to the rank, and the redundancy of an element is its number of atoms minus two. The M\"obius function is that of an Eulerian lattice, the Whitney numbers are the face numbers of the permutohedron, and the characteristic polynomial has the alternating coefficients of the geometric case, but only $\bot$ and $\top$ are left-modular, so the lattice is not supersolvable. We show that it is CL-shellable, we exhibit EL-labelings for $n\le5$, and we compare the independent sets of Raz arXiv:2307.05005 (v3, Jan. 2026) with irredundant families and with the matroid of the vertices of the permutohedron. Replacing ordered set partitions by partial flags of subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ gives a $q$-analogue, whose M\"obius function is $(-1)^{\mathrm{rk}+1}q^{\kappa}$, with $\kappa$ the number of pairs of elements in a common block at $q=1$, and whose characteristic polynomial and Betti numbers are polynomials in $q$.

papers.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

papers.title: The OGLE Collection of Variable Stars. Over 1.3 Million Human-Verified Eclipsing and Ellipsoidal Binaries in the Milky Way
papers.abstract: We present a new release of the OGLE collection of eclipsing and ellipsoidal binary systems in the Galactic bulge and disk. The catalog contains 1 330 024 objects, including 1 280 765 eclipsing binaries and 49 259 ellipsoidal variables, nearly three times as many systems as the previous editions of the OGLE collection. The selection and classification process involved expert visual inspection of the light curves. The catalog incorporates all available OGLE-II, OGLE-III, and OGLE-IV photometry, extending the observational baseline to nearly 28 years for some objects. The orbital periods and other observational parameters of previously known systems have been updated. We present basic statistics of the sample and highlight selected rare and unusual systems.

papers.title: Where Did the Angular Momentum Go? WASP-12 b May Have Circularized on a Retrograde Orbit
papers.abstract: WASP-12 b is the only exoplanet with confirmed orbital decay. Angular momentum transferred from its decaying orbit should have realigned the star's thin convective layer, yet an earlier Rossiter--McLaughlin (RM) measurement suggested a $\sim$60$^\circ$ spin--orbit misalignment. We present two new Keck Planet Finder RM measurements. We measure a sky-projected obliquity of $\lambda=-1.3\pm8.7^\circ$; and the star's projected rotation velocity is $v\sin i_\star=1.3\pm0.1~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, an order of magnitude lower than expected for a star of its mass and age. With WASP-12's low chromospheric activity, $\log R^\prime_{\rm HK}=-5.5$, our analysis favors an aligned system in which $v\sin i_\star$ reflects slow surface rotation with $P_{\rm rot}\sim60$ days, rather than a projection effect. Our evolution models favor a late-main-sequence star rather than a subgiant, with a central convective core found in 99\% of posterior samples. This internal structure suppresses the central-focusing and nonlinear wave-breaking mechanisms for inward-propagating gravity waves. We propose that WASP-12 b was initially placed on a retrograde orbit after high-eccentricity migration, when its host rotated at $v\sin i_\star\approx14$~km~s$^{-1}$ (or $P_{\rm rot}\sim$6 days). Tidal decay transferred orbital angular momentum to the convective envelope, aligning the surface. The retrograde interior acts as an angular-momentum reservoir, while interior--envelope coupling slows the surface rotation. A semi-empirical relation gives an envelope--interior angular-momentum exchange timescale of $\sim4$~Myr, similar to the observed orbital-decay timescale of $\sim3.25$~Myr. The angular-momentum budget also permits this initially retrograde evolution. In contrast, an initially prograde planet would have spun up the surface rotation to a rate substantially higher than observed.
