papers.title: Model-Based Low-Order Wavefront Sensing and Control with a Fully Physical Digital Twin on MagAO-X
papers.abstract: Context. Residual low-order aberrations and post-AO tip-tilt jitter are major drivers of stellar leakage in small-inner-working-angle coronagraphs and limit high-contrast imaging performance. Aims. The aim of this work is to develop a fully physical and differentiable digital twin for the focal plane low-order wavefront sensor on MagAO-X. This digital twin can be used to provide accurate non-linear and fast linearised wavefront sensing and control to deal with low-order aberrations. Methods. We build a physics-based optical model of the focal plane low order wavefront sensor (FLOWFS) system and calibrate it using laboratory and on-sky measurements. The calibrated model is used for non-linear phase retrieval, deriving a model-based linear reconstructor, and generating the corresponding reference image for real-time control. Results. The calibrated digital twin accurately reproduces the sensor response and recovers the dominant low-order aberrations. In the laboratory, non-linear reconstruction achieves residual floors of about 6 to 7 nm over the pupil, compared with about 11 nm for the linear reconstructor, and the same digital-twin framework transfers across different coronagraph and wavelength configurations. On-sky, the model can be recalibrated with limited changes, achieves reconstruction performance close to the residual atmospheric floor, and provides a linear reconstructor that enables stable closed-loop low-order control at kHz speed. Conclusions. A fully physical digital twin can unify accurate low-order wavefront reconstruction, fast linearised control, and transfer across observing configurations and from lab to on-sky operation within a single interpretable framework.

authors.name: R. Landman
authors.institution: Institut de Médecine et d'Epidémiologie Africaines

papers.title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI
papers.abstract: Physical AI requires models that understand spatial relationships and dynamic environments and translate observations into actions under limited onboard compute. We present TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation. TuringPAI-VL is a 0.65B model built on HybridViT-MLQ, which combines convolutional local aggregation with Transformer-based global modeling. Multi-scale Latent Queries integrate spatial features and observation history within the same visual Transformer, providing a compact, structured interface to the language model. Training combines general vision-language data with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. TuringPAI-VL supports general multimodal understanding and improves quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B, while providing a shared initialization for the two downstream VLA models. For autonomous driving, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE metrics within 1.2\% of a full-token HybridViT baseline using the MLQ interface and achieves comparable aggregate scores in an in-house simulation evaluation. Using XPeng Native Runtime (XNRT) on a single NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, TuringPAI-Drive generates trajectories at 12\,Hz in on-vehicle operation. For robotic manipulation, TuringPAI-Embodied achieves a 96.8\% average success rate across the four LIBERO suites. These results demonstrate a shared vision-language foundation for driving and robotic manipulation under practical on-device constraints.

papers.title: A note on the learning coefficient of exceptional singularities
papers.abstract: We compute the learning coefficient of a polynomial neural network at a point of its neurovariety all of whose real parameters are good, and show that it equals $d/2$, with multiplicity one, where $d$ is the difference between the dimension of the parameter space and the dimension of the group of symmetries of the architecture. This is the value attained at a generic point of the neurovariety; consequently, exceptional singularities are invisible to the pair $(\lambda,\theta)$ whenever all real parameters in their fibre are good. By contrast, at a full parameter in the interior of the parameter domain whose differential has non-maximal rank we show that $\lambda<d/2$. The two statements together give a statistical reading of the geometric distinction between nodes and cusps.

papers.title: Modeling the gravitational wave spectrum from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe: constant-in-time and coherent-decay models
papers.abstract: We study the production of gravitational wave (GW) backgrounds from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe, following the Constant-in-Time (CiT) model, presented and validated against simulations of decaying turbulence in arXiv:2201.05630. We extend the CiT model to account for the source decay using a coherent description for the unequal-time correlator (UETC) of the source. We present a generic framework that allows us to study different types of sources. As examples, we discuss the applicability of this framework to the production of GWs from decaying MHD turbulence, sound waves, and bubble collisions in first-order phase transitions. We show that the validity of the CiT and the coherent-decay models presented in this work relies on long decorrelation times of the source. However, as the decorrelation timescale of the UETC becomes short, a resonant term grows on top of the GW spectrum predicted by the CiT model, as found, for example, in earlier analytical studies of GW production from turbulence and sound waves. This model is compatible with previous numerical results and explains why sound waves in a radiation-dominated fluid are more efficient than subrelativistic MHD turbulence in producing GWs, which is no longer the case for relativistic turbulence. The CiT model predicts a generic spectrum that scales as $k^3$ in the IR regime, develops a linear $k$ at intermediate frequencies, and decays as $k^{1-b_\Pi}$ at frequencies above the inverse correlation length scale of the source, where $b_\Pi$ is uniquely determined by the type of source and the UV slope of its spectrum. Since the $k^3$ and $k$ scalings always appear for slowly-evolving sources and they are commonly found in studies of GW production, we motivate checking the potential applicability of the CiT to other sources of GWs.

papers.title: Topology-Enabled Self-Verification of Quantum Hall Resistance Standards
papers.abstract: The scaling of multi-element quantized Hall array resistance standards necessitates rigorous validation that internal quantization has not broken down without relying on the verification of dissipationless edge state transport. One proposed solution is to use a Symmetric Precision Quantization Reliability criterion, a mathematical framework that statistically assures such validation strictly through outer terminal measurements of Cn-symmetric designs. This criterion essentially bounds the likelihood of hidden localized defects arising from quantum Hall breakdown and has potential uses in quantum computing and semiconductor testing but is presented in the context of its application toward quantum electrical standards.

papers.title: The upper copula capacity
papers.abstract: Many problems in statistics, combinatorics, econometrics, and other fields are expressible in terms of the upper probability of all copulas. We formally study this capacity, which we call the upper copula capacity, as a mathematical object. In particular, we examine the capacity of given sets and integration with respect to this capacity. For two-dimensional convex sets, the upper copula capacity equals the smaller of the two coordinate projection lengths. We also give an exact formula for the capacity of lower-tail events for positively weighted sums in any dimension and characterize when the upper Choquet integral equals the supremum of expectations over all copulas. Various problems in different fields can be formulated via the upper-copula capacity, and we discuss how known and new results connect to offer new perspectives on these problems.

authors.name: Benjamin Cote
authors.institution: Laboratoire d’Annecy de Physique des Particules

papers.title: Scaling limits for products of induced symplectic Ginibre matrices
papers.abstract: We study the local eigenvalue correlations of products of independent induced symplectic Ginibre matrices in the large-dimensional limit. We establish the scaling limits of the correlation functions in the bulk, at the spectral edges, and outside the limiting spectral support, both near and away from the real axis. At regular spectral points, we show that the limiting correlations coincide with those of a single symplectic Ginibre ensemble, exhibiting Pfaffian structures near the real axis and determinantal structures away from it. At the origin, where the limiting spectral density develops a singularity, we derive an integral representation of the parameter-dependent limiting Pfaffian prekernel. Our proofs are based on a unified approach involving a differential equation for the skew prekernels and their asymptotics.

papers.title: Regularity transfer for the Ritz projection
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex polytope in arbitrary dimension $n\geq 1$, and consider the Ritz projection on quasi-uniform triangulations of $\Omega$. We prove a new pointwise estimate in terms of the sharp maximal function and use it to establish stability in weighted Lebesgue, Orlicz, and Lorentz spaces. We then introduce discrete higher-order smoothness spaces based on oscillations and a smooth companion construction, and prove discrete analogues of classical embedding and compactness results. Finally, we establish stability of the Ritz projection in these discrete spaces, together with localized estimates. These results provide a framework for transferring higher-order regularity through the Ritz projection. As part of our analysis, we also study approximation properties of the Scott-Zhang projection in Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.

papers.title: A universal modal-noise limit for multimode photonic systems
papers.abstract: Modal noise limits the photometric and spectroscopic stability of every multimode-to-single-mode photonic system, yet it is quantified device by device. For isotropic modal excitation at fixed input power, the fractional power fluctuation of any linear multimode system is shown to be fixed by one number: the participation ratio M_eff of the eigenvalues of K = T{\dag}WT. Monte Carlo for spatially filtered fibres, lossy lanterns, and integrated mode converters confirms the law, which recovers the classical speckle limits. Extending K to K({\lambda}) gives the spectral correlation of modal noise and a closed-form velocity error, maximal when the correlation width equals the line width.

papers.title: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing
papers.abstract: Many prompt-driven FLUX editing methods rely on injecting source features into target-conditioned generation, creating an inherent trade-off between source preservation and the desired edit. We address this problem by controlling where source features are injected and which transformer blocks are used. First, we introduce adaptive masks that spatially gate feature injection using differences between source- and target-conditioned block outputs at matched inversion states. Second, we use REINFORCE to select Top-K injection blocks under different preservation-editability objectives. The selected blocks are fixed at inference and require no online search. On PIE-Bench with FLUX.1-dev, spatial masking controls the alignment-preservation trade-off. On 60 validation examples, a learned nine-block set gives lower whole-image LPIPS than the 18-block RF-Edit set within the same masked pipeline, with slightly lower alignment. Among 50 random nine-block sets, it has the lowest LPIPS but not the highest reward. Separate objective sweeps reveal different block preferences for preservation and alignment.

papers.title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
papers.abstract: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. For judgments of whether German texts were written by a human or an AI, probes and word n-gram classifiers separated the classes well, but the answers did not and often ordered the texts inversely. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average ($\Delta d' = -0.34$ across model families; -0.29 across three prompts). It also changed the use of a stated base rate: Base models shifted their log-odds by less than the stated change in prior odds, most post-trained models by more. In two models with stage-wise checkpoints, the change occurred during supervised fine-tuning, model stitching implicated the early layers, and from mid-depth on internal states at positions after the text, not those of the text, transferred the change between checkpoints. Our corpora cannot be shared, so we add a case reproducible from public data, the truth of negated statements. Here, post-training acted in the opposite direction: Probes decoded truth at or near ceiling in every model, the answers of several base models did not use it, and post-training repaired them; by mid-depth the repair resided at the positions after the statement; below it, the representation of the statement contributed, strongly in one of four models. In a training study, adding 2,000 correctly labeled authorship judgments of news texts to otherwise identical fine-tuning data improved the answers on our newspaper and textbook corpora and inverted them on the chats, where they followed a news-trained probe of the base model. Post-training thus changed how a judgment is read out of what a model represents, and a small training signal can set its direction.

papers.title: SCARVA: Interpretable Agentic Reasoning in Software Supply-Chain Analysis
papers.abstract:
Complex applications may inherit security vulnerabilities from their dependencies, though a vulnerable dependency does not necessarily endanger the application. Existing tools flag dependencies associated with public vulnerabilities, and more advanced ones analyze the call graph to assess whether the vulnerable code is reachable. However, these approaches are limited to specific programming languages and ecosystems. LLM agents are promising candidates for this task, yet they hallucinate, take shortcuts, and reward hack. As these behaviors are opaque, the agents' conclusions may not be trusted.
  We present SCARVA a framework designed to produce interpretable reports. SCARVA combines advanced agent reasoning with an evidence-collection methodology that assesses the agent's analysis and improves its trustworthiness. Specifically, the ANALYST performs a software security assessment while SCARVA records every tool call, file access, and web request. Then, one or more independent JUDGE agents inspect the ANALYST's result and produce an evidence-backed report. We evaluate SCARVA on 54 manually curated cases, balanced across exploitable, non-exploitable, and vulnerability-free projects, using both open-weight and frontier models. The best ANALYST model, Qwen 3.8, reaches 82% balanced accuracy and surpasses the evaluated proprietary models. Human annotation validates the JUDGE findings: Claude Opus 5.5 performs best, agreeing with annotators in 94% of claim checks. Finally, we discuss the most common failure modes of agents on supply-chain vulnerability assessment.

papers.title: Euler up-down numbers and quiver representations
papers.abstract: We show that Euler up-down numbers enumerate isoclasses of representations arising from quiver Grassmannians which provide an explicit realization of PBW degenerate flag varieties. Using this geometric realization, we derive several formulas connecting Euler up-down numbers, median Genocchi numbers, and Motzkin numbers. We also define a new $q$-analogue of Euler up-down numbers and derive several formulas for these polynomials. We describe a natural poset structure on the set of isoclasses of subrepresentations and describe it in terms of the classical degeneration order. Finally, we prove that the finer strata defined by fixing isotypes of sub- and quotient representations are the orbits under the automorphism group of the ambient quiver representation.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method
papers.abstract: Pulsars are difficult to discover via $\gamma$-ray pulsations because typically only one photon is observed per ${\sim}10^8$ rotations. We report the first $\gamma$-ray pulsar discovered with an extension of a recently proposed algorithm, which uses efficient tools for identifying short vectors in high-dimensional lattices instead of exhaustively searching for periodic signals. PSR J1622$-$7204, an isolated pulsar spinning at 261 Hz, was found in 15 years of Fermi-LAT data using about ten CPU hours. In contrast, the previous state-of-the-art (a semicoherent search) failed after ${\sim}600$ CPU years. This new approach may enable the discovery of many new $\gamma$-ray pulsars, including in binary systems, a previously intractable problem without detailed prior knowledge of the orbital parameters.

authors.name: Daniel Pook-Kolb
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

authors.name: Colin J. Clark
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

authors.name: Bruce Allen
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics

papers.title: Dephasing-free plasma acceleration with millijoule picosecond lasers
papers.abstract: Laser-plasma accelerators reach gradients a thousand times above radio-frequency cavities, but need joule-class femtosecond lasers firing about once per second, and electrons outrun the wave. A comb of laser lines spaced by the plasma frequency, each in its own mode of a matched channel, drives a wake moving at the speed of light. In particle-in-cell simulations a 175\,mJ, 0.5\,ps drive holds 21\,GV/m over 10\,mm with a 0.15\,rad phase drift; a test electron gains 208\,MeV, 2.6 times more than in one mode. Because the wave builds up resonantly, the required energy falls steeply with density: a 29\,mJ drive sustains 20\,GV/m, and a 10\,mJ drive, within reach of kilohertz industrial lasers, gives a test electron 170\,MeV over 30\,mm. A simulated stage transfers 5\,\% of the laser energy to the wake; the Manley--Rowe limit is about 18\,\% for five lines.

papers.title: A Three-Factor Hull-White Scenario Generator for Macro-Financial Stress Forecasting
papers.abstract: This paper builds a scenario engine that maps a yield-curve path into a distribution of macro-financial outcomes. A three-factor Hull-White model generates arbitrage-free curves whose factors are simulated under the physical measure, with an estimated and reported market price of risk. A Minnesota-prior VARX maps the simulated curves into weekly equity returns, the federal funds rate, the Weekly Economic Index, inflation and a bank Marginal Expected Shortfall proxy, with a sign-restricted policy shock adapted to weekly data. Evaluated out of sample from 2017 to 2024, the term-structure block has the lowest forecast error in 13 of 20 maturity and horizon cells, and the density forecasts are well calibrated for the continuously moving variables. At weekly frequency the curve carries no incremental information about these variables once their own lags are controlled for, so the engine's value lies in conditioning on a specified curve path, which no benchmark can do.

papers.title: Aggregating soft-photon recoil with a positive finite-step sampler
papers.abstract: We model stochastic radiation reaction by aggregating soft photons into one positive recoil, retaining the local no-emission probability and two loss moments of the crossed-field QED kernel. Unlike Gaussian diffusion, the sampler preserves one-sided energy loss. Analytical synchrotron moments expose a finite-step cooling bias, which state feedback reduces. Laser and ion-channel tests probe excessive-loss risk and directed radiation spectra, providing a practical route to stochastic particle simulations without resolving individual soft emissions.

papers.title: Operator generated topologies and the Krein property
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $\sigma(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $\sigma(X,Z)$-compact set is $\sigma(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $\sigma(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $\sigma(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $\mu(X,Z)$ and $\mu(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $\mu(E^\odot,E)$ and $\mu(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.

papers.title: General Methodology for Asymptotically Balanced Multiple Tests
papers.abstract: In statistical applications, often more than one hypothesis is of interest and, thus, multiple testing problems occur naturally. To control the family-wise error rate, popular adjustment methods, like the Bonferroni and Holm correction, have been developed. However, these methods do not use the dependence structure of the test statistics. Consequently, they are conservative in most settings. To increase the power of the tests, the joint dependence structure of the test statistics can be incorporated for the construction of critical values, for example, by using resampling schemes as bootstrap procedures to approximate the joint distribution. This has already been applied in several contexts. In this work, we develop a very flexible and general theoretical foundation, which can be used to construct asymptotically balanced multiple tests that control the family-wise error rate in the strong sense. Additionally, we prove in the general setting that consistent resampling schemes satisfy the needed conditions.

papers.title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
papers.abstract: A distinctive feature of burning aluminum particles is the condensation of the primary combustion product, alumina, forming an oxide cap that covers part of the aluminum particle and alters the local combustion characteristics. This study systematically investigates the effects of an oxide cap on the combustion characteristics and interfacial processes of aluminum particles, using boundary-layer resolved simulations, considering variations in cap size, cap position relative to the flow direction, and the particle Reynolds number, $\mathrm{Re_p}$. The oxide cap modifies both the interfacial transfer and the surrounding combustion characteristics. Front caps enhance local evaporation near the junction between the cap and the aluminum body, whereas heat absorption by rear caps contributes to lower reaction temperatures. Variations in integrated heat release generally follow those in the evaporation rate. Based on the simulation results, the Lagrangian modeling framework was first revised for spherical particles. The film state is approximated using a 0.55-rule applied to temperature, species mass fractions, and pressure, from which the remaining thermophysical properties are derived. A simplified composition scheme enables film-state viscosity and fuel diffusivity to be pre-calculated as functions of temperature. Optimized Whitaker and Schiller-Naumann correlations were developed for the mass evaporation rate and drag force coefficient, respectively, showing good agreement with the simulation results. The framework was further extended to doublet particles with oxide caps. Accounting for the exposed aluminum area provides good evaporation predictions for rear caps, while front caps require a correction to the surface-averaged evaporation mass flux, particularly at high $\mathrm{Re_p}$.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Potential Optimization for Partially Observed Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: We develop a Hamiltonian potential optimization method for partially observed stochastic optimal control with continuous-time state dynamics and discrete-time noisy observations, including controlled sensing. Rather than solving the infinite-dimensional belief-space Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, we optimize over parametrized potentials depending on the state variable and the available observation history. The associated Hamiltonian minimizers induce admissible continuous controls and, when observations are controlled, sensing decisions. An extended Hamiltonian incorporating a cost multiplier provides a common representation of the induced belief dynamics and running and observation costs. This construction yields a finite-dimensional optimization problem, with gradients computed by a forward simulation and a backward discrete adjoint sweep. The numerical implementation uses Gaussian beliefs represented by conditional means and covariances. For nonsmooth Hamiltonians arising from switching controls, we introduce smooth Hamiltonian approximations to enable gradient-based optimization. To assess the resulting policies, we develop belief-space information relaxation lower bounds. A separate optimization of the dual test functional provides a lower bound which, paired with the admissible policy cost, yields an a posteriori primal-dual diagnostic. Numerical experiments investigate scalar and multidimensional linear-quadratic-Gaussian problems, controlled sensing with and without control bounds, a nonquadratic obstacle penalty, and Hamiltonian smoothing for a discontinuous control selector.

papers.title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
papers.abstract: Calibrating a hyperelastic constitutive model for a soft material traditionally poses two problems: an expert must choose its functional form, and several homogeneous tests must determine its parameters. Neural constitutive models solve the first, but either remain black boxes or draw on a library of candidate terms fixed in advance. Full-field measurements, such as those from digital image correlation (DIC), promise to solve the second, replacing those tests by a single heterogeneous one. Two gaps remain: flexibility during training with interpretability afterwards, and a way to train such a model on one heterogeneous test. Here we close both. We embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network (CKAN) in finite element model updating (FEMU) and train it by minimizing the mismatch between the predicted and the measured kinematic fields and reaction forces. Pruning and symbolic regression then reduce the trained network to a compact closed-form strain energy that satisfies every constitutive requirement. On perforated natural-rubber membranes, the CKANs reproduce the DIC displacement fields with median errors between one and two percent, and transfer to a hole pattern withheld from training. On a perforated silicone plate, a CKAN trained on one stretch profile at a single load reproduces that profile and the measured reaction force to within a few percent. On an aortic specimen inflated under pressure, an anisotropic CKAN predicts the inflated three-dimensional shape. The discovered closed-form energies match the CKANs they replace on the training data and can be compared directly with established models.

papers.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
papers.abstract: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and shortlists cross features from a combinatorial candidate space, and all features are then ranked by several importance methods. Feature blending mixes these rankings into a single selection, using Pareto fronts across tasks for multi-task models. An LLM Researcher agent then tunes the feature selection in 10--25 asynchronous trials under resource caps, and a trimming step keeps the pipeline cost within budget. Across production models, the system improves normalized entropy by 0.31% on average within each model's budget, and the trimming step cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% with no regression beyond measurement noise. The optimized models were launched, and in online A/B tests they improved a primary online metric by 0.20%.

papers.title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
papers.abstract: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM). Both the GFM and IFM predict the metric motion between consecutive frames, and a lightweight learned fusion head quantifies the reliability of each estimate and blends them in a single forward pass. Across nine datasets recorded from cars, legged and ground robots, and handheld and head- mounted devices, AnyVIO reduces the metric position error of its visual model by 36% while publishing each pose esti- mate 70 ms after an image is received. We further deploy AnyVIO onboard two real vehicles at up to 140 km/h, where it remains accurate in poor lighting and heavy dust.

papers.title: Invariance and Expressiveness: Modal Variations
papers.abstract: This contribution focuses on bisimulation invariance as the hallmark of modal model theory and of modal modelling. It exemplifies traditional as well as more recent ramifications \&\ extensions of classical results -- involving variant modes of bisimulation equivalence and matching modalities also beyond plain Kripke structures, and emphasising especially the technical challenges in finite model theory and other non-elementary settings. Main results to be discussed revolve about the theme of expressive completeness phenomena: beside expressive completeness under bisimulation invariance in relation to first-order background logics, in the style of van Benthem--Rosen characterisations, this also concerns maximality results under criteria form abstract model theory, in the style of Lindstroem theorems.

papers.title: Equity and Aggregate Ambiguity
papers.abstract: Equitable resource allocations in the context of symmetric risk exposures are intuitively desirable and sometimes even expected in public planning. However, public planners generally are also concerned with mitigating risk and, more generally, uncertainty and ambiguity. We study a fundamental conflict between equity and ambiguity avoidance in public risk allocation problems. Our main results are framed and established in the setting of general symmetric aggregate losses equipped with dependence uncertainty among individual losses. Specializing to the classical model of Keeney (1980), we prove that an increase in equity is equivalent to an increase in aggregate ambiguity. We then provide a quantitative characterization of equity and ambiguity avoidance through the $\alpha$-maxmin preference framework, establishing conditions on ambiguity and risk attitudes under which each criterion holds. Specifically, equity corresponds to ambiguity or risk proneness, while ambiguity avoidance corresponds to ambiguity or risk aversion. The analysis extends to general classes of symmetric aggregation functions, where we show that ambiguity attitude is the primary determinant of preference, though aggregation structure and risk attitude also play important roles. Numerical illustrations validate our theoretical findings and explore the equity-ambiguity tradeoff.

authors.name: Tiantian Mao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: The Bolker condition and overdetermined FBI transforms
papers.abstract: We study real analytic canonical relations satisfying the Bolker condition and show that, in the FBI representation, they can be described by phases of overdetermined FBI transforms. As an application, we give a simplified proof of an analytic regularity result for generalized Radon transforms due to Mazzucchelli-Salo-Tzou.

papers.title: ResVision: Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection for Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract: Agentic visual reasoning improves vision-language models by selectively enlarging evidence without adding new scene content, but the benefit depends on whether fine structure remains accessible and whether local observations stay grounded in the full scene. We identify three recurring bottlenecks: high-frequency detail can be attenuated during visual-token formation; spatially distributed evidence can remain encoded yet difficult for the language model to retrieve; and isolated crops can weaken whole-detail correspondence through scale and positional mismatch. ResVision addresses these limitations with two complementary components. Spectrum-Matched Resizing (SMR) estimates image complexity and selects an adaptive global sampling scale, avoiding unnecessary enlargement on simple inputs while allocating more visual tokens to detail-rich images. Context-Preserving Inspection (CPI) returns each inspected crop together with the complete working view, preserving local detail and global context across tool turns. We evaluate Direct and Agentic variants on four frontier VLMs and 29 benchmarks spanning six visual-reasoning families. Complete ResVision (Agentic Base plus SMR plus CPI) is best for every model, improving by 3.36 to 4.94 points over Direct Base and 1.87 to 2.94 points over Agentic Base. These results show that adaptive visual sampling and context-preserving inspection address distinct, complementary constraints in multimodal reasoning.

authors.name: Yahui Liu
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: What If Chain-of-Thought Is Not Enough?
papers.abstract: Reasoning capabilities in large language models have evolved from prompting-based methods to internalized model behaviors. In this paper, we investigate whether the internal thinking model of an LLM can be deliberately changed and whether such a change is beneficial. Instead of relying on Chain-of-Thought, we train models to follow Question--Option--Criteria (QOC), a structured decision process that decomposes a task into explicit questions, competing options, and evaluation criteria. We present a three-generation development pipeline that ranges from a basic QOC decision core to richer answer synthesis and statistically enriched QOC reasoning. We then evaluate the resulting models with respect to both internal consistency and output quality. Across the reported experiments, QOC-based fine-tuning improves answer quality relative to non-fine-tuned base models and yields particularly strong gains once models are large enough to execute the underlying QOC computations reliably. The results suggest that the internal thinking model of an LLM is trainable and that structured alternatives to Chain-of-Thought can provide a promising path toward more reliable, interpretable, and task-adapted decision support.

authors.name: Marc Jansen
authors.institution: Ruhr West University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: Client Exits - A Way to Increase LLM Transparency on the Client Side
papers.abstract: Textual recommendations generated by large language models (LLMs) can be difficult to inspect. This paper introduces \emph{Client Exits}, a lightweight mechanism for enriching LLM responses while separating semantic intent from client-specific presentation. The model inserts predefined, machine-interpretable markers into its output, and the receiving client decides whether and how to realize the corresponding enrichments. This allows supplementary information to be presented as graphics, text, speech, or other modalities without prescribing a concrete interface. We implement a prototype combining a finetuned Qwen model with a modified LibreChat client. Using the Question--Option--Criteria (QOC) approach including three XML-based client exits. We evaluate two QOC-oriented model variants trained on essentially the same examples, with client-exit annotations added for one variant. Across 100 test questions, the client-exit model includes all three markers in every response. An LLM judge, informed about the mechanism without being instructed to favor it, prefers this model's answers in 66\% of the comparisons. These results demonstrate successful marker generation on the evaluated test set and support the feasibility of client-controlled enrichment.

authors.name: Marc Jansen
authors.institution: Ruhr West University of Applied Sciences

papers.title: Top-heavy Initial Mass Functions are not enough at cosmic dawn
papers.abstract: A top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) has been proposed to explain the unexpected abundance of ultraviolet (UV)-bright galaxies at cosmic dawn. We test this possibility using the metallicity-dependent, top-heavy IMF recently proposed by Chon et al. (2024), which is motivated by simulations of metal-poor star formation. We compare this IMF with a Salpeter IMF, self-consistently including the associated changes in UV emission, supernova feedback, metal enrichment, and dust production. At fixed star formation rate, the Chon IMF enhances the intrinsic UV luminosity by a factor ${B}_{1500}\simeq4.7$-$2.8$ over halo masses $M_h=10^{8-12}\,M_\odot$. However, its larger supernova rate suppresses star formation and increases dust attenuation, reducing the net boost to ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq2.0$-$1.06$. For halos relevant to the bright end of the UV luminosity function, the enhancement is only ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq1.2$-$1.4$, or about $0.3$ mag. Calculations with the DELPHI semi-analytic model confirm that the self-consistent Chon and Salpeter UV luminosity functions differ by less than $0.5$ dex at $z\simeq11$-$17$. Thus, a top-heavy IMF alone cannot explain the bright galaxy excess. Conversely, the predicted pair-instability supernova abundance differs by factors of $2$-$6$ between the two IMFs, providing a potentially cleaner observational diagnostic of the high-mass stellar populations at these early epochs.

papers.title: Axioms of Phyllotaxis
papers.abstract: Observations of simultaneous occurrence of new objects in the early developmental stage of flower heads challenge the classical model of phyllotaxis. Prusinkiewicz (2026) applies Lindenmayer's axiomatic approach to a model of the initial expansion stage and explains the origin of the divergence angle 137.5{\deg}, a characteristic by which the classical model consistently demonstrates its validity. This paper proposes a generalised axiomatic model of initial expansion and applies it to a handful of relevant divergence angles.

papers.title: Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
papers.abstract: We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings. With the smallest open instance having as few as 512 binary decision variables, the proposed IPs offer a challenging and intriguing combinatorial problem. In addition, we extend the problem to higher-dimensional grid graphs and provide solutions for unexplored and unsolved instances.

papers.title: Subexponential Algorithms for Continuous Euclidean $k$-Means in Subpolylogarithmic Dimension
papers.abstract:
Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{Q}^d$ and an integer $k$, the continuous Euclidean $k$-means problem asks for $k$ centers in $\mathbb{R}^d$ that minimize the sum of squared distances from the input points to their nearest centers. In one dimension, the problem can be solved in polynomial time by dynamic programming. In higher dimensions, the algorithm of Inaba, Katoh, and Imai [SoCG 1994] runs in polynomial time when both $k$ and $d$ are fixed. Mahajan, Nimbhorkar, and Varadarajan [TCS 2012] showed that the problem is NP-hard even in the plane when $k$ is part of the input, answering a question of Dasgupta [2008].
  In this paper, we give a deterministic exact algorithm for continuous Euclidean $k$-means. For arbitrary $k$ and $d=(\log n)^{o(1)}$, the algorithm runs in $O^*(2^{o(n)})$ time and uses polynomial space.
  Aman, Karthik C. S., and Punna [ESA 2024] asked whether the $2^n$ time bound for Euclidean $k$-means can be improved in high dimensions. Our result gives an affirmative answer to the corresponding question in subpolylogarithmic dimension.

papers.title: ChainAgent: Automated Chainable Vulnerability Discovery in PHP Web Applications
papers.abstract:
High-impact attacks on PHP web applications often chain limited-capability vulnerabilities with other flaws or intended behaviors. Discovering these chains requires identifying flaws and the dependencies enabling capability composition. Existing vulnerability discovery techniques analyze flaws in isolation, while attack planning assumes known components. This separation makes it difficult to discover previously unknown components whose security relevance becomes apparent only through their potential roles in an exploit chain.
  We present ChainAgent, a goal-directed LLM-agent framework that jointly discovers exploit-chain components and their capability dependencies in source code. Guided by an empirical study of 386 real-world web exploit chains, ChainAgent represents vulnerabilities and functional gadgets--intended program behaviors that can be repurposed in attacks--through preconditions and capabilities over security-relevant objects. Instead of discovering vulnerabilities first and constructing attack paths afterward, ChainAgent uses an evolving exploit graph to guide source-code inspection. It searches backward from unmet preconditions for capability producers and forward from discovered capabilities for functional gadgets that consume or amplify them. Object-centered chaining knowledge from our empirical study directs searches toward promising vulnerability classes, functional operations, and object accesses.
  We evaluate ChainAgent against Codex, a general-purpose coding agent, on 15 PHP applications across three shared LLM backends. ChainAgent achieves 42.02%--44.63% recall for goal-reaching components and recovers up to 4.4 times as many correct goal-reaching dependency edges as Codex. An additional evaluation of 30 real-world PHP applications identifies 20 vulnerabilities and 13 exploit chains, nine of which achieve remote code execution (RCE).

authors.name: Yang Xiao
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: How zonal states beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes stabilize micro-turbulence in tokamak plasmas
papers.abstract: The effects of zonal states (ZS) beat-driven by Alfven eigenmodes (AEs) on micro-turbulence stability are investigated; taking toroidal Alfven eigenmode (TAE) and ion temperature gradient mode (ITG) as an example. The analysis is carried out by deriving the nonlinear gyrokinetic equation describing particle response to ITG, in the presence of TAE beat-driven ZS. It is found that, the phase space zonal structure generated by AEs could lead to a significant reduction in the local nonuniformity drive and, thereby, stabilize the local ITG instabilities. The zonal flow induced shearing, on the other hand, contributes only to a real frequency shift and, typically, negligibly small additional stabilization.

authors.name: Liu Chen
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
