authors.institution: King Mongkut's Institute of Technology Ladkrabang

papers.title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

authors.name: Zihao Wang
authors.institution: Key Laboratory of Symbolic Computation and Knowledge Engineering of Ministry of Education, Jilin University

papers.title: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions
papers.abstract: Continuous diffusion models generate discrete data through stochastic dynamics in an embedding space. We consider jump diffusions that additionally reset coordinates to embeddings of categorical values. A coordinate's own corrupted state can make prediction easy, potentially reducing the pressure to learn dependencies between coordinates. We study leave-one-out (LOO) prediction, in which each coordinate is predicted from the corrupted states of the other coordinates. We show that, under stated assumptions, jump diffusions with complete coordinate resets and state-independent clocks preserve the prescribed marginals when reset destinations use exact LOO probabilities and the drift uses the full endpoint posterior. We further show that this drift can be constructed from LOO probabilities by analytic likelihood completion without additional network evaluations. We evaluate unrestricted, LOO, and completed predictions on Text8 and LM1B text generation and ZINC250k molecular graph generation. LOO-based variants improve key generation metrics over matched unrestricted controls on all three datasets. Controlled interventions assess reliance on local inputs and context, and we analyze the effect of analytic likelihood completion.

papers.title: Complete Test Suites for Effectful Automata
papers.abstract:
Complete test suites for automata are (finite) sets of words that enable testing an implementation against a specification: when a (black-box) automaton passes the test suite, completeness guarantees that it is equivalent to the specification on all (infinitely many) words. A well-known method for constructing complete test suites for deterministic automata is the W-method, used in conformance testing and automata learning.
  Based on a recent categorical generalisation of the W-method, we propose a framework for~the construction and analysis of test suites for a certain class of effectful automata defined by commutative monads. By working in the Eilenberg-Moore category of the associated monad at hand, we obtain a generic notion of effectful W-method, together with a completeness theorem. We show how to apply the framework and derive complete test suites for non-deterministic and weighted automata.

authors.name: Balint Kocsis
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

papers.title: Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are increasingly integrated into self-driving laboratories (SDLs) to plan experiments and interpret results. However, analytical reasoning alone does not make a laboratory autonomous: autonomy in an SDL is achievable only when the agent can be trusted to act on physical hardware unsupervised and knows when to defer to a human. Here, we present an architecture that integrates an agent at the Analyze-Design interface of the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle, enabling agent-driven measurement selection and data interpretation while ensuring that state-changing operations are authorized, validated, and auditable. We demonstrate this architecture on a liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) instrument in an oxidant-screening campaign for synthesizing an organic dye. Within human-defined campaign limits, the agent submitted measurement jobs, interpreted mass spectrometry (MS) and diode-array detection (DAD) data, flagged failed experiments, and produced an oxidant ranking. This ranking matched that obtained from scripted peak integration, and organic chemists confirmed the agent's spectral interpretations and failure assignments. In a simulated environment that replays the archived LC-MS data, where the agent chose which wells to inject under varying injection limits, it measured the highest-yielding condition at about its seventh injection, against 14.5 on average for a random order, and identified it in every campaign with a limit of eight or more injections. An agent can therefore close the analysis-to-design gap while its actions stay bounded and verifiable, which is a step toward greater autonomy for SDLs.

authors.name: Yimeng Liu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Eric Isbrandt
authors.institution: Centre for Catalysis Research and Innovation

authors.name: Yang Cao
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Towards consensus on practical probabilistic evaluation metrics for clinical decision making in radiotherapy
papers.abstract:
Introduction: The main aim of this paper is to identify clinically feasible probabilistic evaluation approaches for radiotherapy and to assess whether they can support clinical decision making better than current robustness evaluation approaches. To this end, we calibrate probabilistic clinical goals and identify evaluation metrics with a team of medical physics experts and apply these to three patient cohorts.
  Methods: Sixty intensity-modulated proton therapy plans from three Dutch proton centers were included: 20 neuro-oncological, 20 head-and-neck, and 20 breast cancer cases. Probabilistic evaluation was performed using polynomial chaos expansion with 10,000 simulated fractionated treatments per case. Volumetric and dosimetric CTV goals were calibrated at a 90% probability level. Selected probabilistic evaluation metrics were applied to representative patient cases and eight radiation oncologists participated in semi-structured interviews addressing preferred metrics and probability levels.
  Results: The calibrated volumetric goals were V0.95Dpres = 99.95%, 99.80% and 99.54% at a 90% probability level for the neuro-oncological, head-and-neck, and breast cohorts, respectively. The dosimetric goals were D98%,CTV = 0.973Dpres, 0.968Dpres and 0.967Dpres at a 90% probability level. All radiation oncologists considered the probabilistic evaluation metrics suitable for clinical decision making, and most regarded them as an improvement over the currently used VWmin/max approach. Preferences for individual metrics and probability levels varied among radiation oncologists, centers and treatment sites.
  Conclusion: Probabilistic evaluation metrics are expected to be clinically usable and an improvement over current methods by the interviewed radiation oncologists. Further consensus and clinical validation are needed before widespread clinical implementation.

papers.title: DRVEXO-4B-Unified: Design and Evaluation of a Modular Speech-Vision System
papers.abstract: We present DRVEXO-4B-Unified, a modular multimodal assistant built around a 4B language backbone. A self-contained checkpoint combines text, image, and speech inputs with reference-conditioned speech output and structured interaction. A temporal residual connector adapts acoustic sequences to the language interface; explicit text boundaries support incremental speech synthesis; and three task-conditioned scoring heads rank supplied action candidates alongside generative tool calls. These interfaces connect conversation to application-defined choices while leaving action authorization to the application. The system obtains 74.22% on all 900 MMMU validation questions, exceeding the published validation scores of Gemma 3 4B IT and InternVL3.5-4B without test-time scaling. Strict prompt-level IFEval accuracy is 82.26% and MATH-500 accuracy is 89.40%, above the original Qwen3-4B non-thinking report's 81.2% and 84.8%, respectively. On NVIDIA GB10, the model achieves a speech-synthesis first-chunk latency of 390 ms. For concurrent text generation, a growth-aware admission policy completes a 128-answer batch at 594.41 output tokens/s, including filling and draining, without preemptions. We plan to release the model weights and accompanying code under Apache License 2.0, retaining applicable third-party terms.

papers.title: Sign-Controlled BIC Merging and Flatband Formation in C2-symmetric Photonic Lattices
papers.abstract: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) on flatbands promise long-lived, weakly dispersive photons, yet their interplay remains elusive. Here, we develop a four-mode non-Hermitian Hamiltonian for $C_2$-symmetric photonic-crystal slabs. We show that the sign of the interpair coupling determines whether two Friedrich-Wintgen (FW) BICs and a symmetry-protected (SP) BIC occupy the same photonic band, a necessary condition for merging. In rectangular lattices, merging eliminates the quadratic radiative-loss term in a perfect-square form and strongly suppresses the quartic contribution, giving an effective $Q \sim k^{-6}$ scaling. Deviations from rectangular geometry induce noncollinear radiation polarizations, converting FW-BICs into quasi-BICs with $Q_{\mathrm{qBIC}} \sim (90^\circ-\theta)^{-2}$ and restoring the asymptotic $Q \sim k^{-2}$ scaling. Unlike BIC band selection, quadratic band flattening is insensitive to the coupling sign and can occur without BIC merging, even in oblique lattices. Our results reveal distinct conditions governing BIC merging, higher-order radiation suppression, and band flattening.

authors.name: Zimeng Zeng
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: PriTabICL: Differentially Private Tabular In-Context Learning with Task-Aligned Cluster-Wise Synthesis
papers.abstract:
Tabular in-context learning (TabICL) enables large language models (LLMs) to predict target records using a handful of labeled demonstrations in their prompts. However, these demonstrations often contain sensitive personal information. Differential privacy (DP) offers principled protection, but noise-based methods introduce substantial noise, distorting the feature-label relationships essential for accurate prediction, especially as data dimensionality grows.
  In this work, we study DP data synthesis for generating privacy-preserving TabICL demonstrations. We identify two limitations of directly applying general-purpose DP synthesis to entire datasets: modeling a global distribution can obscure local structure and minority patterns in heterogeneous data, while measuring broad attribute dependencies under a limited privacy budget can reduce the accuracy available for relationships most relevant to prediction. More broadly, global statistical fidelity may fail to preserve heterogeneous structures needed by downstream predictive and generative models. To address these challenges, we propose PriTabICL, a general framework compatible with existing DP synthesis algorithms. It partitions records into DP clusters and synthesizes each independently, using a fixed feature-target workload to prioritize prediction-relevant statistical relationships. At inference, each query is routed to a DP cluster, and demonstrations are sampled from its synthetic dataset without additional privacy loss for the original records. Experiments on four real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods across heterogeneous datasets. In particular, one of our instantiations, PriTabICL-PrivSyn, improves over global PrivSyn in 8 out of 12 settings and outperforms existing private TabICL approaches in nearly all evaluated settings. Open-source code is available.

authors.name: Heber H. Arcolezi
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université Grenoble Alpes

authors.name: Chen Gong
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Qianqian Tong
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Greensboro

papers.title: Multiple-Camera Tracking of Rigid Objects
papers.abstract: In this paper we describe a method for tracking rigid objects using one or several cameras. The tracking process consists of aligning a 3-D model representation of an object with image contours by measuring and minimizing the image error between predicted model points and image contours. The tracker behaves like a visual servo loop where the internal and external camera parameters are updated at each new image acquisition. We study in detail the Jacobian matrix associated with this minimization process in the presence of both point-to-point and point-to-contour matches. We establish the minimal number of matches that are needed as well as the singular configurations leading to a rank-defficient Jacobian matrix. We find a mathematical link between the point-to-point and point-to-contour cases. Based on this link we show that the latter has the same kind of singularities than the former. Moreover, we study multiple camera configurations which optimize the robustness of the method in the presence of single-camera singularities, bad, noisy, or missing data. Extensive experiments done with a complex ship part and with up to three cameras validate the method. In particular we show that the tracker may well be used as a camera calibration procedure.

authors.name: Radu Horaud
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université Grenoble Alpes

papers.title: Cyber-Physical RSI for AI-RAN: A Case Study
papers.abstract: Learned models for radio access networks (RANs) are often developed using simulation, yet their predictions can shift when exposed to physical propagation conditions, protocol behavior, and equipment implementations. This paper presents a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework for AI-RAN that connects a task-oriented student model, an experiment-planning coach agent, a calibratable virtual environment, and a physical host agent. Physical measurements are organized as evidence for both model adaptation and subsequent experiment planning. We examine an implementation of the physical-feedback pathway using ping-pong handover as a case study. The system completes 12 physical executions organized into six baseline--candidate pairs, updates the student from measured outcomes, and evaluates the revised model on reserved physical configurations. In the observed short-window tests, increasing the time-to-trigger from 320 to 1280\,ms changes the ping-pong count from three to zero. The updated student achieves a grouped-validation mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.673 round trips/min, while a common three-configuration physical evaluation yields MAEs of 1.240 and 1.601 round trips/min for the pre-feedback and post-feedback models, respectively. These results characterize both the operational feedback loop and the parameter-dependent generalization behavior revealed by new physical experiments.

authors.name: Ye Ouyang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Jinan University

papers.title: Planning to Stop: Factored Certification and Terminal Repair for Noncircular Robots
papers.abstract: Tight-space navigation requires a robot to clear obstacles and stop inside its goal despite uncertainty. We present GeoDiff, a motion-program planner coupling original-goal stopped-set inclusion, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation. An exact feasible-translation characterization guides repair; request-local reuse reduces repeated geometric work. We establish conditions for compiler equivalence and reach-and-stop soundness. Across 11,440 floorplan-derived jobs, GeoDiff certifies 61/139 tasks at 5-cm tolerance within 15 s, versus 44/139 for the stop-set baseline. The strongest observed external certificate adapter certifies 13/139 tasks from 119/139 native routes, separating route availability from certification. On tasks derived from public BARN maps, GeoDiff certifies 202/270 at 5-cm tolerance for a Jackal-shaped body, versus 3/270 for the portal baseline. Development analyses distinguish emitter savings from solver coverage, and 1,420 route-tracking episodes characterize the execution interface. These results show how terminal reasoning and proof reuse increase finite-budget certification coverage while preserving the original physical task and goal.

papers.title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

authors.name: Hongwei Niu
authors.institution: China University of Petroleum, East China

papers.title: On the Informativeness of Structural Stability Bounds for GNNs: GINs versus GATs
papers.abstract: Stability bounds for graph neural networks limit how much node representations can drift when the graph changes, but they are rarely compared with the simplest alternative: a bound on the distance between any two outputs, whatever the graph. We derive structural stability bounds for Graph Isomorphism Networks (GINs) and single-head GATv1 networks under deterministic edge perturbations that need not be small, and compare each with such a perturbation-independent diameter bound. For GINs, we characterize exactly when the stability bound is tighter, through a condition linking perturbation size, depth and maximum degree; it holds with a wide margin on Cora, but fails beyond a few layers on the low-degree MUTAG graphs. For GATv1, the bound is never tighter, which calls for analyses based on attention masses.

papers.title: Attraction kinetics controls permanent shear banding in particulate dispersions
papers.abstract: We investigate the connection between kinetic attractive interactions (i.e. particle attraction that turn on and off at finite rates) and the formation of permanent shear bands in particulate systems. To that end, we develop a mean field constitutive theory based on the idea that, under shear, kinetic attraction generates an overstress only when the shear rate is comparable to the attraction kinetic rates. We verify our theory using simulations of a jammed particle system with kinetic attractive interactions. We measure the homogeneous flow curves of our system at small system sizes, and find them to be in good qualitative agreement with our theory. At larger system sizes, permanent shear banding is observed. We discuss the generality of our theoretical framework.

papers.title: Bayesian optimization on amortized search space
papers.abstract: In real-world black-box optimization problems, a mechanistic simulator is often available that approximately predicts the behavior of the system as a function of the parameters being optimized. Here, we show how an amortized inverse map of such a simulator can be used in Bayesian optimization to restrict the search space while using a Gaussian process kernel that is aware of the original problem geometry. This allows for efficiently leveraging the low intrinsic dimensionality of the optimization problem. We characterize its approximation bias and information gain, and derive an intrinsic-dimension-dependent regret rate under additional geometric and Gaussian Process assumptions. We illustrate the method with an application to drug dosing personalization in Parkinson's disease. We use, as a simulator, a pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model of a drug, a mechanistic model calibrated on population data with quantified parameter uncertainty. A dosing neural network is trained offline against the model, amortizing the map from patient PK/PD parameters to the regimen predicted to be optimal, and online Bayesian optimization then searches over this learned, low-dimensional representation rather than over raw dosages. Numerical simulations demonstrate the improved performance of our method in this application, as well as under simulator misspecification.

authors.name: Federico Pavone
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Chloe Geoffroy
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.

authors.name: Aurelien Delaitre
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

authors.name: Vadim Okun
authors.institution: National Institute of Standards and Technology

papers.title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
papers.abstract: KV cache compression is critical for large reasoning models, where most of the cost comes from long generated reasoning traces rather than the input prompt. These traces often contain redundant and low-utility tokens due to looping, self-verification, and corrections. However, such tokens may still receive high attention scores, making it difficult to remove them without harming the reasoning process. We propose RoCoKV, a KV cache compression method designed for large reasoning models. RoCoKV introduces two key components. First, uncertainty-guided adaptive pruning adjusts the compression strength based on the model's confidence, allocating more memory during uncertain phases and applying stronger pruning when the model is confident. Second, redundancy-aware token selection reduces the impact of tokens that are highly similar to recent reasoning content, encouraging the model to retain more informative and diverse tokens. Beyond the algorithm, we co-design RoCoKV with the serving stack: we develop fused three-phase CUDA decode kernels and integrate them into vLLM as a drop-in plugin that preserves its paged KV layout and CUDA graph capture, turning algorithmic savings into real end-to-end speedups. Extensive experiments across three reasoning benchmarks and two reasoning models demonstrate that RoCoKV consistently improves reasoning accuracy under constrained KV cache budgets, achieving higher accuracy compared to state-of-the-art KV cache compression methods. For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B in vLLM, RoCoKV achieves a 1.27X speedup and 38% higher throughput on AIME25, the most challenging evaluated reasoning benchmark, and a 1.43X speedup and 45% higher throughput on the long synthetic benchmark, compared with Full-KV.

authors.name: Tanish Patwa
authors.institution: Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering

papers.title: Coherent belief and opinion propagation produces more echo chambers: corrected version
papers.abstract: The occurrence of echo chambers is a well-known phenomenon in social networks. Echo chambers are groups of agents satisfying three properties: homogeneity, i.e., sharing the same opinion, segregation, i.e., listening primarily to agents of the same group, and reinforcement, i.e., increasing opinion similarity over time. Opinion dynamics models have been used to explain how echo chambers occur through agents updating their opinions. However, social network users also exchange beliefs supporting their opinions. Here, we aim at identifying the effect of propagating beliefs together with opinions on the formation of echo chambers. For that purpose, we complement an existing opinion dynamics model with classical belief merge operations. Beliefs and opinions are also maintained coherent guided by values that agents share. We introduce measures, applying to either beliefs and opinions, to identify echo chambers based on the three properties. This model is used to simulate opinion and belief propagation with varying initial conditions and agent tolerance for different opinions/beliefs. Results confirm the occurrence of echo chambers observed in previous opinion dynamics studies in a different setting and with a stricter measure. They also demonstrate the occurrence of echo chambers with belief propagation. Finally, they show that connecting opinions to beliefs and maintaining their coherence increases the number of belief echo chambers, but that they involve a reduced number of agents.

papers.title: Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain
papers.abstract: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.

papers.title: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models
papers.abstract: Differentiable programming enables online calibration of numerical models by minimizing errors accumulated along simulated trajectories. This includes estimating physical parameters and training neural sub-models in hybrid configurations. Gradients are typically computed using adjoint methods, or backpropagation through time (BPTT), whose computational and memory costs grow with the length of the training window. This limits the duration and resolution of hybrid-model training, a major bottleneck for realistic geophysical applications. Approaches like truncated BPTT reduces memory use by discarding sensitivities across truncation boundaries, introducing gradient bias and neglecting long-range dependencies. We propose a class of gradient approximation methods that preserve the adjoint recurrence over the full trajectory while approximating only the pullback operators within it. Exact pullbacks are computed by automatic differentiation at sparse anchor states only. Between anchors, sensitivities propagate either through the identity (Zero-order) or through a reused, frozen pullback (Pullback Reuse). This approximation makes the parameter pullback constant within each chunk, allowing the gradient sum to factorize so that a single evaluation per chunk replaces one per time step. We evaluate both on three systems of increasing complexity, an incomplete Lorenz-63 model, a large-eddy closure for two-dimensional quasi-geostrophic turbulence, and bias correction in a multilayer quasi-geostrophic ocean model. Peak memory falls by up to an order of magnitude and runtime up to fourfold, with Pullback Reuse staying closest to the exact gradient direction. In all three cases, approximate gradients support hybrid-model training at comparable accuracy, showing that effective online learning does not require exact gradients.

authors.name: Pierre Tandeo
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Said Ouala
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Feasible sub-replicating portfolios for basket options via the block rearrangement algorithm
papers.abstract: We construct sub-replicating portfolios of vanilla options for a basket call when the marginal distributions of the underlying assets are known and their dependence is not. To do so, we reduce the n-asset problem to n two-asset problems of the type solved by Hobson, Laurence, and Wang (2005a), and use the Block Rearrangement Algorithm1 (BRA) to approximate the minimising dependence among the assets. The cash component of the portfolio is computed exactly, so that its price is a valid lower bound, and reassembling the BRA output with the original marginals gives an upper bound computed by quadrature; together they bracket the minimum basket-option price. In log-normal examples with three and six assets the bracket has a relative width of at most 0.1%, and the corresponding sub-replicating portfolios are sparse, using only two strikes per asset, while the resulting bounds are tighter than those obtained from a general-purpose multi-marginal optimal-transport algorithm with strikes on a grid. We also give the lower bound and an optimal portfolio in closed form in three special cases: a deep in-the-money basket, a basket with one dominant asset, and jointly mixable marginals.

papers.title: Monomial singularities of maps in low codimension and their deformations
papers.abstract:
We study complex analytic map germs whose coordinate functions are monomials up to a change of coordinates. Motivated by recent normal form results of Rodrigues Hernandes and Ruas for $\mathcal{A}$-finite monomial maps in the range $p\ge 2n$, we address the remaining gap $p<2n$, solving an open problem posed in their work in the range $n<p<2n$. Our main results show that a monomial map germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ with $p < 2n$ and $(n,p) \neq (1,1)$ is $\mathcal{A}$-finite if and only if it is $\mathcal{A}$-equivalent to an $\mathcal{A}$-stable germ. For $n = p = 1$ we also obtain the family of simple singularities of type $A_k$.
  Finally, we construct new families of $\mathcal{A}$-finite (generally non-monomial) map germs starting from monomial ones.

authors.name: R. Gimenez Conejero
authors.institution: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

papers.title: Sherlock 'Chrones: The Curious Case of NGC 6791 and Asteroseismic Targets Therein Reveals Mixing Length Dependence on Evolutionary Stage
papers.abstract: As single-aged populations containing stars spanning a range of masses but otherwise with similar properties, star clusters provide valuable testbeds for stellar evolution theory. The old, metal-rich, open cluster NGC 6791 is well studied, but the availability of asteroseismic observations of individual cluster members allows for a more in-depth analysis. Driven by mounting evidence that the solar assumption for convection used in almost all 1D stellar models is not adequate, and in light of the increased precision provided by modern data and asteroseismic constraints, we built and compared custom isochrones with varying values of the convective mixing length, $\alpha_\text{MLT}$, to two clusters with well-determined ages: NGC 6791 and the well-studied, metal-poor globular cluster M92. For both clusters, we found that the best-fitting mixing length parameter decreases monotonically as a function of evolutionary phase, finding values between $0.98-1.10\alpha_{\odot}$ for NGC 6791 and $1.16-1.21\alpha_{\odot}$ for M92. In NGC 6791, this corresponds to an 18% decrease in the best fitting mixing length between the main sequence turn-off and upper end of the red giant branch. The degree of variation found within this one object is therefore comparable to variation across the literature in $\alpha_\text{MLT}$ fits for other non-solar targets, calling single-valued $\alpha_\text{MLT}$ fits to clusters into question. It is also consistent with $\log g$-$\alpha_\text{MLT}$ trends predicted by higher-fidelity, 3D convection analyses. Our results therefore illustrate the need for more flexibility in our treatment of the mixing length in isochrones to properly model clusters.

papers.title: A Simple Proof of Koray's Theorem
papers.abstract: In this note, I provide a direct and self-contained proof of Koray's (2000) theorem, by which a neutral and unanimous social choice function is universally self-selective if and only if it is dictatorial. Koray's (2000) original proof relies on results by Sen (1970) and Houthakker (1950) to construct a social welfare function for each alternative set. He then shows that these functions are Paretian and independent of irrelevant alternatives, allowing him to apply Arrow's (1950, 1951) impossibility theorem. Instead, I construct a cyclic preference profile and show that the voter who ranks the chosen alternative first is the dictator on every finite nonempty alternative set.

authors.name: Hector Hermida-Rivera
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

papers.title: Wigner-Dyson correlations in selected sectors of an integrable spin chain
papers.abstract: In quantum many-body physics spectral statistics is often used as a probe to distinguish integrable and chaotic models. We find a special case of an integrable spin chain with unusual spectral properties. With open boundary conditions the model has homogeneous exponential degeneracies; these are split for periodic boundary conditions. In the latter case, we find that a small number of sectors (selected by a global symmetry) showcase Wigner-Dyson spectral statistics, which usually signals quantum chaos. Our model is clean, translationally invariant, and it fits into the standard Yang-Baxter framework. We identify Hilbert space fragmentation as the key mechanism behind the spectral properties. The fragmentation is non-local, and its extent is different in the case of open and periodic boundary conditions. We argue that the dynamics of the model is not chaotic despite the unusual spectral correlations.

papers.title: Multiplicative Sidon basis
papers.abstract: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

authors.name: Sandor Z. Kiss
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

authors.name: Csaba Sandor
authors.institution: HUN-REN Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics

papers.title: A note on a recent result by Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar, or the counterexample which I missed
papers.abstract: Recently Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar showed, among others, that the inverse of an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup on a Hilbert space need not to be an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup. In this note we show that with the ingredients of that paper, the example can be constructed more directly. Furthermore, the author reflects on the reason why he did not construct this a decade ago.

papers.title: A non-zero gap for the planar Mumford-Shah convex lifting and the nonexistence of crack-tip calibrations
papers.abstract: We prove that the convex lifting of the Mumford-Shah functional constructed through the notion of calibration introduced in [2] is not sharp in dimension two. For Dirichlet boundary data prescribed by the crack-tip function, we construct a lifted competitor whose energy is strictly lower than that of the crack-tip subgraph. Since the crack-tip minimizes the original Mumford-Shah functional, this establishes a strict gap between the infima of the original and lifted problems. As a consequence we establish that the crack-tip admits no calibration.

papers.title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions
papers.abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) often answer questions from incomplete records. Missing information might be interpreted as unknown or false, depending on the completeness of the source. Current evaluations fail to distinguish these two aspects, as they are usually interwoven with other reasoning demands. We present ClosureBench, a benchmark that tests whether LLMs follow the stated rules for dealing with missing information. Every base scenario is tested under OWA, CWA, and LCWA, and only the treatment of missing information changes between variants. ClosureBench provides a verified base benchmark as well as agent extensions for action choice, source scope, and updates. A model is considered correct on a base scenario only if it provides correct answers in all of its closure variants. Across 960 instances, overall accuracy can mask substantial closure mistakes. Models achieve overall accuracy from 71.18% to 99.86% across replicated runs, but their core switch accuracy, measured on the scenarios whose gold label actually changes with the contract, varies between 18.23% and 99.31%. Large discrepancies emerge under LCWA. For example, some agents choose unknown despite the prompt indicating that missing information should be treated as false. Our findings demonstrate that evaluations of AI agents should not only measure whether agents can reason over existing facts but also whether they use the appropriate assumption when information is absent.

papers.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
papers.abstract: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.

authors.name: Luis Fredes
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Self-supervised Vision Backbones Survives Distribution Shift in Radar Micro-Doppler HAR
papers.abstract: Micro-Doppler radar enables contactless, privacy-preserving human activity recognition (HAR), but deployment robustness remains underexplored. We compared full fine-tuning, frozen probing, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) using subject-disjoint in-distribution cross-validation and few-shot cross-age, cross-orientation, and cross-dataset transfer. Full fine-tuning suffered negative cross-dataset transfer, while frozen features under-adapted on cross-orientation. Only PEFT avoided both failures. We paired DINOv3 with all-layer principal-singular-direction adaptation (PiSSA), to our knowledge the first application of a self-supervised image foundation backbone to radar micro-Doppler HAR. DINOv3-PiSSA ranked first among PEFT methods in every evaluated setting. Under our protocol, its Small variant matched the in-distribution accuracy of the prior Base-size PEFT state of the art using 4.5x fewer total parameters, with only 3% trainable. It surpassed a size-matched variant of that baseline in every evaluated setting, with transfer gains increasing with shift severity: 2.1, 6.6, and 8.9 percentage points, respectively. Ablations attributed improvements to both pretraining and adapter recipe, with the pretraining contributing most under compound shift. Code and protocol are available at https://github.com/KeryanChelouche/udoppler-ssl.

authors.name: Nistor Grozavu
authors.institution: Laboratoire d'Informatique en Images et Systèmes d'Information

papers.title: FrontierReplay: Split-Free Exact Prefix Caching for Hybrid Language Models
papers.abstract:
Hybrid language models combine self-attention with recurrent layers whose in-place state updates restrict prefix reuse to exact saved positions. Saving states on a coarse grid wastes reusable prefixes, whereas existing fine-grained exact caches must cut the prefill forward pass at each mid-prompt checkpoint, adding scheduler steps that outweigh the reuse gains under load.
  We observe that across multi-turn chat, agent loops, document question answering, and tree search, prefix reuse almost always ends at structural boundaries predictable in advance, such as turn ends and known branch points. We present FrontierReplay, a prefix caching system that materializes exact checkpoints at these boundaries without cutting the prefill. While the forward pass runs uncut, FrontierReplay logs a short window of recurrent-layer inputs and invokes a cross-layer, state-only replay kernel to build the target state 6-37x cheaper per token than full recomputation without host synchronization. A frontier-aware retention policy prioritizes active anchors and proven branches while lending dead checkpoint slots to the attention KV cache.
  Across diverse hybrid architectures, model scales, and workloads, FrontierReplay delivers clear gains over existing exact caches, lowering median time to first token (TTFT) by 16-89% (up to 8.9x), raising 80% service-level objective (SLO) capacity by up to 1.73x, and improving goodput by up to 4.26x (3.67x at larger scales). Compared with approximate replay methods, FrontierReplay delivers up to 1.54x higher goodput while preserving exact task accuracy, avoiding the up to 17% accuracy drop suffered by approximation on long contexts.

papers.title: Investigating Thermal Boundary Conductance in Monolayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: A Systematic Comparison of Advanced Nanoscale Thermometry Techniques
papers.abstract: Thermal boundary conductance (TBC) plays a crucial role in heat dissipation in two-dimensional (2D) devices. However, reported values for 2D material classes such as monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) can vary by more than an order of magnitude across the literature, making it difficult to determine whether these differences come from the materials themselves or from the measurement methods used. To address this issue, this article presents a systematic, cross-technique study of the interfacial heat transport in four TMD monolayers supported on a sapphire substrate, using three of the most representative methods: Raman thermometry, scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) and frequency domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). By conducting all measurements on the same sets of samples, the influence of sample-to-sample variation is minimized allowing for a direct comparison of the three approaches. The results reveal a variation in the measured values depending on both the material and the measurement technique. By directly comparing these results we can elucidate on the origin of the differences and underpin sources of uncertainty in each of the characterisation methods. Taken together, these results provide a direct experimental benchmark for studies of 2D material interfaces and offer practical guidance for the selection and interpretation of thermal metrology.

authors.name: Timm Swoboda
authors.institution: Institut Català de Nanociència i Nanotecnologia

authors.name: Severine Gomes
authors.institution: Centre d'Énergétique et de Thermique de Lyon

authors.name: Stephan Roche
authors.institution: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

authors.name: Marianna Sledzinska
authors.institution: Institut Català de Nanociència i Nanotecnologia

papers.title: From a mass invariant in a gravo-turbulent medium to the characteristic mass of the star-forming cores
papers.abstract: The origin of the observed universality, or, say, the limited variations, of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and its precursor, the prestellar core mass function (CMF), and thus of the characteristic mass of stars and cores, across a wide range of different galactic environments remains an open, fundamental problem in astrophysics. In this paper, we demonstrate that we can explain this property from gravity and turbulence only, using a mass time-invariant that remains valid for a broad class of turbulent flows throughout the star formation process. This mass invariant is entirely determined by the large-scale normalisation of the field of density fluctuations in the Galactic Interstellar Medium (ISM), induced by turbulence. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we first verify that the temporal invariance of this quantity is preserved in a self-gravitating turbulent medium. Then, introducing a self-consistent model of the statistical properties of the density field in the self-gravitating multiphase turbulent ISM, we show that the universality of the characteristic mass of star-forming cores is imposed by this invariant together with the scaling of the Larson relations. Our model successfully predicts the characteristic mass of the cores in Milky Way-like star-forming regions, as well as in more extreme environments such as high-mass star-forming regions and massive early-type galaxies. This scenario suggests that the characteristic mass of the CMF, and then probably the characteristic stellar mass, originates from a universal, fundamental property of turbulence and is imprinted both by the very early stages of the star formation process in the gravo-turbulent interstellar medium, when the dynamics of the medium are still dominated by turbulence, and by the statistical properties of small-scale self-gravitating structures.

authors.name: Etienne Jaupart
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

papers.title: Obvious group manipulations in voting
papers.abstract: We study obvious group manipulation in voting and characterize it as manipulation identifiable from a coalition's option sets alone. Our analysis focuses on two overlapping classes: tops-only rules and rules satisfying the majority criterion, including all Condorcet-consistent rules. On the universal domain with at least three alternatives, a tops-only rule is not obviously manipulable by groups (NOMG) if and only if it is dictatorial. For rules satisfying the majority criterion, NOMG is impossible when $n,m\geq3$, except with four voters and three alternatives. We quantify the coalition sizes behind these restrictions, obtaining sharp bounds for efficient tops-only rules and an exact threshold for majority-criterion rules with odd electorates. In the exceptional configuration, we characterize an interval of NOMG scoring rules containing Borda, which is also Condorcet consistent there. We further characterize NOMG with two alternatives and apply our tops-only characterization to generalized median voter schemes and voting by committees.

authors.name: R. Pablo Arribillaga
authors.institution: Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas

authors.name: Agustin G. Bonifacio
authors.institution: Groupe d'Analyse et de Théorie Economique Lyon St Etienne

papers.title: Contrast Where It Matters: Visual Evidence-Guided Decoding for Mitigating Hallucinations in LVLMs
papers.abstract: Despite strong multimodal capabilities, large vision-language models (LVLMs) often hallucinate when linguistic priors outweigh visual evidence or when predictions are grounded in irrelevant or misleading image regions. Training-free contrastive decoding mitigates hallucinations by contrasting the original prediction with an auxiliary one that exposes linguistic priors. Yet existing methods focus on altering the auxiliary input or computation and do not ensure that either branch uses query-relevant visual evidence during decoding. We propose Visual Evidence-Guided Decoding (VEGD), a training-free framework that identifies query-relevant visual evidence and guides its use throughout contrastive decoding. VEGD locates this evidence by aggregating localization heads with strong visual responses and coherent spatial structure, then selectively weakens it in the auxiliary image. During generation, VEGD directs visual-carrier heads in both branches toward the same evidence location, strengthening access to intact evidence in the main branch while anchoring the auxiliary branch to its weakened counterpart. An adaptive distribution fusion strategy then combines or contrasts their predictions according to distribution divergence. Experiments across diverse LVLMs and benchmarks demonstrate that VEGD consistently reduces hallucinations.

authors.name: Zichang Tan
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Interacting framework for the free magnetic dynamics
papers.abstract: This is the second paper of a program aimed at a rigorous many--body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, built on the asymptotic quasi--local structure that the magnetic coherent--state frame induces on the CAR algebra. Here we study the free dynamics. We show that a Bogoliubov dynamics preserves the local structure exactly if and only if it is generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian. For this class we compute the hopping coefficients in closed form, prove that the Lieb--Robinson velocity vanishes, and determine when the almost--local algebra lies in the domain of the generator. For the Landau Hamiltonian the dynamics turns out to be periodic. We then describe the ground states and the KMS states at every temperature, prove their ergodicity under magnetic translations, and recover the KMS states at positive temperature as thermodynamic limits of local Gibbs states. Finally, we relate the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model. These results confirm that the frame--induced local structure is a consistent setting for the perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics to be studied next.

papers.title: 3D Binary Evolution of a Merging Binary Black Hole Progenitor
papers.abstract: Mass transfer is a highly dynamical 3D process that spans evolutionary timescales in binary stars. It is key to the production of gravitational waves through formation of binary black holes and other double compact objects. We integrate global 3D hydrodynamics into stellar evolutionary modeling to resolve mass transfer across nuclear timescales. We employ the shellular approximation in the stellar evolution code MESA to map a 3D spatial structure by equipotential shells in the Roche geometry to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium across tidally-distorted surfaces. We employ the method of time-incremented multiscale evolution to alternate between stellar evolution and 3D hydrodynamics to span large timescales with dynamical feedback. We employ this framework to examine a likely merging binary black hole progenitor system of a low-metallicity 30Msol donor star and 9.3Msol black hole from the end of the main sequence to core Carbon depletion. We modeled two complete mass transfer phases in 3D while self-consistently accounting for stellar evolution. These comprised a thermal-timescale early Case B phase and a nuclear-timescale late Case B phase. The prescription of Kolb & Ritter (1990) closely predicted the results of 3D evolution, except at the end of the first phase of mass transfer; our 3D model remained well-contained by the outer Lagrange point, despite 1D predictions of substantial L3 overflow during this stage. We find incorporating 3D hydrodynamics during Case B mass transfer did not significantly impact expected merger times. Our model never overflowed L3 as predicted by 1D prescriptions. L2/L3 outflows formed even while underflowing those equipotentials. Our model suggests these outflows can be neglected for the evolution of similar systems, but were dense enough to potentially impact X-ray observations.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Channel Prediction in Satellite-Mounted Metasurface Reflection Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Satellite-mounted metasurfaces (MS) provide a low-power programmable paradigm for 6G satellite-terrestrial networks, effectively compensating for severe free-space path loss under stringent payload constraints. However, accurate channel prediction for such systems remains fundamentally challenging due to the coupling of dynamic orbital topology, stochastic user geometry, and hardware-imposed phase quantization. This paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) framework that embeds the physics of wireless communication, including monotonicity constraints and asymptotic decay properties, into a deep neural network for outage probability (OP)-aware channel prediction. We construct a realistic system model incorporating spherical user distribution, Spherical Poisson Point Process-based satellite constellation, and practical metasurface quantization. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves over 0.99 prediction accuracy with physically consistent outage trends under varying geometric configurations, constellation densities, and quantization resolutions.

papers.title: Connecting Coronal Loop Scaling Laws and Kink Wave Heating: An Analytical and Numerical Study
papers.abstract: Turbulent dissipation of kink waves has been proposed as one of the mechanisms responsible for the observed high coronal temperatures. We test this hypothesis by examining the effect of this heating mechanism on coronal loops. The coronal loop static and dynamic behaviour is investigated under the assumption that the heating in the loop is primarily provided by kink wave dissipation. The heating term is borrowed from the recently developed UAWSoM model. Loop modelling is done in 1D using three different methods: one analytical following the principles first set in the RTV scaling laws, and two numerical: one based on the setup used to derive the RTVS scaling laws, and UAWSoM. We provide scaling laws and estimate density, temperature, and pressure, as well as kink wave heating rate and kink wave energy density needed to counteract energy loss by thermal conduction and radiative cooling. Estimates of kink wave energy density needed to heat the loop to 1 MK correspond to maximum velocity amplitudes of around 35 km s$^{-1}$ near the loop apex. Loop radius, density contrast and filling factor are found to affect the predictions significantly. The two numerical methods agree to a high degree. The analytical method predicts that $W_\textrm{k} \propto PL^{-2/3}$, while the two numerical methods show a wider range of scaling exponents which depend on the location in the loop. UAWSoM simulations suggest that loops may exhibit dynamic behaviour for a wide range of loop conditions, which may include thermal non-equilibrium cycles and periods of emerging and dissipating slow waves. Overall, estimates of kink wave energy density and scaling laws provide observational constraints on the importance of the proposed kink wave heating mechanism, with the current preliminary results suggesting that the uniturbulent kink wave heating may be a significant source of energy and heat in coronal loops.

papers.title: Temporal Contrastive Alignment of EEG and Naturalistic Video Only Beats Linear Decoding On In-Sample Stimuli
papers.abstract: Neural tracking, the temporal alignment between a continuous stimulus and the elicited brain response, enables decoding of attention from electroencephalography (EEG), yet its application to naturalistic video remains largely unexplored and mainly relies on linear canonical correlation analysis (CCA). We investigate whether a temporal contrastive model, pairing pretrained VideoMAE features with a lightweight EEG encoder trained on a correlation-based InfoNCE objective, can strengthen EEG-video alignment. Benchmarked against CCA under three generalization regimes, the model outperforms CCA across subjects (leave-one-subject-out), matches it within the stimulus manifold (leave-video-segment-out), and falls behind CCA when extrapolating to entirely novel videos (leave-one-video-out). Because this advantage appears only for seen stimuli, we probe its basis: a sham control shows that a high accuracy does not certify genuine alignment, as a synthesized correspondence fit to the seen stimuli can reproduce it without genuine temporal alignment in the training pairs. This does not preclude practical use: on a downstream attention-decoding task with seen stimuli, the model remains better than CCA since the decoding only requires a strong statistical coupling, regardless of whether that coupling is physiologically meaningful. Using a group-averaged EEG reference, we further show that genuine, generalizable coupling is nonetheless learned, only buried in the noise of single-subject EEG. These results indicate that progress hinges on data scale, diversity, and single-subject denoising.

papers.title: High-Power Short-Wavelength Frequency Comb from Coherent Radiation of Uncompressed Electron Beams
papers.abstract: High-power frequency combs at short wavelengths would open new opportunities for precision measurements and high-resolution spectroscopy. Here, we propose a frequency comb based on coherent undulator radiation from uncompressed electron bunches. An optical frequency comb serves as the seed, establishing a common phase reference for microbunching in successive electron bunches and transferring its phase coherence to short-wavelength harmonic radiation. By exploiting interference between distinct laser-induced microbunching pathways, we reduce the sensitivity of the harmonic bunching phase to electron-beam energy fluctuations, a major challenge for maintaining interpulse coherence. Start-to-end simulations demonstrate frequency comb generation in the vacuum-ultraviolet (148 nm) and soft X-ray regimes, yielding average radiation powers of approximately 1 W and 100 mW, respectively, with approximately 6 $\mu$W and 100 nW concentrated in individual comb teeth. These results establish a promising route toward high-power, phase-coherent short-wavelength frequency combs for precision spectroscopy, including searches for the nuclear transition in trapped $^{229}$Th ions.

authors.name: Hanxiang Yang
authors.institution: First Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University

papers.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it. Data can satisfy the FAIR principles and still mislead a machine acting alone. We propose that Earth-science data become AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled), an agent-specific requirements layer that extends FAIR, within a three-part agenda: AWARE data, bounded tools, layered validation. The ingredients exist across community infrastructure. We outline a staged, measurable path to adoption, intended to reduce silent error.

papers.title: Parafermi algebra and semiprimality
papers.abstract:
The principles of  rational parafermi algebra of Mersenne order $p=2^n-1$, developed in an earlier work, are recapitulated in the introduction:  A Continued  Kronecker Square-root process (CKS)  dispenses with irrational numbers.The process creates two types of lower triangular square matrices, called of $G$-type and $J$-type, whose elements  decompose Catalan numbers in particular ways.  Trilinear relations, which have the lower-left matrix part interact with a suitably chosen block-diagonal part, are only semi-conservative in that  $G$-type and $J$-type elements are  preserved but appear in an operational context  showing  different direction of rotation. The second section begins with an examination of the immersion effect,  a tendency of LL$(G_{\mu,
u}^{(p')})$ (for $G$-like lower-left part at order $p'\hspace*{-0.8mm}:=2^{n+1}\hspace*{-0.5mm}-\hspace*{-0.5mm}1$) to adopt  pecularities of LL$(J_{\mu,
u}^{(p)})$: a semiprime  in LL$(J_{\mu,
u}^{(15)})$ leads to a semiprime  in LL$(G_{\mu,
u}^{(31)})$; diagonally repeated semiprimes  in LL$(J_{\mu,
u}^{(31)})$ prompt diagonally repeated semiprimes in LL$(G_{\mu,
u}^{(63)})$. After translating  opposing directions of rotation to differently directed paths that emerge when the ordinal number of the second factor of a semiprime with first factor 3, 7 or 11 is varied,  a rulebook is formulated which reveals that paths associated with LL$(J_{\mu,
u}^{(p)})$ are not only aimed differently; they occur  five times as often as paths associated with LL$(G_{\mu,
u}^{(p)})$. The coincidence of the frequency ratio ${\cal G}^{(p)}/{\cal J}^{(p)}$ with  the mass ratio of conventional matter over dark matter is commented upon at the close.

papers.title: SEP Analysis of Fluid Antenna GSC Reception under Correlated Nakagami-m Fading and Imperfect Channel Estimation
papers.abstract: Channel estimation (CE) errors and correlation among the fading channels are two of the most fundamental factors degrading the performance of any multi-antenna system. This paper aims to analytically capture their joint effect on fluid antenna systems (FASs) performing generalized selection combining (GSC), i.e., combining the received signals at the best $\tilde{L}$ of the $L$ available ports using maximum ratio combining (MRC). More specifically, the FAS receiver is subject to arbitrarily correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading channels following the fully correlated Jakes' model, and employs a pilot-aided maximum-likelihood rule for CE prior to data detection. A novel tight moment-matching-based Gamma approximation is proposed for the marginal distribution of the estimated channel gains, which is then used to derive the joint statistics of the estimated correlated channels for the case of non-identical integer or half-integer fading severity parameters. Considering that the transmitter employs $M$-ary phase-shift keying or quadrature amplitude modulation, the joint statistics are further exploited to obtain exact finite-integral symbol error probability (SEP) expressions for a GSC-based FAS receiver, along with closed-form counterparts for the case of identical fading parameters. In addition, asymptotic SEP expressions at high signal-to-noise ratio are derived, analytically establishing that non-ideal CE and fading correlation degrade only the FAS's coding gain, while the diversity order is preserved and governed solely by the number of combined ports and the estimated fading severity. The presented numerical SEP investigations offer concrete design insights into the trade-offs between CE quality, fading correlation, and port selection for the GSC-based FAS receiver.

papers.title: Particle physics science communication with grass-roots Instagram: a success story
papers.abstract: Communicating science to the public is an integral part of the work of a research collaboration, not an afterthought. Institutional and collaboration-level social media accounts are often run by professional communicators rather than by practising scientists, and single-scientist ``influencer'' accounts are demanding to sustain. We describe {\em CMSatDESY}, a crowd-sourced Instagram account on which the CMS group at DESY tells its own stories, each member in their own voice. In the first half of 2026, the science communication activities through this reached 140k+ unique accounts and received 250k+ views, with an engagement rate of 7\%. We discuss experiences and best practices that can be used by other groups, and describe how the account doubles as a science communication playground for outreach training for a large particle physics group.

papers.title: Recursive extrema extraction tracks temporal organization through progressive data reduction
papers.abstract: Temporal organization is commonly characterized at a prescribed observational scale. Here, a sequence is repeatedly reduced by retaining only the local maxima surviving the preceding extraction. After each step, retained maxima are re-indexed, discarding the original clock and generating a hierarchy whose successive scales are determined by the surviving observations. Mean and variance of gaps between local maxima define hierarchical maxima-gap statistics (HMGS), represented as a trajectory in a two-dimensional statistical plane. Continuous independent and identically distributed (IID) signals generate a distribution-independent reference trajectory, whereas the displacement of structured processes may collapse, persist or amplify relative to it. Crucially, collapse becomes visible only when the accessible hierarchy reaches the characteristic scale of the organization, coupling the required record length to the scale being tested. These fates occur across stochastic, chaotic and event-derived systems and cannot generally be inferred from the first level. HMGS complements analyses based on correlations, entropy, recurrence or prescribed scales by asking a distinct question: whether organization identified at one level remains detectable as the observations themselves define successively deeper levels, without fitting a generative model or prescribing an external coarse-graining scale. In synthetic neuronal populations, superposition creates non-IID trajectories, while source organization persists or is attenuated according to its temporal structure. For mouse population spike trains, median covariance-normalized separation from matched shuffled-source controls decreased from 9.1 times intrinsic null variability at the initial level to 1.2 times after three recursive reductions. HMGS thereby probes which signatures of temporal organization survive progressive data reduction.

papers.title: How to Effectively Manage the Energy in Residential Systems: Development and Comparison of Methods
papers.abstract:
The transition from fossil fuels presents significant challenges in energy management. To ensure a sustainable energy future, it is crucial to reduce energy consumption when possible and to synchronize electricity consumption and storage with the production from sources with low greenhouse gas emissions. This thesis explores a variety of energy management methods used to manage batteries, heat pumps, and other energy-related systems. The thesis presents three simulation cases alongside one real-world experiment to compare energy management done through simple rules, optimization, and machine learning methods. Furthermore, this thesis introduces TreeC, a novel machine learning-based method that learns understandable yet efficient energy management strategies, applicable to many cases.
  The three key contributions of this thesis can be summarized as follows: 1) The developed TreeC method demonstrates competitive performance compared to a variety of energy management approaches, such as model predictive control and reinforcement learning, across a diverse set of energy management problems. The understandability of TreeC's energy management strategies greatly improves the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning-based energy management. 2) The real-world experiment highlights the need to validate energy management methods on actual hardware and not solely on simulations. Both TreeC and model predictive control performed worse than in simulations, due to, respectively, insufficiently representative training data and the real-time input data not being reliable enough. 3) Energy management algorithms reduce costs in electrified Belgian dwellings, particularly in poorly insulated dwellings, electric vehicle chargers, and photovoltaic installations. However, on average, these cost savings do not yet outweigh the current costs and effort required to implement such algorithms.

papers.title: Should Belgians Install an Advanced Energy Management System in Their Electrified Dwelling ?
papers.abstract:
As dwellings electrify and more complex electricity pricing spreads in Belgium, the question arises: What are the potential benefits of installing an advanced energy management systems in an electrified Belgian dwelling ?
  To answer this question, we simulate 500 representative Belgian dwellings in which fossil systems are replaced by controllable electric technologies: space heating via air-to-air heat pumps, domestic hot water via electric boilers, and private transport via electric vehicles with home chargers. Photovoltaic systems are assigned according to current adoption rates.
  We evaluate two advanced energy management systems (EMS): model predictive control (MPC) and TreeC, a machine learning method using decision trees to model the EMS strategy. These are compared to a rule-based controller (RBC) that mimics default operation and an MPC with perfect forecasts (MPC P) as an upper bound. Performance for these EMSs is assessed for 2023 under a real contract with hourly prices and a monthly peak tariff.
  Average annual savings versus RBC are 82.5 EUR, 116.6 EUR, and 177.4 EUR for TreeC, MPC, and MPC P, respectively. All EMSs deliver similar thermal comfort (26-31 Kh). MPC saves more, while TreeC achieves higher EV charge completion (93.3% vs 88.8% for MPC, with a max charge of 95%) and a smoother aggregate load across the 500 dwellings. Savings remain modest relative to EMS purchase (280-680 EUR) and subscription (0-360 EUR/year) costs which is not favourable towards widespread adoption.
  The data and code to reproduce this study are available at https://github.com/EVERGi/should_belgians_install_advanced_ems_paper.

papers.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
papers.abstract: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity of this problem, we measure one such paid-content operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts associated with the network comprising 466,357 inferred promotional placements. We find that the network promotes products across diverse categories through a growing pool of accounts, conducting coordinated campaigns spanning months across multiple platforms while evolving its listicle content over time. Across nine generative engines from both the US and China, we find that 4.5% to 20% of retrievable cited pages are attributable to the network, depending on how strictly attribution is drawn. On eight of these engines, its clients are named in 52% of answers, against 68% for category leaders. Our work demonstrates the effectiveness of UGC GEO placement at influencing generative engine outcomes, and reveals content-level defenses as insufficient against coordinated UGC placements, where account-level and platform-level signals are necessary for proper defense.

authors.name: Yuan Tian
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: Persistent Identity in Person Tracking: Online Enrollment and Registered Recognition
papers.abstract: We extend PoseTReID with online appearance-bank matching (Gallery) and a residual-conflict guard for registered SVM recognition. All methods use supplied ground-truth (GT) person boxes. We average all-box assessment IDF1/HOTA equally across videos. On six SportsMOT clips, StrongSORT leads standalone trackers (79.44/84.72%) and exceeds both Gallery variants. Over eleven videos, Gallery AIN (83.29/85.44%) and COPE (84.66/86.38%) exceed standalone trackers with complete results. This lead depends on two retrospectively added GTA development compilations and is absent on the original nine videos. Registered SVMs lead both cohorts among complete results, with AIN at 95.72/94.82% over eleven videos. They use every GT crop from approximately 20% of frames, including future appearances. On MOT20-03, registered AIN reached 96.80% IDF1 and assigned the correct enrolled name to 90.72% of assessment GT observations. Gallery and standalone trackers receive no per-video labelled enrollment. Both identity routes restore identities across internal title cards, but Gallery trails SORT on three videos (four in HOTA) and both SVMs trail SORT on MOT16-04/MOT20-03. Under six-clip persistent-only scoring, native Gallery gains 2.39 percentage points in mean IDF1 over a matched control, with lower correct-P coverage and 5.02 times as many encoder attempts. Pose gating is mixed; the guard's metric effect is not isolated.

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

papers.title: Power Setpoint Tracking for Large-Scale EV Charging: Transformer-Constrained Charging Policy Learning with Self-Tuning Constraint Prices
papers.abstract: In power setpoint tracking (PST), an operator follows a purchased charging profile without overloading shared transformers or undercharging vehicles. PST is cast as a constrained Markov decision process that minimizes tracking error subject to overload and mean user-satisfaction constraints. Transformer-Constrained Charging Policy Learning (TC-CPL) extends soft actor-critic with proportional-integral Lagrange-multiplier updates from measured violations, a residual on the incumbent dispatcher that is warm-started from its demonstrations, and a transformer-aware encoder shared by all ports. It observes no departure times or states of charge. Simulations (five seeds, 100 paired days) compare it with the incumbent, Round-Robin. On a 600-port, 122-substation district, raw overload falls from 3.59 to 0.0017 kWh/day (overloaded seed-days from 77% to 0.4%), and absolute tracking error falls by 27%. Delivered energy rises by 16%, and satisfaction rises from 0.959 to 0.989. On a 42-kW transformer with household load, overload falls from 1.86 to 0.0014 kWh/day and satisfaction rises from 0.974 to 0.985, but absolute tracking error is 22% higher. Against hand-set fixed multipliers, self-tuning is statistically indistinguishable on the district. On the single transformer, it raises satisfaction by 0.011 at similar overload, but a short sweep found a better-serving fixed pair. The overload multipliers stay below their cap.
