The efficient periods lie in a window bounded by two kinematic conditions: every fluid parcel must see at least one reversal of the walls, and the fluid at mid-channel must be displaced by about one channel width per half period. Below the window, fluid escapes in pulses through the cells of an almost steady flow; above it, fluid is held near the arcs without being folded. The window closes below $\Lambda\approx7$ and moves to faster forcing as $\Lambda$ increases. Inertia strengthens the stretching but opens a weakly stirred wake, so that the efficiency is highest at moderate inertia ($Re\approx8$) and decreases beyond. The efficiency decreases only slowly with $Pe$, and a lamellar model based on the measured stretching extends the results to the Peclet numbers of applications. The energy cost grows as $\Lambda^2$ and does not depend on the period, which should therefore always be chosen inside the window.

authors.name: Teodor Burghelea
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Signed Powers-of-Two Greedy Vector Approximation of Zadoff-Chu Sequences
papers.abstract: This paper explores the use of sums of signed powers-of-two (SOPOT) for a representation suitable for multiplierless applications of ZC sequences, where multiplications are reduced to a prescribed number of shift-and-add operations. The SOPOT representation is achieved using a greedy algorithm that outperforms other approaches for multiplierless approximations, such as CORDIC and CSD. The proposed algorithm is based on the matching pursuits using generalized bit planes (MPGBP), and the proposed modification enables robustness to hyperparameter tuning. The resulting sequences retain, to some extent, the good autocorrelation properties of ZC, as shown in a matched-filter detection simulation. This corroborates to their use in various practical applications across mainstream cellular systems and devices requiring moderate computational cost.

authors.name: Luiz Coelho
authors.institution: Hospital das Clínicas da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais

authors.name: Paulo Diniz
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

authors.name: Didier Le Ruyet
authors.institution: Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers

papers.title: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk $-$ new insights from GALAH DR4
papers.abstract: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk has drawn extensive attention since ESA's \textit{Gaia} launch. Complex structure appears across a multi-parameter space of stellar abundances, ages, and kinematics. Using GALAH DR4, we investigate ridge and phase-spiral structures in chemical-abundance, phase ($v_i,x_i$), action--angle ($J_i,\theta_i$), and frequency--action ($\Omega_i,J_i$) spaces ($i=R,\phi,z$). Our sample includes 333,412 disk stars with reliable chemodynamical data. In the $R$--$v_\phi$ plane, ridges trace near-constant $J_\phi$ tracks and show coherent variations in $\theta_R$ and $\theta_\phi$. In $J_\phi$--$J_R$, ridges are most prominent when encoded by $z_{\rm max}$ and preferentially associate with metal-rich, low-$\alpha$ populations. In the solar neighbourhood ($R=7.2$--$9.2$\,kpc), we recover a clear phase spiral in $z$--$v_z$. Encoded in $v_\phi$, $\Omega_R$, or $\Omega_\phi$, one-armed spirals appear, whereas the $v_R$-encoded map shows a two-armed spiral. Projecting actions onto $z$--$v_z$ reveals residual spiral signatures in $J_R$ and $J_\phi$, indicating that the phase spiral encodes in-plane orbital information. Both structures depend on age: ridges remain at similar locations with varying contrast, while the phase spiral is more tightly wound in younger and more loosely wound in older populations. Several ridges correspond in $J_\phi$ to known moving groups, and excluding stars in all six moving-group regions makes the phase spiral less distinct in mean radial velocity maps. These links support interpreting ridges, phase spirals, and moving groups within a common phase-space dynamical framework. Combined with trends in orbital properties, age, and abundance, these findings suggest a common dynamical origin and distinct chemodynamical responses of a perturbed Galactic disk.

authors.name: Hai-Feng Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Joss Bland-Hawthorn
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Kun Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Shrinking Limit for the Stationary Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation on Cross-Shaped Infinite Domains
papers.abstract: We study the stationary nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on a planar, cross-shaped infinite domain and in the shrinking limit. For any fixed thickness, we establish the existence of solutions through a variational approach. To overcome the loss of compactness inherent to the unbounded geometry and bypass the regularity obstructions caused by the re-entrant corners, we constrain the minimization problem to a cone of symmetric and monotonic functions. We then establish the resolvent-preservation property, ensuring the constrained minimizers are stationary solutions. As the transverse width vanishes, we establish a transverse collapse phenomenon, that is, the two-dimensional solutions flatten across the central junction and become purely one-dimensional along the infinite branches. In this way, we prove that cross solutions converge strongly to a stationary solution on the limiting graph in a suitable sense. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this dimensional reduction recovers both vertex continuity and the Kirchhoff conditions.

authors.name: Boris Shakarov
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries
papers.abstract: A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.

authors.name: Fioralba Cakoni
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

authors.name: Michael Levitin
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: ForeSeek: Foresight-Driven Reasoning for Long-Form Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Long-form video understanding, as a fundamental yet crucial vision task, is being revolutionized by multimodal large language model (MLLM)-based video agents. However, the retrieval-driven nature inherent to these agents creates a significant bottleneck, forcing them to reactively fetch clips based on local saliency without a global temporal plan. To address this, we present ForeSeek, a foresight-driven video agent that transforms long-video reasoning from reactive retrieval into predictive exploration. Rather than blindly probing the timeline, ForeSeek forms visually grounded expectations over unseen temporal regions, verifies them through targeted observations, and continuously refines its search based on emerging evidence, where failed expectations serve as informative signals for principled backtracking. Furthermore, we develop a two-stage training framework that equips MLLMs with foresight-guided reasoning and efficient decision making. Extensive experiments on five long-video benchmarks demonstrate that ForeSeek consistently improves the efficiency--accuracy trade-off of long-video reasoning, achieving competitive or superior accuracy while observing $2.5$--$4.4\times$ fewer frames than the strongest search-based agent. Code is available at https://github.com/harry0021/ForeSeek

authors.name: Shi-Zhe Chen
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Sharp minimax rates and adaptive estimation of latent proportions in bivariate Poisson mixtures
papers.abstract: We study estimation of the mean latent composition in a bivariate Poisson mixture. Conditional on an unobserved intensity S and proportion U, two counts are independent Poisson variables with respective means SU and S(1-U). The mixing law is unrestricted on the Cartesian product [a,b] x [0,1], where a and b are finite constants satisfying 0 < a < b, and dependence between S and U is allowed. Although the mixing distribution is identifiable, the usual ratio of mean counts estimates an intensity-weighted proportion and may be biased for theta = E[U]. We construct polynomial estimators based on factorial moments and establish the exact leading exponent of the minimax squared-error risk on the logarithmic scale, without claiming an exact multiplicative minimax constant. We also derive the sharp logarithmic separation exponent for testing zero latent covariance and construct an adaptive estimator achieving parametric squared-error risk on the zero-covariance submodel while retaining the optimal full-model logarithmic minimax exponent. Simulations illustrate the bias-variance trade-off, the role of polynomial regularization, and the distinction between theoretically guaranteed and empirically calibrated adaptation.

authors.name: Essoham Ali
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Complete-SVD: A Functional Norm Approach to Low-Rank LLM Compression
papers.abstract: Post-training low-rank compression of neural networks must not only approximate the original weights but also preserve the model's input-output behavior. Recent output-aware methods measure the compression error beyond the compressed layer, at the model output, weighting logit changes by the observed next token or by the model's predicted probabilities. We propose Complete-SVD, a method for large language models that minimizes the $L_2$ distance between the logits of the original and compressed models, weighting all logit changes equally. Linearizing the network around the original weights, together with a Kronecker-factored approximation, reduces this objective to a weighted SVD with a closed-form solution. Its output-side factor is intractable to compute; we estimate it without bias from random probes, at a cost of $K$ backward passes per sequence, independent of vocabulary size and sequence length. At matched settings with uniform ranks and WikiText-2 calibration, Complete-SVD achieves the lowest C4 and PTB perplexity in every setting, and at ratio 0.7 under LEMS rank allocation. Replacing the $L_2$ distance by the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KL-SVD), with the same estimation framework, lowers calibration perplexity in most settings and raises downstream accuracy, but raises cross-corpus perplexity. Complete-SVD also improves IFEval instruction-following accuracy over the strongest prior output-aware methods throughout.

authors.name: Alper Kalle
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

authors.name: Theo Rudkiewicz
authors.institution: TAU: IA : vers des problèmes mieux posés

authors.name: Mohamed Tamaazousti
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

papers.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
papers.abstract: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained. Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, where recurrent weights are kept frozen and only a linear readout is trained, the same network but with its synapses trained by reward-modulated spike timing dependent plasticity and eligibility propagation, and finally backpropagation through time as a non biological baseline for comparison. All schemes relied on distillation of a reinforcement learning expert policy with dataset aggregation. We show that e-prop reached 100% survival rate matching backpropagation through time, whereas both the fixed reservoir and the reward-modulated STDP, though the closest to biological cultures, plateaued at a much lower performance (~43.7% and ~11% survival). We explore in further detail which trends a real culture could and could not produce until now. Finally we demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full size humanoid H1-2.

authors.name: Christian Bergaud
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Olivier Stasse
authors.institution: Laboratoire d'Analyse et d'Architecture des Systèmes

papers.title: Spectral localizers in phase space: $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants for higher-order, semimetal, and valley modes
papers.abstract: Topologically protected gapless modes emerge across multiple platforms, ranging from nodes in the band structure to boundary states in topologically non-trivial insulators, with each case governed by distinct topological classifications and invariants. Here, we generalize the spectral localizer method to establish a unified framework for topological gapless modes. The spectral localizer reduces the original Hamiltonian to a zero-dimensional operator by recursively applying quantum confining operators, which need not be diagonal in either position or momentum space, as previously assumed. In phase space, the zero-manifold of the semiclassical confining operators forms a shell enclosing the gapless mode of interest, analogous to the Teo-Kane framework for topological defects. The localizer yields a zero-dimensional invariant, such as a signature, a determinant sign, or a Pfaffian sign, capturing both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ classifications. This single construction thus encompasses diverse scenarios, including hinge modes in higher-order topological insulators, individual Dirac nodes in semimetals, and valley-selective topological boundary modes. We illustrate our approach using lattice models in symmetry classes A, AIII, AII, and D, verifying that topological transitions coincide with a vanishing gap in the spectral localizer operator.

authors.name: Christophe Mora
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: The LEMAITRE project: An Independent Probe of the $w-w_a$ Tension
papers.abstract: Recent BAO, CMB, and Type Ia supernova constraints on the dark-energy equation of state show a tension with the cosmological-constant model at the heart of $\Lambda$CDM, partly driven by low-redshift supernova measurements. We present the LEMAITRE project, a new measurement of the dark energy equation of state, based on a distinct SN~Ia dataset (2800 from ZTF, 170 from SNLS and 300 from HSC), a dedicated calibration program, and a new, independent analysis pipeline.

authors.name: Nicolas Regnault
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Calibrating the cosmic distance ladder for independent dark energy constraints
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological results presented by the DESI collaboration show a clear deviation from the $\Lambda$CDM model when considering a time-dependent dark energy equation of state. This deviation is strongly driven by the SNe Ia surveys, which all share the same low redshift sample. The ZTF survey provides the current larger SNe Ia sample at low redshift, which will significantly increase the constraining power. In this context, the LEMAITRE collaboration aims to provide new constraints on dark energy parameters using three independent SNe Ia datasets: ZTF, SNLS and HSC. This effort requires robust photometric calibration, with a particular focus on filter transmission measurement and star catalog calibration. The target for LEMAITRE is to control the calibration systematics on distance moduli below 0.4%.

papers.title: Structural economic change under the digital transformation
papers.abstract: Productivity improvements in digital industries could massively reshape the structure of production networks and drive significant labour reallocation across sectors. We examine these adjustments using a calibrated agent-based model of the global economy. We consider two scenarios with the same cumulative increase in digital-supplier productivity, which differ in how digital inputs in exposed industries are incorporated into production. The key difference is whether digital inputs enter as standard intermediate inputs (low embeddedness) or are combined directly with primary factors (high embeddedness). Across economies, both scenarios generate gains in gross output, household utility, and GDP, although value-added gains are more modest and unevenly distributed across sectors. High embeddedness generally amplifies production responses, particularly in industries highly exposed to digital inputs. Structurally, as digital industries become central in the production network and attract labour from other activities, other industries move further upstream and downstream. Persistent labour reallocation pressures also indicate potential unemployment risks where workers cannot move to expanding industries. These findings stress that, beyond productivity gains derived from advances in digital technologies, economic and social consequences depend on how digital inputs integrate into production and on workers' possibilities to adapt to structural change.

authors.name: Marco Duenas
authors.institution: Universidad de Bogotá Jorge Tadeo Lozano

authors.name: Antoine Mandel
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Hydrodynamic modeling of liquid metal field emitter deformation under combined RF and DC magnetic fields
papers.abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) breakdowns, also known as vacuum (or electrical) arcs and breakdowns, or electrical discharges, have been studied for over decades, but the mechanisms of the RF breakdown are still questionable. This phenomenon reduces the stability of the beam, damages the RF cavities, and thus limits the achievable accelerating field in the particle accelerator. In the case of Muon Collider, the RF cavities have to withstand an electric field of the order of multi tens of MV/m and a DC magnetic field of a few tens of teslas, with a minimum rate of RF breakdown. Different models have been proposed, and some important factors that could lead to the RF breakdown have been identified, such as the field emission current, irregularity of the surface , presence of hot particles on the surface and the role of the DC magnetic field. In this paper, we give insights to the mechanism of RF breakdowns using a hydrodynamic and a magnetohydrodynamic approach, focusing on understanding the forces that deform the liquid copper emitter. We found that if the local RF electric field is sufficiently high, it could provoke the emission of hot copper droplets into the cavity. Our simulations use the computational fluid dynamics module, the magnetic and electric field module, and the level set method in the COMSOL software to simulate the behavior of a copper liquid emitter with the Navier-Stokes equation under the influence of the pressure radiation, and the surface tension force.

authors.name: Guillaume Ferrand
authors.institution: Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives

papers.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar
papers.abstract: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.

authors.name: Patrick Perez
authors.institution: Laboratoire d'Economie et de Sociologie du Travail

papers.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
papers.abstract: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples. We detect tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies at $22.5\sigma$ and radial alignment of red spheroidal galaxies at $65\sigma$. By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.

authors.name: Calum Murray
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Martin Kilbinger
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Cail Daley
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Ken Ganga
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Functional Estimation under Local Differential Privacy: General Lower Bounds and Applications to Entropy and Power Sums
papers.abstract: We study the estimation of functionals of discrete distributions under local differential privacy (LDP). Even for well-studied examples like Shannon entropy and power sums, the existing bounds left open how the minimax risk scales with the alphabet size, the sample size, and the privacy parameter. To understand these dependences, we establish two general minimax lower bounds for the broader class of additive functionals. The first lower bound links the difficulty of estimating a functional to how well it can be approximated by polynomials of a given degree. The second complements the first by capturing how sensitive the functional is to small changes in the underlying distribution. To illustrate the effectiveness of these two bounds, we apply them to the estimation of Shannon entropy and power sums. In both cases, they close the existing polynomial gaps and, perhaps surprisingly, show that simple plug-in type estimators already achieve the optimal polynomial rates.

papers.title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors
papers.abstract: We study data-sharing among firms competing in the same market through the quality of their predictive models. We model firms' profit through two main components, precision and market share, where the former depends on the firm's own number of datapoints and the latter depends on the endowments of all firms. We characterize Pareto-optimal contracts as those in which at least one firm receives all of the other firms' datapoints. We then propose a parametric family of data-sharing contracts and show that, under any of them, the relative market shares of all firms remain constant, eliminating the negative effect of sharing data with competitors and equalizing all firms' gains relative to the no-sharing scenario. We further show that one contract within this family satisfies both Pareto-optimality and strategyproofness against firms attempting to under-declare the size of their initial endowment. Finally, using a real-world dataset, we empirically test the gain in profit for all firms under the contract described above, and show that data-sharing is particularly beneficial when the machine learning task is harder or when firms' initial endowments are closer to homogeneous.

authors.name: Patrick Loiseau
authors.institution: FAIRPLAY: IA coopérative : équité, vie privée, incitations

papers.title: Cooling Noisy Population Protocols -- Vanishing-Gain Averaging and Localisation under Persistent Errors
papers.abstract: We study noise-tolerant coordination in anonymous population protocols whose agents interact in uniformly random pairs, maintain real-valued labels, and have no global clock. Each agent cools its updates using a gain $\gamma_k=(k+1)^{-p}$ computed from its own local interaction counter. First, for pairwise averaging with independent communication errors drawn from a fixed centred finite-variance distribution, we prove convergence with probability 1 to a common finite random value for every $1/2<p\le1$, and derive convergence-rate exponents under the same assumptions. Second, for one-dimensional localisation with fixed non-degenerate Gaussian displacement errors, we show that the one-sided RightAlign rule rectifies centred noise and cannot stabilise; a signed update based on the relative-position discrepancy restores convergence to the true agents locations up to one finite random translation. Third, we analyse the setting in which both communication errors and displacement-measurement errors depend on the physical distance between the interacting devices. For additive independent Gaussian errors, the two sources combine into one centred effective error whose variance is the sum of the distance-dependent component variances. The signed updates protocol remains convergent for every fixed finite geometry, and the average combined variance determines the leading common-translation fluctuation. These results distinguish cooling-compatible signed corrections from one-sided updates that turn persistent noise into drift.

authors.name: Grzegorz Stachowiak
authors.institution: Polish Mother’s Memorial Hospital Research Institute

papers.title: Real Cameras are Radiometric
papers.abstract: We propose the radiometric camera, a model that lifts any central geometric camera model to a radiometric one. The lifted model keeps the projection of the geometric model and adds a finite aperture, a free-form focus surface and a generic vignetting function. We calibrate it by inverse rendering directly on the relative irradiance of the sensor, from the same images of standard calibration targets used in geometric calibration. Geometric calibration absorbs the bias of its feature detections. The proposed radiometric calibration uses no features, and our radiometric cameras have lower reprojection errors on held-out test sets. The focus surface extends defocus modeling from the thin lens to any central camera, and we use it in a first multi-view radiometric reconstruction, which recovers the in-focus reflectance of a texture from defocused images. The vignetting is estimated jointly and accurately reproduces a flat field measured through a diffuser. Because every standard camera model lifts to a radiometric one, the radiometric camera naturally and directly extends generative scene models beyond multi-view geometry to multi-view radiometric ones, where phenomena such as lighting and attenuation can be accurately estimated.

papers.title: Below Three: A 2.8027-Approximation for Moldable Precedence Scheduling
papers.abstract: We study makespan minimisation for nonpreemptive moldable jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on identical processors. Each job runs on a chosen number of processors that remains fixed throughout its execution. Allocating more processors to a job can shorten its execution, but may increase total work and delay other jobs. We assume nonincreasing processing times, nondecreasing work, and a convex duration--work relation after dominated allocations are removed. This model includes jobs with concave speedup, for which Jansen and Zhang obtained a $3.291919\ldots$-approximation. Independently and concurrently with our work, Chen obtained a $3.016208\ldots$-approximation for the full convex model and a $2.973912\ldots$-approximation for concave speedup. We give a deterministic polynomial-time $2.8027$-approximation for the full convex model and every number of processors. Our result breaks the factor-three barrier for this model and also improves the approximation guarantee for concave speedup.

papers.title: Efficient and Variation-Tolerant Tree Inference via Compact and Scalable Mapping in Analog CAMs
papers.abstract: Tree-based machine learning methods are widely adopted for their interpretability and state-of-the-art accuracy on tabular data. These methods face efficiency challenges on conventional architectures due to irregular memory access patterns during tree traversal. Prior work uses analog CAM to accelerate tree traversal, but inefficient mapping requires exponentially more analog CAM columns as tree depth increases. Accuracy is also degraded by device non-idealities such as programming variations and soft decision boundaries. To address these challenges, we propose ACTIVAR, a compact variation-tolerant tree implementation in a dense analog CAM array via software-hardware codesign. On the software side, we introduce an analog-CAM-aware compact tree model that employs hierarchical subtrees with shared features to maximize hardware utilization. This dense mapping introduces redundancy, improving both model accuracy and hardware defect tolerance. Additionally, we develop Variation-Enhanced Training, which utilizes a fuzzy overlap boundary strategy to build models resilient to analog noise. On the hardware side, we design a FeFET-based analog CAM cell with a driver to sharpen decision thresholds and implement a pipelined multi-core architecture to optimize throughput and energy consumption. Across 13 classification and regression datasets, ACTIVAR maintains near-software-level accuracy while reducing hardware overhead by up to 99% compared with prior analog-CAM-based soft-tree designs. Under realistic hardware noise conditions, ACTIVAR limits accuracy degradation to just 3.7% on the MNIST dataset, whereas baseline models suffer a catastrophic 49.6% drop. Furthermore, the ACTIVAR architecture achieves energy efficiency gains ranging from $10^4$ to $10^6$ times over commercial general-purpose processors, establishing it as a highly efficient solution for high-capacity machine learning at the edge.

authors.name: Wenqing Shi
authors.institution: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel

authors.name: Pengyu Ren
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

papers.title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models
papers.abstract:
Estimating the score function of a distribution plays a central role in statistics and machine learning, with applications in distribution estimation, sampling, and score-based generative modeling. However, learning scores from sensitive data raises privacy concerns. These concerns are particularly pronounced in score-based generative modeling, where trained models may memorize individual training examples and expose sensitive information through membership inference and data extraction attacks.
  Although non-private score estimation has been extensively studied, the statistical limits of its private counterpart remain less understood. In this work, we study score estimation under $(\alpha,\beta)$-differential privacy for $d$-dimensional sub-Gaussian distributions with locally $\gamma$-H\"older-continuous scores. We develop a sampling-based private score estimator using quadratic B-splines and the exponential mechanism, and we implement our proposal through projected Langevin Monte Carlo with runtime polynomial in the sample size $n$. The proposed estimator satisfies $(\alpha,\beta)$-differential privacy, and achieves expected density-weighted squared error $\mbox{polylog}(n) \max(n^{-2\gamma/(d+2\gamma+2)},\,(n\alpha)^{-2\gamma/(d+\gamma+1)})$. We also establish a nearly matching private minimax lower bound, thereby characterizing the privacy-accuracy trade-off for score estimation. As an application, we construct a differentially private diffusion model whose privacy guarantee is independent of the number of denoising steps. We show that, with an appropriate discretization scheme, the resulting diffusion model attains nearly minimax optimal expected total variation error among all private distribution estimators. We validate our theoretical findings through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

authors.name: Yuchen Wu
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Yi Yu
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Physique des 2 Infinis Irène Joliot-Curie

papers.title: Neckpinches in a Positively Curved Market: Ricci Flow with Surgery on the Nikkei-225
papers.abstract: We study the intrinsic geometry of the Nikkei-225 through the discrete Ollivier-Ricci curvature (ORC) of its empirical correlation graph, using the graph Ricci flow and surgery methodology of arXiv:2510.15942. The 226-node correlation graph, built from daily returns between January 2020 and June 2026, is ORC-spherical: every edge has strictly positive curvature before any flow, close to the equal-weight value $\kappa\approx0.502$. Under a fixed 20-iteration Ricci flow the curvature distribution polarises into a high-curvature bulk and a low-curvature minority, and cutting the low-curvature edges splits the graph into components of 184 and 42 nodes. The recursive ARCUS procedure (Adaptive Ricci Curvature Unsupervised Surgery) stops the flow at each node once a curvature gap ratio $G$ exceeds $G_{\min}$ and the surgery set is stable. With $G_{\min}=10$ and a minimum cluster size of 15, ARCUS performs 28 surgeries over 13 levels and ends in 29 terminal clusters of 2-14 nodes. The stopping rule fires at every node, with $G$ between 10.0 and 92.4, and the top-level split reproduces the fixed-schedule 184/42 partition exactly. Eight small subgraphs stop with $G<15$, so the deeper levels are conditional on $G_{\min}$. Many terminal clusters are single industries by inspection, among them nine banks, five insurers, five general trading companies, three steelmakers and three shipping lines. Two delisted stocks without price data enter as zero-correlation placeholders; with them excluded, every terminal cluster is more strongly correlated internally than with the rest of the index.

papers.title: An Explicit Three-Dimensional Dispersing Billiard with Finite Horizon
papers.abstract:
We construct an explicit three-dimensional periodic Lorentz gas whose
  quotient by the period lattice \(2\Z^3\) has 38 spherical scatterers
  with rational centers and four rational radii. The scatterers are
  strictly separated, so the associated dispersing billiard has no corners
  or cusps. We prove finite horizon by establishing a common blocking
  margin for every rational direction. A projected-lattice estimate for
  the face-centered cubic core leaves nine exceptional directions,
  handled by a finite line-space covering certificate. Simultaneous
  rational approximation transfers this margin to every direction and
  yields an explicit upper horizon bound. All finite calculations use exact
  arithmetic, with verification data and algorithms included. The positive
  separation and blocking margins also ensure stability under sufficiently
  small independent perturbations of the centers and radii.

papers.title: ALIoTh: Orchestrating Multi-Agent LLMs for Autonomous IoT Penetration Testing
papers.abstract: Penetration testing in Internet of Things (IoT) environments, especially those composed of various different devices, e.g., smart plugs, smart cameras, and smart doors, presents great challenges across the phases of information gathering, attack surface enumeration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. This paper introduces ALIoTh, a multi-agent, workflow-driven penetration testing framework that integrates Large Language Models agents within a Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Self-RAG) architecture to autonomously identify and exploit vulnerabilities in IoT and Industrial-IoT (IIoT) environments. By leveraging state-of-the-art language models and orchestrating specialized agents via the LangGraph framework, ALIoTh dynamically plans and executes a full-spectrum offensive pipeline. This includes network, devices, and service enumeration, vulnerability assessment, payload generation, reverse shell deployment, and privilege escalation on each device. The Self-RAG mechanism equips expert agents with contextual access to IoT security knowledge, e.g., related documentation, tool manuals, and known attack techniques, enhancing their reasoning capabilities in scenarios involving multiple device exploitation and group policy manipulation.

papers.title: RAVEN: A Self-RAG Based Agent for Threat Classification and Response
papers.abstract: Security event analysis in large enterprises can be overwhelming, as each alert typically requires manual in- spection by human operators. This process is time-consuming and prone to inconsistencies, especially in high-volume Secu- rity Operations Center (SOC) environments. In this work- in-progress paper, we present RAVEN: Retrieval-Augmented Vulnerability & Event aNalysis, an agentic framework designed to support SOC analysts by automating the initial stages of alert investigation. The proposed system leverages a Self- Reflective Retrieval-Augmented Generation-based approach to provide an initial classification of security events and enables interactive refinement through analyst-in-the-loop queries. Un- like traditional approaches that rely on generic mitigation strategies, RAVEN generates context-aware remediation sug- gestions by incorporating knowledge of the target enterprise infrastructure. We implement an early-stage prototype and report preliminary results on three balanced test sets of 400 curated web payloads each (SQLi, XSS, SSTI) and a qualitative case study of mitigation generation; an evaluation on IDS- generated alerts and a user study are ongoing and outlined as remaining work.

papers.title: A note on a nonlocal antisymmetric barrier
papers.abstract:
In this note, we present a barrier function for an equation involving the fractional Laplacian in the antisymmetric setting, providing an explicit inequality in the full positivity set of the function. This leads to an improvement of the quantitative maximum principle given in [DPTV26], where the bound was obtained in a strict subset of its positivity set and required additional assumptions on lower order coefficients.
  As a consequence of this, we give an optimal lower bound on the growth of antisymmetric solutions from the symmetry hyperplane.

papers.title: Three-mode chimera-like states in a minimal network of active camphor ribbons
papers.abstract: Chimera states are a remarkable manifestation of symmetry breaking, wherein identical units spontaneously split into coherent and incoherent groups. The term "chimera" itself is inspired by the mythological creature having parts of different animals, reflecting the coexistence of distinct dynamical behaviors within a single system. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the existence of a three-mode chimera-like state in a system of four identical camphor-infused elliptical rotors, each pivoted at a corner of a square base. When placed on a water surface, the rotors self-propel and rotate due to Marangoni-driven flows. Chemical coupling mediated through the shared water interface gives rise to three distinct collective dynamical states, namely a synchronized one, an antisynchronized one and an incoherent one. Our results validate recent theoretical work about three-domain chimeras in reaction-diffusion models, providing new insights into nonlinear dynamics and suggesting that this new type of chimera may be observed in a broad class of physical systems.

papers.title: Prime-Power Expansions and Boundary Corrections for the Secular Coefficients of Riemann-Zero Windows
papers.abstract: We study the secular coefficients of characteristic polynomials attached to finite windows of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, mapped onto the unit circle. Starting from the Riemann-von Mangoldt formula and Newton's identities, we derive a symmetric prime-power model for their generating function. The model carries an explicit boundary factor $(1-w)^{-\Delta S}$, where $\Delta S$ is the variation of $S(t)$ across the window. The boundary correction is determined by the integer zero count of the window rather than by a fitted parameter. For finite prime-power tails we prove a mean-square identity with an explicit diagonal term and an explicit error bound, using the Montgomery-Vaughan generalisation of Hilbert's inequality. Numerical experiments near $T = 10^6$, on computed but uncertified zeros, show that prime powers up to $Q = 32$, the zero count of the window and the known smooth term reproduce the secular coefficients. The median relative residual energy is $1.3 \times 10^{-4}$ for $H = 181$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-5}$ for $H = 724$; the means are $2.1 \times 10^{-3}$ and $2.7 \times 10^{-3}$. The error is strongly asymmetric across windows. An exact convolution identity separates a residual, whose measured size does not depend on the boundary exponent, from its amplification by the boundary factor; the measured amplification follows the exponent over eight orders of magnitude. The diagonal prediction matches the measured power-sum residuals within 16% in the tested regimes. Exact identities and finite Dirichlet-polynomial estimates are kept separate from the numerical reconstruction. Extending the mean-square estimate to the true $S(t)$ is open and appears tied to pair correlations of zeros. This note does not propose a route to the Riemann hypothesis.

authors.name: Francesco Cordella
authors.institution: National Agency for New Technologies, Energy and Sustainable Economic Development

papers.title: Can next generation CMB experiments discriminate between $\Lambda$CDM and dynamical dark energy? A Bayesian forecast for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4
papers.abstract: The combination of Planck CMB data with BAO measurements from the second data release of DESI has revealed a statistically significant preference for a time evolving dark energy equation of state parameterized in the Chevallier Polarski Linder (CPL) form. When type Ia supernovae are included, the preference reaches a significance of $4.2\sigma$ with DESY5, $3.8\sigma$ with Union3 and $2.8\sigma$ with Pantheon+. These hint at a departure from $\Lambda$CDM model. Our previous Fisher matrix analysis suggested that future CMB experiments could probe such a scenario without external low redshift data sets. Here we extend that study by performing a full Bayesian MCMC forecast for the Simons Observatory (SO) and CMB-S4 experiments, assuming as fiducial the DESI+CMB best fit in the $w_0 w_a$CDM model. We generate mock power spectra with the Cobaya mock CMB pipeline. To quantify the geometric degeneracy in the CMB between $w_0, w_a$ and the matter density, we compute for each mock the $\Lambda$CDM "shadow" model that preserves the CMB shift parameter R and produces an equivalent first acoustic peak. SO and CMB-S4 alone cannot distinguish CPL cosmology from its $\Lambda$CDM shadow since the posteriors in the $w_0, w_a$ plane remain broad and largely overlap. This is more pessimistic than our previous Fisher matrix expectation, showing that the Gaussian approximation underestimates the impact of the geometric degeneracy. Adding BAO and Pantheon$+$ supernovae data, yields $\sigma(w_0)\simeq 0.05$-$0.06$ for both experiments. However, the resulting preference for dynamical dark energy depends on the BAO data set, for instance, SDSS BAO moves the constraints close to the $\Lambda$CDM. Our results quantify the discriminating power of future CMB surveys in a Bayesian framework, and highlight the role of low redshift distance probes in establishing or rejecting a dynamical dark energy scenario.

authors.name: Alessandro Melchiorri
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Roma I

papers.title: Nondegeneracy and uniqueness of ground states of the Schr\"odinger equation with Neumann conditions in a weakly nonlocal regime
papers.abstract:
We consider the nonlocal Schr\"odinger equation driven by a fractional Laplacian of order~$2s$, with~$s$ close to~$1$. Differently from the existing literature, which focused on either global problems in the whole of~$\R^n$ or Dirichlet conditions, we study here the case of nonlocal Neumann conditions in the halfspace.
  Moreover, we prove that ground states are nondegenerate, i.e. the only solutions of the linearized equation are linear combinations of the tangential derivatives of the ground state.
  Consequently, the ground state is unique, up to tangential translations and a change of sign.

papers.title: The Depth of a Prediction: Where Language Models Resolve a Word Predicts Human Reading Time
papers.abstract: Surprisal from a language model's final layer predicts how long people read a word, yet the model computes its prediction across many layers. We read each word's prediction at every layer with the tuned lens and summarize this layerwise surprisal trajectory by its resolution depth, the depth around which its change is centered. On eight English eye-tracking and self-paced reading corpora (81,957 words) and ten GPT-2, OPT and Pythia models, words that a model resolves later, and the words after them, are read more slowly than equally surprising words. Resolution depth improves held-out prediction beyond final-layer surprisal, entropy and the best single layer by 0.26 millinats per word (pooled p = 0.001), about a third of entropy's gain, and each model family gains, GPT-2 and Pythia through one corpus each. The net gain varies between corpora (random-effects mean 0.07, p = 0.37); against layer-shuffled depth, which adds as many coefficients, it is positive in seven of eight corpora (random-effects mean 0.23, p = 0.016), and untrained networks show no gain under the logit lens. Pooled over corpora, the effect holds with corrected word probabilities and beyond first-to-last-layer divergences, and a whole-trajectory functional regression adds no significant information beyond resolution depth.

papers.title: Energy estimates of open-weight large language models across stated food weights: a dose-response evaluation
papers.abstract: We tested whether energy estimates of open-weight large language models (LLMs) scale proportionally with an exactly stated food weight, and whether computing energy density times weight removes the error. Under a prespecified protocol, seven open-weight LLMs estimated the energy of 168 randomly drawn foods from the USDA Food and Nutrient Database for Dietary Studies at nine stated weights, from 0.25 to 4 times the default amount. The primary outcome was the elasticity of the estimate with respect to weight (1: proportional scaling). A two-step estimate multiplied each model's own stated energy density by the weight in code. All seven models compressed their estimates, with elasticities from 0.548 to 0.979 (every 95% CI below 1); four compressed severely (0.548 to 0.709). These four overestimated a quarter of the default amount by 47% to 130% and underestimated four times it by 20% to 34%. Supplying the density restored near-proportional scaling in three of the four, and the two-step estimate cut the typical error factor at these extremes from 1.47-2.43 to 1.20-1.38. Compression persisted at full precision and grew in five of seven models under a plain question. The models hold the energy densities needed for proportional scaling and answer near a typical serving, reproducing the flat-slope syndrome of dietary recall. Accuracy at usual portions does not reveal it. Food-logging tools should compute the energy of weighed entries as density times weight, and evaluations should test fixed foods across stated weights.

papers.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
papers.abstract: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. First, frontier agents outperform AutoML, which reaches less than half the best agent's score, and faithful implementations of published methods on four datasets, of which only 6 of 30 beat the strongest agent's own design; published accuracies, where reproducible, rest on the papers' own conventions, and a single convention, capping the remaining life of test engines, can halve the reported error. Second, the agents' advantage is a design made on each machine's data; once made, a plain-text plan of a few hundred words carries most of the gap between two frontier agents, and given a weaker agent's plan, the strongest agent falls to that agent's level, often to identical predictions. Before touching the data, however, it matters little whose plan an agent carries out, and domain toolkits appear to help neither: what sets the strongest apart is how much it learns from the data. Third, such designs reach only implementers that can execute them: given the strongest agent's designs, a locally deployable open-weight model delivers half as often, even when they are lightened, and scores no higher than without them. Generality, we argue, is not disappearing but moving, from the model to the modeler.

papers.title: Bond yield dynamics: a multi-country multi-horizon string model
papers.abstract: This article extends the forward rate curve model of Baaquie and Bouchaud (2004) and Le Coz and Bouchaud (2024) to the multi-country setting of government bond markets. Cross-country blocks of correlation matrices of realized yield changes are found to display significant asymmetry between maturities. In the framework of the proposed model, this amounts to give to each country an idiosyncratic time scale. Each time scale describes how the perceived time between future dates depends on the dates themselves. The differences between these time scales structure the interactions between curves and reproduce the characteristic asymmetry of cross-country correlation matrices. The proposed model captures the full set of cross-curve correlations simultaneously at both daily and intra-day frequencies. When calibrated on government bonds issued by nine countries of the euro-zone, the typical reconstruction error is 1.7%.

papers.title: Large $k$-cross-free families
papers.abstract: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.

papers.title: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $\Lambda_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$. In this paper we prove that $\Lambda_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)= o_L[[o_L]]$, answering the question posed in [AB24].

papers.title: Outflow Properties from a Broad Range of GR$\nu$RMHD Stellar-Mass Black Hole Accretion Disks
papers.abstract: The majority of the mass ejected by neutron star mergers comes from accretion disk outflows. Over timescales of seconds, the thermodynamic evolution of the disk and its resultant outflows set the stage for the ejecta properties which manifest in kilonova observations at later times (hours/days). Kilonova observables depend sensitively on key properties of these outflows -- mass ejection, the ejecta velocity distribution, late-time ejecta morphology and nucleosynthetic yields -- which can only be modeled with a detailed treatment of microphysical interactions including neutrino and general relativistic effects. In this work, we present a library of 25 general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic accretion disks with neutrino transport, to our knowledge the largest to date, spanning a broad range of black hole and accretion disk combinations. From fits to our simulations, we derive analytic estimates of the average ejecta velocity distribution and mass ejection both at simulation end and extrapolated out to the end of the disk's lifetime. We also report ejecta morphology at timescales relevant to kilonova modeling, present spatially-dependent nucleosynthetic yields, and discuss the latter's dependence on initial disk conditions. While our disk library primarily includes initial conditions expected after neutron star mergers, a subset of our disks are applicable to other kilonova-adjacent scenarios.

papers.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
papers.abstract: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $\theta=\pi$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

papers.title: The American Medical Directory Panel: Comparing AI-Assisted and LLM Transcription with Manual Data Entry at Scale
papers.abstract: How closely does machine transcription agree with manual double-entry data? We digitize the 1912 and 1921 editions of the American Medical Directory, a national register of US physicians with roughly 140,000 and 150,000 entries in the two volumes, and compare five machine-extraction workflows with a full-count double-entered manual transcription. Like many historical directories, the AMD is semi-structured rather than tabular, so errors arise from misreading the layout as well as the text. A script that parses commercial OCR text using rules written by coding agents recovers about 97 percent of manually transcribed records with similar precision, more than a multimodal language model workflow (gemini-2.0.flash) that reads the page images and the OCR text. When the two methods fail, they fail on partly overlapping sets of records, so reconciling their outputs raises both recall and precision to about 98 percent. An open-weight LLM pipeline run on a local GPU server falls between the parser and the multimodal workflow in recall, and replacing the commercial OCR model with an open-source alternative lowers its recall by only about 2 percentage points. As the manual transcription's own error rate is unknown, these rates measure agreement rather than accuracy. Direct processing charges for the commercial OCR and multimodal workflow were about 0.03 euro per page, compared with 14.70 euro per page for manual transcription.

papers.title: Leveraging Restrictions to Optimize Register Automata Learning
papers.abstract:
Active automata learning algorithms, especially those that are able to learn extended finite state machines, such as register automata, can capture the behavior of complex systems and help analyses that uncover critical bugs in them. However, the performance and scalability of these algorithms often becomes an issue when models increase in size.
  $SL^{\lambda}$, the current state-of-the-art algorithm for learning register automata, uses a cost-efficient data structure with mechanisms for computing short and restricted tests. In this paper, we present $SL^{\lambda}_{=}$, an extension of $SL^{\lambda}$ for the theory of equality, which improves scalability by employing knowledge gained from prior tests at subsequent steps to restrict future tests to only those that are necessary to achieve progress in the next step.
  We have implemented $SL^{\lambda}_{=}$ as a new algorithm in RALib, and evaluate its performance by comparing it against $SL^{*}$ and $SL^{\lambda}$ on a series of benchmarks, including five widely used implementations of DTLS servers. Our evaluation shows that $SL^{\lambda}_{=}$ needs significantly fewer tests than $SL^{*}$ and $SL^{\lambda}$ to infer models of systems, and scales clearly better than them.

papers.title: Canonical and Canonoid Transformations of Hamiltonian Systems on $q$-Cosymplectic and $q$-Contact Manifolds
papers.abstract: $q$-Cosymplectic and $q$-contact structures equip presymplectic and precontact geometry with additional one-forms and a normalized family of Reeb vector fields. We study canonical and canonoid transformations relative to these data, with particular attention to their origin in constrained mechanical systems. In the $q$-cosymplectic and uniform $q$-contact cases, we establish local normal forms, characterize infinitesimal automorphisms, and obtain Noether-type relations between symmetries and conserved or dissipated quantities. For a one-parameter group of canonoid transformations with generator $X$, we show that $[X,X_H]$ is Hamiltonian and determine its Hamiltonian function. In the uniform $q$-contact case, simultaneous constant rescalings of the defining forms provide canonoid transformations for every Hamiltonian. The geometric constructions are illustrated by regular relativistic mass-shell constraints and by global Lagrangian descriptions of a charge in magnetic monopole fields. These examples distinguish parameters along constraint orbits from physical time and clarify the role of gauge directions. They also recover the total angular momentum of free relativistic particles and the Poincar\'e angular momentum of the charge--monopole system. For two monopoles, we construct a non-uniform $2$-contact structure and prove a topological obstruction to a uniform structure with the prescribed gauge generators as Reeb fields. Irrationally related magnetic charges additionally obstruct the intermediate quotient that would produce a single contact manifold. This example identifies a limitation of the uniform theory and motivates its extension to non-uniform structures.

authors.name: Giuseppe Marmo
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Napoli

papers.title: Context as a Resource
papers.abstract: Managing concurrent tasks across separate agent sessions quickly exhausts human attention, motivating always-on personal agents behind a single continuous interface. Yet when every context shares identical frozen backbone weights, funneling interleaved dialogues and external events into one linear session induces cross-topic constraint bleed and head-of-line stalling. Conversely, router-ticket hierarchies incur lossy prose handoffs, heavy routing overhead, and blind merges - collapsing true-conflict repository merges to a 33.3% three-run mean despite high isolated branch passes. Rather than scheduling anthropomorphic roles, we introduce ClonAct, a routerless architecture that virtualizes context blocks directly through a pluggable single-pass non-generative Context MMU, in-place Context Cells, a footprint-aware Synaptic Bus with an isolated trial merge gate, and a wave-flushed Shared Trunk. Across three programmatic multi-stream benchmarks and three model families, our portable trial merge gate lifts true-conflict merges to 63.3%, while ClonAct's routerless virtualization attains this ceiling with 45.9% fewer prompt tokens and prevents compact-model router collapse. Under continuous surge streams, ClonAct matches top completion (95.0%) with the lowest median wait and zero timed-out status checks.

authors.name: Xufei Tian
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Industrial Control Technology

papers.title: Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
papers.abstract: Topological equivalence between two gapped band structures is determined by whether their occupied states can be continuously deformed into one another without closing the energy gap or breaking the protecting symmetries. We show that this relative topology can be read directly from the overlap matrix between the two occupied subspaces, in a way that treats Chern and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants within a single framework. The determinant of the overlap matrix defines a global section of a line bundle over the Brillouin zone, which vanishes at the momenta where the map between the subspaces fails to be invertible. A singular connection, whose curvature is concentrated at these zeros, assigns each zero an integer charge given by its phase winding. In two-dimensional class A, the total charge equals the difference between the Chern numbers of the two systems. In class AII, time reversal pairs zeros of opposite charge, and the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant is the parity of the total charge in half the Brillouin zone; the Kane-Mele Pfaffian is recovered as a special case. The zeros coincide with the gap closings of an interpolation between the two systems, and crystalline symmetries constrain their positions and charges. We illustrate the construction in the Haldane, Kane-Mele, and Qi-Wu-Zhang models, including cases where rotation symmetry alone enforces the zeros.

papers.title: CAIMS: Scalable Cross-Array In-Memory Search
papers.abstract: Search, especially top-k similarity search, plays a vital role in many applications, but its performance can be severely limited by memory access overhead. In-memory search (IMS), an alternative to CPU/GPU-based approaches, exploits massive parallelism within a content-addressable memory (CAM) array to perform search in situ and provides both low latency and high energy efficiency. However, the capacity of a single CAM array is often insufficient for modern workloads, requiring data to be distributed across multiple arrays. Deploying scalable top-k similarity search across multiple CAM arrays poses a fundamental problem that existing designs fail to address: how to accurately and efficiently reduce local binary match results to global top-k results. This work introduces CAIMS, a cross-array IMS framework that is agnostic to memory technologies and applications, enabling scalable and efficient top-k similarity search while preserving accuracy. To enable accurate top-k result reduction, CAIMS leverages the existing threshold match functionality with a combined offline and online parameter selection approach to transform local binary match results that lack globally comparable similarity information into global coarse-grained similarity scores. To further improve efficiency, CAIMS conducts hierarchical reduction and transfers only the selection results and necessary control signals with lightweight local peripherals. Implemented on a 3D NAND Flash model and demonstrated using the retrieval phase of retrieval-augmented generation, CAIMS improves throughput by up to $22.3\times/10.1\times$ and energy efficiency by $426.6\times/23.7\times$ compared to the server-class CPU baseline and prior 3D NAND Flash accelerators, respectively, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

papers.title: What Does Anti-Hallucination Training Buy? Saying Less, Cheap Pruning, and the Rest
papers.abstract: Preference training is the standard recipe for reducing object hallucination in vision-language models, and each new method reports a lower CHAIR score. We ask what that reduction consists of. Every trained system is compared with its base model's caption truncated to the same object recall, which removes the part of the gain that comes from saying less; the remainder is compared with what a deliberately weak, frozen, eleven-feature post-hoc probe fitted on 500 annotated images can reproduce. All criteria were specified in the analysis code and frozen before the outputs they judge existed. For eight public methods on LLaVA-1.5-7B, the probe reproduces at least two thirds of what training removes beyond saying less for 7 of 8 methods on COCO, 8 of 8 on AMBER and 6 of 8 on Object HalBench, with RLAIF-V the consistent exception; a later public method released for both LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL (SENTINEL) meets the same bar on both. On our own DPO checkpoints the accounting holds on Qwen2.5-VL but fails on InternVL2.5 on COCO (2 of 4 training designs). At matched recall, the base model plus the probe beats truncation for 8 of 9 LLaVA-1.5 systems on COCO and 9 of 9 on AMBER, on the two newer backbones, and when realized as actual sentence deletion. The same measure prices training signals: DPO on the model's own samples labelled by the probe or by an object-level CLIP score recovers 0.70 and 0.87 of the beyond-brevity gain of ground-truth-labelled DPO on Qwen2.5-VL (the probe 0.73 on InternVL2.5), both beat length-matched random labels, and CLIP labels buy more than probe labels on COCO. Human judgements show that the sentences the probe deletes are wrong more often than those truncation would delete; a human check of the CHAIR evaluator's precision falls below our pre-set bar, which we report as a limitation.

papers.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
papers.abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

papers.title: Causal Effect Estimation Under Uncertain Statistical Surrogacy
papers.abstract: Surrogate endpoints can improve the efficiency of causal effect estimation, but such gains may depend on structural assumptions. One such assumption is statistical surrogacy, which requires the primary outcome to be conditionally independent of treatment given the surrogate and baseline covariates. We study causal effect estimation with multiple candidate surrogates of uncertain validity under statistical surrogacy, considering settings where the primary outcome is either fully observed or subject to missingness. We characterize the asymptotic efficiency differences between surrogate-assisted and benchmark estimators, examine the bias induced by violations of statistical surrogacy, and identify conditions under which incorporating surrogate information leads to efficiency gains or losses. To address uncertainty in surrogate validity, we propose Surrogate-assisted Adaptive Causal effect EStimation (SACES), a procedure that anchors estimation to a robust benchmark while adaptively selecting among a finite set of surrogate-assisted estimators using an estimated mean squared error criterion. SACES aims to leverage efficiency gains when statistical surrogacy holds while preserving consistency when the assumption is violated. Simulations demonstrate that SACES achieves a favorable bias-variance trade-off across varying degrees of surrogacy violation. We illustrate the proposed methods using data from the ACTG 175 clinical trial to demonstrate how surrogate information can be adaptively incorporated into causal effect estimation.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: A photon-number-conserving multimode framework for pulse propagation dynamics across zero nonlinearity: Kerr-Raman cooperation and competition
papers.abstract: Raman scattering in multimode fibers shifts pulse spectra to lower frequencies and transfers photons between spatial modes. When the nonlinear coefficient changes sign within the pulse spectrum, the ordinary generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) can give unphysical predictions. Existing photon-number-conserving formulations either treat a single mode or exclude Raman scattering. We develop a time-domain multimode GNLSE that conserves photon number, includes the full Raman response and remains well defined at the zero-nonlinearity frequency. For narrowband pulses with a constant positive nonlinear coefficient, the framework reduces to the standard multimode GNLSE with instantaneous Kerr and delayed Raman terms. We then apply the framework to three coherently excited modes whose spectra shift across the zero-nonlinearity frequency. The Kerr and Raman processes first cooperate and then compete. In the first stage, both processes transfer photons into the fundamental mode, contributing about 2\% and 43\% of the initial total photon number. In the second stage, Kerr transfer drives photons out of the fundamental mode, while Raman transfer drives photons back, contributing about $-27\%$ and $+15\%$, respectively. Consequently, the fundamental-mode photon fraction rises from 20\% to 65\% and then falls to 53\%. Kerr terms that leave the modal photon populations unchanged still reshape the fields and thereby enhance Raman transfer. Moreover, changing only the relative input phases can reverse the initial Raman-driven flow into the fundamental mode, even for identical modal spectra. Taken together, the results show how instantaneous and delayed nonlinear responses, together with intermodal phase, govern photon redistribution across zero nonlinearity.
