papers.title: Personalized Privacy-Aware MARL Offloading in the Edge-Cloud Continuum
papers.abstract: Task offloading in End-Edge-Cloud computing enables resource-constrained User Devices (UDs) to execute computation-intensive applications with reduced latency and energy consumption. However, existing task offloading schemes generally overlook the heterogeneous privacy requirements of users, leading to inefficient privacy-aware offloading decisions. In this paper, we propose a personalized privacy-aware task offloading framework, where the privacy requirement of each task is quantified through a User-Centric Privacy (UCP) model that considers task sensitivity, user privacy preferences, and task urgency. The task offloading problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to jointly optimize the offloading ratio and the target computing server while minimizing the long-term system cost under latency, energy, and privacy constraints. To efficiently solve the resulting high-dimensional continuous optimization problem, we develop an Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) algorithm under the Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves lower average system cost, lower energy consumption, and higher task success rate than representative baselines under diverse privacy requirements.

papers.title: Regime-dependent reconstruction of structural connectivity: an in silico study of spatially constrained modular neuronal networks
papers.abstract: Inferring structural connectivity from neuronal activity is a major challenge in neuroscience, yet the conditions under which inferred interactions faithfully reflect anatomical connections remain unclear. Here, we investigate in silico how spatial constraints in a neuronal network and its dynamical regime jointly shape structural recoverability. We construct modular networks with varying average axonal lengths and simulate spontaneous activity using the Izhikevich model with synaptic depression across a broad range of excitatory strengths and background noise levels. Using Generalized Transfer Entropy, we infer effective connectivity and compare it with the underlying structural ground-truth at the levels of individual connections and global topology. We observe that the richness in the repertoire of activity patterns is highest in an intermediate regime between globally synchronized and noise-dominated activity, reflecting a balance between global excitation and stochasticity. Optimal structural reconstruction generally occurs under these same conditions, although this correspondence depends on network architecture and is weaker in highly modular networks. Together, these results show that structural recoverability depends jointly on network organization and dynamical regime. More broadly, our findings highlight the risks of treating inferred effective connectivity as a direct surrogate for structural connectivity.

authors.name: Hideaki Yamamoto
authors.institution: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University

authors.name: M. Angeles Serrano
authors.institution: Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats

papers.title: Coordinated Offloading: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Edge-Cloud Continuum
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for intelligent, low-latency services in edge-cloud continuum systems poses new challenges for dynamic and efficient task offloading. We propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for distributed task offloading under partial observability, where each device offloads only a portion of its computation to a target edge server while executing the remaining portion locally (partial offloading). The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each device independently learns an optimal policy under partially observable system states. To address the non-convexity, high-dimensional state space, and continuous action space, we develop a multi-agent Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based computation offloading algorithm. The proposed method combines the stable policy updates of PPO with an advantage-weighting mechanism inspired by AWAC to emphasize higher-quality actions during training. To encourage cooperation without inter-device communication, a shared global reward aligned with system cost is employed. Extensive simulations demonstrate rapid convergence and significant improvement in overall system cost compared with baselines, e.g., Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Deep Q-Network (DQN).

papers.title: Elementwise Precision-weighted Compositional Data Analysis by Weighted Alternating Least Squares
papers.abstract: Logratio principal component is a multivariate method commonly used for exploring compositional data sets. This method is mostly used in an unweighted manner, employing the centred logratio transformation of the compositions. The smaller elements of a composition usually have a higher relative error, and can be downweighted using part-wise weighting. In this article we focus on weighting compositional data and propose elementwise precision weighting of compositions. This is particularly convenient for compositions with parts that fluctuate from rare to frequent; e.g. parts acting as traces in some samples, but being abundant in others. We suggest to weight in the logarithmic or logratio scale, with the inverse of the standard deviation of the logratio, the latter being estimated for each part of each composition separately. A weighted least squares algorithm is used for dimension reduction and compositional biplot construction. Several applications of elementwise precision weighting are described, using compositional datasets from genetics, archaeology and microbiomics that illustrate the power and advantages of a fully weighted compositional analysis.

papers.title: Statistical, Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Missing Covariates: An Empirical Evaluation with Applications to Alzheimer's Disease Research
papers.abstract: Missing data are common in biomedical research, particularly when biomarkers are costly or require invasive procedures to obtain, such as cerebrospinal fluid measures in Alzheimer's disease. Although a wide range of missing data methods exists, from traditional statistical approaches to modern machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) algorithms, their comparative performance under different missingness mechanisms remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we provide an empirical evaluation of eight methods for handling missing covariates, including complete-case analysis, multiple imputation, ML-based techniques, and DL frameworks such as multilayer perceptrons, variational autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks. We summarize their conceptual foundations, practical implementation considerations, strengths, and limitations. Through extensive simulations, we assess estimation bias, efficiency, standard error accuracy, confidence interval coverage, and computational burden across different missingness mechanisms and proportions. An application to the Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project further illustrates the implications of different methods for regression analysis in a real-world biomedical setting. Finally, we provide practical recommendations for method selection and highlight remaining challenges that warrant future investigation.

authors.name: Panpan Zhang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Ly$\alpha$ radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al. (2026), our fiducial model assumes $\sim 10^5\,M_\odot$ Pop III.1 stars forming by $z_{\rm flash}=20$ with a comoving number density of $\sim0.2\,{\rm cMpc}^{-3}$. For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than $1\%$ of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements. However, the contribution to the CIB from $z\sim6-20$ SMBH accretion is expected to be larger than the Pop III.1 stellar component for average Eddington ratios $\lambda_{\text{Edd}} \sim 0.01$. Latest CIB observations place constraints of $\lambda_{\text{Edd}} \lesssim 0.3$ for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.

papers.title: Field-free deterministic spin-orbit torque magnetization switching using monolayer WTe2
papers.abstract: An important step towards the practical implementation of spin-orbit torque magnetic memory is the field-free switching of the magnetization vector. In this work, we investigate spin-orbit torque-driven magnetization dynamics and switching devices comprising monolayer $\mathrm{WTe}_2$ as the spin-source material. We perform a comparative analysis of the two phases of $\mathrm{WTe}_2$, namely the $1\mathrm{T}_d$ and $1\mathrm{T}'$ with the necessary symmetries for field-free deterministic magnetization switching. We demonstrate switching in both systems and analyse the dependence of the switching dynamics on the applied bias voltage, ribbon orientation and width of the magnetic layer. Modelling the ferromagnet as an exchange-coupled macrospin within a non-equilibrium Green's function framework, we find that the $x$-ribbon geometry of the $1\mathrm{T}_d$ $\mathrm{WTe}_2$ phase generates a significantly larger current-induced spin polarization than the $1\mathrm{T}'$ phase, resulting in a larger damping-like torque on the adjacent magnetic layer and faster switching. The switching time of $1\mathrm{T}'$ devices varies strongly and non-monotonically with the width of the magnetic layer. In $1\mathrm{T}_d$ devices, it remains nearly constant over a broad range of widths, consistent with an edge-dominated torque. These results identify $x$-ribbon $1\mathrm{T}_d$-$\mathrm{WTe}_2$ as a promising spin source for field-free SOT-MRAM.

authors.name: Ganesh Hanchanahal
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you
papers.abstract: Prosodic prominence can largely be predicted from the words of a sentence, but part of it depends on how the speaker reads it. We study how much of prominence language models recover from text, whether they can report it when asked, and what the speech signal adds. On read English speech labelled for word-level prominence, we compare frozen and fine-tuned text models, prompted large language models (LLMs) and speech models on the same words. All text models end within about one point of each other, at best 68.8% on the 3-way task, and largely make the same errors. With the prompts we tested, LLMs do no better than a word-majority baseline, even with 500 examples. Linear probes find more in their representations. Speech models reach 84.7%. We argue that text determines only part of prominence, and that the rest has to be heard. LLMs encode what the text determines, but prompting does not bring it out: they represent more about where the emphasis falls than they tell you.

papers.title: SHUSH: Emission-Aware Reward Design for Proactive Video Assistants
papers.abstract: Proactive video assistants must decide not only what to say, but also when to speak. Existing reinforcement-learning objectives can reward timely, correct responses without accounting for response volume, thereby encouraging unnecessary or repeated emissions. We identify this failure mode in MMDuet2, whose proactive area-under-the-curve (PAUC) reward promotes timely responses but does not price the number of emissions. We show analytically that this makes additional responses weakly penalized or effectively free, systematically encouraging over-emission. We then propose an emission-aware F1 reward for interval-valued annotations, using exclusive span--emission matching to price false emissions and missed spans. Under MMDuet2's training recipe, our policy on the visual subset of OmniPro replies 2.5x less often than MMDuet2 while raising timing F1 from 0.259 to 0.396 and content-aware F1 from 0.103 to 0.154; a more conservative variant cuts replies by 82.5% and raises precision from 0.161 to 0.418. On ProactiveVideoQA, the same reward adds replies where the baseline is nearly silent, and PAUC ranks a heavily over-emitting policy second despite near-last F1, because it is insensitive to response count. Our results indicate that proactive assistants should be trained and evaluated with objectives that price emissions.

papers.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
papers.abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

authors.name: Kaiwen Zhang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Yiming Gao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ColorRef: Calibrating Verbal Feedback for Color Revision
papers.abstract: People rarely specify an exact color when asking someone to revise a design: they might say \textit{a little darker} or \textit{more blue} after seeing a proposal. A language-model assistant must then infer not only which way to change the color, but how far. We study this distinction with \textsc{ColorRef}, a color reference game in which a model guesses a color from a description and a teacher, knowing a recorded target hidden from the guesser, supplies verbal corrections. On 1{,}000 crowd-sourced description--target pairs, three rounds of deterministic oracle feedback reduce mean target distance from 42.33 to 22.15 $\Delta E_{76}$. However, those corrections provide additional information, and improvement alone does not establish well-calibrated feedback following. A controlled Qwen3-14B diagnostic reveals a more specific failure: following a requested direction and ordering graded phrases do not guarantee a suitable step size; strong modifiers can induce excessive changes. We therefore measure each receiver's typical response to \textit{a little}, \textit{somewhat}, and \textit{much} on separate colors and select wording matched to its observed steps. On 128 held-out starting colors, calibration reduces one-step mean error from 12.36 to 6.86 for Qwen3-14B and from 11.06 to 5.89 for Gemma 4 12B against a fixed graded-wording rule. The benefit is concentrated on large corrections, with many unchanged cases and no consistent increase in threshold success. Our findings show that following the direction of feedback is not the same as making an appropriately sized revision.

papers.title: Learning Reconstruction Errors as Spatiotemporal Evidence for AI-Generated Video Detection
papers.abstract: The proliferation of AI-generated videos has raised growing concerns about misinformation, fraud, and potential societal risks, creating an urgent need for detection. Reconstruction-error-based methods have shown strong empirical performance for AI-generated image detection by exploiting discrepancies between an input and its reconstructed version. Their extension to video detection, however, faces two challenges: (i) a fixed reconstructor is not optimized for the detection objective and may yield weak discriminative signals; and (ii) an additional raw-video feature stream is often introduced to model temporal dependencies, increasing architectural overhead. To address these challenges, we develop a detector that learns and exploits reconstruction errors as a unified source of spatiotemporal evidence. First, we jointly optimize a reconstructor and the downstream classifier to produce reconstruction errors that are more informative for detecting AI-generated videos. Second, we show that consecutive reconstruction errors alone carry temporal evidence, and thus a 3D convolution over them captures spatiotemporal evidence without a raw-video stream. Extensive experiments on over 30 existing AI-video generators demonstrate competitive performance against baselines.

papers.title: Unusual increase in electrical and thermal conductivity of severely deformed CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy: Roles of disordering and nanostructuring in electron and phonon transport
papers.abstract: This work investigates how defect engineering and nanostructuring via severe plastic deformation influence electrical and thermal transport in the high-entropy alloy CrMnFeCoNi. High-pressure torsion (HPT) for up to N = 4 turns produces a hierarchical defect structure, including deformation twins at low strains, dislocations and Lomer-Cottrell locks at intermediate strains, and a high fraction of high-angle grain boundaries at large strains. While hardness naturally increases and saturates at ~520 Hv, both electrical and thermal conductivity exhibit an unusual increase upon HPT processing (from 0.953 MS m-1 and 10.3 W m-1 K-1 after homogenization to 1.003 +- 0.005 MS m-1 and 14.4 W m-1 K-1 after N = 4). Analysis based on the Wiedemann-Franz law indicates a modest increase in electron transport (~5%) and a significant increase in phonon transport (~100%) after HPT processing. The phonon mean free path remains small on the order of 0.6-1.1 nm, and comparison with the Cahill-Pohl model shows that heat transport occurs near the minimum thermal conductivity limit, where vibrational modes are strongly scattered. This suggests that the enhancement in thermal transport is not governed by conventional defect scattering, but it is hypothesized that modifications in atomic-scale disorder, such as deformation-induced short-range ordering, are responsible for this unusual behavior. Specific heat capacity increases after HPT, consistent with stored defect energy. The linear thermal expansion exhibits a non-monotonic behavior, decreasing initially due to internal stresses and relaxation effects, and increasing at higher strains due to grain boundary-induced anharmonicity. These findings highlight the complex interplay between defects, atomic-scale disorder, and nanostructure in governing the electrical and thermal properties of severely deformed high-entropy alloys via electron and phonon scattering.

authors.name: Dmitry Chernyshov
authors.institution: P.N. Lebedev Physical Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Better Retrieval, Not Better Binding: Pretraining Exposure in Egocentric Video Retrieval
papers.abstract: Video-language models (VLMs) achieve strong performance on video-text retrieval and are increasingly used for egocentric video understanding. Yet, despite gains in zero-shot retrieval, they have shown limitations in compositional understanding, and it remains unclear whether they understand compositional relationships between verbs and nouns. In this work, we introduce Ego-ExBind, a compositional diagnostic protocol for analyzing pretraining exposure and verb-noun binding in egocentric video-text retrieval. Ego-ExBind consists of an Exposure Ledger built from the EgoClip pretraining corpus used by EgoVLPv2, which defines Seen Composition, Unseen Composition, and Unseen Atom splits for EPIC-KITCHENS-100 multi-instance retrieval (MIR). We further probe noun and verb binding channels through controlled noun-swap and verb-swap negatives. We find that zero-shot retrieval is positively associated with pair exposure within seen compositions, even after controlling for the marginal frequencies of verbs and nouns. However, higher pair exposure is associated with larger noun-swap margins and slightly smaller verb-swap margins. This asymmetry motivates us to test whether exposure reweighting can improve retrieval with little change in the measured swap margins. To isolate the effect of exposure input, we keep the trained checkpoint fixed and replace only the exposure input at inference. We demonstrate that this exposure reweighting can improve video-text retrieval without stronger verb-noun compositional understanding, and that the gain depends on the correct sample-level exposure correspondence. By separating exposure-driven retrieval gains from verb-noun binding, Ego-ExBind provides a diagnostic framework for evaluating whether future improvements in egocentric MIR reflect compositional understanding rather than pretraining familiarity.

authors.name: Yuqi Guo
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers
papers.abstract: Zero-shot large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as text classifiers, but their labels are only useful when we know to what extent we can trust them. We compare black-box methods (verbalised confidence and sampling) with white-box methods that read token probabilities (P(True), and multiple logit-scoring methods using constrained generation). We evaluate eleven open-weight LLMs (1B-32B parameters) on five classification datasets with 3 to 151 labels, measuring classification performance (accuracy, F1-macro), discrimination (AUROC), and calibration (ECE and Brier score). The choice of confidence method rarely impacts accuracy significantly, but logit-based scoring methods lead to much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than black-box methods (AUROC 0.57-0.66). Replacing labels with single-token identifiers preserves discrimination but costs 3-6 accuracy points on average. We also introduce decision-only scoring, which only scores positions where labels diverge in the prefix tree (trie). It reduces decode steps by 88-96% on the three largest label sets and performs comparably to full-label scoring. The best open-weight model-method configurations (Gemma 4 31B and Qwen 3.5 9B) are competitive with the commercial Jev 1.13.0 classifier.

papers.title: Local orbital magnetization and Chern markers from equilibrium local currents
papers.abstract: Local currents carry the orbital magnetization of a macroscopic sample and are key for modeling inhomogeneous magnetic materials and for understanding magnetoelectric and topological responses. However, producing realistic simulated images of local currents in inhomogeneous systems remains challenging. Building upon recent work on stochastic estimation methods for tight-binding models, we show that all matrix elements of positive semidefinite operators defined on a lattice can be obtained at once from a single set of filtered random vectors. This eliminates the need for independent simulations previously required for off-diagonal elements, which significantly speeds up the calculation of spatial maps of local currents. Further, we express bond currents in terms of loop currents that obey a discrete Poisson equation, with the current vorticity acting as the source term. Its solution yields a local orbital magnetization. In analogy with the global St\v{r}eda relation, the derivative of this magnetization with respect to the chemical potential defines a new local Chern marker. Built entirely from bond currents, it requires no position operator and is not bound by the zero-sum rule of projector markers in open samples. Hence, it is free of boundary-compensation artifacts, and its sample average converges to the bulk Chern number in a controlled fashion.

authors.name: Caio H. Lewenkopf
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

authors.name: Joao M. Viana Parente Lopes
authors.institution: Centro de Física das Universidades do Minho e do Porto

papers.title: Frequency-Synchronized Boundary Coupling for Training-Free Multi-Prompt Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Text-to-video generation has made remarkable progress with diffusion models and transformer-based video architectures, yet generating coherent long videos from evolving textual descriptions remains challenging. Training long-video models from scratch requires substantial computation and large-scale multi-event data, while training-free multi-prompt generation must activate new prompt semantics without breaking temporal continuity. We identify a frequency-agnostic boundary coupling problem in existing transition strategies: weak coupling causes abrupt changes, flicker, and background jumps, whereas overly strong or coarse coupling may over-preserve source semantics and produce ghosting or duplicated subjects around prompt boundaries. To address this problem, we propose FreqSync, a training-free framework that formulates prompt transitions as frequency-selective boundary coupling. FreqSync combines Frequency-Synchronized Source-Conditioned Attention (FS-SCA) with Residual-Clipped Spectral Stitching (RCSS), enabling adjacent segments to share stable low- and mid-frequency structure and motion cues while keeping high-frequency prompt-specific details target-dominant under explicit residual constraints. Extensive experiments show that FreqSync achieves state-of-the-art transition smoothness and prompt alignment while maintaining strong perceptual video quality, demonstrating its effectiveness for coherent multi-prompt long video generation.

authors.name: Jiayu Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Rediscussion of eclipsing binaries. Paper 33. The A-type system CW Canis Majoris in the PLATO southern field
papers.abstract: CW CMa is a detached eclipsing binary containing two A0 V stars in a circular orbit of period 2.12 d. We analyse the light-curves of this system from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) together with published radial velocity measurements to determine the masses and radii of the component stars to high precision, obtaining masses of 2.087 +/- 0.022 Msun and 1.972 +/- 0.024 Msun, and radii of 1.841 +/- 0.012 Rsun and 1.748 +/- 0.014 Rsun. We detect a changing orbital period over the four available TESS sectors indicative of the presence of a companion on a wider orbit. We develop a new method to determine the effective temperatures of the component stars using their measured radii, the Gaia parallax, and surface-brightness calibrations to reduce the degeneracy between temperature and extinction. The method gives temperatures of 9850 +/- 280 K and 9570 +/- 270 K and an interstellar extinction of A(V) = 0.32 +/- 0.06 mag. The properties of the system can be matched by theoretical models for a subsolar metal abundance (Z = 0.010) and an age of 400 +/- 20 Myr. CW CMa has been selected as a target for the PLATO satellite, with which it will be observed for at least two years.

papers.title: From Data Alignment to Parameter Generation: Few-Shot Cross-City Traffic Prediction with Conditional Diffusion
papers.abstract: Accurate mobile traffic forecasting is crucial for network service management, supporting proactive capacity provisioning, congestion mitigation, and energy-efficient operation. However, many cities and regions are data-scarce (e.g., newly deployed or poorly instrumented areas), thus making traffic prediction a few-shot learning problem and limiting the practicality of standard data-driven models. Existing cross-city solutions primarily rely on data-space alignment to match traffic distributions between data-rich and data-scarce cities, but such alignment is often brittle under real-world distribution shifts, measurement noise, and city-specific bias. To address these limitations, we propose a Conditional Diffusion-based Parameter Generation (CDPG) framework. Instead of aligning raw data, CDPG learns the conditional distribution of high-performing predictor parameters for source cities and directly generates node-specific model parameters for the target city. To support reliable adaptation for network traffic prediction, CDPG conditions parameter generation on multi-modal spatio-temporal context. Specifically, CDPG captures spatial environment cues by combining satellite imagery with large language model (LLM)-derived semantic descriptions, and summarizes complex temporal behaviors via unsupervised pattern clustering. These contextual components guide CDPG in producing parameters tailored to each base station's operational context, thereby improving robustness under cross-city and cross-region shifts. Extensive experiments on three large-scale datasets show that CDPG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art cross-city few-shot baselines by up to 9.72% on standard forecasting metrics and remains robust for few-shot multi-step prediction. The code is available at https://github.com/LingoodBoy/CDPG.

authors.name: Wenjie Chen
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Lightweight Low-Frequency Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring via Karhunen-Lo\`eve Feature Distillation and Temporal Convolutional Networks
papers.abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a critical enabler for demand-side management which allows for smart grid optimization. A deployment-ready NILM solution necessitates three key features: accurate disaggregation, low-frequency sampling, and low computational cost. This paper proposes a lightweight, edge-oriented NILM framework that combines activity-boundary-aware synthetic data augmentation with Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transform (KLT) feature extraction and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN). The augmentation stage extracts and recombines complete or near-complete appliance activation segments so that the model can be trained without new fully labeled household aggregates. The KLT filter bank extracts decorrelated, appliance-informed temporal features which are then fed into a compact TCN along with the original aggregate for energy disaggregation. Evaluations on two standard NILM datasets, UK-DALE and REDD, at 10-s sampling and with leave-one-house-out testing, demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves comparable or superior disaggregation accuracy relative to NILMFormer, BERT4NILM, BiLSTM, and BiGRU. The computational footprint of the framework is 31,009 parameters, the fewest of the five models compared, and on a single CPU thread it needs 2.78 ms per 1000 samples, 84-95% less than the baselines. These results demonstrate a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for low-frequency smart-meter NILM.

papers.title: Conditional-Hierarchical Open-Set Deep Learning for Robust Radio Signals Intelligence
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an open-set radio-frequency (RF) deep learning (DL) framework that jointly performs conditionally hierarchical multi-level radio signal classification and out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. To exploit image-based classification models, the raw radio samples are transformed into time-frequency representations using the short time Fourier transform (STFT) to pre-process the radio signals. A lightweight novel architecture using neural network (CNN), that applies con- ditional hierarchical multi-task classification heads, is introduced, and compared to two baselines including: (1) The conventional convolutional neural network (CNN) and (2) Swin-T model with multitask classification heads, where the model accuracy and complexity perspectives are considered for the comparison. Moreover, to address open-set scenarios, we introduce the fusion of two OOD detectors each of which is fitted to a Gaussian mixture model by using the learned feature space (e.g. the feature embeddings and logits) from the multi-head classifica- tion network. The overall training process is achieved on two stages following a post-hoc design: the in-set classification neural network is trained first, then the learnable parameters are frozen in the evaluation mode to process the training dataset again to aggregate the embeddings and logits used to fit the GMMs for OOD detection. Moreover, a proof of concept using experimental setup is implemented to validate the operation of the introduced models and algorithms in practical scenarios. The simulation- based trained model is fine-tuned using experimentally measured radio signals. For the experimental setup, a USRP-B210 acting as a transmitter, and an edge Deepwave Air-T software-defined radio, which is equipped with the fine-tuned neural networks is used as a detector or receiver.

papers.title: 20 ghz longitudinal surface acoustic wave resonators in 100-nm x-cut lithium niobate on silicon carbide
papers.abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15~GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling ($k^2$). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high $k^2$ in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7~GHz and reaching a $k^2$ of 8.1\%, a maximum Bode $Q$ of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24~GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength ($\lambda$) keeps the normalized LN thickness ($h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$) large, sustaining both $k^2$ and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing $\lambda$ from 292 to 471~nm lowers $h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05~km/s, within 1.1\% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and $k^2$ falls from its 8.1\% peak at $\lambda = 322$~nm to 1.7\% at $\lambda = 471$~nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for $\lambda \geq 518$~nm ($h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda \leq 0.19$), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5\% of its maximum for $h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.

authors.name: Jiajun Huang
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Ziqian Yao
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Ruochen Lu
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: The final stages of a Chapman-Jouguet detonation: support by its own products
papers.abstract: A planar Chapman-Jouguet detonation that runs out of fuel must become a shock. We show that, when the chemical energy decreases in the direction of propagation, the wave does not pass through the local Chapman-Jouguet states. The products of the richer mixture are at a higher pressure than the local Chapman-Jouguet state, so the wave is overdriven, it loses its sonic point, and forward characteristics carry the state of the rich products to the shock. The rarefaction behind the wave removes this support only if the distance travelled since initiation is small compared with the thickness of the fuel gradient, which is rarely the case. The wave speed instead approaches an envelope given by a Riemann problem between the rich products and the local mixture, ending at the Mach number of the shock transmitted into inert gas. For strong detonations this Mach number tends to a fraction $C$ of the Chapman-Jouguet value, with $0.621<C<0.625$ for every ratio of specific heats. The mechanism is purely gas-dynamic. Shock-fitted computations with a two-step chain-branching mechanism, for gradients 1 to 1000 induction lengths thick, confirm that no sonic point forms and that the induction zone never decouples.

papers.title: $C^{0}$ stability of torsion-free $G_{2}$ structures along the Laplacian flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that torsion-free $G_{2}$-structures are (weakly) dynamically stable along the Laplacian flow for closed $G_{2}$-structures in $C^{0}$-open neighbourhood. This weakens the assumption in \cite{LW19} and confirms Bryant's expectation \cite{Bry06} in the $C^{0}$ norm.

papers.title: Loss-Guided Tsetlin Machines: Making the Learning Objective Explicit
papers.abstract: The Tsetlin Machine (TM) has no explicit notion of a loss function. Its learning signal is fixed to an implicit, margin-based update rule (MBUR), with no way to choose an objective function suited to a specific task. This paper introduces Loss-Guided TM, which replaces MBUR with an explicit and swappable loss function. In our proposed method, clause feedback and weight updates are driven by the loss, while keeping the Tsetlin Automaton and clause logic unchanged. The approach incorporates cross entropy (CE), symmetric cross entropy (SCE), and asymmetric loss (ASL). We evaluate Loss-Guided TM across six datasets that span multiclass, multilabel, and binary classification tasks. With a suitable loss, Loss-Guided TM matches or improves accuracy and F1 over MBUR on five of the six datasets. The gains are greatest for the imbalanced multilabel datasets, where ASL improves macro F1 by up to 9 percentage points. With CE, Loss-Guided TM is also significantly better calibrated than MBUR on all six datasets, reducing calibration error by a factor of 3 to 11. A qualitative inspection shows that the clause-based global interpretability, examined at the per-class level on image and text data, is preserved when using the Loss-Guided mechanism. These results show that our explicit TM learning objective allows direct targeting of uncertainty calibration, data imbalance, and task structure, opening the TM to the broader literature on loss functions.

papers.title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
papers.abstract: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the event stream corresponds to a derivative-like interferogram, and another with a temporal modulation of a broadband LED, which produces an intensity-like event response. Both approaches are able to retrieve the principal spectral profiles of photographic filters, showing a good qualitative match with both frame-based and spectrometer references. Compared against the typical 15-minute acquisition time for step-scan reference configuration, both methods represent a speedup larger than 3 orders of magnitude, entering real-time acquisition speeds: the derivative-based method acquires the useful interferometric range in approximately 200 ms, corresponding to an effective rate of approximately 5 hyperspectral cubes per second, whereas the modulation-assisted method achieves an experimentally measured spectral resolution of 17.9 nm at an effective acquisition rate of 2.5 datacubes per second. Finally, reflection-mode imaging and motion-compensated reconstruction of moving particles further demonstrate spatially resolved spectral recovery beyond static transmission measurements, establishing the solution as a promising technology for continuous, wide-field hyperspectral imaging.

papers.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
papers.abstract:
In the standard $\Lambda$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. For the mass accretion histories, the modified gravitational effect can produce systematic departures from GR, generally corresponding to more rapid halo growth. The deviations are relatively small when the MG effect is weak, while they become more pronounced in models with strong deviation from GR and can exceed $15\%$ in the extreme case.
  For the halo merger rate, we find that the nearly universal behavior is well preserved across all the gravity models, with only weak dependence on redshift and halo mass, reflecting the unbiased accretion nature of halo growth. However, apparent deviation from this universality can arise if the halo mass is not defined consistently with the modified gravity model.

papers.title: Eigenspectra of Poisson-sampled stellar population models: Statistical fingerprints of cool giant stars in unresolved early-type galaxies
papers.abstract: The light of unresolved galaxies carries the imprint of their underlying stellar populations, yet isolating contributions from specific stellar types remains challenging. If multiple spectra of the same population are available, e.g. from high-resolution integral field unit (IFU) observations, random sampling variation can be exploited to extract information beyond that carried by the integrated light. We develop a principal component analysis (PCA) approach, applied to Poisson-sampled stellar population models, to probe the most luminous cool giant stars in old galaxies. Across all wavelengths (0.45--2.4\,$\mu$m), and over all ages and metallicities explored, Poisson-sampling variation are dominated by a single PCA component. This leading component typically describes the most massive and coolest giant stars in the population. In the infrared, it resembles the integrated-light spectrum since the latter is already dominated by such stars; even so, all features from warmer stars are greatly suppressed. In the optical, by contrast, the method instead reveals cool M-giant contributions which are subdominant in the integrated light. A second PCA component is present in some bands, which is related to the variation in spectrum along the giant branch. Our model predictions are largely insensitive to age or the initial mass function, but show some dependence on metallicity, reflecting changes in the temperature and shape of the giant branch. The method can be applied to IFU observations in a purely data-driven way; comparison to our predictions will provide a new approach to testing some of the uncertain ingredients in stellar population models for early-type galaxies.

papers.title: Breaking the background and linear degeneracies: Using nonlinear clustering to discriminate between dark energy models
papers.abstract: We show that the traditional approach of parameterizing the background and linear-perturbation evolutions, through the equation-of-state parameter $w(a)$ and a time-dependent sound speed squared $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, does not fully specify the cosmological behavior of dark energy theories. Using a new, fully nonlinear fluid framework, we perform spherical-collapse simulations of two clustering dark energy models with identical $w(a)$ and $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, finding that their central dark-energy densities differ by up to 50\% for cluster-sized dark matter halos. We identify the departure of the local sound speed from $\bar{c}_s$ as the main driver of these differences. In contrast, all other theory-specific quantities in the fluid equations can be described by their background values to a very good approximation. The results demonstrate that nonlinear structure formation encodes critical additional information about the underlying dark energy theory, opening an avenue for discriminating between models using observables on small scales.

authors.name: Yunhao Gao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Splitting the action: A fully nonlinear fluid method for clustering dark energy
papers.abstract: While the background evolution of dark energy is relatively straightforward to model, its perturbations, especially on nonlinear scales, generally require significantly more sophisticated treatment. Existing simulation methods for clustering dark energy --- a large class of interesting theories which are until now not well studied --- usually rely on grid-based solvers and perturbatively derived equations, whose validity in the nonlinear regime remains unknown. In this paper, we introduce a novel fluid method based on splitting the dark energy action into two parts: a kinetic part and a potential part. The resulting fluid equations are fully nonlinear and not reliant on simplifying approximations, making them suitable to describe the small-scale evolution of clustering dark energy theories, such as $k$-essence models with small sound speeds. We demonstrate the numerical implementation of this framework through spherical-collapse simulations of two representative $k$-essence models, evolving dark matter and dark energy simultaneously. The simulations are able to follow the development of dark-energy density perturbations throughout halo collapse, to $\mathcal{O}(\textrm{1}-10)$. By investigating their dependence on the dark-energy sound speed and dark-matter halo mass, we illustrate how dark-energy clustering responds to variations in the competing effects of pressure support and gravitational pull. These results demonstrate the applicability of this new framework to study nonlinear dark-energy clustering across a range of physical conditions, providing the foundation for its future extension to fully three-dimensional cosmological simulations through particle-based algorithms such as smooth particle hydrodynamics (SPH).

authors.name: Yunhao Gao
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $\deg g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope. We show that the Kozlov simplex $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$ is a lecture hall simplex and that every point of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ has a unique chained decomposition into points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$. Hence the lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ are exactly the sums of shifted lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$, the polytope has the integer decomposition property, every lattice point is a Hilbert function when $n\le 3$, and lattice-point counts and Ehrhart polynomials are products of transfer matrices of the kind used in Part II. We determine the codegree of every Kozlov polytope and show that none is Gorenstein for $n\ge 3$. Finally we compare discrete and continuous invariants: the number of Hilbert functions against the volume and the lattice-point count, where we prove Kupreyeva's observed limit for the fraction of lattice points that are $f$-vectors and extend it to every rank. We also compare the centroid and second moments of the Hilbert functions with those of the polytope.

papers.title: Disentangling star formation rate indicators in H-ATLAS galaxies: UV, FIR and radio diagnostics from energy-balance SED fitting
papers.abstract: We compare three star formation rate (SFR) tracers --- far-ultraviolet (FUV), far-infrared (FIR) and 1.4\,GHz radio emission --- for \Nsamp\ galaxies (median redshift 0.12) from the Herschel Astrophysical Terahertz Large Area Survey Data Release 1 catalogue, excluding quasars, AGN-dominated galaxies and unreliable redshifts. Energy-balance spectral energy distribution fitting with \textsc{cigale} gives their attenuations, dust luminosities and SFRs self-consistently. The FUV attenuation correlates strongly with FIR luminosity (Spearman $\rho=0.84$), largely through their common dependence on redshift (partial $\rho=0.57$ at fixed $z$), and more tightly with the infrared excess ($\rho=0.96$). The uncorrected UV SFR is over ten times below the FIR SFR for 67 per cent of the galaxies, and for all with $A_{\rm FUV}>4$\,mag. For 714 galaxies the FIRST 1.4\,GHz flux density is at the noise level and is treated as an upper limit; as detections, these values push the fits to unrealistically low dust temperatures. The 84 radio detections have a median $q_{\rm IR}$ of 2.51, close to the assumed 2.58. SFRs averaged over 10 and 100\,Myr differ by under 2 per cent, because the model star formation histories are smooth. Without access to high-performance computing, all galaxies were fitted at $z=0$, with distance-dependent quantities rescaled. This lowers dust temperatures by a factor of about $(1+z)$ and biases stellar masses and, at $z>0.2$, attenuations, but changes dust luminosities and SFRs by only a few hundredths of a dex. These fits, with 16.3 million models per galaxy, show what UV-to-radio SED modelling can deliver on modest hardware.

papers.title: Inference in High-Dimensional Linear Mediation Models
papers.abstract: Mediation analysis plays an important role in psychology, epidemiology, and genomics. Al- though high-dimensional mediation has been studied extensively, existing inferential methods typically rely on sparsity assumptions that may be difficult to justify when many individually weak mediators collectively produce a substantial effect. We study inference for both the over- all indirect effect and the effect transmitted through an individual mediator in a proportional high-dimensional regime, where the number of mediators and the sample size grow at compa- rable rates, without imposing sparsity on the mediator effects. Standard debiasing procedures for high-dimensional inference commonly rely on design-covariance information or additional structural assumptions on precision-matrix directions. In mediation models, however, the full outcome-design covariance depends on unknown mediator-model coefficients, creating an addi- tional challenge when such information or structure is unavailable. To address this challenge, we introduce an approximate debiasing procedure based on partial ridge regression and show that the resulting estimator is asymptotically bias-corrected and Gaussian. We also develop a cross-fitted estimator with a smaller asymptotic variance than its sample-split counterpart. In addition, we construct consistent estimators of the limiting variances of both the sample-split and cross-fitted estimators. Together, these results provide feasible inferential procedures for global and pathwise mediation effects.

authors.name: Rajarshi Mukherjee
authors.institution: Aintree University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

papers.title: Twindex: Index Cache Offloading with Coarse-to-Fine Selection for Long-Context Sparse-Attention Serving
papers.abstract: In long-context decoding, GPU memory (HBM) caps how many requests a GPU decodes at once. Sparse-attention models such as Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.2 add an indexer: at every step it scores all past index entries with its own indexer cache, and attention reads the main KV of only the top-k entries. We find that once serving systems move the main KV to host memory, the indexer cache becomes the HBM bottleneck, at 63% of per-request HBM on Qwen and 75% on V4.1 at 1M tokens. Therefore, we introduce Twindex, which keeps only a compact copy of the indexer cache in HBM and the full indexer cache in host memory. At each step, the copy selects a larger candidate set, and the model's own indexer picks the top-k from the original rows of the candidates in host memory. The copy combines the shared component with the compressed residuals, both learned once offline. Twindex changes no model weights and runs inside CUDA graphs. At 1M tokens on modern GPUs, Twindex fits $1.78\times$, $1.62\times$ and $3.03\times$ as many requests as KV offloading alone on Qwen, V4.1 and GLM-5.2, and reaches $1.44\times$, $1.25\times$ and $2.54\times$ decode throughput when host memory does not limit the batch. Every request keeps its own index, and Qwen and GLM requests share prefix main KV in host memory. In our evaluations, mean benchmark scores are at most 3.1% below the baseline's.

authors.name: Hao Mark Chen
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology

papers.title: SteerTrace: Tracing How Target Attacks Steer World Action Models
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict future videos and actions with one backbone, and their imagined future is often seen as a safety signal. We introduce SteerTrace, a targeted universal attack on WAMs that also traces its effect inside the model. One $\ell_\infty$-bounded (4/255) perturbation per model, shared across frames, tasks, and camera views, pushes the executed action toward an attacker-chosen target. On eight WAMs from four families (FastWAM, Faster-WAM, OpenWAM and LingBot-VA) on LIBERO and RoboTwin, it drives task success close to zero and moves the attacked action toward the target. Same-budget noise and BadWAM produce little action shift in the target direction. We use the signed targeted effect to measure how much of the effect each intervention removes or reproduces. Under the standard attack, restoring future tokens removes 61-94% of the targeted effect in the five models whose action experts attend to them. When the attack is constrained to keep the predicted future close to the clean prediction, the targeted effect can become more dependent on current-frame tokens. In three of these five models, restoring current-frame tokens removes 87-99% of the effect, compared with 9-15% for future tokens. In six models, restoring just 0.36% of the FFN neurons in layers 10-29 of the video expert removes 72-96% of the targeted effect. Residual directions 2-16 hold only 11-18% of the shift energy, yet removing them cancels most of the targeted effect.

authors.name: Tianshi Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Jingjing Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Lei Zhu
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.

authors.name: Chuhan Wang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: High-Dimensional Structured Light Tomography with a Tilted Lens
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate high-dimensional spatial mode tomography using intensity measurements and the astigmatic transformation implemented with a tilted lens. We improve the method previously published in Ref. [1] to perform the spatial tomography not restricted to a fixed order, which allowed us to achieve good fidelity for a mode space dimension as high as $D=66\,$. Since the literature is not unanimous, we also present a comprehensive revision of light propagation through a tilted lens for an accurate description of the transformation used for tomography. We derive its effective focal lengths, and analyze its role as an astigmatic mode converter. Moreover, we establish its explicit domain of validity within the Hermite-Gaussian basis.

authors.name: Marcos G. de Oliveira
authors.institution: University of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro

papers.title: Data-driven Linearization of Operational Dynamics of Soft Open Points in Power Distribution Networks
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel data-driven linearization of operational power losses in a Soft Open Point (SOP). The proposed learning-based representation, combined with the standard segmentation of the quadratic device capacity inequalities, linearizes the operational dynamics of SOPs in unbalanced power distribution network applications without a significant drop in power loss estimation accuracy. The technique was tested in three applications using a three-phase extension of the IEEE 33-bus network. The case studies include a sizing application for a multi-terminal phase-changing soft open point (PCSOP), an operational optimization application for an active distribution network featuring a PCSOP, and a system simulation engine built for a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) application that trains an agent to optimally dispatch a PCSOP in an unbalanced distribution network. The results of the three case studies were validated against the standard nonlinear AC load-flow representations and point to the efficacy of the proposed solution.

papers.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection in medical images is a complex task, requiring the development of a robust model using only healthy patient data. Without access to labeled data, modern approaches typically employ self-supervised learning to obtain a model of normality. Since world models promise to build strong internal representations of their environment, we consider them as suitable candidates for the medical anomaly detection environment, namely medical investigations of healthy patients. To this end, we propose MADJEPA, a medical anomaly detector based on an enhanced multi-stage joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA). We design a multi-stage training pipeline to produce a robust detector: (1) image-based JEPA (I-JEPA) training aims to learn a strong representation of normal training data; (2) target encoder distillation aims to modulate over-generalization of I-JEPA representations to abnormal data; (3) pseudo-anomaly classification aims to calibrate anomaly predictions by learning a tight boundary around the normal data manifold. To demonstrate our design, we carry out comprehensive experiments on six datasets covering various medical image domains (e.g.~MRI, OCT, X-ray, histopathology), comparing our MADJEPA with numerous state-of-the-art methods. The results show that our carefully designed world model, MADJEPA, attains competitive results, ranking first on three datasets. Our ablation studies further confirm the utility of each training stage, indicating that I-JEPA alone is not sufficient to obtain competitive results in medical anomaly detection. We publicly release our code at https://github.com/Sabina085/madjepa.

authors.name: Andreea Iuliana Ionescu
authors.institution: Carol Davila University of Medicine and Pharmacy

papers.title: Characterizing and Detecting Unfaithful Work Reports by Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents increasingly carry out long-horizon development tasks, autonomously planning and executing multi-step actions that span files, tools, and sessions. Because developers rarely follow each action, and agents resuming the work depend on records of what was done, the agent's work report often becomes the primary account of what was changed and established. When the report contains false or unsupported claims, it gives recipients false assurance: incomplete work may be accepted without verification, incorrect assumptions about the current state can propagate to later steps and agents, and evaluators that credit stated success may reward the report rather than the work. Yet little is known about what unfaithful reporting looks like in real development work, or how developers and agents handle it once it surfaces. Starting from real developer--agent conversations in SWE-chat, we conduct a systematic mixed-methods analysis of self-admitted unfaithful reports. We identify eleven subtypes in four categories: misreported observations, misattributed evidence, overstated task success, and faulty technical explanations, with overstated task success the most common. Handling these problems involves on average 4.3 further user turns and 12.71 minutes of recorded response and execution time, and users express dissatisfaction more often. Among 435 work reports that we separately sample and annotate, \NaturalPositiveShare{}\% contain at least one unfaithful claim. We also develop FaithDetector, a detector for unfaithful reporting informed by the observed patterns. On naturally sampled reports, FaithDetector attains \NaturalDetectorMacro{}\% macro-F1, about 13 percentage points above the baseline. Together, our findings and FaithDetector provide empirical evidence and an automated method for checking reporting faithfulness, informing agent evaluation and training feedback.

papers.title: Plane curves attaining the Dimca-Sernesi bound and Jacobian syzygies of pencil-type curves
papers.abstract:
For a reduced plane curve $C:f=0$ of degree $d$ with only weighted homogeneous singularities, Dimca and Sernesi proved that the minimal degree of a Jacobian relation satisfies $\mathrm{mdr}(f)\geq \alpha_C\, d-2$, where $\alpha_C$ is the minimal Arnold exponent of the singularities of $C$. We call $C$ DS-extremal (Dimca-Sernesi extremal) when equality holds. We show that curves of pencil type $f=\Phi(g,h)$, in particular curves of $(p,q)$-torus type $g^p+h^q$, are DS-extremal, the minimal syzygy being $
abla g	imes
abla h$. Under a natural transversality assumption we determine the minimal free resolution of the Milnor algebra of such a curve: it depends only on $d$, $\mathrm{deg}\, g$ and $\mathrm{deg}\, h$, and the module of Jacobian syzygies is generated by $
abla g	imes 
abla h$ and the three Koszul syzygies. For irreducible sextics with six cusps we prove that $3\le \mathrm{mdr}(f)\le 4$, that $\mathrm{mdr}(f)=3$ for curves of torus type, and that $\mathrm{mdr}(f)=4$ for the general curve in the component of non-torus sextics containing Oka's curve. Hence Zariski's classical pair is a Ziegler pair detected by $\mathrm{mdr}$, and the reason is the extremality of the torus member. We conjecture that every DS-extremal curve is of pencil type and support this by the nodal case and by computations.

authors.name: Gabriel Sticlaru
authors.institution: IMAR - Institutul de Matematică „Simion Stoilow” al Academiei Române

papers.title: Symmetry of pole order spectra and freeness of plane curves
papers.abstract: Let $C:f=0$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $d$ having only weighted homogeneous singularities, and let $\mathrm{Sp}_P^0(f)$ be the pole order spectrum of the top cohomology of its Milnor fiber. Writing $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)=\sum_q m_q\,t^{q/d}$, we show that $m_q-m_{2d-q}=n(f)_{q-3}-n(f)_{q+d-3}$ for every integer $q$, where $n(f)_k$ is the Hilbert function of the Jacobian module $N(f)$. Consequently, $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)$ is symmetric with respect to $\alpha\mapsto 2-\alpha$ if and only if $C$ is free. For a free curve with exponents $(d_1,d_2)$ we give a closed formula: $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)-t^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}^1_P(f)$ depends only on $(d,d_1)$. This explains the symmetry of pole order spectra of reflection line arrangements, an open problem raised in Dimca's monograph on hyperplane arrangements.

authors.name: Gabriel Sticlaru
authors.institution: IMAR - Institutul de Matematică „Simion Stoilow” al Academiei Române

papers.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly reuse executable capabilities through skills, but a skill that works on one OS may fail on another because OS assumptions are spread across guide text, scripts, metadata, install contracts, and local entrypoints. Diagnosing such failures by running every skill on every OS is expensive: many executions spend model tokens, runner time, and review effort before revealing whether the failure is truly OS-related. We present SkillBridge, a contract-based workflow with three stages: static analysis, dynamic validation, and repair. SkillBridge first screens 3,270 skill-target-OS cases, covering 1,090 skills across Linux, macOS, and Windows, to find OS-sensitive contract evidence. It then runs dynamic tasks and root-cause review on selected cases to confirm whether a failure is caused by an OS assumption, and repairs the contract field that caused the failure, such as guide text, package scripts, dependencies, or platform declarations. Repair raises the reviewer-judged target-task pass rate from 30.6% to 38.4%, a gain of 7.8 percentage points. A retrospective Linux/macOS budget analysis further shows the efficiency effect: SkillBridge reaches 38 confirmed OS issues with 185 dynamic validations, where uniform random selection would require about 865 validations in expectation.

papers.title: Separating Interpretability and Reconstruction in Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. However, a single sparse representation in traditional SAEs is responsible for both reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, which are not guaranteed to align. To separate these objectives, we propose DualSAE, a modular framework that augments standard SAEs with a plug-in Residual Branch. A standard SAE serves as the Sparse Branch, learning a sparse code that contains the dominant semantics of the input. The added Residual Branch models the non-semantic information omitted by the Sparse Branch. We ensure that the contributions of the two branches towards the overall reconstruction have minimal overlap through a decorrelation loss. We also adopt a two-stage training strategy that first stabilizes sparse representation learning before coupling with the Residual Branch. Across diverse encoder-SAE configurations on two vision datasets and two language corpora, DualSAE achieves mean relative improvements of approximately 29% in reconstruction fidelity and 34% in interpretability (measured by monosemanticity score). Moreover, with more interpretable representations, DualSAE yields consistent performance gains in the downstream applications of topic modeling, hypothesis generation, and LLM steering. Qualitative analysis further suggests that the Sparse Branch indeed preserves dominant semantic content, whereas the Residual Branch captures non-semantic information to improve reconstruction fidelity.

papers.title: Coordinated Use of Large Language Models in Academic Research
papers.abstract: This study proposes a methodological framework for the coordinated use of multiple large language models in academic research. Its central argument is that involving more models does not in itself guarantee more reliable results; what matters is how cognitive and verification operations are organised. The framework is based on seven principles (procedural independence, functional allocation, the diagnostic value of divergence, the diagnostic value of convergence, external verification, proportionality of checking, and human epistemic responsibility) and sets out a non-linear multi-LLM protocol in which independently obtained results are compared, critically examined and, where necessary, verified against external sources. The approach is illustrated through real-world cases drawn from research practice. The study concludes that moving from a single language model to a coordinated multi-LLM process represents a change in the organisation of research, in which the researcher makes the final decisions and bears scholarly responsibility.

authors.name: Vladislav Marinov
authors.institution: St. Cyril and St. Methodius University of Veliko Tarnovo

papers.title: Self-similar rupture of a thin viscous filament in a Hele-Shaw cell
papers.abstract:
In this report, we shall revisit the rupture problem for thin filament in a Hele-Shaw cell. For a slightly perturbed interface with periodic boundary conditions, all modes of perturbation decay in such a way that the interface levels off and becomes flatter over time. On the other hand, if the two ends of the filament are pinned in place and fluid is withdrawn from each end with a sufficiently high outward flux, then the loss of fluid causes the filament to thin and ultimately to rupture at a finite time. This type of filament rupture has been studied at length, most notably in the 1990s. We illustrate typical solution behaviours, including infinite-time levelling and those that appear to approach symmetric and asymmetric rupture in finite time. For the symmetric case, we demonstrate how rupture is described by a similarity solution of the second kind. We briefly frame our results in a broader perspective by considering similarity solutions for the thin film equation with an exponent $m$, which reduces to the Hele-Shaw case for $m=1$, and comparing with recent results in the literature.
  This report presents the results of a project undertaken by the first author at the MATRIX Workshop \textit{Slow Viscous Flows with Interfaces}, 7--18 July 2025, under the supervision of the other authors.

papers.title: RL Can Only Reinforce What It Sees Succeed
papers.abstract: When a familiar rule stops working, an agent has to weigh what pre-training taught it against what it now observes. We ask how outcome-reward reinforcement learning (RL) changes this balance, in a puzzle world where both sides are known: small language models trained from scratch on games played by a Bayesian player, so that the prior and the right answer are exact. Base models hedge as their corpus did, and RL turns that hedging into decisions, in whichever direction the reward favours. But RL can only reinforce what it sees succeed. When the right action is rare, each run either learns it everywhere or not at all, and which runs take off is predicted before training by one count: the expected number of groups of attempts in which the action wins. About 35 such groups give even odds. The count holds for new and repeated problems and for groups of 4 to 256 attempts, and across learning rates, optimizers, GRPO variants and model sizes from 1.3M to 85M parameters, which move the threshold but not what is counted.

papers.title: On Riemannian $r$-th order recurrent spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with irreducible local holonomy which is $r$-th order recurrent, $\nabla^r R=t^{(r)}\otimes R$, is locally symmetric, for every $r\ge1$. Without any assumption on the holonomy, we show that such a manifold is either locally symmetric or, locally, a flat extension $\Sigma^2\times\mathbb R^{n-2}$ of a surface: the only possible exceptions to local symmetry are essentially two-dimensional.

papers.title: When Is an OIRI-Algebra a Banach Lattice? Structure Theorems and Counterexamples
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the exact conditions under which a relatively uniformly complete semiprime $f$-algebra whose order ideals are ring ideals (an OIRI-algebra) admits a norm turning it into a Banach lattice or an AM-space. While recent literature claimed that this equivalence holds automatically in the presence of a weak order unit, we construct a concrete counterexample within a relatively uniformly complete vector lattice showing that this assertion fails in general. By analyzing the canonical embedding $\psi:A\rightarrow Orth(A)$, we prove that the equivalence between being an OIRI-algebra, admitting an AM-space or Banach lattice norm and satisfying $Orth(A)=$ $Stab(A)$ $=Z(A$) holds under the assumption that $\psi\left( A\right) $ is relatively uniformly closed in $Orth(A)$ (alongside a characterization via finite elements in the unitization $A^{\sharp}$). We also deduce immediate consequences for unital $f$-algebras and generalize our main theorem to non-semiprime $f$-algebras via the quotient modulo the nilpotent radical $N(A)$.

papers.title: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

papers.title: GridAnchor: Specialized Multi-Agent AI for Safeguarding Autonomous Energy Systems Against Cyber-Physical Hallucinations
papers.abstract: Autonomous energy systems increasingly chain specialized learned agents, such as a forecaster, a state estimator and a dispatcher that may be a language model. These agents can emit confident outputs that contradict physics, and downstream agents may act on them. We define such cyber-physical hallucinations and their cascades, organize them in eight types, and build CPH-Bench, a generator of labeled episodes on SimBench feeders. We propose GridAnchor, a verification layer whose Physics-Residual Graph Transformer scores every claim from residuals between the claims, the measurements and a linearized grid model. Mondrian conformal p-values with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure turn the scores into decisions, a root head attributes cascades, and a quadratic program repairs unsafe actions with a voltage margin calibrated at repaired steps. On a simulated rural medium-voltage feeder, GridAnchor reaches a message-level area under the precision-recall curve of 0.846, against 0.837 for the strongest of six baselines, a difference within the confidence interval. It leads on estimates and actions, whereas a self-consistency check that knows the label tolerances reaches 0.874 by leading on forecasts. The false-alarm rate stays within 0.17 percentage points of the nominal level on steps without injected hallucinations. In closed loop, GridAnchor leaves no bus outside the voltage band on the test days, against 0.0700% of the bus-steps without protection, and simpler detectors with the same mitigation come close. Stale but coherent messages and single-bus forecast errors remain mostly undetected.

authors.name: Hasan Masrur
authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models have greatly improved input understanding in universal multimodal embedding models. However, this understanding does not ensure that their embeddings preserve the evidence needed to distinguish relevant items from confusable alternatives. To preserve essential discriminative evidence in embeddings, this paper proposes DiLE, a discrimination-aware latent-space learning framework that combines task guidance with on-policy retrieval feedback. Specifically, a few learnable queries are used to encode task-relevant information in a compact latent space. Reasoning instructions and auxiliary answer-generation supervision shape these representations to support both task understanding and retrieval discrimination. To address task-specific discriminative needs, we design shared-private expert adaptation that integrates cross-task knowledge sharing with task-specific representation learning. Building on this, the on-policy hard-negative distillation is introduced: the student retrieves confusable candidates, and a reverse KL divergence objective aligns its embedding-based similarity distribution with the teacher's fine-grained relevance distribution over these candidates. Candidates are periodically refreshed using updated student snapshots, tying teacher supervision to the student's evolving retrieval behavior and confusions. Across four model configurations that span two backbone generations, DiLE achieves state-of-the-art performance on MMEB-v2, UVRB, and MRMR, demonstrating its effectiveness across modalities and tasks.
