papers.title: Blind tests of a simple-body model of submarine target strength on open benchmarks
papers.abstract: Finite-element and boundary-element models of a submarine's sonar echo need a mesh and a solver, and their cost grows quickly with frequency. SSR-Sim takes an analytical route. The hull is cut into a few simple bodies, the echo of each is a closed-form result of geometrical acoustics or of the Kirchhoff approximation, the surface enters through a plane-wave reflection coefficient, and the echoes add in energy. This paper describes the method, including the reduction of a hull and its sail to simple bodies, and tests it on three open cases. (1) The reflection coefficient of a 50 mm rubber tile on steel plating, computed with finite elements by Yang et al., is reproduced to 0.02 rms or better at incidence angles from 0{\deg} to 75{\deg} once the layer is allowed to refract. (2) For the rigid full-scale BeTSSi submarine at 1 kHz, a prediction fixed before the reference was opened agrees with the boundary-element results of Ven{\aa}s and Kvamsdal to within 0.7 dB in every aspect sector from the bow to 150{\deg}; in the stern sector it is 5 dB high. (3) For a 1:15 BeTSSi model with 10 mm tiles measured in a lake, a second blind prediction is within -3.1, +1.4 and -0.5 dB of the measured level over aspects 0-120{\deg} at 5, 15 and 20 kHz, against -3.1, +3.1 and +3.5 dB for the Kirchhoff-finite-element computation published with the measurement. At 10 kHz, on a resonance of the tile, the prediction is 6.9 dB low, and in the bow sector it is 7 dB or more low at every frequency. The tests cover the specular component and the coating model only. The failures show what such a model lacks: edge diffraction and the returns that set the off-beam floor of a real model.

papers.title: Quantum many-body scars and zero modes in the spin-1 Kitaev chain
papers.abstract: We study the spin-1 Kitaev chain and, by analyzing its Hilbert-space connectivity in the Cartesian basis, show that it hosts an exponentially large number of exact zero-energy modes protected by chiral symmetry. For even-length periodic chains, their count is lower-bounded by the Jacobsthal number $(2^{L+1}+1)/3$, where $L$ is the chain length. We then construct an exponentially large number ($2^{L/2}$) of zero modes with an analytic expression that have a maximally mixed density matrix for a contiguous bipartition using the operator-state mapping. We further identify an embedded tight-binding structure governing defect dynamics that supports PXP-like quantum many-body scars (QMBS) in multiple sectors previously not reported. The associated forward-scattering approximation (FSA) Hamiltonian takes a universal form across the scarred sectors studied. A simple physical picture of defects propagating between walls provides an intuitive description of these dynamics and a structural guide to identifying sectors with fidelity revivals, while its limitations point to additional scarring mechanisms.

authors.name: Jay Pandey
authors.institution: Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani

papers.title: Mateability of Fuchsian lattices with polynomials, and failure of algebraicity
papers.abstract:
We prove that all Fuchsian lattices, with the possible exceptions of those associated with compact orbifolds of type (0,3) and (1,1), can be mated with complex polynomials, providing the first examples of such combinations beyond genus-zero orbifolds. We also present the first construction of matings between simply degenerate Kleinian groups and polynomial maps. These matings are realized as holomorphic, though not necessarily algebraic, correspondences, demonstrating that Fatou's vision of unifying Kleinian group actions and polynomial dynamics can be fulfilled in the wider setting of transcendental correspondences.
  We achieve this by generalizing the orbit equivalence mating framework introduced in our earlier work. Specifically, we use pinching and acceleration techniques to construct a new class of piecewise M\"obius covering maps of the circle that are orbit equivalent to Fuchsian groups. By mating these circle coverings with polynomials, we construct degenerate polynomial-like maps whose analytic continuations yield the desired correspondences. The quality of this orbit equivalence plays a crucial role in the mating description, as well as in governing whether the resulting correspondences are algebraic.

papers.title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation
papers.abstract: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincar\'e bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact bulk realization. Its axial conductance remains $\kappa V/L^2$, while exactly one positive insulated rate vanishes and the next approaches a positive limit set by axial, chamber and neck diffusion. The slow rate is asymptotically the transverse neck conductance times the sum of inverse chamber capacities. Spectral projection estimates translate this separation into a preparation- and readout-dependent observation window. The result is metastable retention of a temperature contrast under insulated conditions, not a second equilibrium state. It identifies when geometrical control of internal equilibration can be separated from macroscopic heat transport.

papers.title: Multi-View Relighting with Mergeable Radiance Fields
papers.abstract: We propose MergeableRF, a method for radiance field relighting through model parameter merging. Given multi-view images of a scene under known basis lights, our goal is to relight the scene by directly combining the parameters of radiance fields trained under these lights. This is motivated by the linearity of light transport: the image under a mixture of lights is the same weighted combination of the images under each light. However, combining the parameters of independently trained radiance fields does not produce the corresponding combination of images. To address this, we represent a scene with shared geometry and a separate appearance network for each basis light. We start these networks from the same initialization and introduce merge-aware training, which teaches their parameter combinations to reproduce the corresponding combinations of images. Given a target HDR environment map, we compute its basis-light coefficients and use them to merge the appearance networks into a single relit model. Our method supports both Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), without material estimation, additional relighting networks, or target-specific optimization. Unlike image-space blending, it requires only one rendering pass per viewpoint. Experiments on synthetic Neural Gaffer objects and real OLATverse captures demonstrate relighting quality competitive with methods trained on the same multi-light observations.

papers.title: Single-Crystal Growth, Structure, and Physical Properties of Yb2MoO6
papers.abstract: Rare-earth molybdates are functional oxides of considerable interest because their structural and chemical flexibility enables diverse magnetic, electronic, and optical behavior. Here, millimeter-sized single crystals of $Yb_2MoO_6$ are synthesized, their crystal structure determined and physical properties investigated. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of $Yb_2MoO_6$ and yielded lattice parameters of $a = 16.228(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, $b = 10.901(3)$ $\mathring{A}$, and $c = 5.286(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, in good agreement with previously reported neutron powder diffraction data. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy show a Yb:Mo ratio close to the expected 2:1 stoichiometry. Optical measurements based on diffuse-reflectance spectra and Tauc analysis yield an estimated optical gap of $\sim 3.28$ eV under the direct-allowed transition assumption. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal Curie-Weiss-like paramagnetic behavior, with an effective magnetic moment of $\mu_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 4.2\mu_B$ per Yb and an apparent Weiss temperature of $\theta \approx -65.7$ K, consistent with possible antiferromagnetic interactions or correlations, with no clear magnetic-ordering transition observed down to 10 K. These results establish the growth of $Yb_2MoO_6$ single crystals and provide initial insight into their structural, optical, and magnetic properties.

authors.institution: Missouri University of Science and Technology

authors.institution: Missouri University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yew San Hor
authors.institution: Missouri University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Solving the puzzle of tropical cyclone track bifurcation
papers.abstract: Tropical cyclones whose predicted tracks bifurcate are among the most dreaded storms in disaster planning. Understanding when and why these bifurcations occur has been a long-standing puzzle in track forecasting. We address this issue by introducing the concept of "fate boundaries" hidden in the steering flow. Storms located on opposite sides of these boundaries follow dramatically different tracks. By analyzing 1,179 Northern Hemisphere storms over 2011-2025, we identified 61 with a strong signature of bifurcation. In every instance, fate boundaries explained why the ensemble tracks split. Additionally, they can reveal bifurcations days before they appear in any operational ensemble. Because fate boundaries often separate devastating from nearby benign tracks, they mark when and where minimal interventions could, in principle, redirect a storm.

authors.name: Jizhou Li
authors.institution: City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen Research Institute

papers.title: Determining quantum phases of eight-fold quasicrystal optical lattices with angular structure factor
papers.abstract: Quasicrystals have unique geometrical properties and are potential candidates to explore exotic states of matter. In this work, we explore the properties and the rotational symmetries of the quantum phases of ultracold atoms in the Ammann-Beenker quasicrystal optical lattice. We model the system with the quasicrystalline extended Bose-Hubbard model (qeBHM) and use mean field methods to identify the groundstate of qeBHM in the soft-core regime. To examine the diagonal long-range order of the groundstate quantum phases we develop a theoretical method to calculate the structure factor of the state. Our method clearly distinguishes various density wave (DW) and supersolid (SS) phases of the quasicrystal.

papers.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

authors.name: Ritwik Chakraborty
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur

papers.title: SN 2017gkk: A moderately luminous and fast evolving Type IIb supernova
papers.abstract: We present optical imaging (\textit{BVRI} bands) and low-resolution optical spectroscopic follow-up of Type IIb supernova SN~2017gkk that occurred in NGC~2748. These observations consist of 31 and 17 epochs of photometry and spectroscopy, spanning $\sim$\,218 days since the $V$-band peak. The light curve analysis infers that the SN reached maximum in $\sim$\,13~days after the explosion with an absolute magnitude of $M_\mathrm{V}$\,=\,--17.01\,$\pm$\,0.07 mag. The peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of SN~2017gkk is $L_{\rm bol}=(8.37\pm0.19)\times10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Between 25 and 80 days (after maximum), SN~2017gkk displays a fast decline rate of $2.35\pm0.06~\mathrm{mag\times(100d)^{-1}}$ in $V$-band. The photospheric phase spectra are dominated by an H$\alpha$ P~Cygni profile (up to $\sim$\,69~days), which gradually faded and disappeared $\sim$\,90 days after the $V$-band maximum. The \ion{He}{1} lines subsequently emerged after $\sim$\,20 days and became dominant during the transition phase. The nebular phase spectra of SN~2017gkk indicate a relatively low-mass progenitor with $M_{\mathrm{preSN}}\gtrsim3\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}}\approx\,12\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, and it is likely in a binary system. The analytical modeling of the light curve infers a low ejecta mass of $M_{\mathrm{ej}}=1.38^{+0.48}_{-0.31}\, M_\odot$ with relatively lower explosion energy $E_\mathrm{KE}=0.69_{-0.17}^{+0.25}\times10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and a synthesized $^{56}$Ni mass of $M_{\mathrm{Ni}}=0.076_{-0.024}^{+0.032}\, M_\odot$.

authors.institution: Academy of Scientific and Innovative Research

papers.title: Preservation of big diagonal for automorphisms of Hilbert schemes
papers.abstract: If $X$ is a smooth projective surface that is not K3 or abelian surface, we show that any automorphism of the Hilbert scheme of points $X^{[n]}$ preserves the big diagonal. This generalizes several previous works, and gives a complete description of automorphisms of $X^{[n]}$ when $X$ is not K3 or abelian surface. We also obtain a Torelli-type theorem: a smooth projective surface $X$ can be recovered from $X^{[n]}$ unless $X$ is a K3 surface. Further, for each integer $n\geq 2$, we construct automorphisms of $A^{[n]}$ not preserving the big diagonal for an abelian surface $A$.

papers.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
papers.abstract: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most challenging activity classes. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity generation in a pretrained encoder's representation space is achievable and practically useful for cross-subject HAR augmentation.

papers.title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination
papers.abstract: Hallucination research in low-resource languages fragments easily: each newly named failure mode prompts its own dataset, spending scarce annotators on incomparable resources. We argue for consolidation and test it at community scale. Alikbachan is a Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark stratified along three crossed axes: a human-validated cultural-distance band, six task types, and a five-family, 32-mode hallucination taxonomy. It comprises a harvested 2,516-item test set (Phase 1) and a quota-constructed, gold-labeled 5,000-item set (Phase 2). The stratification is diagnostic. Four zero-shot LLM judges vary by over 30 macro-F1 points across strata, and the item-level predictions of 99 Phase-1 and 32 Phase-2 competition systems reproduce the profile: discourse-level omission defeats judges and most teams alike, whereas only a minority over-flag negative controls. The judges' verdict probabilities rank items well (ROC-AUC 0.74-0.95) but are overconfident (ECE 0.04-0.29). An open competition on Alikbachan drew 222 teams and 3,566 submissions, and a single-prompt 32B judge reaches the 57th percentile. Of the 25 teams in both phases, 24 regress on Phase 2 (mean $-17.6$ points) while every zero-shot judge improves, and Phase-1 rank barely predicts Phase-2 rank (Spearman $\rho=0.35$), so a Phase-1 leaderboard alone would have crowned a different winner.
