papers.abstract: We design a polynomial-time algorithm for matroid cups with $O(1)$ discrepancy. Our matroid cups algorithm design consists of a sequence of reductions to simpler instances, culminating in $O(n)$ instances of matroid cups where the matroid has rank 1.

papers.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
papers.abstract: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

papers.title: Topological trapping of active tracers in branched ring polymer matrices
papers.abstract: Branched macromolecular architectures are ubiquitous in living systems and synthetic polymeric systems, create topologically complex media that strongly influence tracer dynamics beyond simple packing fraction-driven crowding effects. Motivated by biological systems such as amoebae, astrocytes, cytoskeletal assemblies, and cyclic bottlebrushes, we investigate active and passive tracer transport in polymeric environments of topologically distinct architectures. Here, using Langevin dynamics simulations, we focus on how polymer topology alters diffusion behavior in a branched-ring polymeric (BRP) environment. To isolate the role of intramolecular topology from monomer density, we specifically benchmark the BRP dynamics against an unlinked linear-ring polymer mixture (LRM). In general, we find that while passive tracers are largely unaffected by the polymer connectivity and bending rigidity, the self-propelled active tracers strongly distinguish between the two architectures. Increasing chain rigidity facilitates active diffusion in the unlinked LRM but strongly restricts mobility in the BRP matrix, driving a transition to pronounced long-time subdiffusion that becomes more prominent with propulsion strength. Different physical observables reveal that interconnected topological cages are formed in the stiff limit, leading to transient weak ergodicity breaking and leptokurtic displacement statistics. Further, the self-intermediate scattering function confirms that the short-range dynamics remain unaltered by the matrix connectivity, while relaxation at large spatial length scales is governed by the topological caging. Finally, varying the branch length and number, we identified an optimal branch architecture that maximizes active trapping. Our results establish that macromolecular connectivity and stiffness dominate the active transport even in the system of identical packing fraction.

papers.title: Geometry-induced orientational trapping dictates escape of active rods in corrugated channels
papers.abstract: The non-equilibrium transport of anisotropic active matter through geometrically confined environments is fundamentally governed by the interplay between self-propulsion and geometry-induced entropic barriers. Using overdamped Langevin dynamics, we reveal contrasting escape mechanisms of self-driven rods in narrow corrugated channels by comparing smoothly varying sinusoidal (SC) geometries to circular (CC) cavities with localized, uniform curvature. We observe a strictly non-monotonic dependence of the mean first escape time (MFET) with increasing Peclet number (Pe) in the CC channel, contrary to the monotonic dependence in the SC channel. This non-monotonicity emerges from a competition between activity-enhanced escape at low-to-intermediate propulsion and persistent, geometry-induced orientational trapping along the circular boundary at high propulsion, which inhibits reorientation toward the exit neck. This regime crossover is further corroborated by trajectory-to-trajectory escape fluctuations and bimodal radial probability distributions reflecting persistent wall-collision and wall-aligned sliding transport. The self part of van-Hove correlation function exhibits distinct anisotropic non-Gaussian displacements in the SC channel, in contrast to symmetric profiles with extended active-trapping plateaus in the CC cavities. These results establish local channel topology as a critical determinant of confined active transport, with direct implications for microfluidic sorting, biological navigation, and targeted drug delivery in corrugated environments.

papers.title: Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.

papers.title: A Practical Proprioceptive Data Collection Utility for the Unitree GO1
papers.abstract: The Unitree Go1 is a widely used platform for legged robotics research, yet collecting proprioceptive data from it is unnecessarily difficult: the Unitree SDK is sparsely documented, and ROS1 (Robot Operating System), the Go1's native middleware, is fully deprecated. We present an open-source graphical utility that enables researchers to reliably record proprioceptive data from the Go1, including joint states, IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) readings, foot force sensor data, and gyroscope measurements, without requiring ROS expertise. The tool provides a simple GUI (Graphical User Interface) for starting, stopping, and labeling recordings in real time. The contribution of this paper is the collection utility. We characterize the acquisition quality of 51 recordings collected with it, including the achieved sampling rate and repeated samples. As a secondary, deliberately modest check that the data is useful, we train a terrain classifier on it. The results are weak: a Temporal Convolutional Network reaches about 38% accuracy on held-out recordings across ten terrain classes (10% would be chance), and a window-level split that ignores recording boundaries inflates the same measurement to about 99%. We report this as a demonstration that the logged signals carry terrain information, not as a competitive classifier. The utility is designed to lower the barrier to collecting Go1 proprioceptive data without ROS.

papers.title: A fast iterative solver for lopsided Sylvester matrix equations
papers.abstract: A generalization of the factored alternating direction implicit algorithm is introduced that makes use of type $(p, q)$ Zolotarev rational functions to apply unequal numbers of left and right shifts. Convergence properties of the algorithm are discussed, as well as a method for computing shift parameters. Several applications are highlighted where the generalized method is useful, including in the solving of a collection of shifted linear systems, for discretizations that involve left and right operators that are not equally amenable to inversion, and for Sylvester matrix equations with differently-sized, differently-structured, or differently-conditioned coefficient matrices.

papers.title: Thinking in Streams: Proactive Spatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Recognizing when a requested spatial condition holds in streaming video can require maintaining and updating spatial knowledge across changing viewpoints. We study this capability through proactive spatial reasoning, where a model receives a query in advance and determines whether and when to respond as the stream unfolds. We introduce ProSpace-Bench, comprising nine tasks across object, camera, and scene reasoning, and ProSpace-Train for supervised training. To support spatial decisions, we propose ProSpace-VLM, which injects explicit geometric encodings estimated causally from incoming frames into intermediate VLM layers, using the existing KV cache as spatial memory and spatial token selection for efficient streaming. Experiments reveal a substantial gap between VLMs and humans, while ProSpace-VLM improves timely responses and correct abstention over fine-tuned baselines. Analyses examine how ProSpace-VLM represents previously observed spatial information across changing viewpoints.

papers.title: Onset of three dimensionality in transonic shock boundary layer interaction over a natural laminar flow airfoil
papers.abstract: The development of three-dimensionality in transonic shock--boundary-layer interactions (SBLI) can significantly influence the aerodynamic response of natural laminar flow (NLF) airfoils, yet the associated vorticity dynamics remain insufficiently understood. The present study investigates the short-time evolution of transonic SBLI over the SHM1 NLF airfoil using high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) simulations at three operating conditions reported by Fujino et al., Natural-laminar-flow airfoil development for a lightweight business jet, J. Aircraft 40, 609-615 (2003). The selected cases represent three distinct operating regimes: the initial development of a normal shock, drag divergence, and shock-induced separation. Comparisons with previously reported two-dimensional (2D) simulations establish the temporal interval over which the spanwise-averaged 3D flow remains close to the corresponding 2D evolution, while departures in surface pressure and skin-friction responses identify the subsequent development of 3D effects within the SBLI region. The temporal evolution of volume-integrated streamwise and wall-normal enstrophies further characterizes the development of the associated 3D vortical field. The compressible enstrophy transport equation (CETE) is subsequently employed to examine the mechanisms governing the evolution of the 3D vortical field. Viscous and compressibility-related terms dominate the normalized enstrophy budget during the early evolution, while vortex stretching remains a minor contribution in the normal-shock and drag-divergence regimes but becomes appreciable, albeit intermittently, with the development of shock-induced separation. Across the three operating regimes, the same principal enstrophy-transport mechanisms remain active, but their relative contributions to the normalized budget are redistributed with the SBLI topology.

papers.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair
papers.abstract: Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-using agents without exposing ground-truth hints or oracle feedback. We evaluate GRODE-RTL across 30 formally validated non-local faults using three LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) alongside a controlled six-configuration ablation study. GRODE-RTL improves pass@1 over source-level exploration by 16.7% on DeepSeek, by 26.7% on GLM-5.2, and by 20.0% on MiniMax-M3, with consistent gains on the hard-to-retrieve far-distance and indirect-anchor subsets of all three models. Our controls isolate structural relevance from generic context expansion, proving that selective dependency organization rather than full graph exposure is key to effective RTL repair.

authors.name: Yi Liu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

authors.name: Bin Sun
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$. In particular, $\dim H_c^{2g + k}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ grows at least exponentially with $g$ for every nonnegative $k \neq 1, 3$. We also give conjectural descriptions of the full mixed Hodge structures in genera four and five, and of mixed Tate subquotients of $H_c^{2g}(\mathcal{A}_g)$ associated with shuffle algebras and multiple zeta values in every genus.

papers.title: Molecular engineering for crack-free transfer of single-crystalline oxide membranes onto silicon
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous integration of single-crystalline complex oxides with silicon offers a route to incorporating their functionalities into next-generation microelectronics. Released from their growth substrates, freestanding oxide membranes enable this integration. However, cracks, wrinkles, and fragmentation during release and transfer limit membrane size and quality. Here, we present an interfacial energy-controlled release strategy that enables crack-free, single-crystalline freestanding oxide membranes with centimeter-scale lateral dimensions. Using SrTiO3 as a model system, time-resolved release studies identify water-induced blistering at the membrane-support interface during prolonged water exposure as the origin of membrane cracking. Lowering the molecular weight of the poly(propylene carbonate) support through polymer deconstruction increases its polarity and surface energy, suppresses interfacial blistering, and reduces organic residue after support removal. The resulting SrTiO3 membranes exhibit optical properties comparable to those of bulk single crystals. We extend this approach to the metallic ferromagnet La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, obtaining crack-free membranes on Si that preserve ferromagnetism and metallicity.

papers.title: A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension
papers.abstract: Let $G=(\mathbb{Z}/2^a\mathbb{Z})^d$, of order $N=2^{ad}$. Given point-query access to any complex signal $X$ with Fourier transform $\hat{X}$ over $G$, we provide a randomized algorithm that constructs a $k$-sparse estimate $\widetilde{X}$ via non-adaptive queries such that, with large probability, $\|\widetilde{X}-\hat{X}\|_2^2 \leq C \cdot \|H_k(\hat{X})-\hat{X}\|_2^2$, for an absolute constant $C>0$, where $H_k(\cdot)$ denotes the best $k$-sparse approximation. The constant $C$ can be improved to any desired $1+\varepsilon$ by either supplying a constant-factor estimate on the $k$-sparse tail norm or allowing an arbitrarily small additive error term $\delta \|\hat{X}\|_2^2$ on the right-hand side. With a supplied tail estimate, we can also satisfy an $\ell_\infty/\ell_2$ heavy hitters guarantee. For fixed $\delta$, the number of samples is $O((k/\varepsilon^2)(\log N)\log(k/\varepsilon))$, and the recovery algorithm requires a polynomial in $(k/\varepsilon)\log N$ exact operations. The algorithm naturally extends to $G=(\mathbb{Z}/b^a\mathbb{Z})^d$ for any fixed integer $b>1$.

authors.name: Jingyi Lyu
authors.institution: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences

papers.title: FPGA-GEN: Target-Aware RTL Generation via HLS
papers.abstract: Successful C/C++ compilation does not guarantee correct or efficient FPGA hardware after high-level synthesis (HLS). FPGA-GEN is an agentic HLS-C generation workflow that encodes specification, readiness, selection, repair, and admission rules in explicit task contracts and bounded tool-feedback loops for candidate-level decisions. On HLS-Eval, five shared-context outputs per task yield 407/425 (95.8%) public-testbench passes. In a cumulative conversion campaign, FPGA-GEN admits 104/107 (97.2%) HLS-LeVeri designs under held-out co-simulation, Vivado synthesis/fit, and same-RTL evidence. In focused TensorCore screening, selected candidate 3 reports 73.7% fewer CSynth cycles and 14.6% fewer LUTs than generated/composed C0, with 26.7% more DSPs, and passes development CoSim.

papers.title: Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies: Spatializing Latent Action Representations for Goal-Pose-Free Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: The success of manipulation policies is closely tied to the spatial relationship between the robot and the target object, as well as the task being performed, making the ability to adjust the robot's pose critical for successful execution. When the robot starts away from the task, such adjustments require coordinating navigation with local manipulation. Jointly training these capabilities incurs substantial computational and data costs, while navigating toward a predefined goal pose limits the flexibility needed to adapt to task-specific manipulation requirements. To address these challenges, we propose Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies (M4M), a framework that learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies. By leveraging the hidden representations of the policy's action-generating network as dense supervision, together with a limited number of manipulation execution outcomes, we learn a spatially conditioned embedding that captures task-dependent manipulation success across candidate robot poses. From the robot's current stereo observations, this representation estimates manipulation success at unvisited poses without rolling out the manipulation policy at each location. It is further integrated into navigation policy training, while a learned handoff policy decides when to transition from navigation to manipulation, enabling the robot to move and manipulate in a unified, task-aware manner. Across eight articulated-object tasks in unseen RoboCasa kitchens, M4M achieves 47.0% mean task success, compared with 26.5% for the strongest baseline and 19.2% for direct manipulation execution, and refrigerator-closing experiments show consistent improvements across four frozen manipulation policies.

authors.name: Zhong Cao
authors.institution: Changsha University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A generic construction of complex codebooks from functions over Abelian groups
papers.abstract: Codebooks with small inner-product correlation play a central role in direct spread code division multiple access communications, space-time coding, compressed sensing, and related areas because they improve system performance. This paper presents a generic construction and a modified construction of complex codebooks from functions on finite Abelian groups. By choosing perfect nonlinear functions, we systematically obtain several families of optimal or asymptotically optimal codebooks with respect to the Welch or Levenshtein bounds. These constructions recover a number of known optimal codebooks and also yield new codebooks with previously unreported parameters.

authors.name: Xiaoyan Jing
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
papers.abstract: One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) is enforcing temporal safety constraints, such as satisfying formal specifications. Existing methods often transform logic formulas into automata for state augmentation and reward shaping. However, this approach assumes that automaton construction is both feasible and tractable, which limits its applicability to small specifications and linear temporal logic (LTL). This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton. The predictor continuously estimates whether a partial trajectory will satisfy the formal specification in a later step, and its learned features are provided as auxiliary inputs to the actor, which is then optimized using GRPO and RWR. We show theoretically that, under sufficient predictive accuracy, the learned representation is equivalent to the automaton state. Experiments on grid world and robotic tasks in Isaac Lab demonstrate that Actor-Predictor outperforms automaton-based baselines on LTL-constrained tasks. It also performs well on non-regular formal specifications, such as $(a^n b^n)$, for which finite-automaton-based approaches are not applicable.

authors.name: Josef Brozovich
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Lei Ying
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Luminescent Materials and Devices

papers.title: Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-H\"older diffusion coefficient
papers.abstract: For every $\gamma\in[3/4,1]$, we prove pathwise uniqueness and strong existence for the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}$ with space-time white noise, Lipschitz drift, and a diffusion coefficient locally $\gamma$-H\"older under suitable growth bounds. The result settles the critical case $\gamma=3/4$ left open by Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins. The proof is based on a newly developed short-time linear comparison method. On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.

papers.title: Design and Evaluation of a Body-Machine Interface as an Alternative Control Paradigm for Pedal-based Sewing Machines
papers.abstract: Body-machine interfaces (BoMIs) exploit body movements to control assistive devices; they have been evaluated primarily in tasks such as cursor control or robotic manipulation where the entire movement repertoire is devoted toward device control. However, tasks with multiple concurrent processes require the user to share the movement repertoire used for device control with other body movements for task execution. This issue is examined here in the context of sewing, where the sewing machine is typically controlled by a pedal in coordination with hand movements for guiding the fabric. We evaluated the learning of a trunk-controlled BoMI for sewing machine control, and compared it with conventional pedal control. Twenty-four novice participants (12 BoMI, 12 Pedal) completed 10 trials of a standardized sewing assessment followed by 3 trials of a transfer task. The BoMI mapped trunk movements to the sewing machine's full functional repertoire, which included continuous speed control of the needle, and discrete actions such as presser-foot and needle lifts. The two groups learned at comparable rates, showing similar completion times and error counts; for both groups, completion time reduced by approximately 30\%. Additional analyses showed that the BoMI group had fewer presser-foot lift errors during training and fewer errors on the first transfer trial. Both groups also exhibited similar subjective workload. These findings collectively demonstrate that a BoMI interface can support sewing-machine control during concurrent manual activity, highlighting the potential for using BoMIs for increasing accessibility in industrial workplace contexts.

papers.title: Rigel-Ladon: An Option-Count Law for a One-Pass Decision Encoder, Tested on Held-Out Option Counts and Held-Out Schemas
papers.abstract: Laya is a small neural network that reads a text, a question and K written options, and returns one probability per option in a single pass. We ask how its accuracy falls as K grows from 2 to 35 and whether that can be predicted. We score nested option sets (every K-option question contains the smaller ones) on four question pools, for the released model (Base) and our fine-tune (FT), and score every item against each single rival. FT trained on one 12-option topic question (in-family); a 12-option HR (department-routing) question is out-of-family. Logit accuracy (the log of correct over incorrect answers) is linear in log(K-1) with slope 0.68 to 0.88. Fitted on K up to 6, the law predicts K=7 to 12 within 0.6 points and K up to 24 within 1.2 (a log-linear rule: 1.6 and 6.7). Taking the slope from the topic question and measuring only two-option accuracy on HR predicts its other K within 0.3 points (FT) and 0.7 (Base). On a 35-label pool of five schemas the law fails (5 to 11 points). Independence of irrelevant alternatives is rejected: the gold-versus-rival log-odds shifts by +0.24 to +2.07 nats per doubling of K, yet pairwise answers reproduce K-way accuracy within 4.7 points. Order averaging (averaging over several orderings of the options), shortlists, a temperature law and calibrated prediction sets did not transfer (FT's 90% sets cover 84% on HR). 2 of 10 predictions made in advance held. Caveats: one model family and LLM-labelled synthetic text.

papers.title: Sirius-Tiamat: How Small Can a One-Pass Decision Encoder Get Before Its Decisions Change?
papers.abstract: A one-pass decision encoder reads a text, a question and several named options, and returns a probability for each option in a single forward pass. We ask how far Laya, a 421M-parameter encoder of this kind, can be compressed before its decisions change. We count decisions that differ from Laya's own full-precision (fp32) answer, and track calibration (how well confidence matches accuracy, measured by expected calibration error, ECE), on 1,221 synthetic items with the training schemas, 273 with an unseen schema, and 800 out-of-family questions from ARC, MMLU and HellaSwag. Layer pruning of a related model family is known; we add flips, calibration, held-out data and retraining. bf16 changes 0.2% of in-family decisions but 2.2% out of family; 6-bit grouped rounding 1.3% and 5.9%; deleting 6 layers 0.9% and 9.1%, while ECE rises from 5.9% to 39.2%. One fitted temperature, needing no labels, restores it to 3.6%. One scale per tensor fails below six bits, and CPU dynamic int8 changes 30% of decisions, nearly all through one layer. Total variation tracks flips for rounding but not for deletion, and an early exit saves layers over a static cut only if its confidence gate is first recalibrated. Distilling a 16-layer student cuts its in-family flips from 44% to 9% (45% out of family). At equal stored size, rounding flips fewer decisions than deletion. Data are synthetic and LLM-labelled, for one architecture.

papers.title: Coordinate Basis Linear Bandits with Sublinear Regret over Low-Rank Clusters
papers.abstract: We study the problem of computational efficiency for linear bandits in high-dimensional settings with a finite arm set. In linear bandits, the increase in the dimension $d$ of the feature vectors leads to growing computational costs of $O(d^2)$ at each round of update. Traditional low-rank approximation methods such as SOFUL reduce computation via fixed-size matrix sketching, yet run the risk of incurring vacuous linear regret when the spectral tail of the data is heavy and the approximation rank is inadequately selected. To guarantee regret convergence and effectively reduce computational costs, we introduce a clustering mechanism and propose the Coordinate Basis Linear Bandit (CBL) algorithm. Our method preserves the full covariance information in each cluster by maintaining an exact orthonormal basis of the cluster's column space together with a low-dimensional coordinate representation, which guarantees robust sublinear regret without spectral-tail vulnerabilities. It performs cluster switching by assigning a sentinel for each cluster, and reduces per-round update computation to $O(\bar r^2)$ in the cluster's effective dimension $\bar r=\min(r,l)$, where $r$ is the intrinsic rank of the data and $l<d$ is a tunable rank bound.

authors.name: Hantao Yang
authors.institution: China Astronaut Research and Training Center

papers.title: Comparative First-Principles Study of the Physical Properties, Phonon-Mediated Superconductivity and Functional Potential of Technetium-Based Binary Borides TcB2, Tc2B and Tc3B
papers.abstract: Phonon-mediated superconductivity in binary transition-metal borides reflects a balance between the metal d-states, metal-boron bonding, and the lattice vibrations that couple to them. Here, we compare P6/mmm TcB2 at 20 GPa with I4/mcm Tc2B and P4/mmm Tc3B at 0 GPa within a first-principles framework. Their mechanical responses differ appreciably: TcB2 is the most rigid under its compressed condition, Tc2B shows the strongest tendency toward ductility, and Tc3B falls between the two. Despite these differences, all three phases remain metallic. The states at the Fermi level are dominated by Tc-4d character, although the extent of Tc-d/B-p mixing varies from one compound to another. Charge redistribution is more directional and B-centered in TcB2, but more delocalized around the Tc network in Tc2B and Tc3B. Inclusion of spin-orbit coupling leaves all three compounds metallic. The optical response remains metallic and electric field polarization dependent, with substantial visible reflectivity and strong ultraviolet absorption. Low-frequency Tc rich vibrations dominate the electron-phonon coupling (EPC). With {\mu}* = 0.10, the Tc values of TcB2, Tc2B, and Tc3B are 24.92, 11.07, and 15.12 K, respectively. Although Tc3B exhibits a higher electronic density of states at the Fermi level, N(EF), TcB2 couples most strongly to EPC-active low-frequency modes, showing that the superconducting hierarchy depends on electronic-phonon matching rather than DOS magnitude alone.

papers.title: Pointwise Minmax Representations for Total Variation Denoising on Graphs
papers.abstract:
Total variation denoising (TVD) is a fundamental method in image denoising, signal processing, and nonparametric regression. We establish exact pointwise minmax/maxmin representations for TVD on arbitrary finite graphs, extending recent one-dimensional results. Under squared loss, fitted values are expressed through corrected local averages over nested connected vertex sets. The correction is a signed boundary count: edges leaving the inner set contribute +1 if they remain within the outer set and -1 otherwise. To the best of our knowledge, this representation is new even for two-dimensional TVD.
  We show that Brunk's classical minmax formulas for isotonic regression on every finite directed acyclic graph arise as special cases of our graph TVD representation. The exact reduction proceeds through asymmetric TVD and nearly isotonic regression, which coincides with isotonic regression above a finite penalty threshold.
  We further extend the representations to arbitrary finite separable convex losses, assuming coercivity of the full objective, but without requiring differentiability or strict convexity. For nonunique solutions, the possible fitted values at each coordinate form a compact interval. Its lower and upper endpoints admit maxmin and minmax representations, respectively, through scalar local optimization problems and are attained simultaneously at all coordinates by two extremal solutions. This yields exact representations for quantile TVD on arbitrary graphs and unifies TVD, nearly isotonic regression, and isotonic regression within a single pointwise framework for general separable convex losses.

papers.title: GenAI-DBT: Evaluating a DBT-Informed Generative AI Platform for Mindfulness Skills Training: A Pilot Randomized Study
papers.abstract: We evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and engagement of three digital formats for dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) mindfulness skills training. In a 30-day randomized pilot study, 45 university students were assigned to GenAI-DBT, a general-purpose large language model chatbot (Chatbot), or a static web resource (Web). Forty-two completed the study, and nine completed follow-up interviews. Usability scores were within acceptable ranges across conditions, with no significant between-group differences. GenAI-DBT showed the highest observed participant-week adherence (71.4%, vs. 53.3% for Web and 42.3% for Chatbot), a descriptive difference. Mindful Attention Awareness Scale and Difficulties in Emotion Regulation Scale scores showed no significant time-by-group interactions, and session-level self-reported mood changes did not differ significantly across conditions. GenAI-DBT showed a larger positive change in linguistic valence than Chatbot (4.28 vs. 1.59, P = .02, Cohen's d = 0.99). Interviewees valued contextualized, scenario-based practice and identified response latency, repetition, and limited personalization as areas for improvement. The findings support the feasibility and acceptability of DBT-informed conversational AI for skills practice and motivate further evaluation in larger, more clinically relevant samples. Clinical efficacy remains to be established.

papers.title: Displaceability of monotone Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$
papers.abstract: We show that the generalized Polterovich submanifold $L_{0, 2}^P$ in $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and the Chekanov-Oakley-Usher Lagrangian $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ in the quadric $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$ are displaceable. Since $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ are in the zero level set of the moment maps of the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-actions on $\mathbb{C}P^3(\sqrt{2})$ and $Q^4(\sqrt{2})$, the main idea is to construct Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms mapping $L_{0, 2}^P$ and $L_{1, 2}^{Q, \mathrm{Ch}}$ to nonzero level sets of the moment maps.

authors.name: Han Lou
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
papers.abstract: Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed retrieval budgets. However, optimizing distribution diversity or target-level interest separation ignores set-level retrieval geometry: sampled queries collapse onto overlapping ANN neighborhoods, while discrete top-K lookup and single-target supervision block end-to-end coverage optimization. We introduce CACO (Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization), a lightweight self-supervised post-training framework that coordinates queries from frozen flow-matching and diffusion retrievers toward complementary item coverage with negligible additional inference latency. CACO uses empirical retrieval frequencies across sampled reference queries as a relevance proxy, formulating a label-free coverage objective that improves recall across all 30 backbone-dataset settings in offline greedy selection experiments. To avoid the inference overhead of generating a large query pool, CACO employs a coordinated query adjustment network that combines inter-query bidirectional attention with gated relative directions, finally updating queries by bounded tangent-space projection and spherical retraction. During training, CACO applies tangential antithetic perturbations and measures each query's marginal gain via counterfactual single-query replacement, yielding an unbiased gradient estimator of smoothed set coverage across non-differentiable ANN search. On eight public benchmarks and an in-house 24-partition streaming industrial dataset, CACO improves Recall@100 by up to 23.7% and Recall@400 by up to 23.9% over the strongest baseline, cuts inter-query overlap by 53.3%-64.9%, and adds only 0.5%-3.0% inference latency.

authors.name: Pan Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Extremal spectral results of outerplanar graphs without starlike trees
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle. When $l_1=l_2=\cdots=l_t=l$, we abbreviate these graphs as $S(t\cdot l)$ and $C_{t\cdot l}$, respectively. Previous results determined $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(t\cdot l))$ for $t\ge4$ [Graphs Combin. 42 (2026) 80] and for $t=3$, in each case for sufficiently large $n$. For $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$, the corresponding extremal graphs are known for $t=2$ and sufficiently large $n$. The sets $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{t\cdot l})$ were also determined for sufficiently large $n$ [Discrete Math. 349 (2026) 114673]. In this paper, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t))$ for sufficiently large $n$ when the branch lengths are not all equal. Our result for $t\ge4$ also includes equal branch lengths. As applications, we determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t})$ for arbitrary cycle lengths and sufficiently large $n$. We also determine $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ for certain linear forests $F=\bigcup_{i=1}^tP_{l_i}$ and sufficiently large $n$. Finally, we apply our main theorems to obtain the known results on outerplanar graphs forbidding matchings or theta graphs for sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: Maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs with given minimum degree and edge connectivity
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $k$. Recently, in [Linear Algebra Appl. 751 (2026) 318-330], Zhao, Ye, and Fan characterized the extremal graph with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $k$ when $n \geq \delta^2+4\delta+3$ and $k \in \{0,1,2\}$, and proposed the corresponding problem for $3 \leq k \leq \delta-1$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the entire range $0 \leq k \leq \delta-1$ and completely remove the order restriction. Specifically, we prove that $$ q(G) \leq q(B_{n,n-\delta-1}^{k}), $$ with equality if and only if $G \cong B_{n,n-\delta-1}^{k}$, where $B_{n,n-\delta-1}^{k}$ is the graph obtained from $K_{n-\delta-1} \cup K_{\delta+1}$ by adding $k$ edges joining a single vertex of $K_{n-\delta-1}$ to $k$ distinct vertices of $K_{\delta+1}$.

authors.name: Joyentanuj Das
authors.institution: SRM Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Where electrons conduct and where to change it: gauge-invariant sensitivities and the networks of sensitive bonds
papers.abstract: Where is the electrical current carried in a disordered solid, and where would a local change alter it? The two questions differ. We answer the second exactly: the derivative of the Kubo-Greenwood conductivity with respect to the Hamiltonian is gauge invariant and gives the response to any local change. The construction applies to any Hamiltonian. We try it on amorphous silicon, with tight-binding cells of up to 10000 atoms and density-functional cells of up to 512 atoms, and compare it with three ways of allocating the conductivity: the space-projected conductivity (SPC), KuboMap, and the local density of states (LDOS). KuboMap follows the LDOS closely (median Spearman correlation 0.97). The sensitivity does not. It ranks the response to an on-site shift accurately and the response to removing an atom poorly, and it transfers between Hamiltonians less well than the other maps. The most sensitive bonds form connected clusters. In three large networks they are tree-like filaments of 24 to 38 atoms in the valence tail and looped networks deeper in the gap; the excess over an LDOS-weighted random selection reaches 48 standard deviations and appears only when the broadening spans about five level spacings. The filament overlaps the tail eigenstate with the most weight on it, and one of the leading conduction channels, far more than a random cluster does, but no single state or channel explains it. The networks are largely lost in thermal snapshots at 300 K. Where the conductivity is carried and where it responds are different problems: local transport maps are useful for the first and limited for the second.

papers.title: Conformal parity
papers.abstract: We call a Riemannian metric on a four-manifold, as well as the underlying conformal structure, conformally even/odd if its self-dual and anti-self- dual Weyl tensors acting on bivectors have, at each point, equal/opposite spectra. The term mixed parity refers to the simultaneous occurrence of both of these conditions, an obvious example being the conformally flat case. After listing various known classes of conformally even metrics, we construct examples of conformally odd ones which are not of mixed parity, as well as some metrics of mixed parity that are not conformally flat. The former examples are provided by left-invariant metrics on Lie groups, and realize uncountably many local conformal-equivalence types. The latter also include some arising from Lie groups, as well as certain 1+3 Riemannian products that are not locally conformally homogeneous.

papers.title: GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers
papers.abstract:
Decision models enable fast, confidence-aware decisions by scoring candidate answers in a single forward pass, without generating text or intermediate reasoning. Yet reasoning can substantially improve decision quality, raising the question of whether its benefits can be retained without the cost of generating it. We investigate this question with \textbf{GLiDE}, a family of decision models spanning 0.4B to 27B parameters.
  Building on Qwen hybrid language models, GLiDE enables bidirectional interactions between the context, question, and candidate answers by removing causal masking from full-attention layers. To transfer reasoning capabilities into single-pass inference, we combine soft-target distillation from multiple teachers, including a reasoning model, with progressive post-training on diverse decision tasks. We further explore parameter-free recurrent depth to increase inference-time computation without generating tokens.
  Across five model sizes, GLiDE lies on the performance--parameter Pareto frontier of the Hugging Face \DI{}, with each model outperforming evaluated alternatives of equal or smaller size. \dmtwo{} (27B) achieves a hidden-set score of 71.52, with an expected calibration error of 2.0\% and a median latency of 92.9\,ms on a single GPU. Further checkpoint averaging and parameter-free recurrent depth yield GLiDE~27B, which reaches 73.37 with an expected calibration error of 2.1\%.

authors.name: Julia White
authors.institution: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center

papers.title: Beyond Restoration: Content-Degradation Factor Unfolding for Real-World Concealed Object Segmentation
papers.abstract: Reliable visual perception under degradation requires distinguishing task-relevant content from degradation-induced variations, especially in concealed object segmentation (COS), where foreground cues are inherently weak. The central challenge is not merely improving visibility, but identifying reliable content evidence amid degradation-induced variations. RGB-space segmentation often entangles content and degradation cues, while restoration-based methods primarily focus on image recovery and task interaction. This motivates explicit factorization to distinguish content evidence from degradation effects and assess its reliability. Retinex provides a spatially aligned basis for this separation but remains illumination-centric. We therefore extend it to content-degradation formation with task-asymmetric factor roles. The Factor Unfolding Network (FUN) uses the content factor R as the sole source of direct semantic evidence for segmentation, while the degradation factor L captures degradation-related variations and generates a spatial reliability map to calibrate this evidence. A unified energy couples observation formation with reliability-weighted foreground-background separation, and its alternating updates yield a coarse-to-fine network without clean-image supervision. In this way, FUN factorizes degradation for perception rather than removing it. Extensive experiments across clean and degraded conditions and diverse segmentation tasks demonstrate robust performance and generalization. Code will be released.

authors.name: Rihan Zhang
authors.institution: Technology and Engineering Center for Space Utilization

authors.name: Yuhan Chen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Adaptive Tests of Pricing Restrictions with Observed and Latent Factors
papers.abstract: This paper develops a high-dimensional test for asset pricing models with observed and latent factors. The null hypothesis allows the intercepts from an observed-factor regression to be nonzero, provided that they lie in the latent factor loading space. We estimate the pricing errors in three steps: regress returns on the observed factors, extract latent factors from the lagged covariance structure of the regression residuals, and regress returns on both observed and estimated latent factors. The intercept from the final regression serves as the estimated pricing error. We construct Sum and Max tests based on the estimated pricing errors to detect diffuse and concentrated alternatives, respectively, and combine them using a Cauchy procedure. Under suitable regularity conditions, we establish the joint null distribution of the component statistics, their asymptotic independence, and their power against alternative hypotheses. We also propose a residual bootstrap and establish its first-order validity. Simulation studies examine the finite-sample performance of the tests under different pricing-error patterns and factor-number choices. An application to S\&P 500 stocks illustrates the use of the proposed framework in evaluating an observed-factor pricing model after latent-factor adjustment.

papers.title: Remark on Kobayashi's conjecture: a volume Schwarz lemma
papers.abstract: This remark offers an expository reconstruction of OpenAI's proof of Kobayashi's ampleness conjecture for compact K\"ahler manifolds, together with new results. We extract a volume Schwarz lemma for extremal discs and derive a pointwise volume comparison: the volume form of a K\"ahler metric with $\mathrm{Ric}(\omega)\ge-\omega$ is bounded below by an intrinsic volume form built from the K\"ahler--Einstein metrics of pseudoconvex domains containing the Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix. As a consequence, if a compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ has nef canonical bundle and its Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix is bounded at some point, then $X$ is of general type.

papers.title: Compiling Constraints into Neuromorphic Ising Machines
papers.abstract: Most practical combinatorial optimization problems involve constraints, and an Ising machine that flips one spin at a time can respect them only through energy penalties that raise barriers between feasible solutions. Here we show that a higher-order neuromorphic Ising machine can enforce constraints through programmable transitions rather than penalties. In an autoencoder-like architecture, each inner-layer neuron represents a move, a family of multi-spin transitions that maps every feasible state to another feasible state, receives the energy change of its move through connections that outer-layer neurons multiplicatively switch on or off, and updates the state through the same connections. A compiler turns constraints into this wiring with a number of auxiliary clauses that grows only polynomially for parity, cardinality, one-hot, partition and permutation constraints. Restricting the search to feasible states reduces constraint handling to move design, and we show that the fastest-annealing moves are not those that mix fastest but those that lower the deepest energy barriers, and that moves chosen from the objective lower them further than random ones. On third-order graph matching, the machine needs orders of magnitude fewer iterations than penalty-based neuromorphic machines. Configured as a sampler on a field-programmable gate array, it decodes the surface code with maximum-likelihood accuracy up to code distance 15 within 52 $\mu$s per shot and, under noisy syndrome measurements, decodes in real time for millisecond measurement rounds up to distance 9 with fewer logical errors than belief-propagation decoders.

papers.title: StarMPI-SVD: Distributed-Memory Parallel Star-M Tensor SVD
papers.abstract: The star-M tensor algebra generalizes the optimal compression guarantees of the matrix singular value decomposition (SVD) to higher-order tensors. The t-SVDM-I decomposition is computed using a set of invertible transformations and slice-wise truncated SVDs with a prescribed rank, and its adaptive, multirank variant t-SVDM-II can determine slice-wise ranks to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance. Existing implementations of these algorithms are limited to shared-memory environments, restricting their applicability to modern large-scale datasets. In this work, we present the first distributed-memory implementations of t-SVDM-I and t-SVDM-II, which are generalized to N-way tensors. To address computational and communication bottlenecks, we design asynchronous, non-blocking communication strategies for efficient data redistribution to obtain highly efficient key computational kernels. Strong-scaling experiments demonstrate the efficiency and scalability of our approach (at least 70% parallel efficiency on up to 128 nodes, or 6144 cores), and we apply the star-M compression techniques to a set of application datasets of size up to 768 GB.

papers.title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
papers.abstract: Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $\alpha$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN's slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{\alpha+1}{\alpha-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $\gamma > 0$, showing a $\tfrac{2}{\gamma}$ approximation on navigable graphs ($\alpha \approx 1$), where greedy search admits no guarantees. In this work, we unify and generalize these results by proving that ABS with parameter $\gamma$ on $\alpha$-reachable graphs achieves an approximation of $\tfrac{\alpha+1}{\alpha(\gamma+1)-1}$ for any metric. Moreover, on sorted $\alpha$-reachable graphs (introduced by Gollapudi et al.) under the $\ell_2$ metric, we obtain the tighter bound $\max\bigl(\tfrac{\alpha}{\alpha(\gamma+1)-1}, \tfrac{\alpha^{2}+1}{\alpha^{2}(\gamma+1)-1}\bigr)$. Beyond these theoretical results, we design a beam predictor using features inspired by fine-grained analysis of ABS, trained via a constrained objective that minimizes mean distance computations subject to a target recall. On three 100-million-point benchmarks, using graphs built by DiskANN's practical construction, beam predictor lowers mean query latency on SSD-resident indices at matched recall by up to $29.6\%$ relative to classical beam search (CBS). Relative to ABS, it is faster in $11$ of $15$ settings, by up to $6.5\%$, and at most $1.4\%$ slower in the other $4$; at $95\%$ recall, its advantage over ABS grows from $0.8$--$4.2\%$ for $100$ neighbors to $4.6$--$5.6\%$ for $500$ neighbors. In memory, it needs $1.3$--$23.7\%$ fewer distance computations than CBS and $0.0$--$3.9\%$ fewer than ABS.

papers.title: Single-fit inference for the realized prediction error of a logistic model with many predictors
papers.abstract: When independent validation data are unavailable, evaluating a fitted logistic model on new patients requires estimating prediction error and uncertainty. Evaluating the fit on training data is often optimistic. Bootstrap validation is widely used to correct this bias, but with many predictors, it can retain bias and yield unreliable confidence intervals. In this article, we study these limitations and develop single-fit estimation and inference without resampling. When the number of Gaussian predictors grows proportionally with sample size, we analyze unpenalized logistic models. We prove that standard bootstrap correction can have nonzero limiting bias even as the resample count grows and location-shifted intervals can have zero limiting coverage. Instead, we adjust the fitted scores to consistently estimate realized Brier and log losses. We account for common fitting and adjustment error to construct valid marginal intervals and joint regions. We also establish these single-fit estimation and inference guarantees for certain non-Gaussian designs in proportional dimensions. Under moderate dimension growth and possible misspecification with general predictors, we extend single-fit inference to ridge regularization and construct asymptotically valid confidence intervals for realized log loss. Simulations and analyses of hospital and diabetes datasets support our theory and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

authors.name: Seyoung Park
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
papers.abstract:
Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems.
  We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.

authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: AscMLA: Unlocking FP4 Efficiency for Long-Context MLA Decoding through Asymmetric Scaling
papers.abstract: Long-context decoding repeatedly reads a growing KV cache. FP4 reduces cache storage and traffic but needs block scaling to handle its limited dynamic range. Applying FP4 to multi-head latent attention (MLA) requires reconciling different K/V scaling requirements on a shared latent. Existing approaches address this mismatch through dequantization or separate encodings, adding execution or storage overhead. We present AscMLA, which combines asymmetric K/V scaling with pipelined scale delivery to process a single FP4 payload directly. AscMLA uses 38.2% less cache memory than FP8 and achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.35x over TRT-LLM's FP8 and 1.26x over CAKE's NVFP4 MLA kernels.

papers.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
papers.abstract:
Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions.
  In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

authors.name: Alexander Varchenko
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
papers.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.

papers.title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about knowledge, persona directions mainly track a reply's wording: where lies and honest denials share their words, our three main contrasts stay inside the random-direction band on Llama and Qwen and reach only its edge on Gemma, though on Mistral one clears it. A knowledge direction contrasts questions the model can answer with ones nobody can, each followed by the same scripted denial. It separates lies from identical honest denials on two models and narrowly on a third, but not on the fourth; its other results partly depend on the benchmark's wording. On the Gender-Secret fine-tune it clears the band by a few hundredths on Llama and fails on Mistral. The sum of the two directions ranks lies better than a supervised probe at the same depth on all four models (on one, both near chance) but is level with the persona direction on Llama's average and behind that probe on held-out lies. More varied role-play questions do not help the persona direction on Liars' Bench.

papers.title: MambaLIFT: Reference-Based Mechanism-Aware Attribution for VMamba
papers.abstract: Attributing predictions of visual state-space models remains challenging because input-dependent selective dynamics couple feature selection, recurrent state propagation, and shared computational pathways. We introduce MambaLIFT, a reference-based, multiplier-first attribution framework for VMamba that propagates contributions through its computational graph using interaction-aware rules for selective-scan injection, recurrent memory, LayerNorm, and shared pathways. MambaLIFT decomposes the reference-relative class-logit difference, \(f_c(x)-f_c(x^0)\), by spatial position, VSS block, scan direction, and computational mechanism. Experiments on ImageNet-1K evaluate VMamba-T and VMamba-B, with hyperparameters selected on a calibration set and faithfulness assessed on a disjoint held-out evaluation set. MambaLIFT achieves numerical conservation to floating-point precision across audited attribution interfaces in both configurations. Under mean-colour pixel flipping, it achieves significantly higher mean faithfulness scores than MambaLRP on both configurations and the highest scores among the evaluated methods, including Integrated Gradients with matched references. Under blurred replacement, MambaLIFT is non-inferior to MambaLRP on VMamba-T and equivalent on VMamba-B, indicating that its advantage depends on the replacement protocol. Ablations on VMamba-T show that interaction allocation, temporal propagation, and pathway composition affect attribution maps. Mechanism-level analyses further show that exact relevance conservation does not imply additive effects under finite interventions: the mechanism decomposition accounts for the reference-relative logit difference but does not estimate intervention effects or establish causal validity.

papers.title: Rate-distortion Assessment for Hierarchical Content Summarization
papers.abstract: Powerful generative models including large language and vision models have demonstrated success across a wide range of content generation, editing and manipulation tasks via end-to-end prompt-based generation. However, current assessment of the quality of generative content manipulation remains subjective, limiting scientific understanding of model capabilities. Inspired by rate-distortion theory from Shannon information compression theory, in this work we formalize hierarchical content summarization as an information encoding problem. We design a principled framework to extract the semantic hierarchy of the source content to support quantitative characterization of the rate-distortion trade-off between compression efficiency (rate) against information loss (distortion) during generative content manipulation, which allows us to benchmark various models with respect to performance conditional on rate budget of interest. We demonstrate the use of the framework with empirical experiments on content summarization for long-context question-answering with state-of-the-art large language models, offering new insights into their efficiency and comprehension capabilities. We further demonstrate the use of the semantic hierarchy as guidance for performing effective retrieval augmented generation, showing improved rate-distortion characteristics against current baselines.

papers.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
papers.abstract: Multimodal foundation models are advancing embodied navigation, but frequent inference incurs substantial computational cost. We present Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy. Retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback determine the cognitive horizon, or how many cached waypoints the robot executes before refreshing its prediction. At the policy's stop request, local visitation history guides a bounded correction with at most one extra movement and no additional model calls. CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% on HM3D-OVON and 64.7% on R2R-CE, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, respectively. Success rate and success weighted by path length improve per model call on both benchmarks. Across four physical navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 successes versus 14 for native execution, reducing model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%.

papers.title: Auto-Alpha: A Framework for Autonomous Factor Research
papers.abstract: Autonomous factor research requires generating economic hypotheses as well as implementing and testing them. We present Auto-Alpha, a framework that connects report-guided initialization to self-directed research through a test-driven implementation loop. An idea agent proposes economic mechanisms and signal constructions; a research agent develops them with backtest feedback. Semantic audit, quantitative review, and human admission select factors for a persistent library, while an Experience Library retains research insights. Starting from 120 research reports, Auto-Alpha builds an initial library of 32 factors. It then generates new ideas and refines existing candidates, producing 420 implementations and retaining 62 additional factors. We evaluate factor quality and portfolio performance using a fixed library snapshot of 105 factors. The median 1-day Rank IC is 0.0301, and a weekly Top-300 portfolio returns 16.81% annualized after stated costs over 2020-2026, versus 1.71% for the CSI 1000 price index. These retrospective results document an operating research process and its artifacts; controlled evaluation is needed to isolate the contribution of its components.

papers.title: Question, Then Affirm: Restoring Commitment Does Not Restore Refusal
papers.abstract: We find that safeguards for image generation can be bypassed without changing what a message says. A sign stating a harmful proposition is blocked, but the same proposition phrased as a question and followed by a check mark is generated, even though the resulting image endorses the original claim. On a 300-case challenge set, gpt-image-2 returns images for 43.3% of question-affirmation requests versus 16.3% of direct statements, with 41.3% versus 15.3% of cases yielding images that endorse the original proposition. We define this as Deferred Semantic Commitment (DSC): commitment is withdrawn by the question and restored by a separate element, while safety behavior follows only the withdrawal. To investigate why, we study an open-weight language model and find that re-endorsement only partially reverses the refusal-related change introduced by questioning. These findings reveal a mismatch between recovered meaning and refusal behavior, motivating safeguards that assess the completed message rather than its individual elements.

papers.title: Optimal Radius Ratio of Compact Nonuniform Packings
papers.abstract: We study the ratio of the smallest to the largest radius in a nonuniform disk packing whose tangency graph triangulates the plane. We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest possible ratio is $s=0.651050185882609\ldots$, attained uniquely up to similarity by packing~53 of Fernique, Hashemi, and Sizova. In fact, every nonuniform packing with radius ratio at least $0.65105$ is similar to this packing. No periodicity or restriction on the number of radii is assumed; the radii are required only to have a positive infimum and a finite supremum. Following the finite-subgraph exclusion program of Connelly and Zhang, we first restrict the degree-five flowers and their pairings. The remaining exceptional degree-seven corona forces seventeen complete flowers on an unfolded disk with thirty-seven labels. An exact interval certificate excludes their angle equations. A comparison of logarithmic radii on a recurrent network then forces the radii and the three local degree words. We identify the entire triangulation by reducing these words to the square--octagon tiling and showing that its decoration is forced.

papers.title: GraF-VTA: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Vision and Temporal Logic via Graph-Based Fusion
papers.abstract: Robotic planning from visual observations and signal temporal logic (STL) requires grounding task requirements in scene evidence while adapting plans to execution feedback. We present GraF-VTA, a graph-based framework that extends Vision-TL-Action with structured task representations, causal observation history, and closed-loop trajectory generation. Bidirectional cross-attention fuses STL syntax tokens with visual features, while an optional frozen automaton embedding supplies complementary untimed task structure. A temporal pyramid preserves detailed current observations and compresses older frames to provide recent execution context. Conditioned on these features and robot state, a flow-matching model generates plans whose action prefixes are executed before replanning from refreshed observations. Across five simulation environments, the single-graph configuration achieves higher open-loop Success@$K$ than TeLoGraF and Vision-TL-Action on four environments at the reported budgets $K\geq16$. On Panda, matched-update ablations increase Success@256 from 53.91\% without observation history to 62.50\% with pyramid memory. In closed-loop Dubins evaluation, it reaches 64.06\% Success@1024, compared with 12.50\% for adapted S-MSP and 27.34\% for adapted Logic-VLA. These results support combining structured visual conditioning with observation history and replanning to improve coverage of STL-satisfying trajectories.

papers.title: PDE-State Conditioning for Learned Optimization Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural network (PINN) optimization depends on global properties of the underlying PDE and how the physics residual evolves across the domain. Standard optimizers such as Adam use fixed gradient-based statistics, while learned PINN optimizers replace the fixed rule with a learned update built from local parameters and optimization-history features. However, none explicitly use PDE-level information. We study two coupled design questions: what PDE-level information should a learned optimizer observe, and how should that information influence its update? We introduce an 11-dimensional PDE state-capturing operator structure, residual geometry, and short-horizon update response, and use it to condition a structured meta-learned optimizer through bounded feature-wise modulation. Repeated design studies identify the compact residual-geometry state G2 and bounded FiLM as the strongest overall choices among those tested. The resulting PDE-State-conditioned optimizer improves all evaluation metrics (relative-L2, L1, solution MSE, and physics MSE) over Adam and the unconditioned learned optimizer on Linear Advection, KdV, and Burgers.

papers.title: Separated solutions for a critical competitive system with sublinear coupling in domains with shrinking holes
papers.abstract: We construct nonnegative, fully nontrivial separated solutions for the critical competitive system of two coupled elliptic equations with a sublinear competitive coupling, in a bounded domain with two shrinking holes, for $N\ge5$ and every fixed $\beta<0$; each component concentrates at one of the holes and vanishes near the other. The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument. This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.

papers.title: Diagnosis is not a policy: a state-transition audit of caoability-conditioned test-time inference
papers.abstract: Test-time actions can satisfy retrieval, state-realization, program-consistency, or rendering objectives without correcting an answer. Test-time Error Response and Realizability Audit (TERRA) is an evaluation/auditing protocol, not a new inference algorithm. It uses a unified decomposition of intervention outcomes into applicability, target-state realization, endpoint translation, harm, and resource/inference cost. Paired comparisons fix the incoming state and evaluation conditions; cross-model analyses vary the receiving configuration. Executable financial reasoning experiments yield three findings: the same context expansion can harm one configuration and benefit another; sufficient evidence does not ensure correctness because configurations differ in evidence-to-answer translation; and diagnostic headroom---accuracy attainable with idealized diagnostic information over the measured baseline---plus local consistency does not ensure practical gains. Action value is $V(a\mid x,m)$, not diagnosis alone; diagnosis is not a deployable policy $\pi(a\mid x,m)$.

papers.title: VisualJevBench: A Benchmark and Black-Box Attacks for Visual Typed Decision Models
papers.abstract: Typed decision models (TDMs) return structured decisions instead of generating free-text responses, enabling fast and cheap decisions in real-world applications. Recent support for image inputs extends Jev, a representative TDM, to visual decision-making. We refer to this setting as Visual Jev. However, red teaming of Visual Jev leaves two gaps: a systematic evaluation of direct image manipulations is lacking, and universal visual attacks remain underexplored. To address these gaps, we introduce VisualJevBench, a benchmark for evaluating the adversarial robustness of Visual Jev. It comprises 800 images and 3,200 questions across eight scenarios and four visual attack surfaces: typographic manipulation, visual evidence spoofing, target selection interference, and geometric transformation. We also introduce Adaptive Black-Box Parameter Search (ABPS), a lightweight framework that uses typed-output feedback to find effective image manipulations. ABPS supports both image-specific attacks and universal attacks that transfer to unseen images and tasks in new scenarios without further optimization. Extensive experiments on jev-1.14.0 show that image-specific attacks achieve an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 69.6%, while universal attacks achieve an average ASR of 33.15% on unseen images. Geometric transformations achieve an average ASR of 40.09% in cross-scenario transfer.

papers.title: Depth of Powers of Cover Ideals of Path Ideals
papers.abstract: Let $ J_t(P_n) = (x_1, \ldots, x_t) \cap \cdots \cap (x_{n-t+1}, \ldots, x_n) $ be the cover ideal of the $t$-path ideal of a path graph inside the polynomial ring $ S = K[x_1, \ldots, x_n] $ over a field $K$. For every $ n \ge t \ge 2 $ and $s \ge 2$, we prove that \[ \operatorname{depth} \left ( S/J_t(P_n)^s \right ) = q(s+1) + \left\lfloor \frac{r-1}{t} \right\rfloor, \] where $ n = q(ts + 1) + r $ with $ 1 \le r \le ts + 1 $. Our proof shows that all powers of $J_t(P_n)$ have linear quotients in increasing lexicographic order and explicitly describes the corresponding colon ideals.
