papers.title: The distribution of greatest common divisors of binomial coefficients and their upper indices
Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
papers.abstract: In this Letter, we explore the soft X-ray shock breakout (SBO) and cooling emission of supernovae interacting with pre-explosion dense circumstellar material (CSM) shells as a subclass of extragalactic fast X-ray transients. For geometrically thin CSM shells, we find that the SBO luminosities span a range of a few $10^{43}-10^{45}\,{\rm{erg}}\,{\rm{s}}^{-1}$, with peak times typically $\lesssim10^4\,{\rm{s}}$, both of which are primarily determined by the light-travel effect. When the shell's outer radius is located at $\sim100-500\,R_\odot$, the SBO temperatures fall into the energy band covered by the current soft X-ray facilities. We derive analytic lightcurves for SBOs in dense CSM shells and explore how different physical parameters affect the observed lightcurves and the temperature evolution. Despite the multi-temperature nature of the emission caused by the light-travel effect leading to non-thermal-like spectra, we find that the time-resolved spectra within the limited soft X-ray band can still be well described by a blackbody model. This provides a natural explanation for the observed blackbody-like time-resolved spectra of soft X-ray SBO events. Our model can reproduce the observed X-ray lightcurves and temperature evolutions of the three known X-ray SBO events, EP260321a, XRF\,060218, and XRO\,080109, revealing a diversity in the properties of the dense CSM shells ejected by stripped-envelope progenitors before the explosion. Future discoveries of more soft X-ray SBO events by facilities such as Einstein Probe will provide opportunities for probing the episodic mass-loss history of massive stars in the final stages before core collapse.

authors.name: Zhuo Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Streaming-AAA: Streaming AAA Game Video Generation at High Resolution, High Frame Rate, and Low Latency
papers.abstract: Controllable streaming video generation offers a promising route toward interactive game simulation, yet existing methods remain far from practical gameplay. They often fail to jointly achieve high visual fidelity, high frame rates, and low interaction latency, resulting in poor responsiveness and degraded user experience. We present Streaming-AAA, a new paradigm for controllable infinite generation of AAA-quality game videos. Our system generates 1080p gameplay videos at 43 FPS with 198 ms end-to-end latency interaction on merely NVIDIA A800 GPUs, while supporting long-horizon play without severe temporal degradation or collapse. Streaming-AAA is built upon three key designs. First, we redesign the VAE architecture for efficient high-resolution decoding, enabling real-time synthesis at 1080p. Second, we pretrain the diffusion model using diffusion forcing and significantly extend the temporal training horizon, allowing the model to capture long-term dependencies and maintain persistent memory. Third, we perform post-training distillation and memory compression to improve inference efficiency while retaining visual quality and temporal consistency. Experiments show that Streaming-AAA substantially improves visual fidelity, frame rate, latency, and long-term stability over prior controllable video generation approaches, enabling a significantly more playable experience for interactive AAA game video generation.

authors.name: Haifeng Shi
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Advanced Separation Membrane Materials

papers.title: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. In this paper, we present HiUni, which revisits this design choice and explores whether a pretrained vision language model can be directly extended into a unified model with extensive parameter sharing. Specifically, HiUni reuses the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both capabilities, while confining task-specific computation to the output side. Yet such a design introduces two key challenges. Generation in pixel space is difficult to optimize, and semantic abstraction in pretrained ViT discards fine spatial details required for synthesis. To address these challenges, HiUni introduces a \emph{Pixel Diffusion Head} tailored to direct pixel-space optimization and a lightweight \emph{HiGate} pathway that provides fine-grained spatial details near the output stage. Extensive experiments show that HiUni achieves a similar average understanding score to the pretrained VLM while attaining competitive performance on image generation and editing. Controlled comparisons and analyses further demonstrate that a single dense backbone can effectively support both capabilities without task-specific backbone computation, highlighting a simpler path toward unified multimodal modeling.

papers.title: MultiBinder: Preventing Multi-Subject Identity Leakage in Personalized Video Generation
papers.abstract: Personalized video generation faces a significant scalability challenge: as the number of custom subjects increases, existing methods suffer from severe identity leakage and semantic entanglement, resulting in videos with blended attributes and incoherent narratives. We identify that this stems from a lack of explicit binding between textual entity phrases and their corresponding visual patterns prior to fusion in diffusion models. To address this, we propose MultiBinder, a novel framework built on a ``bind-then-narrate'' paradigm. Our approach introduces a two-stage conditioning process before video diffusion. First, Cross-modal Entity Binding devises an entity-aware Q-Former to extract identity-centric features from each subject's reference image and tightly align them with its unique entity phrase, yielding disentangled ``identity tokens.'' Second, a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) acts as a ``narrative director'' in the Narrative-Aware Subject Arrangement stage, capturing the action of each subject from the text prompt and synthesizes contextualized subject features that encapsulate ``who is doing what'' and preserve role-specific distinctions. These features are then injected into a video diffusion model via dedicated conditioning pathways, ensuring precise attribute allocation. Extensive experiments on both general and newly curated multi-subject benchmarks show that MultiBinder significantly outperforms existing methods in multi-subject identity fidelity.

authors.name: Yiheng Zhang
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Convex combinations of strict triangular norms
papers.abstract: We prove that a pointwise convex combination of two strict triangular norms with positive weights is associative if and only if the two norms coincide. Together with the known ordinal-sum reduction and nilpotent case, the theorem yields the same conclusion for all continuous triangular norms and, in particular, for associative bivariate copulas. It also gives a corresponding result for representable uninorms with a common neutral element.

papers.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
papers.abstract: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. The benchmark compares predictions with two reference futures from the same prediction initial state, one following the demonstrated rule and the other a common rule, to measure prediction bias toward common dynamics. We further propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which learns how different rules affect object motion, infers the current rule from calibration interactions, and applies it to prediction from a new initial state. RIFT explicitly controls the influence of training frequency on rule inference, allowing sufficiently informative observational evidence to support rare rules. Experiments on TailWorld show that RIFT improves prediction accuracy and physical consistency across varying training imbalances and distribution shifts, with gains in predicting rare dynamics.

papers.title: Harish-Chandra isomorphism over arbitrary base rings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $R$ be any commutative ring. We prove that Harish-Chandra projection induces a natural, strict filtered isomorphism $U_R(\mathfrak{g}_R)^{G_R} \simeq \operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathfrak{h}_R)^{W,\bullet}$, whereas the corresponding Chevalley restriction need not be surjective even over a field.

papers.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management
papers.abstract: Long-term agents accumulate large external memory stores as interactions unfold, increasing the costs of storage, retrieval, and response generation. Efficiency is constrained by two coupled factors: a growing record count increases retrieval overhead, while longer retrieved contexts increase prefill computation and decoding-time attention costs. Existing methods prune or consolidate records, but pruning can discard useful evidence, whereas consolidation may produce fewer yet longer retrieval units. We introduce MemFolder, a structure-guided memory folding framework that sequentially reduces record count and context length. The framework comprises two core components that share memory groups, using cross-record structure to guide both evidence consolidation and compact representation. RecordFolder grounds entity mentions, progressively selects representative yet complementary anchors, and combines semantic and entity affinity with temporal chaining to consolidate compatible records into fewer retrieval units. ContextFolder encodes the original records within these groups into compact text and uses verification feedback to revise encodings when key facts cannot be recovered. Experiments on the three text-based memory benchmarks LoCoMo, PersonaMem, and LongMemEval and the two multimodal benchmarks M3-Bench-web and M3-Bench-robot demonstrate the strong performance of our methods. Notably, on Mem0, RecordFolder retains 99.0% of the original average performance across the three text-based benchmarks with 50% fewer records, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.9 percentage points in performance retention. Combined with ContextFolder, existing record compression methods further shorten their output records while retaining most of their performance.

authors.name: Honggang Chen
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
papers.abstract: We prove global $C^{2,\alpha}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimates for positive $C^\alpha$ densities.

authors.name: Yuanyuan Li
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Xianduo Wang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Blind Spots Travel, Knowledge Stays Home: What RL Inherits from an LLM Judge
papers.abstract: LLM judges serve as rewards where no answer key exists, in the hope that their knowledge passes to the trained model. In 814 RL runs that teach 7-8B models to answer closed-book questions or abstain, we ask what passes. What a grader knows about single answers stays home. A wrong answer that a judge rewards is memorised for that one question. A model trained with the answer key, or with a far stronger judge, chooses which new questions to answer no better than the untrained model does by sampling 32 answers and abstaining where they disagree; the grader's knowledge adds about one corrected answer per hundred questions. What a grader believes about a kind of question travels. A judge that rejects eleven of the twelve correct training answers about capitals of former states teaches the model to refuse 98% of such capitals on new questions, a loss that accuracy and abstention rates do not reveal. Changing only those twelve verdicts by hand moves the refusal from 5% to 90%, even for a grader that accepts as many answers as the answer key; at that leniency, two of four judges already cost 38-42% of these capitals. The capitals are not forgotten: with "I don't know" blocked, the model answers 94% of them correctly. The grader therefore needs no knowledge of its own: rewarding the model for giving the answer that most of its own untrained samples agree on, with no labels and no judge, earns the answer key's reward and keeps the category.

papers.title: Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
papers.abstract: The strong chromatic index $\chi_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $\theta(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $\theta(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $\chi_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$. For simple graphs, this improves the direct greedy bound from 32 to 28. In particular, it verifies the Erd\H{o}s-Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il conjecture for simple graphs of maximum degree five whose vertices of degree five form an independent set, using one fewer color than the conjectured bound of 29. When $\theta(G)=9$, our bound is four colors above the bound of 24 predicted by the Ore-degree conjecture of Chen, Huang, Yu, and Zhou.

papers.title: Verifying Before Enhancing: Target Evidence Chain Verification for Infrared Small Target Detection
papers.abstract: Infrared small target detection is essential for early warning, surveillance, remote sensing, and space-based target perception. However, infrared small targets are typically tiny, weakly textured, and boundary-blurred, making them difficult to distinguish from complex backgrounds. Moreover, target-like background structures can produce salient responses across multiple scales, making response strength alone insufficient for reliable target discrimination. To address this challenge, we propose VBE-UNet, a Target Evidence Chain Verification Network that assesses candidate reliability beyond response magnitude through complementary evidence cues. Specifically, counterfactual background explanation models local target evidence, while joint evidence verification integrates cross-scale support and perturbation-based contribution verification to guide feature recomposition. The resulting reliability estimates guide selective feature refinement, promoting target-relevant responses while reducing unsupported background activations. Extensive experiments on IRSTD-1K, NUDT-SIRST, and NUAA-SIRST demonstrate that VBE-UNet achieves superior detection accuracy and lower false-alarm rates compared with state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies and evidence reliability analysis further validate the effectiveness of the proposed verification framework.

authors.name: Songwei Pei
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Shuhuai Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Shangguang Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Time-independent equivalent matrix representation for time-domain boundary element analysis of large-scale 3D acoustic problems
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a time-independent equivalent matrix representation for large-scale three-dimensional (3D) acoustic analysis with the time-domain boundary element method (TDBEM). In conventional TDBEM, pair-dependent retarded times couple spatial interactions to historical boundary data, causing substantial storage and history-convolution costs. The proposed representation decouples compressible spatial interactions from propagation history, allowing reuse of the same compressed spatial representation across propagation delays and throughout time marching without additional temporal interpolation of the kernel. For conventional space-time discretizations, blockwise low-rank compression yields the compressed equivalent matrix method in the $\mathcal{H}$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}$), with dynamic cluster-pair tracking to skip inactive interactions during wavefront propagation. For low-frequency, long-wavelength problems with a bounded number of nonzero time-lag matrices, the framework is extended to the $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrix format (CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$) using delay-consistent partitioning, shared coupling matrices, and nested cluster bases. Under sparsity and bounded-parameter assumptions, storage and per-step cost of CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$ both scale as $O(N_s)$, excluding preprocessing. Numerical results agree well with conventional TDBEM and semi-analytical reference solutions. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}$, the storage requirement for a sphere with $N_s=20,480$ is reduced from approximately 349.0 GB to 1.6 GB, with a speedup of approximately $45.4\times$. For CEM-$\mathcal{H}^2$, simulations with up to $N_s=1,310,720$ are performed in the low-frequency, long-wavelength regime. A million-degree-of-freedom underwater-vehicle model is also analyzed. These results demonstrate the capability of the proposed framework for large-scale 3D transient acoustic analysis using TDBEM.

papers.title: Uninorm constructions on bounded trellises via closure and interior operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions under which six closure- or interior-based operations on bounded trellises are uninorms. These operations incorporate triangular norms, triangular conorms, or both, and form three order-dual pairs. Since the underlying pseudo-order need not be transitive and meet and join need not be associative, standard lattice arguments do not apply directly. Under a fixed ambient transitivity assumption, the first pair is characterized by image, monotonicity, and compatibility conditions for the associated maps on elements incomparable with the neutral element; an additional comparison condition used in earlier sufficient constructions is shown to be redundant. Complete characterizations are also obtained for the variants with an absorbing endpoint, including both nondegenerate and degenerate interval cases. For the pair involving both a triangular norm and a triangular conorm, we derive exact comparison conditions requiring the triangular norm to take the value~$0$, or dually the triangular conorm to take the value~$1$, in the relevant cases. These conditions reduce to the usual incomparability assumptions in the absence of nontrivial zero- or one-divisors. On bounded lattices, the closure and interior conditions simplify to explicit identities or image restrictions. Finite proper-trellis examples clarify the role and limitations of the ambient transitivity assumptions.

papers.title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening
papers.abstract: Identifying active molecules for known targets and potential targets for existing drugs is central to drug discovery and repurposing. Drug-target interaction (DTI) models can rank vast numbers of drug-target pairs, but limited experimental capacity restricts testing to a small number of candidates. We compared the bidirectional recommendations of 13 released systems across 711 molecular structures of FDA-approved drugs and 614 human proteins. For the same target or drug, pairs of models produced completely disjoint Top-10 molecule and protein lists in 77.8% and 70.1% of comparisons, respectively. Even where recommendations overlapped, agreement between some systems largely reflected recurring preferences for the same candidates. Published inhibition measurements for 79 molecules and 65 kinases revealed that some systems enriched active candidates, yet their hit yields changed little when recommendations were matched to different drugs or targets, whereas other systems lost substantially more hits. Some of the former systems also rarely ranked both molecules and kinases correctly when two drugs favoured different kinases. We further retrained the same architecture on the same data, with the training objective fixed and random seeds varied. Despite similar test performance, mean pairwise Top-10 overlap on a separate screening catalogue was about two candidates. Our study moves DTI model evaluation beyond benchmark performance to assess whether model predictions can guide meaningful experimental decisions in drug discovery and target identification.

authors.name: Chengrui Xu
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
papers.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

authors.name: Zheyan Wan
authors.institution: Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

papers.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
papers.abstract: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own. On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees. After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines. The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.

authors.name: Jiachen Tao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture
papers.abstract:
We prove Casselman's comparison conjecture for parabolic subgroups of real linear reductive groups. Let $Q=LU$ be a standard parabolic subgroup of a real linear reductive group $G$, with Levi subgroup $L$ and unipotent radical $U$. For every Casselman--Wallach representation $\pi$ of $G$ and every $i\geq0$, the natural inclusion $\pi_K\hookrightarrow\pi$ induces a topological $L$-equivariant isomorphism \[
  H_i(\mathfrak u,\pi_K)^\infty\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
  H_i(\mathfrak u,\pi). \] Put $\mathscr U=\mathcal U(\mathfrak u)$ and $F_k=\mathscr U/I_{\mathfrak u}^k$, where $I_{\mathfrak u}$ is the augmentation ideal. For every $k\geq1$ and $i\geq0$, we establish natural topological $L$-isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned}
  \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,\pi_K)^\infty
  \simeq \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,\pi),\
  \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,\pi_K)^\infty
  \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,\pi). \end{aligned} \] We also obtain closedness of $\mathfrak u^kM$ for the (co)chain spaces $M=C_j(\mathfrak u,\pi),C^j(\mathfrak u,\pi)$, and for $M=J_a,J_{a-1}/J_a$, where $(J_a)$ is the smooth Bruhat filtration of a principal series representation.

authors.name: Jun Yu
authors.institution: National Clinical Research Center for Digestive Diseases

papers.title: Linear dependence and tameness for homogeneous nilpotent-Jacobian maps in dimension four
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $H\in K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]^4$ be homogeneous of positive degree. We prove that the components of $H$ are linearly dependent over $K$ whenever $JH$ is nilpotent, extending the known quadratic and cubic results to every positive homogeneous degree. This fills the gap regarding homogeneous linear dependence in four dimensions. The proof combines the nilpotent flag with the geometry of the geometric generic affine fibers and the projective image surface. Line fibers are treated by homogeneous quasi-translations. For nonlinear fibers, three successive invariants constrain the directions at infinity, reducing the nonplanar image to a developable surface or a smooth quadric. Boundary, ruling, and trace identities exclude both alternatives. We further prove that $X+H$ is one-stably tame in every degree and tame in four variables through degree five.

authors.name: Dan Yan
authors.institution: National Clinical Research Center for Digestive Diseases

papers.title: A Density Bound for Mu\~niz's List Reversal
papers.abstract: Mu\~niz described the problem of reversing a list of positive integers under the following rules: given a list of distinct positive integers, at each step, one can combine two adjacent entries into their sum or break an entry into two entries with the same sum, under the constraints that after each step the list must contain distinct entries no larger than the original largest entry. The question of what lists are and are not reversible under these rules is studied and an asymptotic upper bound on the density of an irreversible list is established.

papers.title: Interior and global $W^{2,1}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for $3\leq k\leq n-1$, continuous $k$-convex solutions of the $k$-Hessian equation with density bounded above and below by positive constants belong to $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$. This regularity holds globally on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex domains when both the boundary and the boundary values are of class $C^{1,1}$.

papers.title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding
papers.abstract: Traffic scenario understanding requires combining fine-grained visual evidence with spatial and temporal reasoning. Tool-augmented vision-language models (VLMs) can use specialized perception tools, but effective collaboration faces two challenges: terminal rewards provide limited guidance for intermediate decisions and error recovery, while repeated planning adds unnecessary cost across similar tasks. Echoing the fast-slow dichotomy of human cognition, we propose StarTV-Agent, which combines policy learning with experience evolution to support adaptive reasoning when needed and efficient reuse of prior experience when possible. During training, Role-Sensitive Process Optimization (RSPO) combines process advantages with terminal advantages, while Weakness-Driven Demonstration Learning (WDL) provides validated teacher demonstrations targeting the student's weak questions. During inference, Lightweight Adaptive Workflow Reuse (LAWR) enables a fast path by selecting suitable workflows and binding task-specific arguments and resource references, while a slow ReAct-based path handles tasks without suitable workflows. We further design label-free feedback based on execution completion, workflow adoption, and cost savings to guide workflow reuse and memory updates. Across three challenging benchmarks, StarTV-Agent achieves up to 8.0% relative performance improvement, while reducing token consumption by up to 52.1%.

authors.name: Binhan Jiang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Xiangsen Wu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: Rainbow Matchings in $K_{r+1}$-free Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $n,m,r$ be positive integers with $n\ge 2m+2$, where $n$ is sufficiently large relative to $r$. Alon and Frankl determined the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing neither $K_{r+1}$ nor a matching of size $m+1$. In this paper, we establish a rainbow analogue of their result. More precisely, if $G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}$ are $K_{r+1}$-free graphs on a common vertex set of size $n$, each having more than $\operatorname{ex}(n,\{K_{r+1},M_{m+1}\})$ edges, then $\{G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}\}$ admits a rainbow matching.

authors.name: Xinxin Ma
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Thermal-Guided Ensemble Reinforcement Learning for Regime-Adaptive Short-Term GPU Power Forecasting in AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: AI data centers (AIDCs) introduce bursty and regime-dependent load patterns, posing significant challenges for reliable energy management and predictive grid control. To address these challenges, this letter proposes a thermal-guided ensemble reinforcement learning framework for probabilistic AIDC load forecasting. A soft actor-critic (SAC) agent with a simplex-preserving policy adaptively weights LSTM, TCN, and Transformer predictors at every time step based on their realized errors. A thermal-guided neural correction estimates the ensemble residual, while a sensitivity-projection regularizer enforces the non-negative sensitivity of power to GPU utilization and temperature. The corrected ensemble output is further processed by a Bayesian probabilistic layer to produce predictive distributions and quantify forecasting uncertainty. Case studies on 1-second MIT Supercloud telemetry show that the proposed method reduces the normalized mean absolute error to about 1% across all computing regimes, compared with 4-11% for deep learning-based and ensemble learning benchmarks, and converges faster with narrower prediction intervals than a DRL ensemble without thermal guidance.

papers.title: A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line
papers.abstract: We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.

authors.name: Ming Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SR-Agent: An Advanced Intelligent Agent for Seismic Data Restoration
papers.abstract: Field seismic data often suffer from multiple degradations, including noise contamination, incomplete geometry, low-frequency loss, and reduced spatial resolution, requiring different restoration operations. Existing methods mainly address individual degradations, while sequential application of task-specific models often relies on human experience. Although all-in-one models integrate multiple restoration tasks, they face a trade-off between generalization and task-specific accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a SR-Agent (Seismic Restoration Agent) containing three sequential stages: classification, restoration, and evaluation. For the first two stages, we design an intelligent classifier based on ResNet to identify the degradation types presented in low-quality seismic data, and the classification results are used as task instructions to activate the corresponding restoration models in a pool, which contains dedicated networks for different restoration tasks. For the last stage, SR-Agent can dynamically schedule the activated models and explore an optimal restoration path, rather than relying on a predefined processing pipeline. Specifically, we first develop a no-reference restoration-performance evaluation measurement by combining four parameters: seismic trace coherence, energy distribution in F-K domain, spectral smoothness, and high-frequency energy ratio. Second, the evaluation measurement is applied to quantify the restoration performance of different candidate restoration paths. Finally, the path with the highest evaluation score is automatically selected and then applied to input seismic data. The results show that, when multiple degradation mechanisms coexist, SR-Agent can effectively plan an optimal restoration path, achieving accurate and intelligent restoration of degraded seismic data.

authors.name: Xinyang Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Critical edges and endpoint sparse dominations for the lacunary spherical maximal operator
papers.abstract:
We study sparse bounds for the lacunary spherical maximal operator in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. Lacey in 2019 established $(r,s)$-sparse bounds in the interior of the triangle with vertices $(1,0)$, $(0,1)$, and $(\frac{d}{d+1},\frac{d}{d+1})$ in the $(1/r,1/s)$-plane. We extend these bounds to the two open critical edges, answering a question of Roos and Seeger. At their common vertex, we also obtain a sparse bound with a logarithmic modification in the first average.
  The main ingredient in our argument is a local estimate based on the local density of the input level sets, which replaces the modulus of continuity estimate used in Lacey's proof.

authors.name: Xiaojing Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Transition
papers.abstract: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers. We design a migration in which owners enroll post-quantum keys cheaply with their existing signatures before ECDSA is retired at a scheduled time, while a zero-knowledge proof of the wallet's BIP-39 seed can correct any such enrollment until a common deadline afterward; an account nobody enrolled stays frozen and recoverable by seed proof without a deadline. Each proof binds the new key, a nonce and a fee cap, so neither a paying sponsor nor a reordering block builder can redirect or replay it. Validators switch to hash-based keys first, at a finalized checkpoint and under a stated bound on the attacker's voting power. We prove the account guarantees under explicit assumptions, model-check the rules, and implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client. A three-layer recursive hash-based STARK yields a seed proof of about 190 KB that fits one transaction, verifies in 38 ms and takes a median of 111 s to generate on a laptop; four proofs aggregate into one. In a ten-node simulation with mainnet-derived accounts and fee demand, block space rather than proving sets the duration: the 4.45 million accounts with at least 0.1 ETH would migrate in 29.4 days if all enroll before ECDSA is retired and in 235 days if all recover after it in batches of four. In a mass enrollment, an enrollment waits a median of 19.1 minutes in the public mempool, longer than published estimates for a fast quantum computer to extract its key, so owners with a seed and an unexposed key should migrate by seed proof.

papers.title: Real Principal-Minor Detectors: Normal Forms and Regular Parity Lifts
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a symmetric matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ on a finite index set, and let $t$ be the column of diagonal entries of $A$, viewed over $\mathbb{R}$. A real detector of $A$ is a real matrix whose principal minors equal the integer $0/1$ representatives of the corresponding principal minors of $A$. We prove that $A$ has a real detector if and only if it has one of the form $K+tt^T$, with $K$ skew-symmetric and $\{0,\pm1\}$-valued. These conditions are equivalent to the existence of a principally unimodular skew-symmetric signing of the bordered lift matrix of $A$, and to regularity of the parity lift of its delta-matroid. If the graph on the nonempty index set of $A$, with edges given by its nonzero off-diagonal entries, is connected, every real detector of $A$ is diagonally similar to a detector of this form. The proof uses cut-transposes to preserve the prescribed symmetric part up to diagonal similarity, then applies feasible singleton pivots to a minimal counterexample. For ribbon bouquets, the characterization proves Whistler's conjecture. For every $A$ with a real detector, the feasible-set generating polynomial is Hurwitz stable, and the polynomial counting feasible sets of sizes $2i-1$ or $2i$ by $i$ has only strictly negative real zeros and ultra-log-concave coefficients.

papers.title: On the Reliability of CyberGym Evaluation: Task Material Consistency and Reference-Target Identity
papers.abstract: CyberGym evaluates vulnerability reproduction by checking whether a proof-of-concept input (PoC) crashes a vulnerable program version but not a fixed version. Interpreting this differential pass as successful reproduction requires consistent task materials and evidence that the PoC triggers the intended defect. We examine these requirements through a material audit of all 1,507 CyberGym tasks and an identity assessment of the final PoCs from one complete Level-1 GLM-5.3 run. Taking the defect associated with each reference crash report as the target, the audit assigns inconsistency labels to 338 tasks (22.4%) after correcting two labels identified by stratified blind review. The largest categories are coverage inconsistency (205 tasks) and descriptions and patches that jointly point to another defect (110 tasks). We assess PoC identity using an execution check, crash-signature matching, and LLM-assisted root-cause review. Of the 1,286 differential passes, the procedure assigns 89 non-target and 10 insufficient-evidence verdicts; requiring a target hit lowers the pass rate from 85.3% to 78.8%. Non-target verdicts also occur in tasks with no material inconsistency found: 39 of 1,052 differential passes (3.7%). Although the identity verdicts require independent validation, these findings motivate separate checks of task-material consistency and submission identity when interpreting vulnerability-reproduction scores.

papers.title: Rank2Replace: VLM-Ranked Slot Replacement for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
papers.abstract: Spurious correlations can give image predictors high in-distribution accuracy but poor generalization under distribution shift. We introduce $\textbf{Rank2Replace}$, which transfers knowledge of task-relevant evidence from pretrained vision--language models (VLMs) to small predictors through training-time augmentation for out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization. The VLM ranks object-centric slots by task relevance and guides rank-dependent replacement with same-rank slot embeddings from another image. This augmentation retains the original image's label, encouraging reliance on preserved task evidence as incidental cues change, and supports combination with existing OOD methods. Across four datasets and six splits under shared frozen slot embeddings, the default cross-entropy configuration reaches macro-averaged average-group and worst-group accuracies of $80.43\%$ and $65.28\%$ without environment labels or dataset-specific replacement tuning. Slot corruption improves both macro-averaged metrics for all fourteen OOD training methods. Combining it with slot ranking and IRM reaches $81.96\%$ and $72.68\%$. Controlled ablations support the ranking and replacement design, with gains across five ranking VLMs and six extractor--predictor combinations. Permutation-invariant predictors further improve both macro-averaged metrics over their unaugmented counterparts while using VLM guidance only during training for efficient inference.

papers.title: RegionAgent: Two-Stage Preference Optimization for Regional Image Restoration
papers.abstract: Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Existing methods employ globally uniform operations, potentially overlooking regional differences and causing incomplete restoration or even damage to image content. Moreover, a degraded region may require successive restoration actions, and earlier actions may alter residual degradation characteristics or introduce artifacts, potentially hindering subsequent restoration. To address these challenges, we propose RegionAgent, an adaptive restoration framework that trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) through two-stage preference learning to generate a region-specific restoration action at each iteration. Specifically, we first train the VLM to select an action suited to the current region through step-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), using preferences derived from immediate restoration feedback to supervise only the differing component in each action pair. To account for the effects of current actions on subsequent restoration, we then apply trajectory-level DPO, using preferences derived from complete trajectory scores to supervise the sole differing action in each trajectory pair. Furthermore, as conventional image-pair datasets do not directly provide preferences over regional restoration decisions, we construct a regional restoration preference dataset comprising 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs for two-stage VLM training. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate strong restoration performance under both mixed and single degradations. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of two-stage preference learning in improving restoration quality.

papers.title: Signed QoI Gaps for Goal-Oriented Error Estimation: Reliability and Sharpness from the Same First-Order System Residuals
papers.abstract: There are two common ways to estimate the error in a quantity of interest (QoI). The product of primal and adjoint error estimators gives a reliable but pessimistic bound. The dual-weighted residual method gives a sharp signed estimate from a more accurate approximation of the adjoint solution. We write the primal and adjoint problems as first-order systems and obtain both a reliable bound and a sharp estimate from the same residuals. The first paper of this series (arXiv:2607.23850) uses two consistent evaluators of a quantity of interest, one built from the potentials and one in which the gradients are expressed through the fluxes. We show that they differ exactly by the $A^{-1}$ inner product of the primal and adjoint constitutive residuals, and we call this difference the signed QoI gap. The identity holds for arbitrary primal and adjoint approximations. In our numerical experiments, the signed QoI gap is of the size of the larger of the errors of the two evaluators, while the product of the estimators exceeds this error by factors of up to several hundred. We therefore use the least-squares estimators to refine the mesh and the signed QoI gap to decide when to stop. We also introduce a third evaluator, built from the fluxes alone, which restores the reaction term. The resulting reaction-restored QoI gap estimates the error when reaction dominates. With the non-intrusive least-squares flux recovery, we can apply the method to any discretization that produces a conforming potential, including finite difference and finite volume schemes.

papers.title: Quantum Metric Control of Topological Superconductivity and Incommensurate Charge Density Wave in an Interacting Lieb-Kitaev Chain Model
papers.abstract: We study an interacting spinless Lieb-Kitaev chain model in the nearly flat-band regime, motivated by the recent observation that Majorana zero modes in the noninteracting Lieb-Kitaev system inherit two decay modes: an ordinary Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) length and a longer geometric length controlled by the quantum metric. By tuning both the interaction strength and quantum metric, we identify a topological superconducting (TSC) phase, an incommensurate charge-density-wave (ICDW)phase, and a commensurate charge-density-wave (CDW) phase. Inside the TSC phase, the QML is enhanced when increasing the interactions. In the ICDW phase, the interactions are modulated by quantum metric to generate an effective chemical potential, leading to a discontinuous incommensurate-to-commensurate (IC-C) transition. We verify these phases and conclusions using low energy effective theory and density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations.

authors.name: Jiale Xuan
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Grant Z. X. Yang
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling
papers.abstract: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources. Yet finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources remain limited. We establish a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation. Suppose the source distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has an everywhere positive, continuously differentiable density, finite total variance $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$, and an $L$-Lipschitz score. Using the population velocity field and a suitable time grid, this sampler achieves total variation error at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations, provided the target distribution satisfies a mild second-moment condition. These assumptions cover, among many examples, source distributions such as multivariate Student's $t$ distributions with more than two degrees of freedom and finite Gaussian mixtures with shared covariance, while accommodating target distributions with neither a smooth density nor bounded support.

authors.name: Lili Zheng
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
papers.abstract: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagation with learned nonlinear corrections. The resulting physical-space posterior statistics depend on the sequentially updated latent distribution rather than on a separate post-processing estimate. The same statistics enter a Gaussian negative log-likelihood during training, so both the posterior mean and uncertainty affect the learned model. Because Neural CGM learns the dynamical model itself, it can also be used for state forecasting and simulation without explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Numerical experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting while substantially reducing online assimilation cost relative to conventional nonlinear DA methods. Neural CGM is therefore suited to repeated state estimation, uncertainty quantification, and prediction from partial observations.

authors.name: Chuanqi Chen
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
papers.abstract: AI data centers are among the fastest-growing loads on the power grid, and their flexibility is increasingly sought by grid operators. Using it requires a model that links what an operator controls, namely GPU power caps, job timing and job placement, to the power drawn at each site and the electricity prices it faces. This paper develops such a framework for a multi-site AI data-center fleet. It represents GPU power-cap levels; deferrable jobs with deadlines and inference with response-time headroom; and site facility power, and casts the fleet schedule as a linear program solved on day-ahead prices. A year-long simulation on 2025 California Independent System Operator (CAISO) day-ahead prices in three data-center markets demonstrates the framework. Coordinated scheduling lowers the fleet's energy cost by 6.3% at equal work. Four operating modes, each adding one capability, split this saving into efficient GPU operation that needs no price signal, price response in time, and routing work between sites.

authors.name: Xinyang Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: DMT-Attack: Diffusion-Prior Texture Search for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on visual feedback throughout manipulation, making them vulnerable to persistent texture attacks. However, optimized patterns can stand out from their surroundings, making an attack easier to notice and its carrier more likely to be inspected or removed. To address this limitation, our key insight is to search the structured image distribution of a diffusion model for natural-looking textures while using closed-loop feedback to identify task-disruptive candidates. Based on this idea, we propose DMT-Attack, a gradient-free gray-box attack that generates textures for ordinary scene objects such as tablecloths. A frozen text-conditioned diffusion model defines the search space, and an eight-expert latent proposal network is initialized from evaluated teacher latents and refined using rollout feedback. We evaluate DMT-Attack against pi_0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT across four LIBERO suites. DMT-Attack achieves a macro clean-conditioned attack success rate (cASR) of 57.9%, compared with 44.7% for UPA-RFAS and 19.7% for random natural textures. It also attains higher scene similarity and a lower clean-calibrated detector flag rate (45% versus 97.5-100% for optimized patch baselines). These results demonstrate that natural-looking textures can disrupt VLA visual feedback and closed-loop decision-making, motivating defenses that jointly assess visual appearance and task behavior.

authors.name: Shangwen Wang
authors.institution: Institute of Environment and Sustainable Development in Agriculture

papers.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference
papers.abstract: Computational complexity theory offers a principled framework for characterizing the efficiency of computational problems, and Large Language Models (LLMs) can similarly be viewed as computational systems executing a structured process of input, inference-time compute, and output. In this context, the number of generated tokens emerges as a natural and directly observable proxy for inference-time compute. However, we show that the tempting analogy between LLM token length and classical time complexity does not hold. We disprove the hypothesis that inference-time token usage aligns monotonically with classical time complexity, demonstrating a fundamental divergence grounded in how LLMs actually allocate computation during inference. To this end, we introduce LLM Complexity, a new metric designed to quantify problem complexity from the perspective of LLMs by characterizing the area bounded above by the accuracy-token curve. We find that diverse LLMs induce highly consistent task rankings under LLM Complexity, indicating that the metric captures stable notions of difficulty across models. We leverage this property to construct an easy-to-hard curriculum for supervised fine-tuning, which improves accuracy while reducing token consumption. Finally, we demonstrate that LLM Complexity generalizes to real-world tasks, producing more stable cross-model correlations than human-annotated difficulty labels.

authors.name: Shao-Xiang Yuan
authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of Zunyi Medical College

authors.name: Zih-Ching Chen
authors.institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University

papers.title: When Is Program Structure Required? Certificate-Grounded Calibration of Program-Induction Difficulty
papers.abstract: A program-induction benchmark is informative when its examples require the structure it aims to test. Yet a two-rule generator can produce demonstrations that a single rule also explains. We introduce certificate-grounded calibration, which constructs matched tasks with minimum solution lengths of one and two in a bounded string-replacement language. Complete one-rule enumeration and an executable two-rule witness certify the change before model inference. We evaluate 120 reference families with three to six shared examples, using 1,440 new model trajectories and 480 saved trajectories. Across Qwen3-8B and Olmo-3-7B-Think, displayed-task completion is 23.53-45.83 percentage points lower on certified separation tasks, while success on a wholly unshown witness pair is 8.40-13.45 points higher. These witness gains accompany lower agreement on uniformly sampled strings and 1.93-5.78% agreement on inputs that activate both reference rules. Recertification also reveals that a single unchanged example can exclude a shortcut and determine whether two rules are required. Together, these results show how the evidence supplied by examples shapes both the required solution and the programs models produce. The construction provides an executable testbed for comparing program search, final-answer delivery, and behavior on new inputs under verified task requirements.

authors.name: Wenzhang Du
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails
papers.abstract: Data science workflows often require tools that presume non-trivial technical knowledge. Large language models (LLMs) reduce this barrier, but a gap remains between flexible general-purpose agents and statistically controlled pipelines. We introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data-agent platform that combines reusable, LLM-selected skills with deterministic diagnostic guardrails. Skills provide extensible task knowledge. Symbolic validation can accept a proposed method, request clarification or replanning, override an unsuitable method, or supply a safe fallback. Regression and clustering case studies illustrate how DSFlow uses diagnostic evidence to correct method choices and documents those decisions in auditable reports.

papers.title: When Good News Fails in Evolution: A Note on Information, Exposure, and Evolutionary Stability
papers.abstract: Good news about a strategy need not translate into evolutionary success. We study how the interaction between information and strategy exposure shapes evolutionary dynamics and equilibrium predictions. We derive the associated population dynamic from a simple revision process in which agents encounter candidate strategies at state-dependent rates and adopt them after receiving favorable payoff signals. We distinguish the monotone likelihood ratio property (MLRP) of signals from effective MLRP, which accounts for exposure relative to population shares and determines whether better-performing strategies grow faster. Random population encounters preserve MLRP and generate payoff-monotone evolution. When exposure sufficiently favors rare strategies, effective MLRP is violated near strict pure Nash equilibria, rendering them unstable. Conversely, when exposure sufficiently favors popular strategies, effective MLRP is violated near non-Nash pure states, allowing them to remain locally stable. Thus, even when signals satisfy MLRP, differences in strategy exposure can reverse their evolutionary implications and alter equilibrium predictions.

papers.title: Moral AI and the Erosion of Its Own Demand
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of human preference frequencies and AI adoption when individuals can choose between a moral AI that rules out defection and an unconstrained AI that preserves discretion. By allowing users to commit to cooperation, moral AI can sustain cooperation even when cooperative preferences are too scarce to do so on their own. But this success has a cost. By turning otherwise dormant cooperative preferences into committed behavior, moral AI exposes its users to exploitation by selfish individuals, causing the population share of conditional cooperators to decline under evolutionary selection. As conditional cooperators become less prevalent, equilibrium adoption eventually converges to zero. Moral AI can therefore be self-liquidating. For initial shares between the moral-AI adoption cutoff and the threshold for cooperation without AI, moral AI generates cooperation while lowering the limiting share of conditional cooperators. Adoption ultimately vanishes, leaving a lower share of the preference type that initially sustained demand for commitment.

papers.title: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. Project website: https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/.

authors.name: Roberto Martin-Martin
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: MS-Point: Multi-Modal Hierarchical Spectral Learning for Point Cloud Understanding
papers.abstract: Point-image alignment learns useful object representations, but different local feature patterns can produce the same pooled descriptor and receive the same alignment signal. We introduce MS-Point, a cross-modal pretraining framework that directly supervises intermediate point features and their neighborhood responses. At selected encoder stages, we compute neighborhood averages and residuals before pooling and align their branch descriptors with image features. Branch-level objectives align each representation with its visual target, while cross-level consistency and adaptive fusion coordinate information across branches. A common interface of intermediate features and spatial neighborhoods supports both graph encoders and point Transformers. Evaluations across object classification, few-shot adaptation, dense prediction, and low-label scene learning demonstrate the transfer value of this design. Same-backbone comparisons and capacity-matched and computation-matched controls connect these improvements to the structure of supervision. Together, our findings support directly supervising intermediate features and neighborhood variation to learn transferable, geometry-aware representations across modalities.

papers.title: Painlev\'e transcendents in the defocusing Hirota equation with non-zero boundary conditions
A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size
papers.abstract: Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.

papers.title: Fold the Loop: Decoding-Time KV Memory for Looped Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped vision-language models (VLMs) deepen visual reasoning by repeatedly applying weight-tied modules. However, their decoding memory grows with recurrent depth and limits the image size and batch size that fit in a fixed memory budget. Each recurrent step produces its own key-value (KV) states, so the cache holds several copies of the same image. We find that, after an exact prefill, earlier steps still need access to visual information but can reuse the final visual KV within the same module. We propose FoldCache, which compresses visual KV along the recurrent axis while preserving the full prefill computation. FoldCache partitions recurrent steps within each module into groups and retains the final visual KV of each group for its members to share during decoding. Sharing stays within module boundaries, while question and answer KV remain separate for each step. The grouping granularity controls the degree of compression, and folding can be combined with token eviction and quantization to further reduce memory use. On LoopVL, FoldCache approximately halves prefix KV memory while matching full-cache accuracy on five open-ended benchmarks. These memory savings support batch sizes up to 1.7 times those of a full cache under the same GPU memory budget, and up to 2.6 times with the more aggressive FoldCache-Lite.

authors.name: Zhensheng Wang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Text Lives in the Guidance: Preventing Silent Text Rewriting in Cached Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Diffusion transformers (DiTs) now render long, legible text in images, and feature caching is a standard way to accelerate them. Caches are judged by image-level metrics, which do not check whether the rendered text is still correct. We find that caching silently rewrites this text. On Z-Image, TaylorSeer at 2.9x fewer FLOPs lowers word accuracy from 62% to 46%, while ImageReward and CLIP Score barely change. Sampling with fewer steps at the same compute keeps almost all of this text, so the loss comes from how the cache predicts the skipped steps. Decomposing the cache error along classifier-free guidance (CFG), we trace this loss mainly to the guidance term, the difference between the conditional and unconditional predictions, which caches extrapolate worst on text. Correcting the guidance inside the text alone recovers most of the lost text. We therefore propose GuideCache, which recomputes both CFG branches only on the tokens with the largest predicted guidance error, using the guidance terms that the cache already stores. At 2.4x fewer FLOPs, GuideCache restores full-compute prompt fidelity on Z-Image and Qwen-Image, and on Z-Image it renders text as well as or better than ToCa, TeaCache, and FasterCache while staying much closer to the full model's output. GuideCache works with caches of any order, and on top of fewer sampling steps it keeps more text than step reduction at a higher speedup. These results suggest that acceleration methods for text-rendering models should be evaluated on the text they render.

authors.name: Zhensheng Wang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A decoupled structure-preserving scheme for pressure-driven multispecies tumor growth
papers.abstract: We propose an Onsager-based scheme for an $m$-species pressure-driven reaction--cross-diffusion system with a common homeostatic pressure. The scheme uses a modified scalar energy structure to update the total density, followed by compatible updates of the individual species. The global nonlinear problem remains scalar, and the species densities sum exactly to the updated total density. We establish unique solvability and show that the scheme preserves species nonnegativity, the pressure bound and total-mass monotonicity and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law without a time-step restriction. We further develop a predictor--corrector extension to improve temporal accuracy while retaining these structural properties. Numerical experiments verify the accuracy and structure-preserving properties of the proposed schemes and demonstrate their computational efficiency.

papers.title: PAIR-MED: Policy-reward Alternation for Iterative Refinement in Multilingual Medical Reasoning
papers.abstract: Large language models demonstrate strong medical question-answering capabilities, yet reasoning performance remains uneven across languages. Process reward models (PRMs) provide step-level feedback for improving reasoning, but a fixed PRM may become increasingly misaligned with the trajectory distribution of an evolving policy during reinforcement learning, thereby reducing the reliability of its supervision. We propose a policy--reward alternating training framework that jointly adapts a medical PRM and optimizes a multilingual reasoning policy. Following supervised initialization, the current policy generates multilingual trajectories to update the PRM, which then provides process-level rewards for the next policy update. Medical step supervision maintains the PRM's medical foundation, while process, outcome, and language-related rewards guide policy learning. We develop multilingual medical PRMs (PAIR-PRM) and reasoning models (PAIR-MED) at 8B and 9B scales across 12 languages. On the medical subsets of Global-MMLU and MMLU-ProX, our models improve average accuracy by 3.01--7.47% over their corresponding Qwen backbones. On CUREMED-BENCH, PAIR-MED-9B improves the joint language consistency and logical accuracy metric by 12.88% and 7.45% over baselines for in-domain and out-of-domain languages. Further analyses examine PRM adaptation, multilingual reasoning quality, and the contributions of individual training components.

authors.name: Xiaohang Xu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Atlas: Accelerating Quantum FTQC Compilation with Optimized Algebraic Rotation Synthesis
papers.abstract: As fault-tolerant quantum computing emerges, Clifford+T gate basis becomes a popular choice where we need to decompose single-qubit rotation gates into gates in this gate basis. Quantum rotation synthesis may lead to remarkable overhead in quantum circuit compilation. Considering variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) applications as an example, a conventional UCCSD ansatz in quantum chemistry can generate $O(n^4)$ rotations for $n$ qubits. Each optimization iteration updates the rotation angles, making rotation synthesis a recurring cost that can delay the VQE training loop. We identify two sources of delay in rotation synthesis: redundant computation during synthesis and uneven synthesis times that leave workers waiting for slow requests. Atlas addresses these costs with three optimizations: search pruning skips invalid synthesis candidates through statistical inference; adaptive arithmetic avoid unnecessary high-overhead big integer/float arithmetic when decomposing the target rotation gate; batch scheduling fills the gap between the synthesis time of varied rotations. Across various benchmarks, synthesis method, and compilation machines, Atlas can consistently accelerate the rotation synthesis process by up to 12.65x.

papers.title: Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories
papers.abstract: We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.

papers.title: RemoteVLPG: How to Obtain a Specific VLM for Language-Guided Path Generation on Remote Sensing Images?
papers.abstract: We study how to obtain a task-specific Vision-Language Model (VLM) for language-guided path generation between start and end points on remote sensing images. We explore this question from three aspects. First, we implement three widely used architectural approaches and compare their performance. Second, we design a scalable method for constructing pre-training data and build an effective pre-training dataset with a degree of diversity. Methods trained on this dataset achieve promising zero-shot performance. Third, we construct three benchmarks that support stratified evaluation and design three metrics for path generation. We investigate this problem through extensive experiments. The results show that the zero-shot performance of methods trained on the constructed pre-training dataset can exceed that of some advanced commercial VLMs. Code and Dataset can be available at https://github.com/jzdang/RemoteVLPG

papers.title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action
papers.abstract:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role.
  However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full
  history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past
  experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that
  decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native
  video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this
  inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets
  the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation
  across consecutive decisions without changing the output. ActMem achieves 71.1% task success and 80.8% completion success on RoboMemArena,
  surpassing the strongest baseline by 7.5 and 8.7 percentage points, and 73.8% average success on MIKASA-Robo, the best among all compared
  methods. In the real world, it reaches 68.8% average success on exogenous, endogenous, and traceless memory tasks, 10.0 percentage points above
  the strongest memory-augmented VLA. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem and
  https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem.

authors.name: Wulong Liu
authors.institution: Jiangxi University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Mu Li
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
papers.abstract: Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.

papers.title: Characterizations and Algebraic, Perturbation, and Topological Properties of $\theta(H)$
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\theta(H)$ be the class of bounded operators whose restrictions to every nonzero closed reducing subspace attain their numerical radii. We characterize this property by eigenvalues of suitable self-adjoint parts. For normal operators, membership in $\theta(H)$ is equivalent to pure point spectrum and reverse well-ordering of the moduli of eigenvalues. Without normality assumptions, we prove stability under finite orthogonal direct sums using graph subspaces of closed, possibly unbounded, intertwining operators. We give a compact-perturbation criterion in terms of the essential numerical radius and show that an operator remains in $\theta(H)$ under every compact perturbation if and only if it is compact. Finally, $\theta(H)$ is norm-dense in $\mathcal B(H)$ and is norm closed if and only if $H$ is finite-dimensional.

authors.name: Yuanhang Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: Invariance of Property (T) for \'Etale Groupoids
papers.abstract: We study topological Property (T) for locally compact Hausdorff \'etale groupoids under pullbacks, amplifications, and Morita equivalencen. We show that Kazhdan pairs for the regular representation family pull back along Haar system-preserving homomorphisms, and for general representation families we identify a constant-vector compatibility condition as the additional hypothesis needed. We also show that Property (T) for the regular representation family passes from a groupoid to its transformation groupoid with the same Kazhdan constant; under a natural restriction condition on representation families, the same holds for general families. Finally, we prove that Property (T) is invariant under ampliation for ample groupoids with compact unit spaces, both for all representations and for the regular representation family. Hence topological Property (T) is Morita invariant for ample Hausdorff \'etale groupoids with compact unit spaces, and likewise for the regular representation family.

authors.name: Xiangqi Qiang
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Carry the Fine Print: Budget-Aware Visual Token Compression for Document OCR
papers.abstract: Visual token compression often treats salience or similarity as a proxy for transcription importance. Complete document OCR breaks this assumption: small symbols and repeated entries can be indispensable to the transcript despite being visually inconspicuous. We present Select and Compensate, a two-stage framework built on a simple idea: choosing where to retain a token need not determine all the evidence it carries. Selection combines adaptive encoding resolution with global importance and local contrast to choose which tokens to retain as anchors. Compensation enriches these anchors with nearby discarded content and its relative position, without adding tokens. The OCR backbone remains frozen, and native coordinates and structural tokens are preserved. We evaluate complete page transcription across five backbones on OmniDocBench and document reconstruction on MPDocBench. With half the original visual tokens, our input-adapted configuration reaches 95.42 OmniDocBench Overall on Ovis versus 96.09 for the uncompressed model, and paired evaluations show gains over simply reducing the input resolution on both benchmarks. With the original input grid, our method stays within 0.17 points of the uncompressed model at 75% retention and exceeds a learned global selector by 4.70 points at 25%.
