In practice, however, the robots rarely operate in the same conditions: an open aisle is far easier to navigate than a cluttered room, and takes less learning to master. Standard federated aggregation rules ignore this. Uniform averaging weights every client equally, whether or not it is still learning, and weighting by episode return is worse, since easy environments permit high returns by construction. Both failures stem from what we call the \emph{plateau problem}: once a client masters its environment, its updates carry little new information even though its reported return remains high. We propose \emph{FedDIA}, which scores each client by how much its local training improves the global model it received, amplified by the difficulty of its environment. Difficulty is inferred from the model's own performance, without requiring any description of the environment. Both signals are measured against the global model, so they are comparable across clients. On a mapless navigation task with eight heterogeneous clients, FedDIA reaches a mean success rate of $75.5\%$ across training and held-out environments, against $68.7\%$ for the strongest federated baseline. Its advantage holds when the models are transferred to hand-authored warehouse and living-space layouts, or when one of the clients is defective.

papers.title: Towards High-Fidelity Learned Video Compression
papers.abstract: Professional video workflows operate at qualities that learned video codecs do not reach. We measure how much of a professional quality range a codec covers, from the lowest quality of the standard test conditions, VVC at QP 37, to the highest 4:2:2 grade of the production codec ProRes. To compare inter-frame coding alone, every codec receives original frames as references at the intra positions. On 10-bit YCbCr 4:2:2 test sequences, four recent learned codecs cover 24 to 38% of this range. Their encoders are feed-forward networks with a fixed latent capacity, the number of latent values per sample, of at most 0.25, and removing their quantization raises the quality by at most 1 dB. We propose a learned inter-frame codec whose encoder searches, as the encoders of conventional codecs do. It searches block motion, which a learned network refines, and it searches among learned block transforms whose latent capacity ranges up to 1, selecting the partition, the skip decisions, and the quantized coefficients by a rate-distortion cost. Our codec reaches the upper end of the range on all six sequences. With all residual blocks fixed to 16x16, whose latent capacity is 0.25, the same codec covers 55% of the range, with or without quantization.

authors.name: Yongseong Kim
authors.institution: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety

papers.title: The rigidity phenomenon for weighted composition operators on the Fock spaces
papers.abstract: We establish the rigidity of canonical sums of any finite number of weighted composition operators acting from a Fock space $\mathcal{F}^p$ into another $\mathcal{F}^q$ for all possible combinations of \(p,q\in (0, \infty]\). Specifically, we show that such a sum is bounded (compact, resp.) if and only if its summands are individually bounded (compact, resp.). In the case \(p\le q\), we present two independent approaches -- one analytic and one largely algebraic -- based on some common preliminary rigidity results. As a natural byproduct of our approach, we also obtain the Reproducing Kernel Thesis.

papers.title: Additive Fr\'echet Regression for Random Objects
papers.abstract: Regression analysis for complex data taking values in a general metric space has gained increasing attention in recent years, particularly in the context of Fr\'echet regression with Euclidean predictors $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. However, local Fr\'echet regression, while more flexible than global Fr\'echet regression, suffers from the curse of dimensionality for the case of multivariate predictors. To address this issue while maintaining model flexibility, we introduce a framework of additive structured nonparametric regression when responses are situated in a general metric space. Overcoming the challenge of the lack of vector space structure in general metric spaces where the responses reside requires a novel approach that incorporates the additive structure via projection operators. This leads to a unified framework of additive regression for a wide range of response types, including one-dimensional distributions in Wasserstein space, network data represented by graph Laplacians and spherical data equipped with geodesic distances, among others. We establish pointwise and uniform consistency, including convergence rates, for the proposed additive Fr\'echet regression estimators, using smooth backfitting. The practical utility of this additive model is demonstrated through applications to brain connectivity network analysis using resting-state fMRI data and distributional physical activity data.

papers.title: Star decomposition of complete multipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We study minimum degree-sum conditions for decompositions into stars of sizes $k$ and $k+1$, where $k\ge3$. Write $\sigma(G)=\min_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)+d(v))$, and let $c_k$ be the least integer threshold guaranteeing a $\{K_{1,k},K_{1,k+1}\}$-decomposition for every finite simple graph. Using Tarsi's sufficient condition, we prove that $K_n$ admits such a decomposition whenever $n\ge2k$. Together with the obstruction $K_{2k-1}$ of Zhao and Wu, this gives the optimal integer threshold $4k-3$ for complete graphs. For complete multipartite graphs, we establish the sufficiency of $\sigma(G)\ge9$ when $k=3$ by a finite computational verification and an extension argument. For every $k\ge3$, the complete tripartite graph $G_k=K_{k^2-k-1,k-2,1}$ satisfies $\sigma(G_k)=k^2-1$ and has no such decomposition. Consequently, $c_k\ge k^2$, even when the class is restricted to complete multipartite graphs. The optimal integer threshold in this class is therefore $9$ for $k=3$. Sufficiency of $\sigma(G)\ge k^2$ for complete multipartite graphs with $k\ge4$, and the exact values of $c_k$ for general graphs, remain open in this study.

papers.title: Rational multisections and unirationality of supersingular K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that every supersingular K3 surface of Artin invariant at most nine is unirational, confirming the question of Artin, Rudakov, Shafarevich and Shioda outside the generic case of Artin invariant ten. In odd characteristic, we reduce the question to Artin invariant nine and sweep out the K3 surface by Abel--Jacobi images of rational multisections of its Artin--Tate twists which vary along the supersingular twistor line.

authors.name: Haitao Zou
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: ICARE: cross-domain text classification with incremental class-aware representation and distillation learning
papers.abstract: The rise of powerful, fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) necessitates robust natural language inference (NLI) systems. These NLI systems ideally train across various tasks, encompassing diverse concepts like sentiment analysis, news classification, and coreference resolution. However, this continual, multi-tasking approach can lead to catastrophic forgetting, where previously learned tasks are lost, especially in domains lacking specific labels. Rehearsing past examples with labels can further exacerbate this issue by causing overfitting, hindering the system's ability to classify new categories. To tackle these challenges, this research proposes ICARE, a novel framework with two key components: an instance selection module and a knowledge distillation method. The former is based on representation learning, which meticulously selects training examples to present to the NLI system. The latter, knowledge distillation with feature and logit-level transfer, facilitates knowledge transfer between tasks. This leverages pruning techniques and optimized objective functions to transfer both essential feature-level and decision-making (logit-level) knowledge, mitigating catastrophic forgetting while adapting to new patterns. Extensive evaluations on benchmark text classification datasets have demonstrated ICARE's effectiveness. The framework achieves a significant improvement in target accuracy and reduction in the ``forgetting metric''. These results solidify ICARE's ability to preserve and leverage learned knowledge across diverse tasks, ultimately enhancing the adaptability and performance of NLI systems. The source code is available at https://github.com/CongSon01/ICARE_NLP.git

authors.name: Hai-Anh Tran
authors.institution: Trường Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Nội

papers.title: Prescribed Bayesian Efficiency under Lifetime Adjustment Costs
papers.abstract: A Bayesian learner may retain an issued action while updating its posterior, trading predictive loss against adjustment charges. We assume population curvature, boundary control, an order-$1/n$ lower bound on expected posterior uncertainty about the optimal action, and an observable unbiased gradient witness whose squared norms are uniformly integrable. Sample losses may be unbounded or nonconvex. Cumulative expected excess measures the loss increase relative to current predictive Bayes actions. For bounded nonnegative nondecreasing charges $c$ with $c(0)=0$ and nondecreasing profiles $G: \mathbb{N} \to [1,\infty)$ with $G(J)=o(J)$, we characterize joint attainability of cumulative expected excess $O(G(J))$ at horizons $T=2^J$ and finite expected lifetime charge. Here $J$ indexes logarithmic time. The criterion is finiteness of a prefix-constrained allocation of tracking-error allowances across action-distance scales, equivalently its decreasing-weight dual. Adaptive timing and private randomization do not enlarge the attainable region. For each feasible pair, a horizon-independent deterministic checkpoint policy attains the profile with lifetime-cost moments of every positive order. For excess $O((\log T)^r)$, $0<r<1$, every policy needs $\Omega((\log T)^{2-r})$ revisions in expectation, and a charge-independent schedule achieves a matching pathwise upper bound for every feasible charge. We verify the assumptions for logistic decision models with nondegenerate covariates, finite second moments and a locally positive smooth prior density, including fixed-ridge models with unbounded parameter priors.

papers.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan
papers.abstract: For each fixed $k$, iterative-width search finds optimal plans in polynomial time on tasks of bounded tuple-chain width, but the approximability of planning width has remained open even when an optimal plan is supplied. When all optimal plans visit the same state sequence, we characterize set and chain width as hitting numbers of competing states. We construct positive-precondition STRIPS tasks with a supplied unique optimal plan, a single reachable goal state, binary branching, and constant-size actions. Every reachable state lies on a goal-reaching execution at most one action longer than optimal, yet distinguishing width $1$ from $\Theta(N)$, where $N$ is the number of atoms, is NP-hard for set, chain, and goal-admissible width. Unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$, no polynomial-time algorithm achieves a one-sided approximation factor $o(N)$ or a symmetric factor $o(\sqrt{N})$, and simple estimates attain both orders. For positive-precondition tasks with a supplied unique optimal plan of length at least two, testing set or chain width against a threshold $k\geq 1$ is coNP-complete for each fixed $k$ and $\Sigma_2^{\mathrm{P}}$-complete when $k$ is part of the input. Both results also hold for goal-admissible width if only one goal state is reachable. On an explicit state graph, a greedy algorithm approximates set width within a logarithmic factor even when optimal plans branch. Thus, knowing an optimal plan does not eliminate the difficulty of certifying substantially smaller width.

papers.title: Exact finite-time fluctuation-response relations for Markov processes: A martingale framework
papers.abstract: Fluctuations and responses of time-integrated observables are both experimentally measurable, and relations between them can reveal the dissipation that sustains a nonequilibrium state. Here we develop a martingale framework that gives exact finite-time fluctuation-response identities for additive observables of general Markov processes. We obtain an exact identity for the variance of an observable in terms of its Doob martingale, which splits the total variance into a part inherited from the initial ensemble and a part generated by noise during the observation. We show that, at fixed preparation, the response of the mean of the observable to any admissible perturbation is the covariance between the Doob martingale and a second martingale that represents the perturbation. For diffusions and jump processes, a single martingale amplitude determines both the fluctuations and the response of the observable. These identities yield inequalities, variational principles, and multivariate and frequency-domain bounds, whose costs are set by the corresponding physical perturbations. Applying the framework to underdamped dynamics, we obtain a friction-response thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR) that can be saturated at any finite time and thus gives a variational principle for the entropy production. We also demonstrate exponentially strong violations of the conventional TUR by velocity-resolved currents, even in linear Gaussian dynamics, and derive a weak-noise dissipation-coherence bound for limit cycles, which shows that inertial oscillators can beat the overdamped bound only if their frequency is weakly sensitive to friction. For overdamped dynamics and jump processes, the framework recovers and extends recent fluctuation-response identities and identifies when the corresponding uncertainty relations are saturated.

authors.name: Van Tuan Vo
authors.institution: Nong Lam University Ho Chi Minh City

papers.title: MATE: Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution for Safe and Efficient Mobile Control
papers.abstract: Mobile agents on personal smartphones can affect private data, payments, settings, and the foreground screen. We present MATE (Mobile Agent Trustworthy Execution), an execution-layer system that controls the boundary between agent action proposals and device effects without modifying the underlying model. MATE represents each UI primitive as a structured action record that combines the instruction, target app, screen context, primitive, and action fields. Runtime Guardrail (RG) maps this record to an allow, block, or user-approval decision; Predefined Task Routing (PTR) serves recurring requests through verified routes with post-execution screen checks; and a floating interface keeps execution in a compact overlay. On MobileSafetyBench, MATE raises high-risk blocking from 29.7% to 97.0% under GPT-4o. On AndroidWorld, it reduces LLM calls by up to 6x and raises recurring-use task success to 95.7%.

authors.name: Changick Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Stationary causal enhancements of fractional Brownian motion at small Hurst indices
papers.abstract: We construct stationary, complete-past causal geometric enhancements of prescribed multidimensional fractional Brownian motion for every $0<H\leq1/4$. They retain the first level, are exactly self-similar, and commute with linear coordinate maps. The construction removes a remote-past cutoff from Volterra signatures. At reciprocal indices $H=1/N$, a lagged top-degree logarithmic-velocity subtraction yields a quantitative joint cutoff and zero-lag limit with sharp moment bounds. Centered velocities and white-noise localization provide the critical cancellation. The limit is stable under weak concentration at zero of deterministic mass-one signed lag profiles on a common bounded lag range, with uniformly bounded total variation. Top-central perturbations give nonuniqueness at nonreciprocal indices, preserving all lower levels and symmetries. At reciprocal indices, square-integrable whole-line causal extensions with fixed lower levels and common-noise shift and scaling identities differ by a deterministic central drift. Logarithmic centering removes this drift. The enhancements yield controlled integration, rough differential equations, a finite-word regularity-structure model and an adapted realization by ordinary signatures.

papers.title: Uniform Positivity of the $F$-Signature and Pure Descent of klt Singularities
papers.abstract: In this paper, we affirmatively answer the question of Carvajal-Rojas, Schwede, and Tucker on the uniform positivity of the $F$-signature, and prove a converse. Namely, given a klt type singularity, we establish uniform lower bounds on the $F$-signatures of its reductions mod $p$ for $p$ sufficiently large. Conversely, if the $F$-signatures of the reductions of a normal singularity are uniformly bounded below by a positive constant on large primes, we prove that the singularity is of klt type. As an application, we give a new reduction-mod-$p$ proof of Zhuang's theorem that klt type singularities descend along pure morphisms.

papers.title: Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: Memory consumption of the key-value (KV) cache remains a central bottleneck for long-context LLM inference. We introduce PRKV, a training-free KV eviction method that estimates multi-hop global token importance by applying Personalized PageRank over attention-induced transition graphs. This enables importance propagation beyond recency or instantaneous attention, without modifying the model. We benchmark PRKV on long-context understanding, sparse retrieval, and chain-of-thought reasoning tasks using multiple LLM families. Under moderate to aggressive compression ratios, including up to 90%, PRKV achieves competitive task performance against established eviction baselines while reducing peak memory usage with low end-to-end overhead. These results demonstrate that multi-hop global influence estimation yields a favorable accuracy--memory trade-off for scalable long-context inference.

authors.name: Noseong Park
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
papers.abstract: Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.

papers.title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
papers.abstract: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. Yet despite producing increasingly realistic videos, current world models often fail to capture how small action changes affect future observations. This limits their use in tasks such as robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning, where nearly identical actions can lead to qualitatively different outcomes. To address this, we propose AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective for learning the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations. Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation. We then train the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state. Across OGBench simulation and real-world DROID and ALOHA-2 setups, AFFECT makes world-model rollouts more faithful to real outcomes. On DROID, the Pearson correlation between policy success rates in the world model and on the real robot rises from 0.47 to 0.79, alongside up to 23% lower FVD. These gains carry over to planning, where selecting actions with AFFECT-trained world models improves task success by up to 8.3%.

authors.name: Yonghoon Dong
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jinwoo Shin
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: SEOYUN: Refusal-Inducing Exam Documents for AI-Glasses Pipelines
papers.abstract: Camera-equipped glasses can convert an examination page into a query to a vision-language model (VLM). Device detection addresses possession; a complementary question is whether an examination document can reduce the usefulness of an unauthorized capture. We present SEOYUN, an application-specific framework for refusal-inducing exam documents, with optical and encoder-level interventions as extensions. We use reverse jailbreaking to describe the direction of the objective: inducing abstention rather than bypassing refusal. Refusal induction and defensive visual prompt injection already have precedents; our contribution is a threat model, analytical limits, and an evaluation protocol for examination use. We distinguish refusal from correct-answer leakage, show why removing an added dummy option is not itself a reduction in the original answer space, and derive a sampling comparison under explicitly stated camera assumptions. The protocol separates digital, simulated, and physical inputs and requires held-out evaluation after subject-specific selection. A local CSAT candidate corpus and rendering harness have been prepared, but this version reports no model-performance measurements, physical validation, or human-subject results. Accordingly, SEOYUN is a research framework, not a validated defense or a basis for allegations against individuals.

authors.name: Dohyeon Kwon
authors.institution: Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science

papers.title: NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agentic tasks require a model to call tools over many steps at contexts of 100K tokens or more, yet many low-bit quantization methods are calibrated on short web text and judged on perplexity. This mismatch is costly: existing quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B at or below 3 bits per weight match BF16 on shorter tasks like AIME, yet in published results solve at most 72% as many tasks as BF16 on DeepSWE, a long-horizon agentic benchmark. We propose NariQ, a trellis-coded post-training quantization method that calibrates on tokens generated by the BF16 model in agent sessions. On Qwen3.8-27B, NariQ at 3.0 and 2.5 bits per weight stays level with BF16 on two long-horizon agentic benchmarks, DeepSWE and Terminal Bench, as well as on AIME and RealWorldQA. Our checkpoint at 2.0 bits per weight trails this performance. To our knowledge, these are the first quantizations at or below 3 bits per weight shown to match their full-precision version on long-horizon agentic tasks. We release the files as Qwen3.8-27B-NariQ-GGUF (https://huggingface.co/nari-labs/Qwen3.8-27B-NariQ-GGUF), with inference available through our llama.cpp fork at https://github.com/nari-labs/nari-llama.cpp.

papers.title: Algebraic independence of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms via period interpretations
papers.abstract: Based on Hartl's de Rham-crystalline comparison isomorphism, we formulate a notion of Andr\'{e}'s $v$-adic periods for a class of Anderson $\mathbb{F}_q[z]$-motives with respect to a degree-one finite place $v$ of a rational function field over a finite field, following Ancona-Fr\u{a}\c{t}il\u{a}'s formulation of $p$-adic periods. The formulation naturally produces deformation series of the resulting periods and Frobenius difference equations satisfied by these series. We then explain how the formulation brings the resulting $v$-adic periods within the scope of Chen's $v$-adic ABP criterion and of difference Galois theory, and gives us a strategy to study the transcendence degrees of $v$-adic periods through their deformation series. We show that certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms can be expressed in terms of Andr\'e's $v$-adic periods. Applying the strategy to these examples, we obtain algebraic independence results for certain special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms; more precisely, the transcendence degree of the field generated by a suitable collection of special values of $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms is one less than the transcendence degree of the field generated by the corresponding special values of $\infty$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms together with the Carlitz period.

papers.title: Lower-Mass Giants Can Spare Inner Planets during High-Eccentricity Migration
papers.abstract: The survival of an inner planet next to a close-in giant is commonly used to argue against high-eccentricity migration (HEM), because the eccentric giant is expected to destabilize the inner system. Existing survival calculations have concentrated on Jupiter-mass migrants, although several Jupiter-sized close-in giants with nearby companions have sub-Jovian masses. We use dissipative three-body integrations to measure the collision-survival boundary at seven giant masses from $0.25$ to $1.0,M_{\rm Jup}$ and combine it with uncompressed equilibrium-tide circularization times. At fixed physical periapse, lower giant mass weakens the forcing of the inner orbit and shifts the survival boundary inward. It also shortens the circularization time for a common radius and tidal prescription. These dynamical and tidal limits enclose a viable HEM region in which a sub-Jovian giant can circularize within a system age while retaining an ultra-short-period companion. We screen known companion-hosting close-in giants and perform system-specific integrations of WASP-132; every current candidate lies outside the region. A future system inside it would show directly that HEM can produce a close-in giant while preserving an inner planet, converting companion survival into positive evidence for this formation channel.

papers.title: Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition
papers.abstract: Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different under the full slip condition when the body is axially symmetric. If, in particular, the body is a ball, we then apply the linear theory developed above to the nonlinear initial value problem to show the stability of the rest state. It is, furthermore, asymptotically stable except for the full slip case.

papers.title: Semiclassical Averaging and Temporal Fluctuations of Quantum Dark Solitons in the Lieb-Liniger Model
papers.abstract: We study the time evolution of quantum dark-soliton states of the Lieb--Liniger model, introduced by Sato--Kanamoto--Kaminishi--Deguchi as equal-weight superpositions of one-hole yrast states, and their relation to Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) solitons. We consider a simultaneous weak-coupling and large-system limit in which the repulsive coupling constant $c$ tends to zero and the particle number $N$ and ring circumference $L$ tend to infinity, with the mean density $\bar n=N/L$ and scaled circumference $\Lambda=L\sqrt{c\bar n}$ fixed. We conjecture that, in this limit, the normalized quantum density and its evolution at fixed scaled time $\tau=c\bar n t$ are described by a canonical-momentum average of normalized periodic one-soliton GP densities, each evolving at its own velocity. We explicitly parametrize the GP family by canonical momentum and provide numerical evidence for this correspondence. The different velocities explain the spreading of the averaged density notch despite shape preservation by individual solitons. In the infinite-line limit, we derive an analytic expression for the initial averaged profile, establish an inverse-fifth-power decay of its density deficit with distance from the soliton center, and express the Fourier transform of its deviation from the background as a series of Bickley--Naylor functions $\operatorname{Ki}_3$. Following the spreading of the initial notch, we investigate temporal density fluctuations of the quantum dark solitons and propose a relation between long-time mode variances and second moments of GP Fourier coefficients, supported by numerical comparisons of individual mode variances and the total variance. Yrast transition frequencies distinguish the initial dephasing time scale from the longer scale associated with finite-time averaging of fluctuations.

authors.name: Kohei Motegi
authors.institution: Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology

papers.title: Scattering Circular Dichroism from Spatially Modulated Anisotropic Magnetic Dipoles in BiFeO$_3$
papers.abstract: Antiferromagnets with broken time-reversal symmetry, including altermagnets, have attracted growing interest because they can exhibit ferromagnet-like responses, such as the anomalous Hall effect and magneto-optical effects, despite their compensated spin structures. Such time-reversal symmetry breaking is characterized by ferroic time-reversal-odd multipoles, distinct from the conventional spin and orbital moments. Among them, the anisotropic magnetic dipole (AMD), which reflects the local orbital anisotropy, shares the symmetry of magnetization and can have a ferroic component even when the spin moments cancel. AMD responses have thus far been identified primarily in antiferromagnets with unit-cell magnetic periodicity, whereas spatially modulated AMDs in long-wavelength magnetic textures remain unexplored. Here, we report resonant soft x-ray small-angle scattering measurements on the antiferromagnetic spin cycloid of the multiferroic BiFeO$_3$. We observe pronounced circular dichroism in the resonant scattering intensity, i.e., scattering circular dichroism, which is not expected from the established cycloidal and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya-interaction-induced sinusoidal spin structures. We show that the staggered rotation of the FeO$_6$ octahedra gives rise to ferroic AMD components despite the antiparallel spin alignment. As the local magnetic symmetry varies with the cycloidal phase, these AMDs are spatially modulated and produce the dichroism through interference with the sinusoidal spin component. Our findings demonstrate that long-wavelength antiferromagnetic textures can host spatially modulated AMDs, opening new avenues for exploring hidden multipole textures in magnetic and multiferroic materials.

authors.name: S. Kawachi
authors.institution: Tokyo Medical University Hachioji Medical Center

papers.title: Direct measurement of the on-shot focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class petawatt laser
papers.abstract: We report a direct, on-shot determination of the focal-spot size of a kilojoule-class, four-beam petawatt laser. Encircled-energy curves were inferred from the energy transmitted around aluminum-coated spheres of varying diameters placed at the focal plane. The 50% encircled-energy diameter D50 of each beam was obtained by fitting a two-component Gaussian mixture with Bayesian inference. With all deformable mirrors optimized in closed loop, the best-corrected alignment beam reached D50 = 34 (+4/-5) um, three times the diffraction limit of 10 um. Under full-power conditions, the thermal distortion of the main amplifier broadened this beam to D50 = 102 (+9/-8) um and reduced its peak intensity ninefold, to 2.2 (+0.6/-0.9) x 10^18 W/cm^2 at 250 J and 1.3 ps. The energy fraction of the narrow component decreased from 68% to 38%. These reference values serve facility users, and a deformable mirror upstream of the pulse compressor, now on one beam only, doubles the on-shot peak intensity.

authors.name: Ryou Oomura
authors.institution: Institute of Laser Engineering, The University of Osaka

papers.title: Effective-dimension estimation of a minimal turbulent channel flow via IRMAE-WD
papers.abstract: The implicit rank-minimizing autoencoder with weight decay (IRMAE-WD) (Zeng et al. 2024) aims to estimate the dimension of the low-dimensional manifold underlying high-dimensional data from a sharp drop in the latent singular values of a single trained model. We apply IRMAE-WD with a three-dimensional convolutional autoencoder to velocity fields of a minimal turbulent channel flow at ${\rm Re}_{\tau}=110$ and examine whether the drop represents the intrinsic degrees of freedom. We also compare the number of coordinates IRMAE-WD needs for a given reconstruction accuracy or smallest reproduced scale with that of proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). We find that a clear drop appears and that the reconstruction rate decreases by at most 0.01 percentage points with truncation at the drop. The drop thus marks the effective dimension of the trained representation. However, the drop position moves to the lower-dimension side as linear layers are added. In addition, the reconstruction error decreases only gradually with the number of coordinates in all but the smallest wavelength band. These results suggest that the drop position is set by the implicit regularization of the linear layers and cannot be regarded as the intrinsic degrees of freedom. In contrast, with transfer learning, the smallest number of coordinates needed for a given accuracy hardly depends on the number of linear layers and is smaller than that of POD up to a reconstruction rate of about 97%. IRMAE-WD also reproduces a given scale with fewer coordinates than POD. Above about 97%, however, POD requires fewer coordinates, mainly because IRMAE-WD reconstructs large-scale structures less precisely. Hence, when the error decreases continuously, as in the minimal channel flow, the number of coordinates needed to represent wall turbulence should be stated with the required accuracy or scale, not as a single number.

papers.title: Genuinely Out-of-Equilibrium Bose-Einstein Condensation
papers.abstract: Bose-Einstein (BE) condensation typically occurs in the ground state. Prominent exceptions include excitons, whose ground state is the vacuum; consequently, they undergo BE condensation only in out-of-equilibrium regimes to counteract rapid decay. Here, we develop a driven-dissipative framework to address this challenge, demonstrating that BE condensates emerge under sufficiently strong excitation in one and two dimensions. In three dimensions, by incorporating effective loss rates and a specified injection energy, we find a percent-level condensate fraction, consistent in order of magnitude with the exciton experiment of Morita et al. (Nat. Commun. 13, 5388 (2022)).

authors.name: Masahito Ueda
authors.institution: RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science

papers.title: Taylor expansions for first-passage time distributions of Brownian motion with moving boundaries
papers.abstract: We analyse the distribution of the first-passage time of Brownian motion to a time-dependent boundary as a function of the boundary. We prove that the boundary-to-distribution map is infinitely many times differentiable along the Cameron-Martin space $\mathscr{H},$ and obtain a with a bound on the truncation error Taylor expansion with a bound on the truncation error. We obtain identities connecting (i) the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution, (ii) the Wiener-It\^o chaos kernels of the indicator that the Brownian motion stays below the boundary, and (iii) Krylov-Veretennikov-Zvonkin-type operators. These identities yield relatively tractable representations for the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution when the taboo transition density is available, notably for linear boundaries. As an application of the above results we propose Taylor approximations up to second order of the first-passage time distribution. In the examples considered, the first-order approximation is more accurate than the classical tangent approximation and its hazard-rate variant, while remaining straightforward to implement.

papers.title: The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice
papers.abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, fundamentally driven by the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm, rely on setting external objectives and iterative trial-and-error. When confronted with complex nonlinear problems containing noise and conflicting constraints, this paradigm inherently induces statistical smoothing and compromise, yielding black-box models that lack interpretability and out-of-distribution generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology, reconstructing the solving process into four irreversible stages: Deconstruction, Structure, Construction, and Solving. The method suspends a priori presuppositions to strip unit coupling, extracts rigid invariants inherent to the problem, constructs equivalent mappings anchored to these invariants, and executes the mapping directly to generate the solution. Evaluation metrics and experience are relegated to a posteriori verification. Demonstrated through cross-disciplinary practices including number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, this methodology transcends the statistical fitting bottleneck. Structure-Driven and Objective-Driven methodologies are complementary: when structure is sufficient, solutions are directly constructed; when lacking, it degenerates into the OD path.

papers.title: GNetSS: Towards Learning GNSS Corrections without Ground Truth
papers.abstract: We present GNetSS, a self-supervised GNSS position correction framework that improves the robustness of single point positioning (SPP) without requiring ground-truth locations for training. GNetSS combines a transformer-based network with a deterministic differentiable positioning solver. The network predicts satellite-wise pseudorange corrections by modelling inter-satellite geometry and temporal context, while the solver converts these corrected measurements into receiver position corrections under GNSS geometry and optional motion constraints. Unlike supervised GNSS correction methods that rely on ground-truth, GNetSS derives its training signal directly from GNSS measurement consistency. Experimental results show that GNetSS improves robustness across open-sky, urban, and forested environments. The method is particularly effective at suppressing large-error outliers, reducing the maximum 3D positioning error by over 50% compared with SPP. These results demonstrate the potential of self-supervised pseudorange correction for scalable and robust GNSS positioning in real-world autonomy applications. Code and the in-house dataset will be released upon acceptance.

authors.name: Fahira Afzal Maken
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

authors.name: Qingqing Cheng
authors.institution: University of Shanghai for Science and Technology

authors.name: Milad Ramezani
authors.institution: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation

papers.title: Polynomial Spaces Are Locally Paley-Wiener: Bulk Universality and Christoffel Asymptotics on Symmetric Convex Bodies
papers.abstract: We prove a bulk universality limit for total-degree polynomial spaces on symmetric convex bodies. For a Bernstein-Markov measure with a positive continuous density near an interior point, the rescaled reproducing kernel converges to the Fourier integral over the dual unit ball of the Baran metric, which we call the local spectral body. After diagonal normalization, the limit is the Fourier transform of the uniform probability measure on this body. The result holds uniformly on compact subsets where the local density assumption holds and yields the corresponding Christoffel asymptotic. Its main constructive ingredient is recovery, with the exact rescaled $L^2$ norm, of Paley-Wiener functions at arbitrary interior centres by Chebyshev ridge polynomials. This extends the classical polynomial-entire function limit at the symmetry centre to a position-dependent local spectrum. Ellipsoidal spectral bodies recover the known Bessel profile on the ball; polytopal spectral bodies give other Fourier profiles. For rectangles, the two-dimensional profile is a product of two sinc functions. On a regular hexagon, the local spectral body changes from a hexagon to a parallelogram across the inscribed circle; explicit Fourier profiles are available in both regimes. The proof uses the Siciak extremal function and does not require a differential operator or an explicit orthogonal-polynomial kernel.

papers.title: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
papers.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

authors.name: Sangwon Jeong
authors.institution: Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Auslander bounds under recollements and arrow removal
papers.abstract: Auslander bounds measure uniformity in the eventual vanishing of extension groups and are closely related to homological conjectures, including the Auslander-Reiten conjecture and finitistic dimension conjecture. We study global and finitistic Auslander bounds of finite-dimensional algebras under recollements and arrow removal. For a recollement induced by an idempotent $e$ of an algebra $\Lambda$, we establish inequalities comparing the bounds of $\Lambda$ with those of the quotient algebra $\Lambda/\Lambda e\Lambda$ and the corner algebra $e\Lambda e$. We also establish comparison results for cleft extensions and deduce that arrow removal preserves finiteness of both the global and finitistic Auslander bounds. Finally, we construct radical-square-zero algebras with $\findim(\Lambda_n)=0$ and $\mr{fab}(\Lambda_n)=\mr{gb}(\Lambda_n)=n$ for every $n\geq1$, yielding arbitrarily large gaps between finitistic Auslander bounds and finitistic dimensions.

papers.title: A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions
papers.abstract: Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times. The inverse preserves the profile and entry bound. We identify every partition missed at the next deficit. A prefix test decides whether any cylinder lies outside this sector and, if so, identifies the unique one of least deficit. This explains the leading coefficient gap in Warnaar's $Q_{n,c}$. We also determine the first correction to the vertex terms of the published bounded determinant.

papers.title: QUBO-based feature selection for MRI undersampling pattern design
papers.abstract: We formulate undersampling mask design for Cartesian magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as a feature subset selection problem. Each sampling line is represented by a binary feature indicating whether it is included in each candidate mask. Using candidate masks and their training-set evaluations, we estimate mutual information (MI) and conditional mutual information (CMI). These estimates and a sampling-count penalty define a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. The model is solved using simulated annealing and quantum annealing to determine a feature subset and its corresponding sampling mask. We assess the selected subsets on the test set through zero-filled reconstruction in Fourier undersampling simulations using fastMRI knee magnitude reference images, with patient-disjoint training and test sets. At all six tested target sampling rates from 15% to 40%, the resulting reconstructions have lower mean root mean square error than those obtained with four conventional sampling methods. They also have higher mean structural similarity than those obtained using univariate mutual-information ranking at all tested rates. These results support information-theoretic feature selection as an approach to MRI undersampling mask design under the tested zero-filled simulation settings.

papers.title: The Scott sobriety on countable Frechet-Urysohn dcpos and locally compact meet-continuous dcpos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we focus on the Scott Sobriety of countable dcpos and locally compact dcpos. Recently, Chen, Kou and Yang proved that every countable dcpo with its Scott topology first-countable is sober endowed with the Scott topology. A natural question is whether a countable dcpo whose Scott topology is a Frechet-Urysohn sapce must be sober. We show that a countable dcpo with condition FG is Scott sober if its Scott topology is Frechet-Urysohn. Besides, a countable Scott non sober Frechet-Urysohn dcpo is constructed. He and Zhang gave two sufficient conditions for the open problem whether every locally compact dcpo is Scott sober. One of their sufficient conditions is that any locally compact meet-continuous coherent dcpo is Scott sober. We further prove that each locally compact meet-continuous dcpo is always sober with respect to the Scott topology.

authors.name: Zhengmao He
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models provide variant-level evidence, but connecting that evidence to phenotype hypotheses requires accounting for uncertainty throughout structured reasoning. We introduce an uncertainty-conditioned path-energy framework that converts sequence predictions and calibrated predictive uncertainty into explicit distributions over graph-supported phenotype hypotheses, without patient-level phenotype supervision. An interpretable learned energy scores admissible gene--disease--phenotype routes, query uncertainty controls the target temperature, and path probabilities are aggregated into phenotype hypotheses. This formulation makes evidence quality an explicit determinant of hypothesis breadth while retaining traceable multi-path support. Exact normalization over enumerable candidate sets provides a reference for evaluating a Hastings-corrected learned revision operator. On AlzKB and Hetionet, phenotype-level entropy tracks upstream uncertainty, with Spearman correlations of 0.951 and 0.878, respectively; ablations identify the contribution of uncertainty conditioning. In masked-edge recovery, the model exceeds chance and degree-matched probability-permutation controls. Training the energy under the uncertainty-dependent temperature yields higher held-out recall@10 than training under a constant temperature of comparable magnitude. Under gene hold-out, recall@10 exceeds that of a trained DistMult embedding on 24 of 30 graph masks (0.183 versus 0.123); this difference is attributable mainly to three genes with many variants and is not established for all genes. These results establish an uncertainty-aware interface from genomic predictions to graph-supported phenotype hypotheses that combines interpretable probability allocation with held-out association recovery of explicitly stated scope.

authors.name: Huixin Zhan
authors.institution: New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology

papers.title: Partitioned iterative FD-SPH for fluid-rigid-body interaction: Stability and validation for lightweight floating bodies
papers.abstract: This study assesses partitioned iterative fictitious-domain smoothed particle hydrodynamics (FD-SPH) for free-surface fluid-rigid-body interaction. Extending a strong-coupling framework for deformable structures, it combines volume-based hydrodynamic loads with Newton-Euler rigid-body updates. Within each time step, the mismatch between pressure-projected fictitious-fluid and rigid-body velocities is fed back iteratively. A fractional-step interpretation identifies conditions under which Passively Moving Solid (PMS) projection and Newton-Euler updates yield identical rigid-body velocities. Single-pass and iterative FD-SPH are compared under matched conditions. A two-dimensional settling-disk benchmark agrees with published results. In three-dimensional buoyancy-driven cube tests, single-pass coupling becomes unstable at specific gravities of 0.1 and 0.2. At 0.1, reducing the time-step size by a factor of 500 does not suppress the instability. Iterative strong coupling remains stable across the tested range of 0.1-1.0. Equilibrium heights and orientations agree with hydrostatic expectations and published stable configurations, respectively. Two- and three-dimensional wet-bed dam-break simulations reproduce experimental trends in wave elevation and floating-body heave and pitch. Two star-shaped rigid bodies demonstrate applicability to complex geometries without explicit interface reconstruction or surface-normal evaluation. All production strong-coupling simulations satisfy the prescribed relative-residual criterion at every time step before reaching the maximum coupling-iteration count. These results support iterative FD-SPH for lightweight and complex floating bodies in transient free-surface flows.

authors.name: Hiroyuki Omura
authors.institution: The Japan Food Machinery Manufacturers' Association

papers.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
papers.abstract: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo. For a related family of lattice-polarized $K3$ surfaces, we give a geometric realization of the ring of meromorphic modular forms with prescribed poles and trivial character and describe the corresponding Looijenga compactification.

authors.name: Yota Maeda
authors.institution: Toyota Central Research and Development Laboratories (Japan)

papers.title: The Scaled Dirichlet Distribution: Lauricella Representations and Estimation
papers.abstract: We derive explicit expressions for the mixed moments of the scaled Dirichlet distribution in terms of the Lauricella hypergeometric function of type $D$. The relationship with Carlson's multivariate $R$-function is stated, and the convergence conditions required for the series derivation are made explicit. The general expressions yield means, second moments and covariances, with Gauss and Appell hypergeometric representations in the bivariate and trivariate cases. Method-of-moments and maximum-likelihood formulations are presented, together with simulation summaries and an illustrative comparison of scaled Dirichlet and ordinary Dirichlet fits to compositional futures-return data.

papers.title: Circuit model for gate-induced excitation of quantum Hall edges tuned by DC gate bias
papers.abstract: Edge excitations, which propagate along the edge of a quantum Hall system, are of great interest in the study of low-dimensional electron systems and mesoscopic transport phenomena. In this study, we investigate the relationship between the input voltage and the excitation waveform for gate-induced excitations. By varying the offset voltage applied to the gate, we observe that the excitation waveform changes from a first-derivative-like response to a response proportional to the input waveform in the time domain. In the frequency domain, we observe that the frequency dependence of the gate excitation changes significantly as the offset voltage crosses the pinch-off voltage. We show that these changes can be described by a single equivalent circuit model with different effective gate-2DEG capacitances on either side of the pinch-off voltage. In addition, we confirm that the effective capacitance obtained from the fitting of the model with the experimental data is consistent with the capacitance calculated from the device structure.

papers.title: Rational Designs and Prouhet--Tarry--Escott Problems
papers.abstract: For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory. We also prove a general theorem transforming integer-weighted rational designs into equi-weighted designs on distinct rational points. On the unit circle $\mathbb{S}^1$, we determine the minimum sizes of rational spherical designs of strengths $4,5,6,7$ and show that they are respectively $2304,4608,9216,9216$. We also show that the minimum size of a rational spherical $5$-design on $\mathbb{S}^2$ is $192$. We further apply our framework to prove a conjecture of Thuswaldner--Ziegler on sums of distinct units and to answer Mahabaduge's problem on convex equilateral lattice polygons affirmatively.

papers.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE
papers.abstract: Crash simulations of glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts are highly sensitive to the fiber-orientation field supplied to the material model. In conventional workflows, that field comes from resin-flow analysis, which requires molding-specialist support and takes about 25 hours of work per part. We previously proposed a surrogate model that addresses this bottleneck by predicting the orientation field in about 3 minutes. This paper reports the implementation, validation, and operational design that turned the model into an engineering tool for Honda design workflows. We present staged validation from 2D plates to production parts, evaluation against a predefined engineering angular-error criterion, and the expert review that approved design use in March 2025; the system has since been transferred to the crash-safety group and is in initial, limited use in directed fracture-prediction scenarios. The developed system combines injection-gate setting support for cases in which gates are unknown (90% gate-count accuracy, mean position error 11% of flow length), voxelization, surrogate inference, automatic mapping to the crash CAE model, and report generation in a single GUI. The complete orientation-preparation workflow takes about 0.1 hours, a 99.6% reduction from the conventional 25-hour flow-analysis route, and can be run directly by crash CAE engineers without molding-specialist support. As evidence of practical impact, component-level crash analysis using the predicted orientation field reduced the absolute peak-force error from 19.0% with an isotropic baseline to 11.4%, while confining predicted fracture to the test-observed region. The deployment lesson is that a surrogate model alone is not enough for practical adoption: gate-setting support, automatic data conversion, and shareable reporting are what make the model usable as a design tool.

papers.title: DfD-GS: Defocus Image Prior for Metric-Scale Single-View Depth Estimation and View Synthesis
papers.abstract: Recovering metric-scale geometry from observations at a single viewpoint remains fundamentally ill-posed, limiting the reliability of novel view synthesis. Recent methods rely on learned monocular depth priors, which provide strong structural estimates but can suffer from scale ambiguity and dataset-dependent biases. We propose DfD-GS, a feed-forward framework that predicts a metric-scale 3D Gaussian scene representation from a single-view all-in-focus--defocused image pair. The key idea is to exploit defocus blur as a physical metric depth cue. DfD-GS first estimates a defocus-based metric disparity map from the all-in-focus--defocused image pair and the corresponding defocus strength. This estimate is used to align and refine a monocular depth prior to metric scale. Visible and hidden 3D Gaussians are then predicted for occlusion-aware novel view synthesis. Experiments on synthetic-defocus datasets constructed from Booster and Middlebury show that DfD-GS outperforms single-image baselines in metric depth estimation and novel view synthesis. On WildRGB-D, DfD-GS achieves lower AbsRel and LPIPS but higher depth RMSE than the single-image baselines. Additional analyses show that DfD-GS maintains a more stable metric scale under field-of-view changes. Qualitative results on a real dataset show recovery of the main scene structure under optical defocus.

papers.title: $p$-adic Fourier theory for unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and weighted Monna maps
papers.abstract: We generalize a recent result of Ardakov and Berger on the $p$-adic valuations of Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials evaluated at Lubin--Tate periods over the unramified quadratic extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. For finite unramified extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ of degree $f \geq 2$, we introduce a weighted analogue of the Monna map and show that it determines the valuations of these polynomial values for Lubin--Tate formal groups whose formal logarithms are $p$-typical. Our proof uses the Artin--Hasse exponential and Witt vectors. As an application, for a distinguished Lubin--Tate formal group, we determine the exact norms of the associated Schneider--Teitelbaum polynomials on Banach spaces of locally analytic functions and obtain an explicit rescaling of the Banach basis constructed by Bannai and Kobayashi so that each basis element has norm one.

papers.title: Elliptic analogues of KP and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions
papers.abstract: We develop a tau-function framework for soliton solutions on elliptic backgrounds associated with the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy and its B-type counterpart (BKP). Starting from discrete KP (dKP) and discrete BKP (dBKP) equations of elliptic type, we construct Casorati and Gram determinant tau functions for the elliptic dKP through Darboux and binary Darboux transformations, and elliptic Pfaffian tau functions for dBKP through the Moutard transformation. Moreover, the higher-order discrete KP and BKP hierarchies together with their tau functions are constructed via Pfaffian identities. Then, through Miwa transformations, the continuous elliptic KP, modified KP, and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions are provided. Suitable constraints on spectral parameters or wave numbers yield reductions to the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV), focusing and defocusing modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV), and Sawada--Kotera (SK) equations, together with their solutions on elliptic backgrounds. We also construct KP line-soliton solutions and obtain lump solutions for the KP-I equation. For selected determinant families, we establish sufficient conditions for real-valuedness and global nonsingularity. The resulting framework provides a common approach to elliptic tau functions, their discrete and continuous bilinear identities, and the construction of solutions through reductions.

papers.title: Detection and Recovery of Core--Periphery Structure in Random Geometric Graphs
papers.abstract: Core--periphery (CP) structure, characterized by a dense core of interconnected nodes linked to sparsely connected peripheral nodes, is a prevalent feature of many real-world networks. We propose a core--periphery random geometric graph (CP-RGG) model in which vertices are independently and uniformly distributed on the unit cube \([0,1]^m\), and each vertex is designated as a core node with probability \(p_n\). Two vertices are connected if their Euclidean distance falls below a type-dependent threshold, governed by three distinct radii for core--core, core--periphery, and periphery--periphery pairs. We investigate the information-theoretic limits for both the detection and recovery of the core in the CP-RGG. For detection in the non-degenerate regime, we prove that the total variation distance between the CP-RGG and a null RGG without CP structure converges to one if and only if the expected number of core nodes tends to infinity. For recovery, we demonstrate that almost exact recovery is achievable if and only if the expected degree tends to infinity. Finally, we establish limits for exact recovery. In the one-dimensional sparse regime (\(m=1\)), we obtain a sharp threshold when the core--core and core--periphery radii coincide. For \(m\ge2\), when the core has polynomial size and the core--periphery radius exceeds twice the periphery--periphery radius, we prove that the exact recovery threshold is sharp up to constant factors, scaling on the order of \(\log n\).

authors.name: Mingao Yuan
authors.institution: The University of Texas at El Paso

papers.title: Sonic Palette: Predicting Dynamic Color Themes from Music
papers.abstract: We present Sonic Palette, a music-driven framework for predicting time-varying color themes from audio. Rather than treating music-to-palette generation as a static problem, our method formulates music--color correspondence as a cross-modal sequence prediction task that models how palette-level visual attributes evolve over time in response to music. Specifically, Sonic Palette uses a music-conditioned autoregressive Transformer to predict frame-wise color themes, each represented by five dominant colors, from input audio features. To support this task, we curate a dataset of paired audio--color sequences derived from 265 full-length official music videos. We further visualize the predicted color themes through a palette-guided recoloring process that preserves image structure while revealing temporally varying color appearance associated with the music. Quantitative results show that Sonic Palette predicts color themes that more closely match the ground truth, while subjective results indicate more natural temporal color transitions and stronger perceived music--color atmosphere alignment, highlighting its potential for music-driven visual design, computational art, and creative visual authoring.

authors.name: Kenneth Yang
authors.institution: The University of Texas at El Paso

papers.title: Chasing the KPZ exponents
papers.abstract: Forty years after it was written down, the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation is the paradigm of scale invariance far from equilibrium. In one dimension it has been solved exactly and confirmed by precision experiments, and its scaling has now been observed in two-dimensional polariton condensates. Above one dimension, however, not a single exponent is known exactly, and even the existence of an upper critical dimension is disputed. In this Perspective we argue that firm statements need not wait for exact solutions. Treating the nonlinearity as an effective noise that acts on a fractal subset of the substrate leads to bounds on the roughness exponent, $1/(d+1)\le\alpha\le 1/d$ in $d$ dimensions. We examine the assumptions behind these bounds, confront them with four decades of theory, simulations and the new experiments, and identify the tests---foremost in three and more dimensions---that would establish or refute them.

papers.title: A Unified Unfolding and Slide-Vector Model for Asymmetric Dissimilarities via Clustered Lasso
papers.abstract: Asymmetric multidimensional scaling (AMDS) methods represent asymmetric dissimilarity data in a low-dimensional space. Existing approaches include the highly flexible unfolding model and the parsimonious slide-vector model. However, a highly flexible model is not necessarily optimal for adequately representing asymmetric relationships, and a model with an intermediate level of complexity may be more effective. In this study, we propose a new AMDS model that integrates the unfolding and slide-vector models by incorporating a clustered Lasso penalty. By fusing similar slide vectors, the proposed method can represent intermediate model structures and adjust model complexity according to the observed data. In numerical simulations, we compared the proposed method with existing methods by varying the number of groups, the number of objects, and the number of dimensions. The results demonstrated that the proposed method achieved high estimation accuracy across various asymmetric structures. Furthermore, in an application to cola brand-switching data, the proposed method achieved the highest accuracy in reproducing asymmetric relationships among the three methods compared and yielded a lower stress value than the slide-vector model. These findings suggest that adaptively adjusting model complexity may be effective for representing asymmetric relationships more accurately.

papers.title: Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincar\'e-type compactification, but a general theory was not established. Here, the two-dimensional ODE system derived by the linear chain trick is rewritten as an orbit equation, and a comparison theorem and an Osgood-type integral condition are applied to obtain a blow-up criterion based on the existence of a subsolution. This characterizes the nonlinearities for which memory-induced blow-up occurs. This paper also gives a necessary condition in a special case, a global existence condition based on a supersolution, and a systematic method for constructing subsolutions for separable nonlinearities. These results recover the author's previous results and are illustrated through several examples.

papers.title: Gaussian Quasi-Likelihood Estimation for Nonsynchronously Observed L\'evy processes
papers.abstract: We study parametric inference for a two-dimensional simple L\'evy process observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon, where the two components are sampled in a possibly non-synchronous manner. Combining Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimation for L\'evy SDEs with the non-synchronous quasi-likelihood methodology, we construct a Gaussian-type quasi-likelihood based on the covariance structure of non-synchronous increments, and we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators. The convergence rates coincide with those in the synchronous setting, while the asymptotic variance depends essentially on the sampling design and becomes more complicated under non-synchronicity. To handle the different moment structure of pure-jump L\'evy processes, we introduce an additional convergence assumption and provide tractable sufficient conditions linked to the observation scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Distributed Fiber Monitoring on a Coherent DSP ASIC: Implementation of Longitudinal Power Monitoring
papers.abstract: Coherent DSP ASICs and transceivers to date report a rich set of optical link metrics, yet these remain cumulative over the link and provide no spatial localization. This paper presents the implementation design of fiber-longitudinal power monitoring (LPM), which recovers spatially resolved power profiles from received traffic, on a coherent DSP ASIC chip. We first identify the challenges specific to DSP implementation, and describe the enabling algorithm and architecture. We then present the key design considerations for retaining the estimation fidelity of the on-chip LPM during in-service operation. On this basis, we implement LPM on a coherent DSP, a 3-nm 800G low-power DSP ASIC housed in an OSFP pluggable module, which constitutes, to our knowledge, the first coherent DSP ASIC and transceiver to perform distributed fiber monitoring and data communication simultaneously. The on-chip LPM is experimentally validated over links of up to 1005 km using 400ZR+ and 800ZR+ traffic, with no measurable impact on Q factor or module power consumption. Multi-vendor interoperability is also demonstrated, where the on-chip LPM operates on signals transmitted by third-party transceivers. These results extend coherent DSPs from cumulative to spatially resolved monitoring, allowing pluggable transceivers, deployable from DCI to long-haul, to act not only as cost-efficient transmission elements but also as distributed monitoring points across diverse optical network infrastructure.

papers.title: Motion-Sickness-Aware Vehicle Control via DKUC-Based Inverse Design and Iterative Feedback Tuning
papers.abstract: Tuning existing vehicle controllers for motion-sickness reduction requires a desired vehicle response that reflects physiological comfort. The six-degree-of-freedom subjective vertical conflict (6DoF-SVC) model can evaluate sensory conflict induced by vehicle motion, but it does not directly provide a target motion for controller design. This paper proposes a 2-step framework to construct such a reference. First, a target SVC trajectory is generated from the baseline response by limiting conflict peaks while imposing a minimum activity level. Second, a lifted linear model identified using Deep KoopmanU with Control (DKUC) is inverted to map the target SVC trajectory to a regularized reference expressed in vehicle-acceleration and angular-velocity coordinates. The resulting motion reference is then used in an Iterative Feedback Tuning (IFT)-style procedure for fixed-structure PI and LQR controllers. In the considered simulation scenario, the selected SVC target reduces the sequence norm by 6.95\% relative to the baseline. Controller tuning with reduced response models decreases the regularized PI and LQR objectives by 49.5\% and 32.3\%, respectively. These results show that a nonlinear physiological comfort objective can be converted into a practical motion reference for tuning fixed-structure vehicle controllers.

papers.title: Koopman Lifting for Linear Encrypted Control of Nonlinear Systems: Applications to LQR and MPC
papers.abstract: Homomorphic encryption enables control computations to be outsourced to a third-party cloud server without disclosing measurements or controller parameters. Applying existing encrypted linear controllers to nonlinear plants requires a compatible representation of the plant dynamics. This paper presents Homomorphically Encrypted Koopman-Based Control (HEK-Control), which connects nonlinear plants to encrypted linear computations through Koopman lifting. A trusted plant-side client evaluates nonlinear functions of the measured state, and a linear predictor identified in these coordinates supports conventional controller design. The resulting control laws retain the server's encrypted linear operations. We demonstrate the framework using state feedback based on linear quadratic regulation and input-constrained model predictive control. Closed-loop simulations with the Cheon--Kim--Kim--Song encryption scheme show close agreement with unencrypted computations. Additional unencrypted simulations compare regulation under input constraints across a common set of controller designs. For a continuous stirred-tank reactor, Koopman lifting supports regulation at input bounds not handled by the tested controllers designed directly in the original state coordinates. Tests of encrypted computations also show that packing multiple values into each ciphertext reduces computation time and communication volume. These results clarify how existing encrypted linear computations can serve nonlinear plants.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
papers.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.
